title: Madālasopakhyāna[satīka]
subject: Kathā
date_note: = Thursday 25 Dec 1721, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti bhāśvatīkaraṇe śatānaṃdaviracite parilekhādhikyaro ʼṣṭamaḥ samāptaḥ || śrīgaṃgāsāgarārppaṇam astu || śake 1643 pauṣe māse śukle 7 gurau (drugulyāṃ) śrīgoviṃdajotirvidā likhitaṃ svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca || atra gauḍagraṃthe siddhāṃtarahasye deśāṃtaraṃ jojanaṃ (!) || 205 śrīrāghavaśarmaṇā likhitam asti tenātrāsmābhir likhitaṃ deśāyo 205 deśāṃtaṃraṃ [[155]] (!) 2135 prabhā 5/10 yadvā 5/8 ----- /// (fol. 6r7-11)
purpose: svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca (for the scribe's own use and for others)
notes: The catalogue lists Rāghava Śarmā as the scribe, which is wrong. The colophon names Govinda Jyotirvid as the scribe of this copy. Rāghava Śarman is cited for a deśāntara value of 205 yojanas in the Gauḍa work Siddhāntarahasya ('śrīrāghavaśarmaṇā likhitam asti tenātrāsmābhir likhitaṃ'). He is probably Rāghavānanda Śarman, the Bengali author of the Siddhāntarahasya, so he is the source of a cited figure, not someone involved in making this copy. 'svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca' could imply Govinda also owned the copy, but because it is for others as well, owner was not added. 'śrīgaṃgāsāgarārppaṇam astu' ('may it be offered to Gaṅgāsāgara') is ambiguous: it could refer to the pilgrimage site or deity, or to a person named Gaṅgāsāgara. No person was recorded for it. The place 'drugulyāṃ' was put in parentheses by the cataloguer, so the reading is uncertain, and it cannot be identified. CE: Pauṣa śukla 7 of ŚS 1643 falls around late Dec 1721 or early Jan 1722, and the weekday has not been checked. The numbers after the colophon (deśāntara 2135, prabhā 5/10 or 5/8) are the scribe's astronomical notes.

title: Śivarātrīvratakathā MTM titles: Kṛṣṇārjunasaṃvāda Dharmalakṣmīsaṃvāda Māsayā khā Siṃjāti *Devastotrasamuccaya
subject: Kathā
date_note: ≈ 1734 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti śrīsivarātrikathā samāptaḥ || (2) saṃvat 8 sara 4 dā dava vera macoyāḥ || : || (exp. 13t1–2)
notes: The year is written as a mix of digits and a number-word: '8 sara 4'. 'sara' = śara, which stands for 5, so with the digits in written order the year is NS 854 = CE 1734. The catalogue gives NS 804 (CE 1684), apparently taking 'sara' as zero, but śara is not a standard word for 0. If the word-numeral convention (right to left) were applied the year would be 458, which is implausible for pracalita script. Either 804 or 854 fits the script. The digits should be checked on the manuscript. 'dā' is Newari for 'year'. In 'dava vera macoyāḥ', 'vera' is probably Skt. velā 'time' and 'coyā' means 'written'. 'macoyāḥ' could be ma- + coyā 'written by/at' or the negative 'not written'. The phrase is unclear, and no name of scribe, owner or king appears.
review: Year reread as NS 854 (CE 1734), not 804: 'sara' is most likely śara, the standard bhūtasaṃkhyā word for 5 (the arrows of Kāma). Nothing in the colophon supports reading it as 0. The catalogue's 804 / 1684 is recorded in the notes.
Notes expanded: 'dā' is Newari for 'year'; possible readings of 'dava vera macoyāḥ' added.

subject: Nāṭaka
date_note: = Wednesday 14 Dec 1689, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti jaiminibhārataṃ saṃpūrṇṇaṃ || || sumatiśrījitāmitra,malladevo mahīpatiḥ || yudhiṣṭhirasya yajñasya nṛtyārambhaṃ karoti hi || śrīsūryavaṃśaśatapatrasahasraraśmir nnamrībhavan nṛpatikairavakānanenduḥ | bhaktāpure jayati bhūpaśirastharatna- bhābhir vvicitrapadapaṅkaśrīnakhenduḥ1 || || jitāmitramallaṃ, gopālaṃ gopālaḥ | jitāmitramallaḥ saputraṃ punātu || || ≪in a later hand:≫ samvat 810 pauṣasudi 3 pyākhana ṛ tayā dina || samvat 809 caitrasudi 13 ghaṃtijyā ārambha yāṅā dina || || samvat 809 śrāvaṇa śudi 1 ghaṃtijyā, dhuna dina || || (fol. 37v)
notes: The dates were added in a later hand and appear to record the production of the play rather than the copying of the manuscript. In chronological order: NS 809 Caitra śukla 13 (c. Mar/Apr 1689), the ghaṃtijyā was begun (ārambha); NS 809 Śrāvaṇa śukla 1 (c. Jul/Aug 1689), the ghaṃtijyā was finished (dhuna); NS 810 Pauṣa śukla 3 (c. Dec 1689/Jan 1690), the day of the pyākhana (dance-drama performance). 'ghaṃtijyā' is unclear; it may mean rehearsal or preparatory work for the play. The phrase 'pyākhana ṛ tayā' looks corrupt. No explicit copying date is given. Jitāmitra Malla (r. c. 1673–1696, Bhaktapur) is praised as the king. His authorship of the play is inferred from 'nṛtyārambhaṃ karoti' and from the usual attribution of the Jaiminibhārata nāṭaka to him; the colophon does not state it outright. 'gopāla' in the closing benediction is the deity (Kṛṣṇa). The catalogue lists Ugra Malla and Bhūpatīndra Malla, but they are not named here; they are only implied by 'saputraṃ' (with his son(s)). 'bhaktāpure' occurs in the praise verse, so Bhaktapur as the place of copying is plausible but not explicitly stated.

Date: kept NS 810 Pauṣa śukla 3 as the main date. Added a note that all three dates are in a later hand and record the play's rehearsal and performance, not when the manuscript was copied. ce_approx 1690 is right by NS+880; in fact the date falls in Dec 1689 or Jan 1690.
Notes: dropped the 'work on a bell' reading of ghaṃtijyā, which is uncertain, and added the chronological order of the three dates.
Place: noted that 'bhaktāpure' comes from the praise verse (where the king rules), not from an explicit statement of where the copy was made.

title: Ākhyātacandrikā
subject: Vyākaraṇa
colophon: ity ākhyātacandrikā samāptā || || vītyāśugābdābdaśake śucer dale ʼṣṭamyāṃ bhṛgau dvandvabhage bhage tv idam | nepāladeśe nijadarśanārtha〈〈ṃ〉〉m alīlikhac chrīdvijalālaśarmmā || 1 || (fol. 14v14-15)
notes:
Role: 'alīlikhat' is strictly the causative aorist of likh ('caused to be written'), so Dvijalāla might have commissioned the copy rather than written it. Nepalese colophons, however, often use alīlikhat simply for 'wrote'. Together with nijadarśanārtham and the catalogue's Scribe field, this makes scribe + owner the more likely reading. Commissioner remains possible.

Chronogram: 'vīty-āśuga-abda-abda-śake' is unresolved. vīti (horse) = 7 and āśuga (arrow) = 5, but 'abda' (cloud? or simply 'year') has no secure numerical value. If the second 'abda' just means 'year', only three digit-words remain, which is too few for a Śaka year. The era is taken as ŚS from 'śake', but 'śaka' can also mean 'era' in general. If the year were ŚS 1757 the date would be about CE 1835, but this is speculative, so ce_approx is left empty.

Pakṣa: 'dale' does not name the pakṣa. Śukla is inferred from the astronomy: Āṣāḍha aṣṭamī with the sun in Mithuna and the moon in Pūrvaphalgunī fits the bright fortnight. 'Śuci' may also denote Jyeṣṭha in some usage.

The 〈〈ṃ〉〉 in nijadarśanārtha〈〈ṃ〉〉m is the cataloguer's mark of a redundant anusvāra.
review: p1 roles changed from commissioner+owner to scribe+owner. 'alīlikhat' is formally a causative aorist, but Nepalese scribes routinely use it for their own copying. 'nijadarśanārtham' with himself as subject and the catalogue's 'Scribe' field both point to self-copying. Confidence lowered to medium.
date.nakshatra_yoga filled: 'bhage' = Bhaga-nakṣatra (Pūrvaphalgunī); 'dvandvabhage' = sun in Mithuna (Gemini).
date.month normalised to Śuci (= Āṣāḍha); era kept as ŚS but flagged as uncertain; chronogram discussed in notes; ce_approx left empty.
date.as_written extended to include the nakṣatra phrase.
notes rewritten.

title: Dānakelikaumudī
subject: Nāṭaka (Bhāṇikā)
colophon: dānakelikaumudī nāma bhāṇikā samāptā grathitā sumanaḥsukhadā yasya nideśena bhāṇikāsrag iyaṃ || tasya mama priyasuhṛdaḥ kaṃṭhataṭīkṣaṇam alaṃkurutāṃ || naṃdīśvare nivasatā bhāṇikeyaṃ vinirmmitā || gate manuśate śāke caṃdrasvararamanvite (!) || atha bhāṇikālakṣaṇaṃ || bhāṇikā ślākṣṇa(!)nepathyā mukhanirbbahaṇānvitā || kaiśikī bhāratīvṛttiyutaikāṃkavinirmmitā|| etc. (fol. 33v)
notes: The colophon gives nothing about the copy itself: no scribe, commissioner, owner, copying date or copying place. All of it is the author's own closing text. It says the bhāṇikā was written at the command of an unnamed dear friend ('yasya nideśena ... tasya mama priyasuhṛdaḥ'). It was composed while living at Nandīśvara ('naṃdīśvare nivasatā bhāṇikeyaṃ vinirmmitā'), the hill at Nandgaon in Braj. The composition date is 'gate manuśate śāke caṃdrasvara(sa)manvite' (the cataloguer marks 'ramanvite' as corrupt with (!)). This reads as Śaka 1471, i.e. about 1549 CE. The work is Rūpa Gosvāmin's Dānakelikaumudī, but he is not named here. After this comes a definition of the bhāṇikā genre ('atha bhāṇikālakṣaṇaṃ ...'), quoted only in part (etc.), so a scribal colophon may follow on fol. 33v without being quoted.
review: Date fields cleared (era 'none'): 'gate manuśate śāke candrasvara-samanvite' is the author's composition verse, not a copying date. Its reading is Śaka 1471 (manu 14 hundreds + candra 1, svara 7 read right to left = 71), about 1549 CE. That reading is correct and is kept in the notes.
Place cleared: Nandīśvara is where the work was composed ('naṃdīśvare nivasatā bhāṇikeyaṃ vinirmmitā'), not where it was copied. It is moved to the notes.
Persons left empty. The author (Rūpa Gosvāmin) is not named in the colophon, and the 'priyasuhṛd' at whose command the work was written is anonymous.

title: Paśupatiprādurbhāvopākhyānanāṭaka
subject: Nāṭaka
date_note: ≈ 1711 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: itiśrī śrījayabhūpatīndramalladeva, mahārājādhirāja, viracitaṃ nalacaritanāma nāṭake (!) pañcamoṅka (!) || śubham astu || || śloka 1601 || samvat [ 808 . . .] śudi 2 roja 2 śrīśivarājopādhyāyale banāyāko pustakam idaṃ bhūyāt || ❁ || (fol. 4v10–12)
notes: The year is uncertain. The cataloguer put '808' in square brackets and it is followed by lacunae. The catalogue itself gives 'NS 808?', and the month is lost. NS 808 (1688 CE) is earlier than Bhūpatīndra Malla's reign in Bhaktapur (c. NS 816–842 / 1696–1722 CE), yet the colophon calls him mahārājādhirāja. So either the reading is wrong (e.g. 818 or 828) or the title was given to him retrospectively. Bhūpatīndra appears here only as the author of the play. The catalogue lists him as 'King', but the colophon does not say this copy was made in his reign. The scribe's name 'śivarājopādhyāya' can be split as Śiva + Rājopādhyāya (the usual Newar Brahmin title) or as Śivarāja + Upādhyāya. The catalogue's 'Śivamarājopādhyāya' might point to Śivarāma. 'banāyāko' (Nepali, 'made') most likely means he copied the book, but it could also mean he had it made. 'pustakam idaṃ bhūyāt' is a garbled Sanskrit ending.

p2 confidence lowered from high to medium: the name might be Śiva + Rājopādhyāya, or Śivarāja + Upādhyāya, and the catalogue gives 'Śivamarājopādhyāya' (perhaps a corrupt Śivarāma)
'banāyāko' ('made') could cover scribe or commissioner; kept as scribe, with the ambiguity noted

notes: The two eras agree: VS 1986 − 57 = 1929 and NS 1049 + 880 = 1929. Bhādra śukla 12 with Indra Jātrā on a Sunday fits about 15 September 1929. title: Vṛttaratnākara
subject: Chandaḥśāstra
date_note: ≈ 1721 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti vṛttaratnākare ṣaṣṭhodhyāya || ❁ || (fol. 45v8) iti śrīmadvidvnmu(10)kuṭaratna śrīmadbhaṭṭarāmeśvarasūnunārāyaṇabhaṭṭaviracitāyāṃ vṛttaratnākaravyākhyāyāṃ prastārādhyāyaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ || ❁ || gaṃthaś ca samāptaḥ (11) || ❁ || nīlalohitatanu svaraśailabhūmitavikramasamā sugatā surasāsuralikhitam idaṃ vṛttaratnākaranāmakaṃ chaṃdaḥ || śubham bhūyāt || śrī | (fol. 46r9–11)
notes: The chronogram is a bhūtasaṃkhyā: nīlalohita-tanu = 8 (Śiva's eight forms), svara = 7, śaila = 7, bhū = 1. Read right to left this gives Vikrama year 1778, about 1721 CE. The catalogue gives SAM 1878 (about 1821 CE). It may have read śaila as 8 or simply be wrong, so the catalogue date conflicts with the colophon. 'sugatā' is unclear: it may be corrupt for a month or pakṣa word, or simply mean 'elapsed'. 'surasāsuralikhitam' is corrupt. It might hide a scribe's name (e.g. Sura..., Sureśvara?), but that cannot be read with confidence, so no scribe is recorded. The colophon names the commentator Nārāyaṇabhaṭṭa, son of Rāmeśvarabhaṭṭa. Kedārabhaṭṭa, who wrote the root text, is not named.
review: Date: chronogram re-read. nīlalohita-tanu = 8 (Śiva's aṣṭamūrti), svara = 7, śaila = 7, bhū = 1. Read right to left this gives VS 1778, not 1878. ce_approx changed from 1821 to 1721.

notes: The commentary is the Vṛttaratnākarādarśa ('vṛttaratnākaraṃdarśaḥ'). The author's genealogy is corrupt: 'śrīmadbhārabdāvā(!)ṣṭha' = Bhāradvāja gotra? 'kṛṣṇabhaṭṭātmaja do bhasūnu' most likely means 'son of [?de]vabhaṭṭa, the son of Kṛṣṇabhaṭṭa'. The father's name is lost; it may be (Mahā)devabhaṭṭa, i.e. the Pāyaguṇḍe family (Bālakṛṣṇa → Mahādeva → Divākara/Dinakara), but this is unverified. 'samāptim aphāṇīt' is a corruption of 'agamat', and 'śrīmārṇastu' of 'śrīr astu'. The era is a bare 'saṃvat', taken as VS. 'rāmanagara bālo' (Hindi -vālā) marks Kṛṣṇa Jośī as being from Rāmanagara (possibly the one near Vārāṇasī). It is not explicitly the place of copying. The catalogue fields (scribe Padmanābhadvija; ŚS 1701 ≈ 1779 CE) do not match this colophon, which names no scribe and gives saṃvat 1864. These fields may belong to another colophon in the same MS or be a cataloguing error.

title: Vālmīkirāmāyaṇa āraṇyakāṇḍam saṭīka
subject: Rāmāyaṇa
date_note: = Tuesday 10 Oct 1843, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: ityārṣe rāmāyaṇe āraṇyekāṇḍe vālmīkīye paṃcasaptatimaḥ sargaḥ (fol. 236r6) iti śrī majjānakīramaṇa padapaṃkajaparicaraṇa parāyaṇa śivalāla pāṭhaka pādānuyāyi bhaṭṭadevarāma saṃgṛhīte śrīmadrāmāyaṇīya viṣamapadavyākhyāne svapāṭārthaṃ rāmāyaṇaṃ saṭipaṇam lilekha kāśikāṃ madhye śrī rāmacaṃdra āleye 1 samvat 1900 kārttika vadi 2 (fol. 236r7-8)
purpose: svapāṭhārtham: for the (unnamed) scribe's own study
notes: The verb 'lilekha' has no expressed subject, so the scribe is not named in this colophon. Devarāma may have copied his own commentary with the text, but the wording does not show this. The catalogue's scribe, Rādhākṛṣṇa, is absent from the quoted colophon and may be named on another folio. Śivalāla Pāṭhaka is described as devoted to the feet of Jānakīramaṇa (Rāma). He is Devarāma's teacher ('pādānuyāyi'), so he is linked to the commentary, not to the act of copying. The commentary is the Rāmāyaṇīya Viṣamapadavyākhyāna. 'āleye' should be read 'ālaye': the copy was made at a Śrī Rāmacandra temple or house in Kāśī. The '1' before 'samvat' is probably a punctuation mark or a stray numeral. Saṃvat 1900 Kārttika vadi 2 is taken as VS, giving about October/November 1843 CE.
review: Purpose normalised to 'svapāṭhārtham: for the scribe's own study'. The scribe is not named in the colophon.

Notes expanded: the subject of 'lilekha' is unexpressed. Devarāma may be both compiler and copyist, but this is unproven. Rādhākṛṣṇa (from the catalogue) is not in the quoted text. Śivalāla is Devarāma's teacher, not the teacher of the scribe of this copy. Place = a Rāmacandra temple (ālaya) in Kāśī. The stray '1' before 'samvat' is noted.

title: Vālmīkirāmāyaṇa
subject: Rāmāyaṇa
date_note: = Sunday 19 Nov 1684, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: ityārṣe vālmīkiye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe svargārohaṇaṃ . . . . . . . . . . || samāpta . . . . samvat 805 kārtikaśuklatrayodaśī śrī śrīsumati jitāmitra malladevasa ājñāna surata . . . . . rāmacandrāya namaḥ || || śrī śrī śrīrāmalakṣmaṇasītābharataśatrughnabhyo namaḥ || || || || śubhaṃ || || . . . . . . . . . . . . . gira pradhānāṅgayā . . . . saṃpūrṇa yāṅādina juro || || . . . (fol. 108r)
purpose: completed by order (ājñā) of King Jitāmitramalla
notes: The colophon is damaged in several places. The king is written 'sumati jitāmitra malladeva'. 'Sumati' is the usual epithet in Jitāmitra Malla's name (Bhaktapur, r. c. 1673–1696 CE). The catalogue's 'Jayajitāmitra' does not match the colophon. NS 805 Kārttika falls in Oct/Nov 1684 CE, which is within his reign. 'ājñāna surata . . .' may contain the start of another person's name (lost). Only the end of the pradhānāṅga's name survives ('…gira'). Newari 'saṃpūrṇa yāṅā dina' means 'the day it was completed'. It names him as the person who completed the copy, probably by royal order, but does not say clearly whether he wrote it or had it written, so he is not tagged as scribe or commissioner.
review: p2: name kept as regnal name Jitāmitramalla; removed 'sumati' and 'deva' from titles. 'Sumati' is an epithet that forms part of this king's name, and '-deva' belongs to the regnal form. Both are recorded in notes.

p3: role changed from 'scribe' to 'minister' + 'other'. 'pradhānāṅga' is a ministerial office, and 'saṃpūrṇa yāṅā' (Newari: 'made complete') does not show that he wrote the copy himself. Name reduced to the surviving fragment '…gira'.
notes: added the fragment 'surata . . .' after 'ājñāna' (possibly a lost name) and the mismatch with the catalogue's 'Jayajitāmitra'.

title: Kavikalpalatā
subject: Sāhitya
date_note: = Monday 3 Oct 1689, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīvāgbhaṭasūnumahā(10)kavideveśvaraviracitā kavikalpalatā samāptā || || || rasavedādricaṃdre ʼbde 1746 ūrjjasyāsitapakṣa(11)ke || paṃcamyāṃ caṃdradivase nakṣatre brahmadaivake || 1 || sukhārāmeṇa cālekhi kavikalpalatābhidhaṃ || mitrarāmadvi(12)jo (!) kāśyāṃ pustakaṃ cālikhan mudā || 2 || lekhakapāṭhakayor vai śubhaṃ bhūyāt tu sarvadā || || śrīr astu || śubhakṛti(13)navaśāstrādrikṣamāsaṃkhyavarṣe sahasi kavilatākhyaṃ kalpamadhyaṃ hi pustaṃ || (fol. 49v9-13)
notes: The era is not named ('ʼbde' only). VS is inferred because the copy was made in Kāśī and the catalogue gives SAM 1746. If the era were ŚS, the date would be about 1824 CE. The weekday and nakṣatra have not been checked against an ephemeris. Two people are said to have written the manuscript: Sukhārāma ('sukhārāmeṇa cālekhi') and Mitrarāma dvija ('kāśyāṃ pustakaṃ cālikhan'). They may have been co-scribes, or one of the verbs may mean something else. The catalogue names only Mitrarāma. The (!) after 'dvijo' marks the irregular form in the original. The final half-verse gives a second date: 'śubhakṛti … navaśāstrādrikṣmā-saṃkhya-varṣe sahasi'. Read right to left, nava 9, śāstra 6, adri 7, kṣmā 1 = 1769, in the Jovian year Śubhakṛt, month Sahas (Mārgaśīrṣa). If this is VS, it is about 1712 CE, 23 years after the main date. It may record a later event in the book's history (e.g. a re-copying or acquisition). This verse is fragmentary and its relation to the main colophon is unclear. The blessing for the lekhaka and pāṭhaka is a formula and names no one.
review: p4 Mitrarāma: residence 'Kāśī' removed; the colophon only says he copied the book in Kāśī (kāśyāṃ … cālikhan), which goes in place, not residence

Date: chronogram checked (rasa 6, veda 4, adri 7, candra 1, read right to left = 1746, matching the figures). Ūrja = Kārttika, asita = kṛṣṇa, caṃdradivasa = Monday, brahmadaivaka = Rohiṇī are all confirmed. The era is not stated and VS is only inferred; this is now said in notes

subject: Sāhitya

colophon: iti srīmahomahopādhyāya (!) śrīgoviṃdaviracite kāvyapradīper ʼthālaṃkāranirṇayo nāma daśama ullāsaḥ samāptaḥ || || 10 || || saṃvat 1738 śamaye nāma phālguna māṃśe (!) kṛṣṇapakṣe prathmādīnāṃ śubhavāśare tādināṃ pustakaṃ śaṃpurnaṃ (!) jādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ maā jadi śūddha a[[śu]]ddhaṃ vā mama doṣo na dīatām|| (!) likhitaṃ bhojarā[[ja]] kāesta (!) notes: The colophon names no era, only 'saṃvat 1738'. I read it as Vikrama because of the Devanagari script, the Kāyastha scribe, and the year itself. NS 1738 is impossible, and ŚS 1738 (1816 CE) is possible but less likely. VS 1738 minus 57 gives 1681, but Phālguna kṛṣṇa of that year falls around February–March 1682 CE. 'mahomahopādhyāya' is a corrupt spelling of mahāmahopādhyāya. The author is Govinda (Ṭhakkura), who wrote the Kāvyapradīpa. 'śubhavāśare' (= śubhavāsare, 'on an auspicious day') is a formula and names no weekday. 'kāesta' = kāyastha, 'maā' = mayā, and 'prathmādīnāṃ' = prathamā tithi. The 'ja' of Bhojarāja is a cataloguer's addition, but the reading is secure.

title: Candrāloka alaṃkāra/Kuvalayānanda
subject: Sāhitya
colophon: śrī śrīmad appadīkṣita viracitorthālaṃkārāṇāṃ lakṣyalakṣaṇa saṃgrahaḥ samāptoyaṃ caṃdrāloka nāmāharinmṛgāṃkayāṃjhava (!) veda pramite vatsare bhādrapadameva ka caturddaśyāṃ śauriyasrānvitāyāṃ caṃdrāloka alaṃkāro likhitaḥ vipaśvitsukhalālākhyena śrīddhariddharesiru (!) rāṣṭrasya vyapāla vāhinīpariveṣṭite alikhi || śrīrastu || (fol. 8v1–4)
notes: The author is Appayya Dīkṣita (written 'appadīkṣita'). His name is given as the stem 'Appa' with 'dīkṣita' as a title. The year chronogram 'harinmṛgāṃkayāṃjhava (!) veda pramite' is corrupt. Only mṛgāṅka (= 1) and veda (= 4) can be read with confidence. Their order does not match 1845 read right to left, which would need a 5-4-8-1 word sequence, so the catalogue's 'SAM 1845' cannot be confirmed from the quoted text. The year 1845 and its era are taken from the catalogue. VS is assumed (= 1788 CE), but ŚS 1845 (= 1923 CE) cannot be strictly ruled out. 'bhādrapadameva ka' is read as 'bhādrapade mecaka' (dark fortnight), which gives kṛṣṇa pakṣa. 'śauriyasrānvitāyāṃ' is read as 'śaurivāsarānvitāyāṃ' (Saturday, Sauri = Saturn). 'vipaśvit' = vipaścit, 'learned', is an epithet. The catalogue's scribe name 'Pipaśvī' comes from misreading this epithet as part of the name. The place phrase is corrupt: 'vyapāla' may stand for 'nepāla' (…rāṣṭrasya nepāla…), and 'vāhinīpariveṣṭite' means 'surrounded by rivers'. The place has not been identified.

colophon: itiśrīmahārājādhirāja śrīrāmacaṃdradevātmaja sakalaśāstrāraviṃdapradyotanabhaṭṭācāryyaviracitacaṃdrālokaprakāśe śaradāgame daśamomayukhaḥ samāptaḥ || || śaradāgamanāmā graṃthaḥ saṃpūrṇāḥ śrīsahasravāhave namaḥ || || śrī śrīrāmaḥ || || vāhne dvīpa surataru brahmasamete śateke kvāpi || || alikhan mathurānātho graṃthaṃ vaiśākha rākāyāmḥ (!) || || śrīrāmaya (!) namaḥ || || subhas tu || || subham astuḥ (!) || || śrīrārāma rāma rāma rāma || || śrīrāma (!) (fol. 26v1–4)
notes: Chronogram: vahni (3), dvīpa (7), surataru/kalpataru (5), brahma (1), read right to left = 1573. The era word 'śateke' is corrupt. It is read as 'śāke', which gives ŚS 1573 ≈ 1651 CE. VS 1573 ≈ 1516 CE would be earlier than the composition of the Śaradāgama under Vīrabhadra of Bāndhava/Rewa (late 16th century), so the era is uncertain but ŚS is preferred. 'rāmacaṃdradevātmaja' (son of Rāmacandradeva) must refer to the royal patron Vīrabhadra, whose name seems to have dropped out of this copy (the catalogue lists 'Vīrabhadra Bhūpati' as King). It does not refer to Pradyotana Bhaṭṭācārya, a brahmin who wrote the commentary. Neither Rāmacandra nor Vīrabhadra is the reigning king of this copy. The catalogue wrongly gives Pradyotana as scribe: he is the commentator, and the copyist is Mathurānātha ('alikhan mathurānātho').

Date: the chronogram is solved. vahni=3, dvīpa=7, surataru=5, brahma=1, read right to left = 1573. 'śateke' is taken as a corruption of 'śāke', so the era is ŚS 1573 ≈ 1651 CE. That also fits the date of the work (late 16th century). VS 1573 (1516 CE) would come before the work was written.

notes: Umāpati(rāja), called mahārājādhirāja, is the patron under whom Bhaṭṭa Keśava composed (udyotita) the campū. He is not attested as the reigning king at the time of this copy. The chronogram 'munikumadakuvājiḥ' is corrupt. It is read tentatively as muni (7), kumada for kumuda, one of the elephants of the quarters (8), ku (1), vāji (7). Read right to left this gives Śaka 1787, about 1865 CE. If 'mada' is not a number word, the reading fails, so treat the year as uncertain. 'nayanahutāśana' (2, 3) in the second hemistich may encode a further date element, such as a tithi or another year figure, but the context is too corrupt to decode. 'amanaṃgaraṅgabhaṅge' (= anaṅgaraṅgabhaṅga?) may be a descriptive phrase or a Śiva-related date term, so it was not interpreted. The place 'sadvalesa pūryām' (some '…purī') is corrupt and unidentified. No scribe, commissioner or owner is named. The colophon ends the 5th stavaka.

title: *Ghaṭakarparakāvyaṭīkā
subject: Kāvya
date_raw: āṅgirā nāmasaṃvatsare kārtikemāse śukravāsare ʼṣṭamyāṃ tithau ... saṃvat 1920 || mi. kā. kṛ. 13 caṃ
date_note: = Monday 9 Nov 1863, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrinandītaṭakṣetrastha mālavadetyupanāmaka vyeṃkaṭeśa sūri viracitā ghaṭakharparakāvyavyākhyā samāptim agamat || śrī || idaṃ pustakaṃ sātāra nagare sānayiti upanāmaka gaṇeśa sūnunā gopālenaāṅgirā nāmasaṃvatsare kārtikemāse śukravāsare ʼ ṣṭamyāṃ tithau sakalaṃ śrī śaṃkaraputra siddhivināyakānugraheṇā mayā llihitam || || ❁ || ❁ || śrīhari || (fol. 6r5) iti ghaṭakarparaṭīkā samāptāḥ || 22 || sampūrṇam || 22 || śubhaṃ bhūyāt || śrīr astu || śubhaṃm astu || saṃvat 1920 || mi. kā. kṛ. 13 caṃ || śubhaṃbhūyāt || śubhaṃm || (fol. 6r7–8)
notes: The colophon has two dates that conflict. (1) The scribe's own date: Āṅgiras saṃvatsara, Kārtika, Friday, aṣṭamī (the pakṣa is not stated; 'śukra' is the weekday, Friday). Āṅgiras is year 6 of the 60-year cycle, so in the southern reckoning used at Satara this is 1872 CE (ŚS 1794); 1812 CE is also possible. (2) 'saṃvat 1920 mi[ti] kā[rtika] kṛ[ṣṇa] 13 caṃ[dravāra]', a Monday. Read as VS this gives 1863 CE, which is not an Āṅgiras year. Read as ŚS it would be impossible. Line (2) follows a second ending ('iti ghaṭakarparaṭīkā samāptāḥ') on fol. 6r7–8 and is probably a later addition, perhaps a Nepalese VS note. The copying itself most likely dates to about 1872. 'śaṃkaraputra siddhivināyaka' is the deity Gaṇeśa, not a person. Mālavade and Sānayiti are upanāmas (family surnames). Satara is in Maharashtra.

title: Naiṣadhadīpikā
subject: Kāvya
date_note: = Friday 28 Jul 1525, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīpaṃḍitacāṃdraviracitāyāṃ naiṣadhadīpikāyāṃ śrīānaṃdāṃke mahākāvye śrīśrīharṣakṛtau śaśāṃkasaṃkīrtanaṃ nāmā dvāviṃśaḥ sarggaḥ || samāptaḥ || || śubhaṃ bhavatu śrīr astu || śrīḥ || || iti || saṃvat 1582 varṣe śrāvaṇa śudi navamyām 9 tithau bhṛhu | sadine yathā nakṣatra yogesamaye | adyeha śrīdevadārūvana vāstavya ācāryamāṇikāsuta kānhākhena pustakām alikhi || (!) paropakārārthaṃ cātmanaḥ paṭhanārthaṃ || (fol. 295r6–11)
purpose: for others (paropakārārthaṃ) and for the scribe's own study (ātmanaḥ paṭhanārthaṃ)
notes: The scribe's name 'kānhākhena' is best read as kānhākhyena, 'by the one named Kānhā'. The catalogue's 'Kāhnā' is probably a metathesis. 'cāṃdra' is probably corrupt for Cāṇḍū Paṇḍita, the usual author of the Naiṣadhadīpikā. Neither the era nor the place is named. VS is assumed because a Devanagari manuscript with Śrāvaṇa śudi uses the 'saṃvat' formula, and it gives c. 1525 CE (ŚS would give 1660 CE). The weekday has not been checked against the date. Devadāruvana ('deodar forest') may be a hermitage or locality; its location is not identified. 'adyeha … vāstavya' suggests the book was copied there. The formula 'yathā nakṣatra yogesamaye' names no specific nakṣatra.
review: Scribe's name: 'kānhākhena' read as kānhā-ākhyena ('named Kānhā'), so the name is Kānhā, not Kānhākha. The catalogue's 'Kāhnā' is probably a metathesis.
Scribe given roles scribe + owner, because he copied it 'ātmanaḥ paṭhanārthaṃ' (for his own study).
Author name changed to Śrīharṣa: here 'śrī' is part of the personal name ('śrīśrīharṣa' = honorific śrī + Śrīharṣa).
Commentator 'Cāndra' kept as written, with confidence lowered to medium. The Naiṣadhadīpikā is usually ascribed to Cāṇḍū Paṇḍita, so 'cāṃdra' is probably corrupt.
Residence removed from Māṇika: 'devadārūvana vāstavya' grammatically describes the scribe.
nakshatra_yoga emptied: 'yathā nakṣatra yogesamaye' is a stock formula and names no nakṣatra or yoga.
Weekday spelled out: 'bhṛhu' is a mistake for bhṛgu (Friday).
Purpose field condensed.

title: Bhaṭṭikāvya
subject: Kāvya
date_note: = Saturday 26 Dec 1772, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti vallabhīvāstavyasya śrīsvāmisūnoḥ bhaṭṭamahāvrāhmaṇasya mahāvaiyākaraṇasyakṛtau bhaṭṭikākāvye rāvaṇavadhe tiṅantakāṇḍe luḍavilasitaṃnāma navamaḥ paricchedaḥ kāvyasyāyodhyā pratyāgamanaṃnāma dvāviṃśaḥ sarggaḥ samāptaḥ samāptam idaṃ bhaṭṭikāvyaṃ dvāviṃśasargātmakaṃ 22 || (fol. 149r7–8) iti śrīvallabhīvāstavyasyaisya śrīsvāmisūnor bhaṭṭamahābrāhmaṇasyaḥ (!) vaiyyākaraṇasyakṛtau rāvaṇavadhe mahātiṅaṃtakāṃḍe ludvilasitanāmno navamaparicchedasya jaṭīśvarojayadevo jayamaṃgala iti + + māstribhi prasiddhasya anekaśāstrānukṛtau ṭīkāyāṃ kāvyasyāyodhyāgamanaṃ nāma dvāviṃśaḥ sargaḥ jayamaṃgalaṃ samāptaṃ || śrīr astu śubham astu saṃkhyā 1500 saṃvat 1830 + + + śāke 1694 mītī pauśa (!) śudi 2 (fol. 149r9–12)
notes: The date gives two eras that differ by one year. VS 1830 Pauṣa śukla 2 falls around December 1773 or January 1774 CE. ŚS 1694 would correspond to VS 1829, which is about December 1772 or January 1773 CE. The equivalent of VS 1830 is ŚS 1695. Possible causes are a scribal slip or a mix of expired and current years. VS is taken as primary. Three characters are lost between the two years ('+ + +'). 'saṃkhyā 1500' is the granthasaṃkhyā. The commentator is given as 'jaṭīśvaro jayadevo jayamaṃgala iti ... prasiddhasya', which is partly lacunose. Jayamaṅgalā is the name of the well-known Bhaṭṭikāvya commentary, which is traditionally ascribed to Jayamaṅgala or Jaya(deva). Here the commentator is taken to be Jayadeva, also called Jaṭīśvara, but the alternative reading 'Jayamaṅgala' as a personal name cannot be excluded. The author's father 'śrīsvāmin' could also be read as the proper name Śrīsvāmin; tradition calls Bhaṭṭi 'Śrīsvāmisūnu' or the son of Śrīdharasvāmin. The catalogue gives King: Narendradeva and Donor: Śrīkṛṣṇajośī Rāmanagara, but neither appears in the quoted colophon; they may come from another part of the MS. The catalogue's 'Place of Copying: Vallabhī' is the author's residence, not the place where this copy was made. The colophon names no scribe or commissioner.

colophon: || iti śrī mahākavi kālidāsa kṛtau meghadūtākhyaṃ kāvya samāptaṃ || || śubhamastu idaṃ pustakaṃ deva divākarena likhisvārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca || || yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṣṛṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā yadi śuddhamaśuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo na vidyate1 || || || || saṃvat 1521 bhādrapada śuddhatrayodaśi kāśyāṃ likhyate || ❖ || ❖ || ❖ || saṃvat || 1751 || || śrīmukhāsaṃvatsare dakṣIṇāyane vasaṃtattau bhādrapade bhaśi (!) śukla pakṣe trayośiṃ (!) meghadūtākhyaṃ kāvyaṃ vāsudeva bhaṭṭa devatsuta deva divākarenanalekhitaṃ || || ❖ || ❖ || || || rāma || ❖ || ❖ || sadā śiva || || ❖ || kāśyāṃ viśvarasaṃnidhau pustakaṃ likhyate || ❖ || ❖ || ❖ || || || (fol. 21v4–22rv)
purpose: svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca (for himself and for others)
notes: The colophon gives two dates. The first, 'saṃvat 1521 bhādrapada śuddhatrayodaśi kāśyāṃ likhyate' (VS 1521 = c. 1464 CE), was probably copied over from the exemplar. The second is the actual date of copying: VS 1751, Śrīmukha year, Bhādrapada śukla 13 = August/September 1694 CE. A Śrīmukha year around 1693/94 is consistent with that date. 'dakṣiṇāyane' fits Bhādrapada, but 'vasantartau' (spring) does not: the scribe made a mistake there. 'bhaśi (!)' is unclear; it may be a garbled weekday or a corruption of a word for the month, so no weekday is recorded. The scribe's name reads 'deva divākarena' (= Divākaradeva in the catalogue). 'Deva' is taken here as a family name or honorific, shared with the father 'vāsudeva bhaṭṭa deva(t)'. The 'na' in 'divākarenanalekhitaṃ' is a dittography. 'viśvarasaṃnidhau' is probably 'viśveśvarasaṃnidhau', i.e. near the Viśveśvara temple in Kāśī. 'rāma' and 'sadā śiva' are invocations, not persons.

title: Praśastiratnāvalī
subject: Kāvya
colophon: iti śrīmad gorṣādhīśvara bhūpālanarabhūpālapautra śrīman mahoddāmakīrti kumāra śrīmacchrīkṛṣṇasāhakāritā śrīmad rājakula śiromaṇi pravilasat pādāravindadvanda śrīmad rāmahṛ(!)yaḥ paṃḍitaśiromaṇi sūnu vāṇīvilāsa kaviviracitā praśastiratnāvaliḥ samāptā || śubhaṃ (fol. 7v9–11) svasti śrī girirājacakracūḍāmaṇi naranārāyaṇetyādi vividhavirudhāvalīvirājamāna mānonnata śrīmanmahārājādhirāja śrī śrī śrīmahārāje gīrvāṇayuddhavikramasāha bahādūrasamser jaṅdevānām sadāsamaravijayinām || || (fol. 8r1–3) svasti śrīśvara caraṇasmaraṇapūrvaka rūpanārāyaṇetyādi vvidhavirudhāvaḷīvirājamāna mānonnata śrīmanmahārājādhirāja śrī śrī śrīman + + + + sena bahādūra devānām sadāsamaravijayināṃ || || (fol. 8r3–5)
notes: The colophon is undated. 'Kṛṣṇasāhakāritā ... kaviviracitā praśastiratnāvaliḥ' makes Kṛṣṇasāha, grandson of Narabhūpāla of Gorkha, the patron of the composition. Nothing says he commissioned or donated this copy, so the catalogue's 'Donor' field is doubtful. Fol. 8r1–5 has two praśasti formulae in honorific genitive plural (devānām ... sadāsamaravijayinām). The first is for Gīrvāṇayuddhavikramaśāha (r. 1799–1816). The second is for a Sena ruler styled Rūpanārāyaṇa, whose name is lost in the lacuna; he is probably of the Palpa/Makwanpur Senas, perhaps Pṛthvīpālasena, but that is unverified. Since this is a manual of praśastis, these may be specimen formulae rather than a statement of the reigning king. If they are contemporary, they put the copy roughly in 1799–1806 CE. That is an inference only. 'rāmahṛ(!)yaḥ' is read as Rāmahṛdaya. 'vāṇīvilāsa' could be the poet's name or an epithet.
review: p1 Narabhūpāla: dropped role 'king'. He is named only as Kṛṣṇasāha's grandfather and died long before Gīrvāṇayuddha's reign (he was king of Gorkha, c. 1716–1743). Role is now relative_only.

p2 Kṛṣṇasāha: role changed from 'commissioner' to 'other'. '-kāritā' goes with 'kaviviracitā praśastiratnāvaliḥ', so he paid for the composition of the text, not for this copy. The catalogue calls him 'Donor', but the colophon does not support that.
Removed the relation p2 under_reign_of p5. Nothing in the colophon ties the patron of the composition to Gīrvāṇayuddha's reign.

p5 Gīrvāṇayuddhavikramaśāha: confidence lowered to medium, and bahādura/śamśera/jaṅga added to titles. The fol. 8r praśastis may be sample formulae added to this praśasti manual rather than a statement of the reigning king.
p6: the name is lost in the lacuna, so 'Sena' alone is not a usable name. The name field now marks the gap, and the role is changed to 'other' (addressee of a sample praśasti), low confidence.
p4 Vāṇīvilāsa: confidence lowered to medium, because 'vāṇīvilāsa' could be an epithet of the poet rather than his name.
p3: confidence for the reading Rāmahṛdaya kept at medium. The epithet 'rājakulaśiromaṇi-pravilasat-pādāravindadvanda' added to evidence.

title: Meghadūta
subject: Kāvya
date_note: = Thursday 5 Sep 1675, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīkālidāsakṛtau meghadūtākhyaṃ mahā(2)kāvyaṃ samāptaṃ || śubham astu || itthaṃ bhūtaṃ sucaritam idaṃ meghadū(3)taṃ ca nāmnā kāmakrīḍāvirahitajane viprayoge vinodi (!) prema(4)ś cāsmin nitinipuṇatāṃ buddhibhāvaṃ kavīnāṃ natvāryāyāś ca(5)raṇayugalaṃ kālidaś cakāra || 1 || || śrī || śrī || saṃvat 1737(6) varṣa āśvinamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe pratipaddine sarojapuṭabhedane (7) likhitam idaṃ kāvyaṃ bhaṭṭagiridhareṇa svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca || (fol. 22v1–7)
purpose: svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca (for himself and for others)
notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as Girirājabhaṭṭa and the date as VS 1732. The colophon clearly reads 'bhaṭṭagiridhareṇa' and 'saṃvat 1737', so either the catalogue is wrong or the cataloguer misread the manuscript. The era is not named, but 'saṃvat' in a Devanagari manuscript points to VS. VS 1737 = CE 1680 (Āśvina, so September–October 1680 if the year starts in Caitra). It would be 1681 if the year starts in Kārttika. 'sarojapuṭabhedane' = 'in the town (puṭabhedana) of Saroja'. Saroja means 'lotus', so this may be a Sanskrit rendering of a place name like Kamala-/Padma-pura. It cannot be identified, so normalized is left empty. The verse after the colophon ('itthaṃ bhūtaṃ sucaritam ...') is an addition with errors ('vinodi (!)', 'nitinipuṇatāṃ' for nīti-, 'kālidaś' for Kālidāsa). It names only the author, not any other person.
review: Added 'owner' to Giridhara's roles: 'svārthaṃ' means he copied it for his own use, which makes him owner as well as scribe ('parārthaṃ ca' adds that it is also for others).
Added the second spelling of the author's name in the closing verse (kālidaś, corrupt for Kālidāsa) to the notes; Kālidāsa stays as author only.
Expanded the notes: the catalogue's scribe name (Girirājabhaṭṭa) and date (VS 1732) conflict with the colophon; possible reading of the place name; how ce_approx was worked out.

title: Meghadūtaṭīkā
subject: Kāvya
date_note: = Tuesday 24 Sep 1538, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti śrīcaritravardhanaviracitā meghadūtākhyakāvyaṭīkā saṃpūrṇā (8) || || || śubham astu || || samāptaḥ || nabhorasābdhyaikamite śakebde saṃvatsare caiva parābhaākye ṛtau śarannāmni karāhvayetho sadosvije (9) māsi ca somavāre|| 1 || ādimāyāṃ tithau caiva site pakṣe ca vaidhṛtau prayoga likhitaṃ hyetat jo(ga)devasya sūnunā || 2 || ...(10) (fol. 29v7–10)
notes: Chronogram: nabhas 0, rasa 6, abdhi 4, eka 1. Read right to left this gives ŚS 1460 (c. 1538 CE), which matches the catalogue. The saṃvatsara is named Parābhava. In the southern 60-year cycle Parābhava falls in ŚS 1468 (1546/47), and ŚS 1460 would be Vilambin. Under northern Bārhaspatya reckoning the name may differ by a few years, so the year and the saṃvatsara do not fully agree. 'sadosvije' is probably a corruption of 'sad-āśvije' (Āśvina). 'karāhvaye 'tho' is taken as the nakṣatra Hasta. 'prayoga' may be a corruption of 'prayāge' (written at Prayāga), but this is uncertain. Both readings fit the anuṣṭubh metre. The scribe is identified in the quoted text only as the son of Jogadeva (reading of 'jo(ga)' uncertain). The name Rāmeśvarabhaṭṭa is the catalogue's tentative suggestion, perhaps from the omitted line 10, so it is not verified. Caritravardhana is the author of the commentary, not connected with this copy.

title: Śiṣuhitaiṣiṇīṭīkā
subject: Kāvya
colophon: iti śrīmālāmanvayasādhuśrī araḍakamallasabhyārthitakharataragachīyataranija(4)prābhācāryaprapādapadmopajīvi naraveśasarasvatīvācanācāryaśrīcāritrabarddhanaviracitāyāṃ rāghavīyaṭīkā(5)yāṃ śuṣuhitaiṣiṇyāṃ paṃcadaśaḥ sarggaḥ || 15 || ❁ || ❁ || (fol. 8v3–5)
notes: This is a chapter colophon inside the text, at the end of sarga 15 of Cāritravardhana's Śiśuhitaiṣiṇī commentary on the Raghuvaṃśa ('rāghavīyaṭīkā'). The catalogue spells the title 'Śiṣuhitaiṣiṇī' and the colophon has 'śuṣuhitaiṣiṇyāṃ'; both stand for Śiśuhitaiṣiṇī. It gives no scribe, date or place for this copy. Everyone named here belongs to the composition of the commentary, not to this copy. Araḍakamalla, of the Śrīmāla lineage, asked for the commentary to be written ('sabhyārthita', probably meant as 'abhyarthita'), so he is the patron of the original work. 'taranija(4)prābhācārya' is corrupt. Possible readings are Taruṇaprabhācārya or (kharatara-gacchīya-)Jinaprabhācārya. Other sources give Cāritravardhana's teacher as Kalyāṇarāja, which this colophon does not confirm. 'prapādapadmopajīvi' probably stands for '-pada-padmopajīvi' (living at the lotus feet of). 'naraveśasarasvatī' is probably an epithet meaning 'Sarasvatī in human form' ('naraveṣa-'), not an office.

p1: 'naraveśasarasvatī' kept in titles but flagged in notes as an honorific epithet ('Sarasvatī in human guise'), not an office

notes: The catalogue names 'Navāva īsavīṣā' as the scribe, but the colophon says 'śrīnavāva īsavīṣāvirācitā … ṭīkā rasacaṃdrikā'. That makes him the commentator, not the copyist. 'Navāva' = Nawab, and 'īsavīṣā' probably renders Īsavī Khān (Īsvī Khān), the known author of the Rasacandrikā commentary on Bihārī's Satsaī. In Devanagari ṣ is often written for kh, so the stem form is uncertain. Vihārī = Bihārī. The colophon names no scribe. The era is not stated ('saṃvat'), but 1874 fits VS (≈1817 CE). The tithi is missing: only Caitra śukla and Monday are given.
review: p1: kept as commentator (not scribe, despite catalogue); 'navāva' identified as Nawab (title); confidence lowered to medium; noted that 'īsavīṣā' renders Īsavī Khān/Īsvī Khān (Devanagari ṣ for kh)
p2: noted Vihārī = Bihārī (Bihārī Satsaī)

title: Raghuvaṃśa
subject: Kāvya
date_note: = Monday 26 Jul 1610, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: || iti śrīmahopādhyāya kolavalamallināthasūriviracitāyāṃ raghuvaṃśaṭīkāyāṃ saṃjīvinīsamākhyāyām ekonaviṃśatimaḥ sargaḥ || || samāptaḥ || śrīgopālajī || || ❁ || || śrī || || jadunāthasvāmī || saṃvat 1667 samaye sāvana sudī chaṭI vāraguravāsare || || (fol. 112r7–9)
notes: The text copied is Mallinātha's Saṃjīvinī commentary on the Raghuvaṃśa, sarga 19. 'kolavala' is a corrupt spelling of Kolācala, Mallinātha's family epithet. 'śrīgopālajī' and 'śrī jadunāthasvāmī' are read here as invocations of Kṛṣṇa, so they are left out of the persons list. A human Yadunātha Svāmin (for example the Vallabha Gosvāmī Yadunātha, early 17th c.) cannot be ruled out entirely. No scribe, commissioner or place is named. The era is taken as VS from the plain 'saṃvat' and Hindi-style month and pakṣa forms ('sāvana sudī'), which fits a north-Indian Devanagari manuscript. This gives c. July/Aug 1610 CE, but the weekday has not been checked.

Date: tithi normalized to ṣaṣṭhī (chaṭI), paksa to śukla (sudī), month to Śrāvaṇa (sāvana), weekday to Thursday (guruvāra); VS 1667 → c. 1610 CE confirmed

title: *Śatakatraya
subject: Kāvya
date_note: = Saturday 20 Jul 1811, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: yathāprati tathā saṃvat 1733 sāvana su[[di]] amavasa (!) kāsīnātha anamahaputaka (!) hirānaṃda dīchīta (!) || 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 (fol. 57r7–9)
notes: 'kāsīnātha anamahaputaka (!) hirānaṃda dīchīta' is a corrupt vernacular (Hindi-type) phrase. 'putaka' most likely stands for pustaka 'book', i.e. '... book of Hīrānanda Dīkṣita'. On that reading Hīrānanda would be the owner and Kāśīnātha possibly the scribe. A reading as putra/putraka 'son' cannot be ruled out, but it is unsupported. The catalogue lists both men as scribes. The era is not named. In a North Indian Devanagari colophon, plain 'saṃvat' is normally Vikrama: VS 1733 is about 1676 CE. The catalogue's ŚS 1733 (about 1811 CE) is possible but less likely. 'sudi' (with 'di' marked as an inserted or uncertain reading) clashes with amāvāsyā, which falls at the end of the dark fortnight. Either the pakṣa is a slip or the tithi is meant as the new moon closing the month. The 'yathāprati tathā' formula means the copy follows its exemplar.
review: Removed son_of relation: 'anamahaputaka' does not clearly contain putra; 'putaka' is more plausibly vernacular pustaka/potaka 'book', so it gives no basis for a father–son link
Kāśīnātha: dropped 'relative_only'; role now scribe (low confidence), following the catalogue
Hīrānanda: roles now owner + scribe (the 'pustaka' reading makes him the owner, the catalogue makes him the scribe); confidence lowered to low
Date: 'saṃvat' without qualification in a Devanagari colophon is normally Vikrama; era set to VS, ce_approx 1676. The catalogue's ŚS 1733 is probably wrong
Notes added: śukla pakṣa with amāvāsyā is a contradiction, and 'di' is an inserted reading

notes: The chronogram 'tryaṅgābda-saṃmite śāke' is incomplete or corrupt. As written, tri = 3 and aṅga = 6, read right to left as 63; 'abda' is probably just 'year', so the higher digits are missing. If 'abda' is a corruption of 'abdhi' (= 4), the reading would be 463, again with the thousands digit missing (e.g. 1463 if a 'bhū' was lost). None of these readings gives the catalogue's ŚS 1800, so the catalogue date may be the cataloguer's estimate or may come from elsewhere in the manuscript. ce_approx is left empty. The catalogue also names 'Dharaṇidhara' as a scribe, but he does not appear in the quoted colophon; he may be named elsewhere (e.g. in an earlier section colophon), so he is not included here. The text ends with the 4th (antardaśā) adhyāya, which appears to complete the work. 'Rāmeśa' is a deity in the dedication and is not counted as a person. 'Uḍudāyapradīpodyota' is a commentary on the Uḍudāyapradīpa (Laghupārāśarī).

title: Candrakiraṇāvalī (golādhyāya)
subject: Jyotiṣa
colophon: || iti śrī sūrya siddhāṃte sūryapuruṣasaṃvāde mānādhyāyaścaturdaśaḥ || 14 || || ○ || (fol. 29r7) || iti śrī cittapāvana mādhavātmaja dādābhāīkṛte caṃdrakiraṇāvalīsaṃjñe saura sūtravivaraṇaṃ samāptam || 14 || || kheṣumegha miteśāke kanyāsakte divākare || sūryasiddhāṃta vivṛttiṃ vedagarbho vyalīlikhat || || || || śrī sūryāya namaḥ || || śrī rāmāya namaḥ || || ○ || || ❖ || ❖ || ❖ || (fol. 29r1&8-9)
notes: The chronogram is kha (0) + iṣu (5) + megha. 'Megha' is not a standard bhūtasaṃkhyā word. Read right to left, the year is [megha]50 Śaka. Dādābhāī (the Cittapāvana author of the Kiraṇāvalī commentary on the Sūryasiddhānta, son of Mādhava) is usually dated to the early 18th century, about ŚS 1641 / 1719 CE. If 'megha' stands for 17, the copy would be ŚS 1750 ≈ 1828 CE, which fits that dating, but this is a guess and ce_approx is left empty. The text could also be corrupt. The scribe's line says only 'sūryasiddhāṃta vivṛtti' and gives no place. The catalogue title 'Candrakiraṇāvalī (golādhyāya)' differs from the colophon, which closes the mānādhyāya (14) and then the whole commentary.

title: Camatkāracitāmaṇi
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Thursday 4 Sep 1777, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: iti bhaṭṭanārāyaṇaviracite camatkāraciṃtāmaṇau grahabhāvaphalādhyāyaḥ || (fol. 15r6) iti śrīcamatkāraciṃtāmaṇer anvayadīpikāyāṃ grahabhāvaphalādhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || || 4 || śakeṃkāṃka bhūpair mite bhādraśukle catur vaktratithye guraubhe pataṃge || camatkāraciṃtāmaṇe dīvyaṭīkāṃ vyalekhi dvijenaś caṅālīpūreṣu || 1 || śrīr astu sarvadā nitarām (fol. 15r4,7–10)
notes: The chronogram is read right to left: aṅka (9), aṅka (9), bhūpa (16) gives ŚS 1699, which is 1777 CE. 'guraubhe pataṃge' is best split as gurau (Thursday) + bhe pataṅge (the nakṣatra of the Sun/Savitṛ, i.e. Hasta). This fits Bhādra śukla 4, when the moon is near Hasta. Reading 'gurubha' as Puṣya is astronomically impossible on this tithi. The weekday has not been checked against an ephemeris. The scribe is called only a 'dvija'. 'dvijenaś' looks corrupt: a name or a word like 'atra' may have dropped out of the bhujaṅgaprayāta verse. The catalogue gives the scribe as Lakṣmīpati, but the quoted text does not confirm this. It may come from elsewhere in the manuscript, or it may confuse him with the author of the Anvayadīpikā. 'vyalekhi … ṭīkām' could also be the commentator's own date verse copied over from the exemplar rather than a statement by this copy's scribe. The commentary (Anvayadīpikā) is mentioned, but its author is not named here.
review: Added the unnamed brahmin scribe ('dvijena … vyalekhi') as p2, role scribe, low confidence. The catalogue gives his name as Lakṣmīpati, but the quoted colophon does not.
Tithi: 'caturvaktra' is a word-numeral for 4, so the tithi is caturthī (4). It was left unparsed.

Weekday and nakṣatra re-parsed. 'gurau' means Thursday. 'bhe pataṅge' is the nakṣatra ruled by the Sun (Savitṛ), i.e. Hasta. The first reading had swapped them, taking pataṅge as the weekday and guraubhe as the nakṣatra.
Place normalised to the stem Caṅālīpura (not identified).
Chronogram and the ŚS 1699 / 1777 CE date confirmed.

title: Tājikanīlakaṇṭhī
subject: Jyautiṣa
date_note: = Friday 2 Mar 1821, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti varṣatantraṃ samāptaṃ || || ❁ || (11) netravedādribhūśākake phālgune kuṃbhabhe 'haskare kālapakṣe bhṛgau || bhūtatithyāṃ girīśasyapuryām araṃ lālaratnākaro 'līlikhat tāji(12)kam || 1 || || tailād rakṣej jalad rakṣet rakṣet śīthalabandhanāt (!) mṛkhahaste na dātavyaṃ evaṃ vadati pustakaṃ || 1 || || śubham astu śrīviśveśvaraprasādāt || (fol. 13r10–12)
notes: The chronogram reads netra 2, veda 4, adri 7, bhū 1. Read right to left, this gives Śaka 1742, which matches the catalogue. Śaka 1742 + 78 = 1820, but Phālguna of that year falls in Feb–Mar 1821 CE. 'bhūtatithi' is taken as caturdaśī (as in bhūtacaturdaśī), but in number-word usage bhūta can also mean 5. Kṛṣṇa 14 with the sun in Kumbha fits Mahāśivarātri (pūrṇimānta Phālguna kṛṣṇa 14), which suits a copy made in Śiva's city (girīśasya purī = Kāśī). The weekday has not been checked. The name appears as 'lālaratnākara' in the verse but as 'Ratnākaralāla' in the catalogue. 'Lāla' may be an appellative such as Lāl, and the order in the verse may be forced by the metre. 'araṃ' means 'quickly'. The final verse is the standard book-curse ('tailād rakṣet…'). The author (Nīlakaṇṭha) is not named in the colophon.
review: Scribe confidence lowered to medium: the colophon has 'lālaratnākaro' (order probably forced by the sragviṇī metre), while the catalogue gives 'Ratnākaralāla'; noted both forms
Recorded the sun's position (kuṃbhabhe 'haskare = sun in Kumbha) in nakshatra_yoga

title: Rasāla, Tājakīnīlakaṇṭhī
subject: Jyautiṣa
colophon: || iti śrīvidvaddaivajñamukuṭālaṃkāra śrīnīlakaṇṭhajyotirvitputra govindajyotirvidviracitāyārasālāyāṃsamāvivekavivṛtiḥ samāptim agamat || || śākeṣṭaṣarāmeṣamiteśukre some kuhūtithau || samāphalīyāṃ sarasāṃ rasālāmalikhadvudhaḥ || || (fol. 111r7–11)
notes: The closing verse ('śāke ... samāphalīyāṃ sarasāṃ rasālām alikhad budhaḥ') looks like the author Govinda's own date of composition, copied along with the text. It is probably not the date of this manuscript. No scribe, owner or copy date is given. The chronogram 'ṣṭaṣarāmeṣa' is corrupt. Possible elements include aṣṭa (8), śara (5), rāma (3), and iṣu (5) or īśa (11), but no combination gives a plausible Śaka year. The expected range is about Śaka 1530–1550 (early 17th century CE), the period of Govinda son of Nīlakaṇṭha. For that reason ce_approx is left empty. 'śukre' is taken as the month name Śukra (= Jyeṣṭha), because the weekday is given separately as 'some' (Monday).
review: Govinda: role changed from 'author' to 'commentator'. The Rasālā is a vivṛti (commentary) on the Samāviveka section of his father's Tājikanīlakaṇṭhī.

Nīlakaṇṭha: role changed from 'relative_only' to 'author' plus 'relative_only'. He wrote the base text and is named here as Govinda's father. Kept 'daivajña' and 'jyotirvid' as titles; the long epithet 'vidvaddaivajñamukuṭālaṃkāra' is moved to the evidence text.

Date: 'śukre' is read as the month Śukra (= Jyeṣṭha), not as a weekday, because 'some' (Monday) is already the weekday. Kuhū = amāvāsyā, the new-moon day, so the fortnight is kṛṣṇa (dark half). The year field now records a tentative split of the chronogram.

Notes: the verse 'samāphalīyāṃ sarasāṃ rasālām alikhad budhaḥ' probably gives the author's own composition date and does not name a scribe. No copyist is identified, and 'budhaḥ' ('the learned one') is not a person entry.

subject: Jyotiṣa

colophon: iti śrīkeśavadaivajñaviracitāyāṃ jātakapaddhatau daśādhyāyaḥ || śrī śubham ||(6) || śrīmajjyautiṣI jo(!) raghoḥ sutanayo nāthāṃta sudyotako horātaṃtrakṛtaśramaḥ saphalayan prāptopa(7)nāmaṃ paraṃ || soyaṃ vyākaraṇādikāvyasuguṇān saṃdhānam ālam naman-n ālekhi dvijavarya(8) bhairavacaṇo viśveśavandyaḥ sadā || 1 || saṃvat 1949 miºº mārgaśīrṣakṛ 7 gurau śubham || || || ❁ || (9) (fol. 7r5–8)

'śrīmajjyautiṣI jo(!) raghoḥ sutanayo nāthāṃta' most likely means 'the good son of the illustrious astrologer Raghu-nātha', with 'nāthānta' meaning 'ending in -nātha'. That makes the father Raghunātha, though 'jo(!)' could also be read as an abbreviation of Jośī. The scribe's name 'bhairavacaṇo' is unclear. It could be Bhairava + -caṇa ('renowned'), or a mistake for Bhairavagaṇa or a similar form. Bhairava agrees with the catalogue's Scribe field. The catalogue's 'Place of Copying: VS 1949' is a field error: no place is named in the colophon, and 1949 is the date. 'miºº' = miti. VS 1949 Mārgaśīrṣa falls in November–December 1892 CE. The Thursday weekday has not been checked.

title: Jñānālaṅkṛtamañjarī
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Saturday 9 Jul 1796, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: ṛṣiśarmācāryaviracitā praśnavidyā || iti nāmavadhapra(15)karaṇaṃ samāptaṃ | (!) saṃvat 1753 || śāke 1718 āṣāḍhaśuddhapaṃcamī 5 maṃdavāsare | likhitaṃ āpābhaṭṭa śubhaṃ vatu bhavatu || || (fol. 18v14–15)
notes: The two eras conflict. 'saṃvat 1753' (VS) gives about 1696 CE, but 'śāke 1718' gives about 1796 CE, a difference of 100 years. ŚS 1718 matches VS 1853, so 'saṃvat 1753' is probably a slip for 1853. ŚS 1718 is adopted here. Weekday check by my own calculation: 9 July 1796 CE was a Saturday and about 3.5–4 days after the new moon of early July, with the Sun in sidereal Mithuna. That fits Āṣāḍha śukla 4/5 well, but it hasn't been checked against a full pañcāṅga. The VS 1753 alternative (1696 CE) was not checked. The colophon gives the text as a 'praśnavidyā' by Ṛṣiśarmācārya and the section as 'nāmavadhaprakaraṇa'. The catalogue title Jñānālaṅkṛtamañjarī does not appear in the colophon. The author's name could be taken as Ṛṣiśarman; '-śarman' was removed as a suffix. 'Āpā' is a common Marathi personal name, so the scribe may be a Deccani brahmin.

title: Narapatijayacaryāsvarodaya
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Monday 6 Apr 1739, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīnarapatijayacaryāyāṃ svarodaye homavidhiḥ samāptaḥ || || || śrīśāke 1661 mā(6)se 4 kṛṣṇapakṣe tithau 14 vāre 2 samāptaṃ || gorṣā nagaryāṃ kilarājadhānyaṃ virājite vainasbhūpanāmni || li(7)lekha śāraṅgadharaḥ sudhīmān svārthāya pāṭhāya mudesuvegāt || 1 || || śākegāṃ ʼkādīnduke sannipāte (!) (8) lekhyo māsi śrāvaṇe śuklapakṣe || gorṣāsthāyī śaṃbhutithābjavāre śāraṅgākhyaḥ pustikeyaṃ lilekha || || śubhaṃ (fol. 57r5–8)
purpose: svārthāya pāṭhāya (for the scribe's own study)
notes: 'vainasbhūpanāmni' is corrupt. It is probably 'narabhūpanāmni' ('when the king named Nara[bhūpāla] shines'). This would be Narabhūpāla Śāha of Gorkha (r. c. 1716–1743), which fits ŚS 1661 = 1739 CE and agrees with the catalogue. The second, metrical date (verse 2) has a corrupt bhūtasaṃkhyā chronogram, 'śākegāṃ'kādīnduke', marked (!) by the cataloguer. Only 'indu' = 1 (the thousands digit, read right to left) is clear. 'aṅka' (9) and 'adri' (7) would not give 1661 unless they are corruptions, for example of 'aṅga' (6). The second verse also gives Śrāvaṇa śukla, tithi 'śaṃbhu' (probably 14, Śiva's caturdaśī; possibly 11 if Śambhu = Rudra), and 'abja' (Moon) = Monday. This conflicts with the prose date, month 4 kṛṣṇa 14, Monday. If month 4 is Āṣāḍha (amānta), the prose date is the same as Śrāvaṇa kṛṣṇa 14 (pūrṇimānta). Even so, kṛṣṇa and śukla 14 are about 15 days apart, so the two dates cannot both fall on a Monday. Perhaps the verse gives the date the copying was completed, or it is a scribal slip. Both dates fall around July–August 1739 CE.

colophon: padyāṃ vayāsā vitalo vipaścic chrinīlakaṃṭhaḥ śrutiśāstraniṣṭhaḥ || vidvac chivaprītikaraṃ vyadhāt tat saṃjñāvivekaṃ sahamāvataṃsam || 3 || || ❁ || || śākenetrābdhyaṃvubhṛtsammiter 1742 ʼke kuṃbhar kṣasthe bhūjavāre sitārddhe || māghe kāśyāṃ lālaratnākareṇa saṃjñātaṃtraṃ viṣṇutithyāṃ hyalekhi || 1 || (fol. 8r8–10)
notes: The scribe's name appears in the verse as 'lālaratnākareṇa', while the catalogue gives 'Ratnākaralāla'. The order was probably reversed for metre; Ratnākaralāla is taken as the normal form. The chronogram 'netrābdhyaṃvubhṛt' is corrupt: 1742 read right to left needs four words (2, 4, 7, 1). Netra (2) and abdhi (4) are clear, but 'aṃvubhṛt' does not clearly give 7 and 1. It may be a corruption of something like 'adri-bhū' (7, 1). The numeral 1742 written beside it settles the year. 'Viṣṇutithi' is taken as ekādaśī (11). In the classical lists of tithi deities, however, Viṣṇu is lord of dvādaśī (12). A rough calendar check puts Māgha śukla 11 of ŚS 1742 at about 13 Feb 1821, a Tuesday, which agrees with 'bhūjavāra' (bhūja = Mars). The sun had entered sidereal Kumbha by then. The authorial verse at the start ('padyāṃ vayāsā vitalo') is corrupt; it refers to Nīlakaṇṭha's Saṃjñāviveka, the first part of the Tājikanīlakaṇṭhī.

title: Parvadvayasādhana
subject: Jyautiṣa
date_note: = Sunday 20 Nov 1735, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti parilekhaḥ || mallārināmā gaṇite pati(9)ṣṭhaś (!) cakrāra parvadvayasādhanaṃ hi | vācyaṃ mahāvegahayoparistha- daivajñavaryeṇa yathā sphuṭārthaṃ | 8 || ❁ || (10) śake 1657 mārgaśīrṣa śuddha 6 ravau tad dine pustakaṃ samāptaṃ | śrīrāmāya jyoºº śrīkṛṣṇa śāºº (fol. 4r8–10)
notes: The verse names Mallāri as the author: 'pati(9)ṣṭhaś (!)' should read pratiṣṭhaḥ and 'cakrāra' should read cakāra. The verse also describes him as daivajñavara, but the referent of that phrase is uncertain. The final line 'śrīrāmāya jyoºº śrīkṛṣṇa śāºº' is abbreviated and its meaning is unclear. Most likely reading: given to Rāma Jyotiṣī (dative) by Kṛṣṇa Śāstrī, the probable scribe. Alternatively, śrīrāmāya is an invocation to the deity Rāma, and the two abbreviated names are owners or scribes. Because of this, all roles here have low confidence. The date is Śaka 1657, Mārgaśīrṣa śukla 6, a Sunday, which corresponds to about November–December 1735 CE. The weekday has not been verified. The colophon gives no place, and the script is Devanagari, so the manuscript may not be of Nepalese origin.
review: The abbreviation jyoºº belongs to the dative śrīrāmāya, not to Kṛṣṇa. Removed 'jyotiṣī' from Kṛṣṇa's titles; Kṛṣṇa keeps only śāstrī.
Added p2 Rāma (śrīrāmāya jyoºº) as a probable human recipient (beneficiary, title jyotiṣī, low confidence) instead of treating him only as the deity in the notes. Renumbered Kṛṣṇa as p3.
Lowered Kṛṣṇa's scribe confidence to low, because no verb of writing is given.
Added a low-confidence relation: Kṛṣṇa wrote_for Rāma.
Added purpose and notes on corrupt words (pati(9)ṣṭhaś for pratiṣṭhaḥ, cakrāra for cakāra) and on the alternative invocation reading.
Weekday given as 'Sunday (ravau)'.

title: Makarandavivaraṇa
subject: Jyautiṣa
date_note: = Sep 1835, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīdaivajñanṛsiṃhasutadivākaravi(10)racitaṃ makarandavivaraṇaṃ samāptam || || śaileṣu śailendu samāsame śake[1757] raṣasya (!) śubhrārddha†padākahā† ravau | strībhe gate rke paśupeśade(11)śe ’do lālaratnākaravi dvide ’likhat || 1 || || (fol. 6r9–11)
notes: The chronogram śaila (7) iṣu (5) śaila (7) indu (1), read right to left, gives 1757. The era is stated as śake, so this is Śaka 1757, about 1835 CE. The catalogue's 'SAM 1757' is only a label; if it were Vikrama the date would be about 1700 CE, but the text says śake. 'raṣasya (!)' is a corrupt month name. The best guess is iṣasya (Iṣa = Āśvina), which agrees with 'strībhe gate 'rke' (the sun having entered Virgo/Kanyā); sahasya (Pauṣa) is less likely. 'śubhrārddha' = the bright half (śukla); the tithi in '†padākahā†' is corrupt (perhaps pratipadā?). ravau = Sunday. The scribe's name is corrupt in '’do lālaratnākaravi dvide ’likhat'. One possible reading is lālaratnākara-vid/vidvān; the catalogue gives Ratnākaralāla. Paśupeśadeśa = 'the land of the Lord Paśupati', i.e. Nepal (Kathmandu Valley). It is the place of copying, not explicitly the scribe's residence.

title: Mukundavijaya
subject: Jyautiṣa
date_note: = Sunday 11 Jul 1604, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: śrīnepālamate gate śrutiśikṣikṣooṇīdharair aṃkite, some paṃcadaśītithau sitarucāvāṣāḍhamāse punaḥ | drāṅnārāyaṇasiṃha eṣa nikhilaprajñāvatāṃ prītaye, lokānandakaraṃ mukundavijayaṃ puṣṭaṃ (!) samastaṃ vyadhāt || (fol. 46v9–10)
purpose: for the pleasure of all wise people (nikhilaprajñāvatāṃ prītaye)
notes: Chronogram: 'śrutiśikṣikṣooṇīdharair' is a corrupt form of śruti (4) + akṣi (2) + kṣoṇīdhara (7). Read right to left, these give NS 724. NS 724 + 880 = 1604, so Āṣāḍha of NS 724 falls around June/July 1604 CE. 'some' means Monday. 'paṃcadaśītithau' means the 15th tithi. 'sitarucau' (moon) together with tithi 15 suggests the full moon, so the fortnight is read as śukla. 'drāṅ' stands for the adverb drāk ('quickly'), not part of the name. Role is uncertain: 'Nārāyaṇasiṃha ... vyadhāt' can mean either 'completed (this copy)' or 'composed'. The verse reads like an author's statement, so Nārāyaṇasiṃha may be the author of the Mukundavijaya rather than (or as well as) its copyist. The catalogue's 'scribe' is kept, but this needs checking. 'puṣṭaṃ (!)' is the cataloguer's marked oddity. The catalogue's king, Jagajjyotirmalla, is not named in the quoted colophon; the date does fall in his reign (c. NS 733–757?), so it should be checked against the cataloguer's source rather than taken from this colophon.
review: Lowered confidence for Nārāyaṇasiṃha's role as scribe from high to medium. 'vyadhāt' (he made) could mean he composed the work rather than copied it; the catalogue's 'scribe' is kept and the ambiguity is explained in notes.
Expanded notes: checked the chronogram, explained the date and month reading (sitarucau, some), and flagged that the colophon does not name Jagajjyotirmalla.

title: Mugdhabodha
subject: Jyautiṣa
date_note: = Sunday 19 May 1805, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti grahaspaṣṭīkaraṇādhikāraḥ || || (2) svastiśrī śāke 1727 jyeṣṭhamāsye (!) kṛṣṇapakṣe 6 dinagatā 9 tadinye (!) likhitaṃ dhaṃjujaisi tasya putre (!) paṭhitaṃ (fol. 6v1–2)
purpose: read by / for the scribe's son (tasya putre paṭhitaṃ)
notes: 'tasya putre (!) paṭhitaṃ' is read as 'read by his (the scribe's) son' or 'for his son's reading'. The son is not named, so he is not listed as a person. 'Dhaṃju' is probably a short form of Dhanañjaya. 'jaisi' is the Jaisī brahmin caste name, so it goes in titles. 'dinagatā 9' is the solar day (gate) 9 of the month Jyeṣṭha. ŚS 1727 + 78 = 1805 CE (Jyeṣṭha falls in May/June 1805). The catalogue gives Śrīdravyasāha as king, but he is not in the quoted colophon. Dravya Śāha ruled Gorkha c. 1559–1570, which does not fit an 1805 copy. The catalogue entry is probably wrong, or the name comes from elsewhere in the manuscript. The colophon ends a section on calculating the true positions of the planets (grahaspaṣṭīkaraṇādhikāra), so this Mugdhabodha is an astronomical (jyotiṣa) text, not the grammar of that name.
review: Purpose added: the copy was read by or made for the scribe's unnamed son ('tasya putre (!) paṭhitaṃ').
Scribe's confidence lowered to medium: 'Dhaṃju' is probably a short form of Dhanañjaya, and the scribe/title split is uncertain.
Date notes extended: 'dinagatā 9' is the solar day (gate) 9 of Jyeṣṭha, as distinct from the lunar tithi 6.
Notes extended: the catalogue's king field (Dravya Śāha, the Gorkha king of c. 1559–1570) does not fit ŚS 1727 = 1805 CE and is not in the colophon.

title: Muhurtakalpadruma
subject: Jyautiṣa
date_note: = Saturday 21 Jul 1668, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: iti kalpadrumaḥ samāptaḥ || ❖ || śrī śrī śrī || śrī śrī śrī || saṃvat 1725 śake 1589 āṣāḍha śuddha 11 śanau likhitaṃ rāmacaṃdrārthaṃ || (fol. 87r6–7)
notes: The catalogue names Rāmacandra as the scribe. But 'likhitaṃ rāmacaṃdrārthaṃ' means 'written for Rāmacandra', so he is the person the copy was made for, not the scribe. The scribe is not named. The colophon does not say that Rāmacandra had the copy made (no likhāpitam), so he is not recorded as commissioner. Calling him owner is an inference from the copy being made for him. The colophon gives two eras: VS 1725 → 1668 CE, but ŚS 1589 → 1667 CE. The usual offset is VS − 135 = ŚS, which gives ŚS 1590 for VS 1725. The one-year gap probably comes from mixing current and expired years. Read that way, both dates point to about June/July 1667, though 1668 is also possible. The weekday has not been checked. 'śuddha' for the bright half of the month and the śake reckoning point to a western or Deccani (Marathi-area) scribe. That is consistent with the text (Muhūrtakalpadruma) and the Devanagari script.

date.paksa normalised note: śuddha = śukla; added note on the one-year VS/ŚS discrepancy

title: Muhūrttamārttaṇḍa
subject: Jyotiṣa
colophon: iti śrīnārāya(8)ṇadaivajñaviracito muhūrttamārttaṇḍo ʼyaṃ samāptim agamat || || śāke kalaṃbāmvubhinīradair (!) mite tviṣe śucau kṛṣṇatithau guror ddine (9) || muhūrttamārttaṇḍam imaṃ tridṛkpure śrīlālaratnākaranāmako ʼlikhat || 1 || || śubham astu lekhakapāṭhayor (!) īśvaraprasādāt || || (fol. 12r7-9)
notes: The chronogram 'kalaṃbāmvubhinīradaiḥ' (marked ! by the cataloguer) is corrupt. kalamba (arrow) = 5 and ambu (water/ocean) = 4, but 'bhi' and 'nīrada' have no clear number value, so the year cannot be read safely. The line scans as Indravajrā/Indravaṃśā as written, so the corruption is probably a word substitution and not a dropped syllable. The catalogue gives '1493/174?'. Note that ŚS 1493 (1571 CE) is the usual composition date of Nārāyaṇa's Muhūrtamārtaṇḍa itself, so 1493 may be a confusion with the composition date and not the copy date. ce_approx is left empty. 'tviṣe' should be read 'tv iṣe' = in the month Iṣa (Āśvina). 'śucau' is ambiguous: as a month name, Śuci normally means Āṣāḍha (sometimes Jyeṣṭha), which would conflict with Iṣa. Here it may be just an epithet ('pure, auspicious'). Pakṣa is kṛṣṇa; no tithi number is given; the weekday is Thursday. The place Tridṛkpura is not identified. Benediction: 'śubham astu lekhakapāṭhayoḥ (read pāṭhakayoḥ)'.

title: Raṇahastiśāstra
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Friday 15 Jul 1547, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: current year, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrīraṇahastiśāstre saptamo dhyāyaḥ || (5) samāptaḥ || 7 || samāgate vikramabhūpate syāt nṛpābhravedaś ca gatetha māse || nabho triyodaśyāṃ (!) aśite ca tithye (!) mārttaṃdavā(6)re parighe ca yoge || || pṛthvīpate śāsati pārakoṭi- kulaje rājye vaśe vuddhimān (!) || tadvipro hṛṣīkeśasuto nivaśate (!) (7) śrīgorṣādurgetyadhaḥ (!) || || bhagnapṛṣṭikaṭigrīvāstabdhadṛṣṭhir (!) adhomukhaṃ (!) || kaṣṭena likhitaṃ graṃthaṃ yatnena paripālayet || || (8) yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭhvā (!) tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā || yadi śudddham aśuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo na dīyate || || || śubham astu || || śrīr asta (!) || (fol. 93r4–8)
notes:
The chronogram is nṛpa (16), abhra (0), veda (4). Read right to left, it gives 4016, which is impossible. So the left-to-right reading VS 1604 (= 1547 CE, matching the catalogue's 'SAM 1604 ?') is adopted, but it is uncertain. 'nabho' = Nabhas = Śrāvaṇa. 'aśite' = asite, i.e. the dark fortnight. 'mārttaṇḍavāra' = Sunday.

'pṛthvīpate' (an error for pṛthvīpatau) is most likely the common noun 'king': '(the) king born of the Pārakoṭi family ruling'. If it were the Gorkha king Pṛthvīpati Shah (r. c. 1669–1716), the date would have to be about VS 1726–1773, which conflicts with 1604. This conflict is unresolved, so the king's name and identity have low confidence. 'pārakoṭi' is obscure and possibly corrupt.

The scribe is not named. He is described only as a vipra, son of Hṛṣīkeśa, living 'below Gorkhā fort' (gorṣā = Gorkhā, with ṣ for kh). That he is the scribe is inferred from 'likhitaṃ mayā'.
review: p1 (Hṛṣīkeśasuta): confidence lowered high→medium. 'Hṛṣīkeśasuta' only describes him as Hṛṣīkeśa's son and is not a personal name. He is identified as scribe only by inference: the vipra living at Gorkhā plus the formulaic 'likhitaṃ mayā'.
p1 evidence shortened to the core substring.

p3 (Pṛthvīpati): the as-yet-unresolved Pṛthvīpati Shah question is now flagged in the notes. The Gorkha king Pṛthvīpati Shah (r. c. 1669–1716 CE) would conflict with VS 1604 = 1547 CE, which is before Dravya Shah founded Gorkha (1559). The word is probably the common noun 'king'.

Date: added a note on reading the chronogram. Strict right-to-left reading (aṅkānāṃ vāmato gatiḥ) gives an impossible 4016, so 1604 (left-to-right, as in the catalogue) is kept. 'aśite' read as asite = kṛṣṇa pakṣa, 'nabhas' = Śrāvaṇa.
Place: noted that 'gorṣādurgetyadhaḥ' probably means 'below Gorkhā fort' and that it is the vipra's residence, taken as the place of copying.

title: Raudrīmeghamālā
subject: Jyautiṣa
date_note: = Tuesday 27 Feb 1629, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: iti śrīraudrameghamālāyāṃ samāptaḥ (!) || ❖ || svasti (8) saṃvat 1695 varṣe śāke 1550 pravarttamāne uttarāyanagate (!) śrīsūrye vasaṃta〈r〉ṛtau śrīphālgunamāse (!) śu(9)klapakṣe paṃcamī bhaumavāsare likhitaṃ medapāṭhajñātīyabhaṭanaraharaprasādāt (!) bhagavānena 〈m〉 īdaṃ pustakaṃ (10) baddha muṣṭi…|| 1 || avamtī(11)kāpurī (!) saniddhau (!) māhākālaharasiddha śiprāsaṃniddhau (!)likhitaṃ || || ❁ || śrīḥ || ❁ || śrīḥ || ❁ || śrī || (fol. 29r7–11)
notes: The two eras conflict. VS 1695 corresponds to ŚS 1560, but the colophon gives ŚS 1550. Phālguna śukla 5 would fall in about Feb–Mar 1639 CE by the VS date, or about Feb–Mar 1629 CE by the ŚS date. The VS reading is preferred here, and the weekday (Tuesday) was not verified. The scribe passage is grammatically corrupt: 'likhitaṃ medapāṭhajñātīyabhaṭanaraharaprasādāt (!) bhagavānena'. There are two readings. (a) The cataloguer's (!) suggests an intended instrumental, making Bhaṭa Naraharaprasāda of the Medapāṭa (Mewar) community the scribe. The catalogue's 'Haraprasāda' fits this and is probably a truncation of Naraharaprasāda; the name could also split as Narahara + prasādāt ('by the grace of Narahara'). (b) It means 'written by Bhagavāna through the favour of Bhaṭa Narahara(prasāda)'. Reading (a) is followed, and Bhagavāna is retained at low confidence. The place is Avantikāpurī, near Mahākāla, Harasiddhi and the Śiprā river, i.e. Ujjain. This is not a Nepalese copy.
review: Scribe role moved to Naraharaprasāda: the cataloguer's (!) on 'prasādāt' marks it as an error for an instrumental (…prasādena), and the catalogue's scribe 'Haraprasāda' points to the same name. Bhaṭa Naraharaprasāda of the Medapāṭa jñāti is now the scribe, with medium confidence.

'bhagavānena' kept as a person (Bhagavāna) but at low confidence and with role 'other', since its function is unclear. The first reading's 'p1 other p2' relation was dropped because it rests only on that unclear reading.
Affiliation normalized to Medapāṭa (Mewar) jñāti. 'Medapāṭha' is a scribal spelling of Medapāṭa.
ce_approx changed from 1638 to 1639. In VS 1695, counted from Caitra, Phālguna falls in Feb–Mar 1639 CE.
Notes now explain the VS/ŚS conflict more fully: VS 1695 equals ŚS 1560, not 1550.
'baddha muṣṭi…' identified as the stock scribal verse (bhagnapṛṣṭhakaṭigrīvo baddhamuṣṭir adhomukhaḥ…). It is not a name.

notes: The chronogram is vila/bila (9), iṣu (5), muni (7), bhū (1). Read right to left it gives Śaka 1759, which is 1837 CE. The tithi is guha (= 6, for the six-faced Skanda) and the weekday is ravau (Sunday). The exact CE day was not checked. The catalogue names Tārānāthaśarmā as the scribe, but the colophon has 'harinṛsiṃho 'py alikhat śrī-tārānātha-śarmaṇe' (Harinṛsiṃha wrote it for Tārānātha Śarman), so Tārānātha appears in the dative. The 'api' is odd: it could be filler for the metre, or it could mean 'Harinṛsiṃha also wrote', which would imply another copyist. Tārānātha's role as owner or beneficiary is inferred from the dative; nothing in the colophon says he commissioned the copy. 'nepāladeśāntare' may mean 'in the foreign land of Nepal', which would suggest the scribe was not from Nepal; this is uncertain.

notes: 'gaṃdhādhareṇa' is a slip for 'gaṃgādhareṇa' (Gaṅgādhara), which is how the catalogue reads it. The father's name is unclear. The cataloguer gives '(dabhikhaṃ)' in parentheses before 'bhaṭṭasute'. This may be an uncertain reading, or a Marathi family name, since the scribe calls himself a Mahārāṣṭra jñātīya. The two eras agree: VS 1724 − 57 = 1667 and ŚS 1589 + 78 = 1667. Bhādrapada kṛṣṇa 8 is Janmāṣṭamī, which falls around August 1667. Identifying Pāṭalipura with Patna is likely but not certain.

title: Āpaduddhāraṇakavaca
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Thursday 31 Mar 1678, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: iti śrī āpaduddhāraṇakavaca saṃpurṇaṃ || || subhaṃ || bhuyāt || || || śrīśāke 1600 māse 12 tithau 10 vāre 5 pūstakaṃ liṣitaṃ valabhadraṃ yo ṣimidaṃ (fol. 3r3–5)
notes: The month, tithi and weekday are given only as numbers, and the pakṣa is not stated. Month 12 is probably Phālguna if months are counted from Caitra; it would be Caitra only if they are counted from Vaiśākha. Weekday 5 = Thursday. ŚS 1600 + 78 = 1678; Phālguna of that year falls in early 1679 CE. 'valabhadraṃ' is a corrupt form, presumably for the instrumental 'balabhadreṇa' ('written by Balabhadra'). The phrase 'yo ṣimidaṃ' after the name is unclear. It may be corrupt, or it may hide a surname, place or epithet; it is not explained here.
review: Month 12: corrected the note. In a Śaka date months usually count from Caitra, so month 12 is probably Phālguna, not Caitra.
Date: added the month and weekday interpretations to the date fields; kept ce_approx 1679, since Phālguna of ŚS 1600 falls around February 1679 CE.
Notes: replaced the conjecture 'yo 'likhad idaṃ' for 'yo ṣimidaṃ' with a neutral flag; the phrase is unclear and may hide a surname, place or epithet.
Person: lowered confidence from high to medium because of the unclear phrase that follows the name.

title: Āpaduddhārastotra
subject: Stotra

colophon: iti śrīrudrayāmale amṛtasāroddhāra(!) āpaduddhārastotraṃ san(!)purṇaṃ || || samvat 882 ākhā(!)ḍakṛṣṇa(!) aṣṭami(!) kuhna coyā dina javo || re(!)khaka daivajñapurandarasi(!)ha†rāmana† (fols. 9r2–3 continue up to the right-hand margin)
notes: The era is not named ('samvat 882'). It is taken as NS because the dating phrase is in Newari ('kuhna coyā dina javo' = 'written on that day'), and the catalogue says NS. NS 882 Āṣāḍha kṛṣṇa aṣṭamī falls in about mid-1762 CE. 'ākhāḍa' stands for āṣāḍha and 'rekhaka' for lekhaka. 'purandarasi(!)ha' is read as Purandarasiṃha. The name is directly followed by the crux †rāmana†, and the cataloguer notes that the line runs on to the right-hand margin. This crux may be the end of a longer name (e.g. Purandarasiṃha + Rāma…) or a separate damaged word, so the name is uncertain.

title: Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra
subject: Vyākaraṇa
colophon: iti śrīmatpadavākyapramāṇapārāvāriṇa(!)dhuriṇa(!)raṃgojibhaṭṭātmajakoḍa(!)-bhaṭṭakṛte vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāre samāpto yaṃ sphoṭaḥ || || śrīpaśupateś carārpaṇam || || gurupurohitapaṃḍitamaṃḍalīmukuṭakāmararājanideśataḥ || likhitam etad aśītighanaprame śakavare śucikṛṣṇadale malaḥ || 1 || likhitam idam pustakaṃ lokajitaśarmaṇā śubhaṃ (fol. 76r7-8)
notes: The commissioner's name sits inside a drutavilambita verse: 'gurupurohitapaṇḍitamaṇḍalīmukuṭa-kāmararāja-nideśataḥ'. It can be divided as Kāmararāja, or as mukuṭaka + Amararāja. 'rāja' may be part of the name, or he may be a king described as the crest-jewel of the gurus, purohitas and paṇḍitas. More likely he is the chief royal preceptor (rājaguru). The year 'aśītighana-prame śakavare' is an unclear chronogram. 'aśīti' means 80, but 'ghana' has no standard bhūtasaṃkhyā value; it could mean a cube or a hundreds component. One possible reading is ŚS 1780 ≈ 1858 CE, but this is not verified, so ce_approx is left empty. Koṇḍabhaṭṭa, the author, lived in the 17th century, which only gives the earliest possible date. 'malaḥ' is probably mala(māsa), an intercalary Āṣāḍha; checking for an adhika Āṣāḍha could confirm the year. The 'likhitam etad' of the verse and the closing prose statement both name Lokajit Śarman as scribe, which agrees with the catalogue field. The name stems leave out the brahmin suffix 'bhaṭṭa' as the instructions require. In the conventional form the author is Koṇḍabhaṭṭa, son of Raṅgojibhaṭṭa.
review: p1/p2: 'bhaṭṭa' removed from the name stems (Raṅgoji, Koṇḍa) and kept as a title; corrupt 'koḍa(!)' read as Koṇḍa

p3: titles guru/purohita/paṇḍita kept, with a note that they come from an epithet ('crest-jewel of the circle of gurus, purohitas and paṇḍitas'), probably meaning a royal preceptor; the name is ambiguous between Kāmararāja and Amararāja (mukuṭaka-amara-rāja); the metre (drutavilambita) does not decide it

date: 'malaḥ' read as mala(māsa), an intercalary month, so the month is possibly adhika Āṣāḍha; the year 'aśītighana' is flagged as an unresolved chronogram (80 + ghana); the ŚS reading of ghana as 17, giving ŚS 1780 ≈ 1858 CE, is offered only as a guess

notes: The catalogue gives the date as [ŚS] 989. That cannot be right: ŚS 989 is about 1067 CE, which is earlier than the Sārasvata grammar itself. A bare three-digit saṃvat in a Newari-script manuscript is Nepal Saṃvat, so NS 989 = c. 1869 CE (the month is Pauṣa, so this may fall in early 1870). 'va' = vadi, the dark fortnight (kṛṣṇa). The tithi is written 'dvitṛyodsyā' and is read as trayodaśī, following the catalogue. The 'dvi-' may be a stray syllable, though dvitīyā cannot be ruled out. The weekday has not been checked against an ephemeris. The text is named in the colophon as 'śāśvatī vyākaraṇaprakriyā', probably a corruption of Sārasvatī. 'kaviḥ' is treated as a title (kavi).

colophon: iti śrīparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīnarendrapurīśrīcaraṇaviracitā sārasvatī prakriyā samāptā || || śubham || || śrīśāke 1939 bāhulamāse śuklapakṣe paṃcadaśyāṃ tithau guruvāsare likhitaṃ viśvānaṃdena jainena (saṃjñānābhidha)pattananarādhipateḥ (kavardāraḥ śrīphaṭ) siṃhanāmnaḥ || || śubhaṃ || || (fol.99r6-7)
notes:
Era: the colophon says 'śāke 1939', but taken literally as Śaka this would be 2017 CE, which is impossible for a microfilmed manuscript. 'Śāke' is probably used loosely for 'year'. Read as VS 1939, Kārttika (= bāhula) śukla 15 falls on Thursday, 26 Oct 1882, which matches guruvāsare, so VS is adopted. The catalogue's '[ŚŚ]' was not followed.

The patron passage is corrupt and partly bracketed by the cataloguer: '(saṃjñānābhidha)pattananarādhipateḥ (kavardāraḥ śrīphaṭ) siṃhanāmnaḥ' means 'of the ruler of the town called …, named Phaṭ Siṃha'. 'Kavardāra' is probably a garbled place name, perhaps Kavardhā/Kawardha (a princely state in Chhattisgarh), and probably not a title. 'Phaṭsiṃha' may stand for Phatehsiṃha (Fateh Singh). Because only the genitive is used, his role (owner, patron or commissioner) is uncertain.

The scribe Viśvānanda calls himself 'jaina'. The town in brackets is the patron's seat, not a stated place of copying.
review: Era changed from ŚS to VS: Śaka 1939 would be 2017 CE, which is too late for an NGMCP microfilm. VS 1939 Kārttika śukla 15 falls on Thursday, 26 Oct 1882, which matches guruvāsare. ce_approx stays 1882. The first reading had era ŚS together with a VS-based CE year, which was inconsistent.

p3 role changed from commissioner to owner, confidence lowered to low: the colophon has only a genitive (…narādhipateḥ … siṃhanāmnaḥ) with no verb meaning 'had it copied'. The wrote_for relation is kept.

p3 titles: 'kavardāra' removed. It is more likely the name of the town or state (possibly Kawardha) than an office title, and the gloss 'kapardāra = storekeeper' was unfounded. 'narādhipati' added as the title actually stated.
Town '(saṃjñānābhidha)pattana' moved from place of copying to p3's residence. The colophon does not say the copy was made there, so place is now empty.
Notes rewritten.

notes: The era is not named; VS is assumed from the catalogue and from the Devanagari, western-Indian style of the colophon ('sudī'; Premaśaṅkara is a Gujarati-type name). 'līdā-' is read as 'li(khitaṃ) dā(sa?)', an abbreviation for likhitam, which would make Premaśaṃkara the scribe. This reading is uncertain. 'dīkpāla' may be a second person, part of the same name, or a corrupted surname; 'sajñāti' (= 'with kinsmen' or 'of the X jñāti/caste') is unclear.
