title: Nṛtyeśvaramahābhairavapūjāpaddhati
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Thursday 8 Feb 1685, weekday verified, nakṣatra not
colophon: iti śrīśrīśrīnāṭeśvara mahā(2)(bhai)ravapūjāpaddhati samāptaḥ || || śrī 3 sveṣṭadevatā prīnātu sarvvadā || || śubhaṃ || || (3) /// (yā)dṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭā, tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā | yadi śuddham aśuddhaṃ vā, mama doṣo nadiyate (4)/// || || śrīnepālasamvat 805 || śrīkarigata samvat 4785 || śrīvikramāditya samvat (5) 1741 || śrīśake samvat 1606 || māghamāse, śuklapakṣa || śrīpaṇcamyāyātithai || reva(6)ti nakṣete || śubhayoge || yathākarana mūhūtake || bṛhaspativāśale || kubhaṃrāsi gate śa(1)(vita)rī || mīnarāśi gate candramaśi || || thvakuhnu śrīśrīsumati jaya jitāmitramallava(2)rmmaṇā svakarena likhitaṃ saṃpūrṇṇaṃ || || aneka karmmanā sveṣṭhā, devī prīnātu siddhidā (3)/// ta kṛtaṃ karma, kṣatu marhasi me sadā || jitāmitrasya bhūpasya, tvāṃ vinā nāsti (4)/// gati .. tvadbhakti tatparā śaktir mmatirbhūyāt kulāmbike || || śrī 3 bhavānīśaṃkrarābhyaṃ (5) namaḥ || || śrīśrīsumati jaya jitāmitramalladevasana śrīśrīśrīnāṭeśvara mahābhaira(6)(va)sake tavagvaḍa ghaṃsthā duṃtāyā thva padhati juroṃ || bhāgīrāmayā verasa juroṃ || || (1) nānā granthasa soyāva pūjāpaddhati saṃphuḍi mahākastana dayakā anahelā yāya mateva ya(2)(tna)pūrvvakana nidāna yāya mālaḥ || || e || || śrīśrīśrīnāṭeśvara prīnātu || śubhaṃ || || (exp. 16b1-17b2)
purpose: pūjāpaddhati prepared in connection with offering a large bell (tavagvaḍa ghaṃṭā) to Nāṭeśvara Mahābhairava
notes: King Jayajitāmitramalla of Bhaktapur wrote the manuscript with his own hand (svakarena likhitaṃ) and compiled the paddhati from multiple texts (nānā granthasa soyāva pūjāpaddhati saṃphuḍi mahākastana dayakā). Bhāgīrāma was the prominent minister/administrator in Bhaktapur under his reign.

title: Vitānapratiṣṭhāvidhi
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_raw: samvat 808 śrāvaṇa vadi 8 kṛrttika nakṣatre dhruvayoga yathākarṇṇa budhavāla siṃha, vṛṣa
date_note: = Wednesday 18 Aug 1688, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: ❖ samvat 808 śrāvaṇa va(15)di 8 kṛrttika nakṣatre (16) dhruvayoga yathākarṇṇa (17) budhavāla siṃha, vṛṣa || (38left1) thvakuhnu dhunakā dina (2) paśaracheyā śrīdeva(3)rāmapatina coyā tha(4)va stī devīmayī mano(5)holā galīlī || thvate vi(6)dyamāna yāṅāva coyā || (7) iti vitānapratiṣṭā(8)virdhiḥ samāptā śubhaṃ || (exps. 37right14-38left8)
notes: The Newari passage reads roughly: 'On this day it was finished: written by Devarāmapati of Paśarache; his wife Devīmayī, Manoholā, Galīlī — having made these present, [he] wrote.' Manoholā and Galīlī are probably further household members, perhaps children, but their kinship is not stated. 'Manoholā' may be a Newari form of Manoharā. 'Paśarache' is given as the scribe's residence (paśaracheyā); it is not explicitly the place of copying, and it has not been identified. The date fits together: Kṛttikā nakṣatra, with the moon in Vṛṣa and the sun in Siṃha, suits Śrāvaṇa kṛṣṇa 8. The meaning of 'yathākarṇṇa' is unclear. The colophon does not say who owned or commissioned the copy.
review: p3: name kept as written 'Manoholā' (the first reading's 'Manoharā' was a guess); role changed to relative_only (low confidence), since the person is listed with the wife as one of 'these' (thvate) present at the copying
p4: Galīlī treated the same way, as a probable household member; confidence low
Date: added the sun and moon signs (Siṃha, Vṛṣa) to nakshatra_yoga and normalised the weekday to Wednesday; ce_approx 1688 confirmed (NS 808 + 880; Śrāvaṇa falls in 1688)
Place: Paśarache is given as the scribe's residence; it is only implied as the place of copying

title: Bhagavadgītā [saṭīka]
subject: Vedānta
date_note: = Tuesday 22 Aug 1843, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrī bhārate gītāsāra samāptaṃ sampūrṇaṃ śubhamastu || || yogeśvarāya namaḥ|| śāke 1765 bhādrapadamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe dvādaśyāṃ tithau bhaumavāsare likhitamidaṃ gītāsārabhāṣā śrīkṛṣṇadeva prasādeva pāpasaṃcayaṃ harati || yadakṣaraṃ padabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ ca yadbhavet || tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ devaṃ prasīda parameśvara || 1 || yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ paṭhitaṃ mayā || yadi śuddhamaśuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo na dīyatām || 2 || oṃ namo paramātmane kṛṣṇāya || (fol. 20r2-3,6-8)
notes: The text 'śrīkṛṣṇadeva prasādeva pāpasaṃcayaṃ harati' is ambiguous. (a) It may be a corrupt '°prasādena': 'written by Śrī Kṛṣṇadevaprasāda; [this text] removes the heap of sins'. Prasāda-type personal names are common in 19th-century Nepal, and the catalogue gives Kṛṣṇadevaprasāda as scribe. (b) It may be 'śrīkṛṣṇadevaprasāda eva pāpasaṃcayaṃ harati': 'the grace of Lord Kṛṣṇa alone removes sins', with no human named. Reading (a) is recorded here, but with low confidence. The weekday has not been checked against the calendar (ŚS 1765 Bhādrapada kṛṣṇa 12 falls around September 1843). The colophon calls the text 'gītāsāra' / 'gītāsārabhāṣā', not the full Bhagavadgītā with commentary given in the catalogue title.
review: Added Kṛṣṇadevaprasāda as scribe (low confidence). 'likhitam idaṃ … śrīkṛṣṇadeva prasādeva' can be read as a corrupt 'śrīkṛṣṇadevaprasādena', i.e. 'written by Kṛṣṇadevaprasāda'. The catalogue also reads it that way. The first reading took it as devotional 'prasāda eva'. That reading is possible, but the syntax after 'likhitam idaṃ' points to an instrumental agent.
Emptied purpose: 'pāpasaṃcayaṃ harati' describes what the text does, not why this copy was made.
Weekday changed to 'bhauma (Tuesday)'. The rest of the date (ŚS 1765 = c. 1843 CE) is confirmed.

title: Samayācāratantra
subject: Tantra
date_note: doubtful: Thursday 13 Jun 1084 is too early for a paper manuscript (an abbreviated or misread year, or the exemplar's date)
date_doubtful: doubtful: Thursday 13 Jun 1084 is too early for a paper manuscript (an abbreviated or misread year, or the exemplar's date)
colophon: iti śrīumāmaheśvarasam(3)vāde samayācārataṃtraḥ (!) samāptam || śubham || || || ❁ || || śubham (4) samvat 1006 āṣāḍhaśukla 7 roja 5 taddine saṃpūrṇaṃ likhiti śaśidharaśarmmaṇā- (fol. 46v2–4)
notes: The era is not stated ('samvat 1006'). The catalogue gives ŚS 1006 (= 1084 CE). That is implausible for a Devanagari paper manuscript, and so is VS 1006 (949 CE), especially since the Persian weekday term 'roja' is a late usage. NS 1006 (= 1886 CE) is the most plausible reading. The weekday has not been verified: by an approximate check, Āṣāḍha śukla 7 of 1886 falls around 8–9 June 1886, a Tuesday rather than a Thursday (roja 5), so the NS attribution is likely but not confirmed. 'likhiti' is a scribal error for 'likhitam'.
review: Weekday normalized to 'Thursday (roja 5)'.

Notes rewritten: the first reading's claim that the weekday confirms 8 July 1886 is unsupported. 8 July 1886 was a Thursday, but by the amānta reckoning that day falls in Śrāvaṇa, not Āṣāḍha; Āṣāḍha śukla 7 of 1886 falls around 8–9 June (a Tuesday). The NS attribution rests on plausibility, not on a verified weekday.
Added a note on the catalogue's ŚS 1006 and on the scribal error 'likhiti'.

title: Tripuramahopaniṣad
subject: Upaniṣad
date_note: = Monday 18 Aug 1913, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: current year, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti bhāṣkararā(7)yeṇa nāmicitā (!) tripurāmahopaniṣadorthāḥ (!) prakaṭayi(1) mayojñām api viduṣāṃ toṣāya katipaye kathitāḥ || (2) iti tripurmhopniṣadbhāṣ〉aṃ sapūrṇaṃ (!) bhagnapṛṣṭhakaṭigrīvā (!) stabdhadṛṣṭiradhorukhaḥ (!) || (4)kaṣṭena likhitaṃ graṃthaṃ yatnena paripālayat (!) (5)saṃ ○ 1970 bhādra kṛṣṇa 2 tithau guruvā(6)sare gurucaraṇāraviṃdārpaṇaṃ || liººgopīnā(7)tha maṃḍalīkaraṇē śubham puºº Śrīkṛṣṇa jyoºº (fol. 58v3–7)
notes: The text is Bhāskararāya's bhāṣya on the Tripuramahopaniṣad. 'maṃḍalīkaraṇē' after the scribe's name is unclear: it could be a caste or office designation (Karaṇa), an epithet, or the locative of a place name. 'puºº' most likely abbreviates pustakam, which would make Śrīkṛṣṇa jyo(tiṣī) the owner; putra or purohita are possible but less likely readings. 'jyoºº' could stand for jyotiṣī or jyotirvid. Date: VS 1970 = 1913 CE. A rough calculation suggests the Thursday weekday fits Bhādrapada kṛṣṇa 2 in the amānta scheme, about 18 September 1913. In the pūrṇimānta scheme the day would fall about 18–19 August 1913, a Monday or Tuesday. This is approximate and has not been checked against a pañcāṅga. The catalogue's scribe field 'Gopīnātha maṃḍalīkaraṇe' matches the colophon. The verse 'bhagnapṛṣṭhakaṭigrīvā...' is the standard scribal formula.
review: p3 name: dropped the honorific śrī ('Śrīkṛṣṇa' → 'Kṛṣṇa'); the abbreviated title is recorded as 'jyotiṣī (jyoºº)'.
p3 evidence and notes: 'puºº' is most likely pustakam, which makes Kṛṣṇa the owner. A reading as putra or purohita cannot be ruled out, so confidence stays medium.
p2: 'maṃḍalīkaraṇē' is kept as a provisional title. The notes add that it could instead be a locative place name, meaning 'at Maṇḍalīkaraṇa'.
p1: evidence shortened; Bhāskararāya is the commentator (author of the bhāṣya), not connected with this copy.
date: the weekday and month were checked; the notes explain which month scheme fits.
purpose: rendered as a dedication at the guru's feet.

notes: The date reads 'saṃvat 164 || 1652'. 164 is unexplained: it may be a miswritten or truncated year, or a year in another reckoning. It does not match 1652 under any standard era. 1652 is taken as VS. Caitra vadi 1 under the pūrṇimānta scheme falls in March 1595 or 1596; the weekday has not been verified. 'idaṃ pustakaṃ mahārājādhirāja rājā śrīsaṃgrāmasāhirāje' could mean 'in the reign (rājye) of Saṃgrāmasāhi'. It could also mean the book belonged to the king. Campā is probably his queen, but the colophon does not say so. 'pradhāna' applied to Makaranda may mean that he was a minister. The catalogue's 'Donor: Queen Caṃpā' is not supported: the colophon only says the book is hers. The catalogue gives Vārāṇasī as the place of copying, but it is not in the quoted colophon.

subject: Vedanta

colophon: iti śrīmatpuruṣottamacaraṇāraviṃdakṛpāmakaraṃdaviṃdupronmīlita vivekatairabhaktasya paramahaṃsa viṣṇupurīgrathītāyāṃ(!) bhāgavatāmṛtābdhilabdha śrībhagavadbhaktiratnāvalī sakāṃtimālā saṃpūrṇaṃ || śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ || śrīkṛṣṇa jayati || saṃvat 1673 varaṣe āsauja sudhi 12 || liṣyataṃ(!) goviṃdadāsa vaiśnava || āmāvatīmadhye devasthalaṃ kalyāṇaśayake || śrīkalyāṇayannamaḥ || śrī śrī || (fol. 44v89-45r1-3)
notes: 'vivekatairabhaktasya' is probably a corruption of '...viveka-tairabhukta-', i.e. a native of Tirabhukti (Tirhut, Mithilā). That fits the tradition that Viṣṇupurī came from Mithilā. Puruṣottama in the opening epithet is the deity (Jagannātha) and is not a person. The text is the Bhaktiratnāvalī with its commentary Kāntimālā, which is usually ascribed to Viṣṇupurī himself. Āmāvatī is probably Āmbāvatī/Amber (Āmer, near Jaipur), but this is not certain. 'kalyāṇaśayake' may be a corruption of 'kalyāṇarāyake' (a Kalyāṇarāya temple?), which would fit the closing 'śrīkalyāṇayannamaḥ'. VS 1673 Āśvina śukla 12 falls in about September/October 1616 CE. Nothing marks this as a Nepalese copy.

purpose: copied on the birthday of Jaṅgabahādura
notes: No era is named. VS is assumed because of the period of Jang Bahadur Rana and the catalogue field. The chronogram reads guṇa(3) anala(3) khaga(9) eka(1). Read right to left this gives 1933 (1876/77 CE). The catalogue's VS 1936 works only if guṇa=6. VS 1933 is also historically more likely: Jang Bahadur died in February 1877 (VS 1933), so a copy made on his birthday in VS 1936 would fall after his death. 'vamarṇo (!)' is probably a corruption of 'varmaṇo' (Jaṅgabahādura Varmā). He was Prime Minister and Mahārāja of Kaski-Lamjung, not king of Nepal, though the colophon calls him nṛpa. 'janmatithi' is his birthday, not a calendrical tithi.
review: Chronogram re-read: guṇa=3, anala=3, khaga=9 (planets), eka=1, read right to left = 1933, not 1936. The catalogue's 1936 needs guṇa=6, which is a rare value. Year set to VS 1933 (ce_approx 1876); the catalogue figure is recorded in notes.

Jaṅgabahādura: role changed from 'king' to 'minister'. He was Prime Minister and Mahārāja of Kaski-Lamjung, not the reigning king of Nepal. The colophon calls him nṛpa, so that title is kept. Confidence lowered to medium.
Relation p1→p2 changed from under_reign_of to other: the copy was made on his birthday and is not dated by his reign.
Scribe's title normalised to 'vidvān'.
Tithi field: 'janmatithi' kept but explained in notes. No calendrical tithi is given.

title: Siddhāntamuktāvalī
subject: Nyāya
date_note: = Friday 28 Sep 1821, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: year read as current
colophon: iti śrīmanmahāmahopādhyāyaśrīvidyānivāsabhaṭṭācāryātma(9)jaśrīviśvanātha paṃcānanabhaṭṭācāryaviracitā siddhāntamuktāvalī sampūrṇṇā || || kīlālākaravedasaīṃdhavarasābhis sammite śākake (10) māsīṣe ghaṭage vivasvatisitai bhāsye tithau bhārgave || śrīviśveśvarapattene samalikhan muktāvalī pustakaṃ tūrṇaṃ śrīgurupādapadmamadhupaḥ śrī(11)lālaratnākaraḥ || 1 || (fol. 40r8–11)
notes:
The year is given as a word-number chronogram, read right to left: kīlālākara (ocean) = 4, veda = 4, saindhava (seven seas) = 7, rasā (earth) = 1. That gives ŚS 1744 = CE 1822, which matches the catalogue.

The month 'māsīṣe' means māsi iṣe, i.e. Āśvina. 'Ghaṭa' normally means Kumbha (Aquarius), which would not fit Āśvina. It may stand for Tulā (cf. dhaṭa, 'balance'), which would fit Āśvina; this is unresolved.

The tithi word 'bhāsye' is obscure or corrupt.

The scribe's name is written 'lālaratnākara'. The catalogue normalises it as 'Ratnākaralāla'.

'śrīgurupādapadmamadhupaḥ' describes the scribe as devoted to his guru, but the guru is not named.

Viśveśvarapattana is Kāśī/Vārāṇasī, which matches the catalogue's place field.
review: Chronogram checked and explained: kīlālākara (ocean) = 4, veda = 4, saindhava (seven seas) = 7, rasā (earth) = 1. Read right to left this gives ŚS 1744 = CE 1822, so the first reading's year was right.
Month normalised: māsi iṣe means the month Iṣa, which is Āśvina. Removed the 'Āśvina/Kārttika?' doubt.
Recorded the solar position 'ghaṭage vivasvati' (sun in Ghaṭa) in the nakshatra_yoga field and noted that it may conflict with Āśvina.
Tithi marked as unclear: 'bhāsye' cannot be confidently resolved to a number.
Notes now mention the catalogue's name form 'Ratnākaralāla' and the scribe's unnamed guru.

title: Suvarṇaprabhāsasūtra
subject: Bauddhasūtra
date_note: ≈ 1669 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: āryasuvarṇṇaprabhāsotamasūtrendrarājaḥ parisamāptaḥ || ❁ || ye dharmmā hetuprabhavā hetu (!) teṣāṃ tathāgato hy avadat teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha || ○ || evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ || ○ || deyadharmmo yaṃ pravaramahāyāyinaḥ paramopāsakaśrījaśodharavihāravāsitaḥ (!), vajrācāryya.. .. .. .. .. likhito ʼgamat sampūrṇṇaṃ śubham astu sarvvadā || saṃvat 789 (fol. 108r1–3)
notes: The name after 'vajrācāryya' is lost in a lacuna. The donor formula (deyadharmo 'yaṃ + genitive) shows that the paramopāsaka living at Jaśodharavihāra is the donor. This is Yaśodhara Mahāvihāra / Bu Bahā in Patan, but it is the donor's residence, not a stated place of copying. The vajrācārya probably belongs to the same donor phrase. The scribe's name may also have been lost in the lacuna before 'likhito ʼgamat', so 'scribe' is uncertain; the catalogue's 'Scribe: … Vajrācārya' is an inference. Corrupt forms: pravaramahāyāyinaḥ for pravaramahāyānayāyinaḥ; vāsitaḥ for vāsinaḥ. The year is plain 'saṃvat 789' with no era named; NS is assumed, which fits the Newari script and the catalogue (≈1668/69 CE).
review: p1: role 'donor' made primary — the deyadharma formula puts the donor in the genitive ('pravaramahāyā[na]yāyinaḥ paramopāsaka... vihāravāsi[naḥ]'). 'scribe' is kept only as a possible role because the name after 'vajrācāryya' is lost before 'likhito ʼgamat'. Confidence stays low.
p1 residence/affiliation: normalised to stem form Jaśodharavihāra (= Yaśodhara Mahāvihāra, Bu Bahā, Patan).
place: emptied. The vihāra is given as the donor's residence, not as the place of copying.
notes: added the corrections pravaramahāyāyinaḥ → pravaramahāyānayāyinaḥ and vāsitaḥ → vāsinaḥ, and explained the donor/scribe ambiguity.

title: Svayambhūpurāṇa
subject: Bauddha Purāṇa
date_note: ≈ 1693 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti dharmmadhātusvayabhūtpattidharmmamāhātmyasubhāṣitasūtraṃ daśamādhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || ○ || ye dharmmā hetuprabhā(!)vā, hetu(!) teṣāṃ tathāgataḥ | hy avadat teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ || ○ || śreyo stu saṃvat 813 dita rāthoke pūrṇṇamāśi kunhu, likhitasaṃpūrṇṇaṃ kṛtvā, gṛhasthāpitā bhavanti | /// ⁅de⁆vācāryeṇa svārthaputrapautrādiśikṣāya (!) hetunārthaṃ likhitaṃ kṛtaṃ || etatpuṇyānubhāvena jajamānasya āyurārogyajanadhanamakānalakṣmīvṛddhir astu | paratra sukhāvatīm āpnuyāt || ○ || śubham astu sarvvadā kāla(!) kalyāṇam astuḥ(!) || (fol. 92r6–92v4)
purpose: Written for the instruction of the scribe himself and of his sons, grandsons and later descendants (svārthaputrapautrādiśikṣā). The merit is wished for the yajamāna: long life, health, people, wealth, a house and prosperity, and rebirth in Sukhāvatī.
notes: Scribe's name: a lacuna (///) comes before '⁅de⁆vācāryeṇa', so the full name is lost. It probably ended in -deva and was followed by the title ācārya, possibly vajrācārya. Month: 'dita rāthoke' is unclear. It may be a corruption involving the Newari month dilā (= Āṣāḍha), but this is uncertain. Pakṣa: pūrṇimā implies śuklapakṣa, but the colophon does not say so. 'jajamānasya' (= yajamāna) refers to an unnamed patron, probably the scribe himself or his household. 'gṛhasthāpitā bhavanti' says the book was installed in the house. The date NS 813 matches the catalogue (NS 813 = c. 1693 CE).
review: p1: the name is incomplete. Only '⁅de⁆vācārya' survives after a lacuna, so the honest stem is a broken name '…deva' with 'ācārya' as a title. Listing 'Devācārya' as the name and also 'ācārya' as a title counted the title twice. Confidence lowered to low.
date.paksa: the colophon gives no pakṣa. Śukla is only inferred from pūrṇimā, so the field is now empty and the inference is in notes.
date.month: kept as written. The reading 'intercalary Āṣāḍha' was guesswork; notes now give the Newari month name dilā (= Āṣāḍha) as a possible reading instead.
purpose: added the merit wish for the yajamāna and rebirth in Sukhāvatī. Added the note that the book was placed in the house (gṛhasthāpitā).

title: kulaja[masāhiba]
subject: Sāhibagraṃtha?
date_note: = Wednesday 6 Oct 1852, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: || śrī śrīkitāba baḍo kyāmata nāmā tamāta huā | śrī śrīkulajamasāhiba tamāma huī || śrībābāju sāheba jīvanadāsajukī gumaṭīmeṃ ho ke liṣyate paṃ śrīpureta lalanajunai śrīdhanavāī kaunai hai pālakī || saṃvatu 1909 || kuvāra vadi 8 budhe kauṃ tamāma hui jathāputaseṃ jo vāceṃ sunai tākoṃ paranāṃma vera vera | muḥ sāhigaḍha || (fol. 730v9-14)
purpose: copied for Dhanavāī (?), from the exemplar (jathāputaseṃ = yathāpustakam); salutations to whoever reads or hears it
notes: The colophon is in Hindi (Braj/Bundeli). It closes the Kayāmatnāmā and the Kulajam Sāhab, the Prāṇanāthī/Praṇāmī scripture. Its author Prāṇanātha is not named in the colophon, so he is not listed. The catalogue gives the scribe as Aṃjīradāsa, but the quoted colophon names only paṃ purohita Lalanajū as the writer ('liṣyate'). Aṃjīradāsa may appear elsewhere in the manuscript; this cannot be checked here. The copy was made in the gumaṭī (small shrine or cell) of Bābā Jīvanadāsa at Sāhigaḍha. This is probably Shahgarh (Sagar district, MP), a Praṇāmī area, but the identification is not certain. 'śrīdhanavāī kaunai hai pālakī' is obscure. It may mean the copy was made for, or belongs to, Dhanabāī (a woman's name), so role and confidence are tentative. title: Bhāvaprakāśa
subject: Āyurveda
date_note: = Friday 10 Jan 1879, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: || iti samvat 1935 sāla miti māgha vadī 2 roja mā liṣitam pāṭana cyāsala tola cikaṃvahīla vaṣnyā vāḍā vaida jīvanasiṃha(!) 1932 sālamā śrī mahārāja raṇauddīpa siṃha rāṇā bahādurakā kalakaṭṭā savārī huṃdā pāuṣārī jādā bhāvaprakāśako kitāp 10 rupaiñā kaṃpanīle kīni malāi vakasa bhayo so kitāp nepālī kagatamā maile sārayā; yo postaka kasaile lobhāni pāpāni nagarnu || yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā(!) tādṛṣṭaṃ(!) liṣitaṃ(!) mayā || yadi śuddham asuddho(!) vā mama doṣo na dīyate || (fol.469r1-5)
purpose: Copy made for the scribe himself from an exemplar given to him (implied; not stated as svārtha)
notes: The Nepali note says that in VS 1932, when Mahārāja Raṇoddīpa Siṃha Rāṇā Bahādur travelled to Calcutta (savārī), a book of the Bhāvaprakāśa was bought for 10 Company rupees and given to me. 'kaṃpanīle' is uncertain: it may mean 'with Company rupees' or 'by the Company'. The scribe says he copied that book onto Nepali paper. So Raṇoddīpa supplied the exemplar, not this manuscript. He became Prime Minister in late 1877 (VS 1934). He was therefore not yet PM in VS 1932, but he was PM when the copy was made (Māgha VS 1935 = Jan/Feb 1879). The catalogue's 'King' field is wrong: Raṇoddīpa was Prime Minister, and the actual king (Pṛthvī Vīr Vikram Śāha) is not named. 'roja' means 'day', not a weekday name. 'vāḍā' is probably the Newar Bāḍā (Bare); 'vaida' means vaidya (physician), which fits a copy of a medical text. The colophon gives Patan as the scribe's residence ('vaṣnyā'), which is only assumed to be where he copied the text. 'jīvanasiṃha(!)' is marked by the cataloguer, but the reading seems sound.

notes: The era is not named, but samvat 964 fits Nepal Saṃvat (1844 CE), as the catalogue also takes it. The scribe's name appears as 'jiṇaratnamunina' (instrumental). The catalogue reads it as 'bajrācāryyamuni Jinaratna', i.e. it treats 'muni' as an epithet. The personal name may therefore be Jinaratna rather than Jinaratnamuni. title: Yogacandrikā
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: iti śrīmadbrahmajñānir vaṃśāvadaṃsadattasuta lakṣmaṇa viracitā yogacaṃdrikā samāptimagamat | 3 bālaya saṃjñake grāme 1 sadattetyādi | haridiśi prācyāṃ 2 ciraṃ caraketyāditāṃtrāṇI (!) śāstrāṇi || durgrarhagūṭhaṃ (!) || 3 || iti yogacaṃdrikāvilāsaḥ samāptaḥ ṭīpitamidaṃ pustakaṃ | ❁ (fol. 274r9–12)
notes: The excerpt is fragmentary. It contains numbered, riddle-like abbreviations ('sadattetyādi', 'caraketyādi', 'durgrarhagūṭhaṃ' = durgraha-gūḍham?), which suggest verses encoding names and places that the cataloguer did not quote in full. The catalogue gives the scribe as Veṇīdattapāṭhaka and the place as 'Vaijayaṃtī payovāhinī taṭinī devālayasaṃjñake grāme' (a village called Devālaya on the Vaijayantī river?). Neither appears in full in the quoted text. 'bālaya saṃjñake grāme' is probably the tail of 'devālaya-saṃjñake grāme'. The scribe is included only on the catalogue's authority. 'ṭīpitam' = 'written down / copied'. It is unclear whether the village is the copying place or the author's home. 'sadatta' might refer back to (Veṇī)datta or to the author's father Datta. No date is given.

Lowered Datta (p2) to low confidence. 'vaṃśāvadaṃsadattasuta' is probably a corrupt '-vaṃśāvataṃsa-datta-suta', so the father's name may be a longer name ending in -datta.

title: Yogataraṅgiṇī

Tithi '++daṃśyo(tithau)' has two lost akṣaras: most likely [trayo]daśyāṃ, possibly [catur]daśyāṃ. The weekday has not been checked against the tithi. 'śrīḥ++śubhasthāle' is probably the stock formula 'śubhasthāne' ('in an auspicious place'), not a toponym, so no place of copying is recorded. Kāśī is where the author composed the text, not where this copy was made. The catalogue names Loknātha as scribe, but that name is not in the quoted colophon (it may be elsewhere in the MS or lost in a lacuna), so no scribe entry was added. The title 'samaptaḥ' (!) is the cataloguer's flag of a grammatical error, not a name.

title: Rasasārakalpanāvidhi
subject: Āyurveda

colophon: iti śrī ḍaṇḍapāṇI (!) putra devānanda vaidyeṇa (!) viracitāyāṃ cikitsāsthāne rasasārakalpanā vidhir adhyāyaḥ samāptam (!) || ❁ || triambaraṃ śūnyamekagatābde jyeṣṭhe 3 site haritithau bhṛguvāsare ca || lipistviyaṃ mukuṭa ānandanena (!) || ||ślokasaṃkhyā 370 || (fol. 19r4–6)
notes: Chronogram tri (3) ambara (0) śūnya (0) eka (1), read right to left, gives 1003. The colophon names no era; the catalogue gives 'SAM 1003'. NS is inferred: Jyeṣṭha śukla ekādaśī of NS 1003 falls around 15 June 1883, which my rough calculation makes a Friday (bhṛguvāsara), so it fits. VS 1003 (946 CE) is implausible for a Devanāgarī paper manuscript. The '3' after 'jyeṣṭhe' is unclear: it may be a solar day, or a misread punctuation mark or abbreviation. 'site' = śukla pakṣa; 'haritithi' = ekādaśī. The scribe's name is corrupt: 'mukuṭa ānandanena' probably stands for mukuṭānandena (Mukuṭānanda), but the catalogue gives Ānandamukuṭa ('Ānaṇdamukuṭa'). Devānanda, son of Daṇḍapāṇi, is the author of the text, not someone involved in this copy.

title: Vārāccanakaumudī (Bījasarvasvapaṭala)
subject: Tantra
date_note: = Monday 17 Jan 1853, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: iti sāra saṃgrahe umāmaheśvara saṃvāde śrīvārāccana kaumudyāṃ bījasarvvasva paṭalaḥ || || śubham || || abde rāmādrivivare pauṣaśuklekṣapākare | saptamyāmalikhac cedaṃ dvijaḥ śrīnidhidevakaḥ || || | saṃvat 973 kārttika vadi 11 śrīdattareva gayāśrāddha ṣaḍdina pāsā bhājudhaṇ dvānyā bhājudhaṃ dvānyā bhājudhaṃ jamādāra strīpuruṣaṃ luja śubhaṃ | (fol. 3v2-4)
notes: The era is not stated in the verse. NS is inferred from the appended 'saṃvat 973' and the Newari script. The chronogram rāma(3)-adri(7)-vivara(9), read right to left, gives 973, which matches the appended entry. 'pauṣaśukle kṣapākare' means Pauṣa śukla on a Monday (kṣapākara = moon). The scribe is Śrīnidhideva ('-ka' is a diminutive suffix and 'dvija' his brahmin status), which agrees with the catalogue. The appended Newari line ('saṃvat 973 kārttika vadi 11 śrīdattareva gayāśrāddha ṣaḍdina pāsā bhājudhaṇ dvānyā bhājudhaṃ dvānyā bhājudhaṃ jamādāra strīpuruṣaṃ luja') looks like a separate later record of a six-day Gayā-śrāddha. It apparently involves Dattareva(?) and companions ('pāsā'), including bhāju Dhana and a jamādāra couple ('strīpuruṣa'). The text is repetitive (probably dittography) and only partly understood, so the persons from this line have unclear roles and are not connected with the copying. If Kārttika vadi 11 is taken in the amānta reckoning, it would fall before the NS year-change. So the note's year may be counted differently, or it was written about a year after the copy.

notes: The author's epithet 'kūrmācalākhaṇḍaladvāragīvāṇaguru' (read gīrvāṇa-, the MS has 'gīvāṇa') most likely means 'Sanskrit preceptor at the court (dvāra) of the lord (ākhaṇḍala) of Kūrmācala (Kumaon)'. The catalogue gives King Śrīpṛthvīpati Sāha Deva, but he does not appear in this colophon excerpt, so he is not recorded here. He may come from elsewhere in the MS or be a cataloguing error. The colophon closes only the first dhārā (prathamadhārā) of the Kumāraśakti.

title: yauvanollāsa
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti śrībhāsurānaṃdanāthacaraṇāraviṃdamiliṃdāyamānamānasenomānaṃdanāthena viracite kalpasūtrānusāriṇi nityotsave nibaṃdhe yauvanollāsasmṛtīyaḥ (!) saṃpūrṇaḥ || idaṃ pustakaṃ devasthalyupanāmakadhuṃḍhirājātmakagaṇeśasūriṇā kṛṣṇabhaṭṭasutalakṣmīnārāyaṇena likhitaṃ. || kive ity umanāmakasya(!) rājābhāu yasya gṛheṃduragrāmamadhye likhitaṃ || svārthaṃ ca parārthaṃ ca || (fol. 41v4-8)
notes: The text is Umānandanātha's Nityotsava. Bhāsurānandanātha is the initiatory name of Bhāskararāya, the author's guru; he had no part in this copy. 'mānasenomānaṃdanāthena' = mānasena + umānandanāthena. 'yauvanollāsasmṛtīyaḥ (!)' probably stands for 'yauvanollāsas tṛtīyaḥ'. 'umanāmakasya(!)' = upanāmakasya, so Kive (Kibe) is Rājābhāū's surname; the Kibe family was prominent in Indore. 'dhuṃḍhirājātmaka-' stands for -ātmaja-. Two people stand in the instrumental (Gaṇeśasūri, son of Dhuṇḍhirāja, surname Devasthalī, and Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa, son of Kṛṣṇabhaṭṭa) before a single 'likhitaṃ'. Their fathers differ, so they are two people. Gaṇeśa could be a co-scribe. Or 'gaṇeśasūriṇā' may be a slip for the genitive '-ṇaḥ', which would make him the owner of the book. The catalogue lists only Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa as scribe. No date is given.
review: p1 Bhāsurānandanātha: role 'teacher' → 'other' (he is the author's guru, not involved in producing this copy); noted identity with Bhāskararāya

p4 Gaṇeśa: confidence high → medium; the colophon has two instrumentals with one 'likhitaṃ', so co-scribe is one reading, but owner (gaṇeśasūriṇā for -ṇaḥ) is also possible; the catalogue names only Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa
p7 Rājābhāū: 'Kive' moved from affiliation to titles as a surname (upanāmaka); evidence trimmed
notes expanded: umanāmakasya = upanāmakasya; smṛtīyaḥ(!) probably = tṛtīyaḥ; dhuṃḍhirājātmaka- = -ātmaja-

title: Vījakoṣa
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Jun 1835, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: kṣa. iti varṇakośa (!) samāptaḥ || bhūdeva śrītīrtharājo vījakośaṃ (!) leleṣat (!) || varṇakośaṃ ca tad api racasya pāṭhārthahetukam || samvat 1892 miti āṣāḍavadi śubhaṃ bhūyāt || || || || (fol. 8v6–7)
purpose: svārtha: for his own study (pāṭhārtha), if 'racasya' = 'svasya'
notes: 'leleṣat (!)' is a corrupt form of 'lilekha'/'alekhat' (wrote). 'bhūdeva' means 'brahmin' and is kept as a title. 'racasya' is probably a corruption of 'svasya' (his own), so the scribe copied the Vījakoṣa and also the Varṇakośa for his own study. That reading is the basis for the 'owner' role, but it is a conjecture, and 'racayya' (having composed) is also possible. No tithi is given after 'āṣāḍavadi'. Taking VS 1892 as caitrādi, the dark half of Āṣāḍha falls around June–July 1835 CE. The catalogue's scribe and date fields agree with the colophon.

Normalised paksa to 'kṛṣṇa (vadi)'

title: Śyāmāsahasranāmastotra
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Wednesday 17 Mar 1847, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīrudrajāmalemahātaṃtre kārttikeyamahādevasaṃvāde trailokyavijayābhidhamaṃtragarbhaśyāmāsahasranāmastotraṃ samāptaṃ śubhaṃ || ❖ || iti saṃvat 967 sāla mi caitra śudi 1 roja 4 thukuhnu śrīgovindacaraṇa upādhyāṃ brahmapūrachesaconā coyāsidhayakā julo || svapna .. .. maṃtragarva śyāmāsahasranāma || phārguṇa vadi 11 ro 6 .. hnusa śakti na svapne thva saphū vilathva kuhnu mīnasaṃkrāṃtilāka vipana sadhīrjavīraṃ yāṃ svapna sathuguyā dhāla dhūktalā vāju Dhaka ukhunuṃ viya halaheyā tayā śrīkālīkāsuprasaṃnostu || śubham bhūyāditi śyāmāsahasranāma || ❁ || ❖ || ❖ || ❖ || (exp. 11 bottom, 4-9)
notes: The era is not named, but 'saṃvat 967 sāla' with a Newari colophon and a Newar Upādhyāya scribe points to Nepal Saṃvat, which gives about 1847 CE. 'brahmapūrachesa conā' means 'staying in the Brahmapūra house', and 'coyā sidhayakā julo' means 'finished writing'. A separate, corrupt Newari note follows, dated Phālguna vadi 11, ro 6 (Friday). It seems to say that Śakti gave this book in a dream ('śakti na svapne thva saphū vila') on the day of the Mīna-saṃkrānti. The phrase 'vipana sadhīrjavīraṃ yāṃ svapna' may hide a personal name, perhaps Dhīr(a)javīra, the person who had the dream. 'vāju' (father/elder) is also mentioned. The text is too uncertain to record either one as a person. The catalogue entry 'SAM 967' agrees with the colophon.

title: Ādyākālikākarpūrakavaca
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Thursday 26 Aug 1847, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrībrahmavidyāyāṃ catusahasralakṣagraṃthe śrīādyākālikāyāṃ karpurakavacaṃ navame dvitīyapaṭalasamāptaṃ || ❁ || śrīśāke saṃvat 1769 sāla śrāvaṇa śu di 15 roja 5 śrīgovindacaraṇaupādhyāyena liṣita idaṃ puṣṭakaṃ śubham || śrīkālikā suprasaṃnostu || vikramābda 1904 || naipālasaṃvat 967 śrīkālikāyā prasādena idaṃ puṣṭakaṃ likṣitaṃ śubham (exp. 50t, 3-7)
notes: The colophon gives the date in three eras, and they agree: Śaka 1769 (+78 = 1847), Vikrama 1904 (−57 = 1847) and Nepāla Saṃvat 967 (+880 = 1847). Śrāvaṇa śukla 15 falls in July/August 1847 CE. 'roja 5' is the fifth weekday, i.e. Thursday; I did not check it against an ephemeris. 'liṣita' and 'likṣitaṃ' are spellings of likhitam, and 'puṣṭakaṃ' of pustakam. The second statement ('śrīkālikāyā prasādena idaṃ puṣṭakaṃ likṣitaṃ') is an invocatory formula and does not add a second scribe. The catalogue's 'SAM 1769' is the Śaka year.

title: Varadagaṇeśasahasranāmāmṛta
subject: Stotra
colophon: iti śrīrudrayāmale mahārahasye śrīvaradagaṇeśasahasranāmāmṛta saṃpūrṇaṃ || ||❖ |||| || ❖ || || ❖ || vārāṇasyāṃ gaṇeśena likhitaṃ puṣpasaṃnidhau || sahasranāmam idaṃ stotraṃ pāvanaṃ paramaṃ śubhaṃ || 16 || (fol. 18v3-7)
notes: The only personal and place information is in the verse 'vārāṇasyāṃ gaṇeśena likhitaṃ puṣpasaṃnidhau || sahasranāmam idaṃ stotraṃ pāvanaṃ paramaṃ śubhaṃ || 16 ||'. Because it is numbered as verse 16 and praises the stotra, it may belong to the text or be a traditional closing verse, perhaps even naming the god Gaṇeśa as the writer. It is not clearly a scribe's statement about this copy, so the scribe and place are tentative. 'puṣpasaṃnidhau' ('near flowers/Puṣpa') is unclear; it may refer to a shrine or locality. The catalogue gives scribe Śrīkṛṣṇa Jośī and place Rāmanagara. These are not in the quoted colophon and probably come from elsewhere in the manuscript. Rāmnagar is opposite Vārāṇasī on the Ganges, so the two places fit together. The colophon gives no date.
review: Lowered confidence for Gaṇeśa as scribe from medium to low. The line 'vārāṇasyāṃ gaṇeśena likhitaṃ puṣpasaṃnidhau' is a numbered verse (|| 16 ||) that ends with praise of the stotra. It may be part of the text or a stock closing verse rather than a scribal colophon. It could also refer to the deity Gaṇeśa as the writer.
Made the place identification provisional in the notes: Vārāṇasī comes from the same doubtful verse.

Rewrote the notes. The catalogue's 'Rāmanagara' does not strictly contradict this: Rāmnagar lies just across the Ganges from Vārāṇasī. The catalogue's scribe Śrīkṛṣṇa Jośī probably comes from part of the manuscript that is not quoted here, so he was not added.

subject: Stotra

colophon: śākedṛk śaratarkkacandragalite śrīnīlakaṇṭhāṣṭakaṃ śrīmanmallajagajjayāvanipatir vyācaṣṭa pṛṣṭvā śivaṃ | etasmin paṭhite śrūte ca manujo jāyeta divye pade modetāpi ciraṃ paraṃ pariṇatau syāt tasya bhūpaḥ śivaṃ || || || iti nikhiladarśanavicāryamāṇapadārthasārthaniṣṭhāvijñānaparamacāturyyavāryyamāṇavividhabudhān adarpyasvarūpajitakandarpya śastrāstrapracāranaipūṇyāt kṛtākhilarājanyavaryyaparamaiśvaryyaśauryyodāryyadhūryyavitatayaśaḥ sudhākarasaṃgītādikalākalāparipūṇavaranepālādidharaṇīdharaparamadevodaya śrīśrīmanmallajagajjayaparamabhaṭṭārakaracitaṃ śrīmatkṛpāvannemunipradarśitavirūpākṣatīrthayātrāgatakrameṇa śrīmatkuśeśvaraprabhṛticatuḥṣaṣṭhiśivaliṅgānāṃ tathā śrīmataḥ paśupateḥ śrīmatyā bhagavatyā guhyeśvaryyās tathā śrīvajrayoginyā nīlakaṇṭhādeś ca varṇṇanaṃ samapūribhūri śubhadam idam astu pāṭhakānā || || ❖ || || || śrīman nepālapāla tvadamitabalador ddaṇḍacaṇḍapratāpas phūryyad vahnipratapte tvadahitanikare padmadāsī davehi | tatratyaṃ kīrttidugdhaṃ samuditam apatat prāñchalad bhatrabhūmau magnaṃ tejaḥ sudagdhaṃ payasi ca bhavataḥ kīrttihaṃsī papau tat || 1 || deva tvatkhaṇḍitākhaṇḍalabalavilasat kāṇḍako daṇḍanirjjā ccaṇḍāṃśūddāmadāroditavitatayaśaś candrapāraṃ śuvṛndaiḥ || viśvaṃ dīptaṃ tadetajjanapadajanuṣāṃ preyasīnāṃ śiro yad vāsaḥ śūnyaṃ tadīyāhitagatakuyaśāṃ sīva kinna vyanaktiṃ || || śrīviśvambharabhūsurendratanūyo nepālanākālayo bhāradvājakulārṇṇave sumudito vidyākalānānnidhiḥ | yatkīrttityujvalakaumudīspharatibhir ddigbhibhipaṣṭīkṛto yo mūrddhāstidhṛtaḥ prakāśan

title: Guhyakālīsahasranāma
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Jul 1762, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: ❖ saṃ 882 śrāvaṇaśuklapūrṇṇimā luhnu śrīmūṇiyā upākarmmasāśrī sirahmakāyana śrīguhyeśvarīyā sahasranāma śrībrāhma yāta dānaviyā juro śubhaṃ || || (exp. 2, 1–2)
purpose: dāna to a Brahmin at an Upākarma ceremony
notes: The Newari text records a gift of the Guhyeśvarīsahasranāma to a Brahmin (śrībrāhmayāta dānaviyā juro) on the occasion of the Upākarma of Muni (śrīmūṇiyā upākarmmasā) by the son of Sirahma (śrī sirahmakāyana). 'Sirahma' is likely a metathesis or colloquial spelling for Sīharāma/Siṃharāma, and 'kāyana' is the Newari ergative 'by the son'. The recipient 'śrībrāhma yāta' refers to a Brahmin generically and is not included as an individual person.

notes: The colophon gives only 'saṃvatsaraḥ 19 21', i.e. year 1921, with no era stated. It is read as VS because NS and ŚS are impossible for that number, which matches the catalogue's VS 1921 (≈1864 CE). The catalogue field 'King: Jaṅgabahādura' is not supported by the colophon, which names no persons. Jang Bahadur Rana was prime minister, not king, in 1864, so the cataloguer probably added the name from the date. He is therefore not listed as a person.
review: Era changed from 'unspecified' to VS. The colophon names no era, but 1921 can only be Vikrama: NS 1921 and ŚS 1921 would both fall in the future. ce_approx 1864 (1921−57) is kept and recorded as inferred.
Notes expanded: the era is inferred, and Jaṅgabahādura (Jang Bahadur Rana) comes only from the catalogue field.

notes: The date and scribe passage is an anuṣṭubh verse: '[mākhaṃṇḍe] māsi site pakṣe bhṛgu[ra]vāsarasaṃmite / jagaṃnāthena likhitaṃ pustakaṃ sādhakāptaye'. 'mākhaṃṇḍe' is corrupt. It may stand for Māgha, or it may be what is left of a year chronogram (bhūtasaṃkhyā). No year can be recovered, so the month is only tentative. 'bhṛguravāsara' should be read as bhṛguvāsara (Friday). Pūrṇānandanātha is named only in a homage ('namaḥ'). The -ānandanātha initiatory name in a Śrīvidyā text suggests he was the scribe's guru, but the colophon does not say so. He could also be a lineage figure, and possibly the well-known Tantric author Pūrṇānanda.

title: Narapatijayacaryāsvarodayaṭīkā
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Monday 25 May 1772, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: || iti tīrabhuktideśīyamāṇḍaragrāmīṇāgnipraveśāntapativrataśīlaratnadevī〈ta〉mahitamahāmahopādhyāyanarasiṃhātmajamiśraśrīnaraharikṛta narapaticayacaryyākhya svarodayaṭīkā samāptā || || śubhaṃ || || śrīśāke 1694 jyeṣṭha śudi24(!) likhitam idaṃ pustakaṃ kāśyapīyajayanārāyaṇaśarmmaṇā karbudānikaṭe tārakagrāmavāsī || || ❖ || a(!)(darśado)ṣān mativibhramād vā tva/// tadaśuddhacarṃ (!) kṣi(!)mantu santaḥ khalu lekhakasya || 1 || ------ khalu lekhakasya || 1 || rāmaḥ || (fol. 139r12–139v3)
notes: The tithi 'śudi 24' cannot be right (the cataloguer marks it with (!)). It may be a misreading of 2, 4 or 14. The Sanskrit compound describing Narahari's lineage is hard to parse. Ratnadevī, a faithful wife who died by entering the fire (agnipraveśānta-pativrata), is most likely Narasiṃha's wife and possibly Narahari's mother; 'mahita' (honoured) is uncertain because of the cataloguer's 〈ta〉. Tīrabhukti = Tirhut (Mithilā). The colophon gives only the scribe's residence, 'living in Tārakagrāma near Karbudā' (not identified). It does not say where the copy was made. The text title in the colophon is spelled 'narapaticayacaryyā' (for -jaya-). The cataloguer recorded the scribe's name as 'Jayanārāyaṇa Śarmā', which agrees with the colophon. The final verse is the standard scribe's request for pardon for errors.

title: Siddhāntasāriṇi
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Wednesday 23 Sep 1896, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: Kārttikādi, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: īti (!) kṣayamāsa sādhanam || || || 1818 samvat 1953 ā (!) śvinavadi 2 oja 1 śubham (fol. 5v12–13)
notes: The colophon names no persons. The first number, 1818, is unlabelled and read as Śaka 1818. 'samvat 1953' is VS 1953. Both give 1896 CE, so the eras agree. The catalogue's 'Date of Copying: SAM. 1818' takes the Śaka year as saṃvat, and if read as VS it would give a wrong date (1761 CE). 'oja 1' is probably 'roja 1' (Sunday), with the initial r- lost or misread. The weekday was not checked against an ephemeris; a rough check found no Sunday for Āśvina vadi 2 in September 1896 (pūrṇimānta), while an amānta reading (late October 1896) might fit, so this is uncertain. The catalogue's 'King: Udyotacandra of Kūrmāñcala' (Kumaon, late 17th c.) is not in the quoted colophon and cannot be the reigning king for an 1896 copy. He probably comes from the text's own context (e.g. patron of the author), so he is left out. The colophon closes the section 'kṣayamāsa sādhanam'.

date_note: = Wednesday 27 May 1801, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrībrahmavaivartte mahāpurāṇe prakṛtikhaṃḍe nārāyaṇanāradasaṃvāde durgopākhyāne prakṛteḥ kavacakathanaṃ nāma catuḥṣaṣṭitamo ʼdhyāyaḥ || || śubham astu śrīr astu || śrīśāke 1723 || jeṣṭā(!)dhikavāre 4 kāṃtipūrvaṃ likhitaṃ śubham śāke guṇe jaladair mite jyeṣṭā(!)dhike budhe tithau śaṃbhoḥ kāṃtipuryāṃ ya(!) padmānāthadvijāṃ likhat(!) || (fol. 185r3–7)
notes: The year is given only as the numeral ŚS 1723 (= c. 1801 CE). The verse chronogram 'śāke guṇe jaladair mite' is incomplete or corrupt. Guṇa = 3 fits the last digit, but the other digits are not recoverable: 'jaladaiḥ' is not a standard bhūtasaṃkhyā word, and the verse cannot confirm 1723. 'vāre 4' agrees with 'budhe' (Wednesday). 'śaṃbhoḥ tithau' most likely means caturdaśī, Śiva's tithi. The pakṣa is not stated. Whether Jyeṣṭha was intercalary (adhika) in ŚS 1723 has not been checked. 'kāṃtipūrvaṃ' is evidently an error for kāṃtipuryāṃ (Kathmandu). The scribe's name is written 'padmānātha' in the accusative with a corrupt verb ('ya ... likhat'). The stem is read as Padmanātha, which matches the catalogue's 'Padma Nātha'.

title: Skandapurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Wednesday 27 Mar 1591, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: year read as current
colophon: iti śrīskandapurāṇe sahyādrikhaṇḍe āmalīgrāmamāhātmye triraśītitamo dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || 83 || || śrīparaśurāmaprītir astu || yugmabhūśailaparipālitacaitraśuklo, nepālapattanavare kila bhaktasaṃle (!) | candrātmajānvitaturaṅgamabheṣusahyam (!) ,āyuridhīramadananta (!) guṇīndramukhyaiḥ || || imāṃ madīyāṃ................................ bhṛṣā vikalpaḥ || || śrībhavānī prīṇās tu || (fol. 226r6–226v6)
notes: The chronogram yugma (2), bhū (1), śaila (7), read right to left, gives NS 712, about 1592 CE (Caitra). The catalogue's 'Scribe: SAM 712' is really the date, wrongly entered in the scribe field. The second half of the verse ('...sahyam (!) āyuridhīramadananta (!) guṇīndramukhyaiḥ') is corrupt. It could be divided as 'āyur iha dhīra-madana-ananta-guṇīndra-mukhyaiḥ', meaning 'by [the wise?] Madana, Ananta, Guṇīndra and others'. The persons named in the instrumental would then be the agents of a lost verb, either copying or having the copy made, so their role is unknown. Only Guṇīndra is entered, with low confidence. Madana and Ananta are possible further names. 'turaṅgamabheṣu' is taken as the nakṣatra Aśvinī. 'iṣu' could also mean the number 5 (tithi pañcamī), but this reading is doubtful. The weekday was not checked against the calendar. The final verse ('imāṃ madīyāṃ ...') is lacunose, apparently a standard scribal apology.
review: Guṇīndra: role changed from 'commissioner' to 'other'. There is no causative verb such as likhāpitam, and the verb of the clause is lost in the corruption. Confidence stays low.
Notes: added that 'dhīramadananta' may contain more names (Madana, Ananta). It may also be the epithet 'dhīra' plus a name. These were not entered as persons because the reading is too uncertain.

Date: the chronogram yugma 2, bhū 1, śaila 7, read right to left, gives NS 712 = 1592 CE (Caitra). This is confirmed. Candrātmaja (Budha) = Wednesday and turaṅgama-bha = Aśvinī are kept. The tithi is not stated. Notes now say that 'iṣu' could also be read as the number 5, which would mean pañcamī, but this is doubtful.
Place: Bhaktapur kept. 'bhaktasaṃle' is probably a corruption of 'bhaktasaṃjñe' (the town called Bhakta[pur]).
Purpose: rephrased as the colophon's pious invocations (wishes), not a dedication of the copy.

(fol. 9r1–9v3)
purpose: svārtha: 'thava yata cvayākula' (Newari, 'written for myself'), with a curse on theft
notes: The colophon gives two scribal statements. (1) Nārāyaṇakṛṣṇa, younger brother of [T/Śr]īnārāyaṇakṛṣṇa and son of 'ā 3 dhārā', wrote it on Jyeṣṭha śukla pūrṇimā, a Tuesday, in saṃvat 975. The Newari note that follows says it was written for himself and calls down sin on anyone who steals it. (2) A final line says 'bhāju narasiṃhavaidyasya liṣtamidaṃ b', and the catalogue lists Narasiṃha Vaidya as the scribe. These two statements may conflict: Narasiṃha could be the actual scribe, a later copyist, or another name for the same person. 'trī-' is probably a misreading of 'śrī-', and if so both brothers are called Nārāyaṇakṛṣṇa, which is suspicious. 'liṣI ā 3 dhārāputra' is corrupt. The father's name is unclear, and 'Āśādhāra' is only a guess. The era is not stated ('saṃvat'), so NS is inferred from the Newari text and the catalogue: NS 975 is about 1855 CE. The weekday has not been checked.

The Newari 'thvakuhnu syāmasena coya dhunakā dina' means 'on this day Śyāma finished writing'. Here '-sena' is taken as the agentive ending, so the name is Śyāma, as the catalogue gives it. 'Śyāmasena' is a less likely alternative reading. The era is not stated, but 'samvat 820' in a Newari colophon is Nepāla Saṃvat. NS 820 Māgha kṛṣṇa 12 falls in early 1700 CE (January–February). The yoga 'suddi' (catalogue: 'sudhi') is corrupt. The best guess is siddhi; no yoga named śuddhi exists.
review: Name corrected from 'Śyāmasena' to 'Śyāma': in 'syāmasena coya dhunakā' the '-sena' is the ergative/instrumental ending (Newari colophon usage modelled on Skt. -ena) attached to the agent of 'coya' (wrote). This agrees with the catalogue's 'Śyāma'. Confidence lowered to medium.
Weekday normalized to 'somavāra' (Monday); nakshatra/yoga normalized to Uttarabhādrapadā and 'suddi' read as probably siddhi.

title: Nāsiketupākhyāna
subject: Kathā
date_note: = Sunday 3 Oct 1632, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti śrīnāsiketopākhyāne śubhāṃśubhaṃ (!) kṛtaṃ karmajanmaṃ (!) ca bhāvavarṇano nāmāṣṭādaśoddhyāya (!) || 18 || saṃvat || 1689 || liṣyataṃ kārttika vadi paṃcami (!) || guruvāre vṛhasyapati (!) || kaṣṭasuṃ likhitaṃ || || || || (fol. 61v7–9)
notes: The catalogue lists 'Bṛhaspati' as scribe, but in the colophon 'vṛhasyapati (!)' comes right after 'guruvāre'. It is almost certainly the same Thursday given again as bṛhaspati(vāra), not a scribe's name. If it were a scribe's name, the attribution would be low confidence. 'Saṃvat' in a Devanagari MS with the Hindi-type phrasing 'liṣyataṃ' and 'kaṣṭasuṃ likhitaṃ' ('written with difficulty') suggests VS, so 1689 VS ≈ 1632 CE. The weekday has not been verified.
review: Removed p1 'Bṛhaspati' as scribe: 'guruvāre vṛhasyapati' is most naturally the weekday given twice (guruvāra = bṛhaspativāra, Thursday). It is not a personal name, and the colophon names no scribe. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Bṛhaspati' looks like a misreading, recorded in notes.
Weekday given as 'guruvāra (= bṛhaspati[vāra])'.
Corrected the note on 'kaṣṭasuṃ likhitaṃ': 'suṃ' is the Hindi/Rajasthani postposition 'sũ' ('with'), so the phrase means 'written with difficulty'. It is not a corruption of 'kaṣṭena'.

title: Svasthānīvratakathā
subject: Kathā
date_note: = Wednesday 20 Jan 1610, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: year + 1, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrīriṅgaṃ(!)purāṇe,, svasthānaiparamaiśvaryyā(!) vratakathā samāptaḥ(!) || jatra(!)ditvā(!) tatra rīkhita(!)mama ṣo(!)na diyate(!) | śrī 2 jaggatrayeti malla deva vijayarāje || śubha || samvat 730 paukhakṛṣṇa ekādaśyāyā tithau ādita(!)vāsare | gopāla siṃharīkhita(!)|| (fol.27r3-27v1)
notes: The king's name 'jaggatrayeti malla deva' is corrupt. The most likely reading is Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur, but his reign is usually dated c. 1613/14–1637, a few years after NS 730 (1609/10), when Trailokyamalla was still ruling Bhaktapur. Jagattraya ('three worlds') means the same as trailokya, so a garbled 'Trailokyamalla' cannot be ruled out. Either the date is misread, the colophon names Jagajjyotirmalla while he was a co-ruler or crown prince, or the name stands for another king. 'jatra(!)ditvā(!) tatra rīkhita(!) mama ṣo(!)na diyate(!)' is the standard scribal formula 'yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā / mama doṣo na dīyate'. 'riṅgaṃ(!)purāṇe' stands for Liṅgapurāṇe. 'siṃha' is kept as part of the scribe's name.

That makes him the person the copy was made for, possibly its commissioner or owner. However, the colophon's Sanskrit is substandard (hāvali for hārāvalī, likhita for likhitā), so the dative may have been used loosely for an agent. That would make Tīrtharāja the scribe, as the catalogue says. No scribe is named otherwise. 'puruśottama' is read as Puruṣottamadeva, the grammarian and lexicographer, author of the Hārāvalī. 'praṇītāhārāvalī' is read as praṇītā hārāvalī. The colophon has no date. The invocation of Rāmacandra, Saṅkaṭā, Hanumān and others suggests a late copy, but nothing more can be said.

title: Kāśīmāhātmya
subject: Purāṇa
colophon: iti śrībrahmavaivartte purāṇe tṛtīyavibhāge rahasyātirahasye kāśīmahātmye ṣaḍviṃśo dhyāyaḥ 26 || śrīrāma likhitaṃ motirāma vidyārathi(!)putrasya haranārāyaṇa || (fol. 161v8–9)
notes: 'śrīrāma' at the start is an invocation, not a name. 'vidyārathi(!)' is very likely a corruption of vidyārthī 'student', describing Motirāma, and not a father's name. 'putrasya haranārāyaṇa' has broken syntax. The reading used here is '[copy] of [his] son Haranārāyaṇa', i.e. written by the student Motirāma for his son Haranārāyaṇa. Another possible reading is 'Motirāma, son of Haranārāyaṇa', with a Hindi-style misplaced genitive. In that case Haranārāyaṇa would be Motirāma's father (relative_only), the relation would be p1 son_of p2, and the owner role would go. The catalogue gives the scribe as '??'. The colophon is undated.
review: Removed 'Vidyārathi' as a separate person: vidyārathi(!) = vidyārthī 'student', an epithet of the scribe Motirāma ('likhitaṃ motirāma vidyārthī'), now in his titles
Haranārāyaṇa: the son relation now points to Motirāma (putrasya = 'of [his] son'), and the owner role is kept at low confidence; an alternative reading is given in notes
Dropped the son_of relation to the non-person 'Vidyārathi'
Lowered the confidence of the Haranārāyaṇa identification

title: Brahmavaivartapurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Saturday 1 Apr 1837, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: year + 1, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrībrahmavaivartte mahāpurāṇe nārāyaṇanāradasaṃvāde gaṇeśakhaṇḍe tulasīgaṇapatisaṃvādo nāma ṣaṭcatvāriṃśo ʼdhyāyaḥ 46 || śrīśāke 1759 caitrakṛṣṇa 11 gurau devadattena lekhayo(!) (fol. 88r6–7)
notes: 'lekhayo(!)' is corrupt (marked by the cataloguer). It could stand for likhitam/lekhitam, which would make Devadatta the scribe. It could also be a causative form (lekhāpitam/lekhayitam, from the stem lekhaya-), which would make him the commissioner. Or it could be Nepali 'lekhyo' ('wrote'). The instrumental 'devadattena' fits either reading. Scribe is the preferred role, but commissioner is possible. Date: ŚS 1759 + 78 = 1837 CE. Caitra kṛṣṇa 11 falls around March/April 1837, depending on whether months are counted amānta or pūrṇimānta. This agrees with the catalogue's ŚS 1759. This colophon closes adhyāya 46 of the Gaṇeśakhaṇḍa, so it may be an internal section colophon rather than the final one.
review: Devadatta: confidence lowered from high to medium. 'lekhayo(!)' is corrupt. It may stand for likhitam (scribe), for a causative lekhāpitam/lekhayitam (commissioner), or for Nepali 'lekhyo' (wrote). Scribe is kept as the most likely role, and the ambiguity is now in notes.
Weekday changed from 'gurau' to 'Thursday (guru)'.
Notes expanded to cover the ambiguity and the date check.

subject: Kāvya
colophon: iti śrimahārāṣṭrakulāvataṃsaciraṃ tanamorvaṇīkaropanāmaka kiṃcit kāla janita vāṃdhavakaropaṇāmaka śrimat samastaśāstrapārāvārapāraṃgamadīkṣia ṭhuḍhirārātmajasāhityaśāstrapārāvārapārīṇakavitākāṃtāra kaṃṭhīravasarvakhadānadīkṣāviakṣaṇa śrīvad dīkṣitavālakṛṣṇatanūjanmaśaṃkaradīkṣitaviracite gaṃgāvataraṇacaṃpūpravaṃdhe gaṃgācaraṃākaḥ saptama ucchāsaḥ || saptamoyaṃgraṃtha || || (fol. 64r4-8)

Śaṅkara was the son of Bālakṛṣṇa Dīkṣita and grandson of Ḍhuṇḍhirāja Dīkṣita, from a Mahārāṣṭrian family (18th century). No scribe, owner, date or place of copying is given. Corrupt readings: 'ṭhuḍhirā' stands for Ḍhuṇḍhirāja, 'dīkṣia' for dīkṣita, 'tanamorvaṇīkara' for ciraṃtana-Morvaṇīkara, and 'vāṃdhavakara' for Bāndhavakara. 'gaṃgācaraṃākaḥ' is probably a corruption of the chapter title and is uncertain.

notes: Newari colophon: 'Sumatijayajitāmitramalla had this book made, at the time when Bhāgirāma was pramāṇa (paramāna = chief minister)'. 'Sumati-jaya-' is the regnal prefix of Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur (r. c. NS 793–816), so it is treated as part of the name and not as a title. The colophon names no scribe; the catalogue's 'Scribe: Bhāgirāma ?' is a misreading, and its 'Donor' field should read commissioner. Bhaktapur as residence comes from the known identity of the king and is not stated in the colophon. NS 810 Kārttika śukla 9 ≈ October/November 1689 CE.
review: p1: 'sumati' is not a title but part of the regnal name (Sumatijaya- prefix of the Bhaktapur kings); name normalized to the standard Jitāmitramalla, titles emptied; roles commissioner + king kept (dayakā = caused to be made; not 'donor' as in the catalogue)
p2: Bhāgirāma's role changed from 'other' to 'minister'; title 'paramāna' given as pramāṇa (chief minister); 'yāvelasa' = 'at the time when (he was pramāṇa)'. He is not the scribe (catalogue's guess)
relation p2→p1 changed from under_reign_of to servant_of (minister of the king)
date: ce_approx corrected to 1689 (Kārttika śukla of NS 810 falls in Oct/Nov 1689); paksa normalized to śukla

notes: Date conflict: the quoted colophon (exp. 161b) reads śrīśāke 1413 (≈1491/92 CE), but the catalogue field gives ŚS 1513 and ŚS 1514. The second colophon (exp. 173b, after Bhoja's Vidvajjanavallabha) reads śrīśāke 1514 idaṃ postakaṃ liṣi(tam) (≈1592 CE). Since 1513 and 1514 are consecutive years, '1413' may be a slip in the cataloguer's quotation and the first part may date to ŚS 1513 (≈1591 CE). The image should be checked. 'vipraḥja (!) jyotiṣI odaṃ postakaṃ || sūnunā prītikareṇa …' is corrupt. It probably means 'this book of the brahmin astrologer (jyotiṣī), written by his son Prītikara', so the father would be an unnamed astrologer and possibly the owner. Prītikara may be identical with the jyotiṣī himself. 'kalaguṇālaṃkṛta' after a lacuna is probably part of a lost epithet. The scribe of the ŚS 1514 colophon is not named; the lacuna (liṣi///) may hide the name.

title: Lagnacandrikā
subject: Jyautiṣa
date_note: = Sunday 26 Jan 1890, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: || iti śrī kāśināthakṛtau lagnacaṃdrīkāyāṃ samāptaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ śubhamastu bhuyāta(!) || || śāke 1711 saṃvat 1846 nepāla saṃvat 909 maghumāse vidyauvāre ṣaṣṭI ṛkṣe ca niriti -------- || likhitaṃ śrīkṛṣṇaṃ nāmaṃ graṃthaṃ ca paścine(!) || tadgrāme nāma likhitaṃ pustakaṃ mayāt || 3 || yādṛśṭaṃ ------ parameśvara || 5 || śrīśāradāyai namaḥ || || (fol. 36v4–11)
notes: The colophon gives three eras: ŚS 1711, VS 1846 and NS 909. ŚS 1711 and VS 1846 agree: the Māgha in those years falls in Jan/Feb 1790 CE. NS 909 started in Kārttika 1788, so a Māgha in NS 909 would fall in early 1789. This leaves a one-year conflict, and I followed ŚS and VS. The catalogue's 'ŚS 1811(!)' is an error for 1711. No pakṣa is stated, and the weekday was not checked by calculation. Scribe: the text reads 'likhitaṃ śrīkṛṣṇaṃ nāmaṃ'. Śrī is taken as an honorific here, giving the name Kṛṣṇa, but the catalogue's Śrīkṛṣṇa could be the full name. Place: the catalogue's 'Viṣṇumatyāpūrvabhailagrāma' (a village east of the Viṣṇumatī) is not in the quoted text. The text only has 'paścine(!) ... tadgrāme', which may be 'paścime' (to the west), and there are lacunae marked with dashes. The cataloguer may have read the place in the omitted part, so the place field is left empty. The verses after the scribe's name are the usual stock scribal formulas.

title: Laghujātakamūla
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Sunday 8 Feb 1959, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrī varāha mihirācārya racitelaghujātake naṣṭa jātakādhyāyo trayodaśa || khakhākaiḥ(!) ślokai saṃpūrṇaṃ laghujātakaṃ 900 || śrī śubham ----- vidvajjana sabhādhīraraṃganātha tanūjaneḥ(!) || daivajña vālakṛṣṇasya sūnunā bhānu śarmaṇā || 2 || nabho gajadhṛti miteśake vikrama bhūpateḥ || māghe māsi site pakṣe pakṣatyāṃ ravi vāsare ------- /// (fol. 33v3–33r5)
notes: The chronogram nabhas (0), gaja (8), dhṛti (18), read right to left, gives 1880. 'śake vikrama bhūpateḥ' names the era of King Vikrama, so this is VS 1880, not ŚS 1880 as the catalogue says. 'śaka' here just means 'era'. VS 1880 corresponds to 1823/24 CE. Māgha śukla pratipad of that year falls in Jan/Feb 1824 CE. The colophon breaks off after the date ('------- ///'), so the verb that would make Bhānuśarman the scribe is lost. Even so, the verse with the instrumental 'bhānu śarmaṇā' almost certainly names the copyist. 'vidvajjanasabhādhīra' is an epithet of Raṅganātha, not a title. 'khakhākaiḥ ślokai' (= 900 ślokas, read right to left) is the extent of the text, not a date. 'tanūjaneḥ(!)' is a mistake for 'tanūjanuṣaḥ'/'tanūjasya' ('son of'), and agrees with 'vālakṛṣṇasya'.

colophon: || iti śrī manorathācārya suta maheśvara viracite vṛttaśataṃ samāptaṃ || || ravākṣi(!)vargayute rudraghane śākerkaraśmibhiḥ || śuṣkekusarite kālehyamāryomalikhadvudhaḥ || || samāptaṃ śubhambhūyāt || || śrī manmaṅgalamūrttipadābjaṃ jayati || || śubhaṃ || (fol. 9r9–10)
notes: The dating verse is an anuṣṭubh: 'ravākṣi(!)vargayute rudraghane śāke 'rkaraśmibhiḥ | śuṣke kusarite kāle hy amāryo 'likhad budhaḥ'. Its first pāda is one syllable short. 'rudraghana' = 11³ = 1331, to which the square of the number in 'ravākṣi(!)' is added. The candidate readings give very different years. If akṣi = 2 alone, 1331 + 4 = ŚS 1335 (c. 1413 CE). If rāma-akṣi = 23, 1331 + 529 = ŚS 1860 (c. 1938 CE). If rasa-akṣi = 26, 1331 + 676 = ŚS 2007 (too late). The year is therefore left undetermined. 'śāke' marks the era as Śaka. 'arkaraśmibhiḥ śuṣke kusarite kāle' describes the hot season (rivers dried by the sun's rays) and is not part of the number. The scribe's name 'hy amāryo' is doubtful. It could be a corruption, e.g. of 'amātyo' (a minister), in which case no personal name is given. 'budhaḥ' ('the learned one') is an epithet. 'maṅgalamūrti' in the closing invocation is a deity (Gaṇeśa) and is not recorded as a person.
review: Date: parsed the chronogram. 'rudraghane' = 11³ = 1331, to which the square (varga) of an uncertain number is added; 'ravākṣi(!)' is corrupt, so the year is left unresolved and ce_approx stays empty. Possible readings are given in notes.

Date: removed 'śāke 'rkaraśmibhiḥ śuṣke kusarite kāle' from the year. It describes the season (rivers dried by the sun's rays, i.e. the hot season) and is not part of the number. The verse is restructured accordingly.
Scribe p3: kept as low confidence. 'budha' moved out of titles: it is an epithet ('the learned one'), not a caste or office title. Evidence string corrected to match the colophon.

colophon: || śārāvalyāṃmuccanīcasvatrikoṇa mitrāri bhavanādhyāyaḥ || || || śubhaṃ || śrīśāke 1647 māse 12 tithau 7 vāre 2 likhitamidaṃ gṛhītamidaṃ vā parahastā cakrapāṇI śarmaṇāsudhiyā śubham || vanhivāṇa nayanamitāḥ 253 sārāvalyāṃ suniścitā ślokāḥ || vāṇananda nayanamitāḥ 295 ślokāśchandairanuṣṭupāsaṃkhyā || || (fol. 7r12–14)
notes: The catalogue field says ŚS 1674, but the colophon reads śāke 1647 (the digits look swapped in the catalogue). ŚS 1647 + 78 = 1725 CE. The month is only given as a number (12), and the pakṣa is not stated. If months are counted from Caitra, month 12 is Phālguna, which would put the date in about Feb–Mar 1726 CE. Weekday 2 is probably Monday. The colophon reads 'likhitamidaṃ gṛhītamidaṃ vā parahastā(t) cakrapāṇiśarmaṇā sudhiyā': Cakrapāṇi either copied the MS himself or obtained it from someone else. So he is clearly the owner, but he may not be the scribe. 'sudhiyā' (sudhī, 'the wise') is a descriptive word, not a title. The two bhūtasaṃkhyā phrases are verse counts, not dates: vahni(3)-bāṇa(5)-nayana(2) = 253 ślokas in the Sārāvalī, and bāṇa(5)-nanda(9)-nayana(2) = 295 in the anuṣṭubh metre. Both are read correctly.

colophon: || iti śrīmahābhārate śatasāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyāsikyāṃ eṣīkaparvaṇI navamodhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || 9 || || śreyostu || śaśisāgarakāṃkeʼsminmārge kṛṣṇe tithau hareḥ | eṣīkaparvavyalikhadrāmaśaṃkaraśarmakaḥ || || || śubhaṃ bhūyāt || samvat 939 vaiśāṣa vadi 5 thvakunhukao didayakādinajulo || || śubhaṃ || || || || (fol. 9v7–9)
notes: The chronogram is śaśi = 1, sāgara = 4, aṅka = 9. Read right to left this gives 941. 'Hareḥ tithi' = ekādaśī. The verse gives no era. NS is assumed because the colophon also has a Newari line, so this is ca. Nov/Dec 1820 CE. If sāgara is taken as 7, the year would be 971. A second date, 'samvat 939 vaiśāṣa vadi 5', follows with a Newari phrase 'thvakunhukao didayakādinajulo', which is unclear: perhaps 'on this day ... was given/completed'. That would be NS 939 ≈ April/May 1819 CE, which is before the chronogram year 941, so the two dates conflict. Either the chronogram or the numeral is a misreading, or the note records a different event. The catalogue's 'VS 923' matches neither date and is probably wrong.
review: Chronogram śaśi(1)-sāgara(4)-aṅka(9) read right to left gives 941, not 939; the verse dates the copying (vyalikhat) to year 941, Mārgaśīrṣa kṛṣṇa, Hari's tithi (ekādaśī = 11). Primary date changed to 941 Mārga kṛṣṇa 11, era not stated but most likely NS (ca. 1820 CE).
The prose date 'samvat 939 vaiśāṣa vadi 5' is attached to a Newari note (thvakunhu ... dina julo) and is now recorded in notes as a separate or conflicting date, not as the copying date.
Notes expanded: 939 comes before 941, and the catalogue's VS 923 does not match either date.

title: Khaṇḍapraśasti
subject: Itihāsa
colophon: || iti śrī hanumadviracitā daśāvatārastutiḥ khaṇḍapraśastiḥ samāptāsīt || || yasyāsti putrodvipavakravakro vighnasya nāśetasoʼrka govat || śambhornagayomalikhadvije śrī tvimanyākhya bhaṭṭogatabhūmidaivaḥ || (fol. 18v4–6)
notes: The scribal verse is badly corrupt. 'yasyāsti putro dvipavaktravaktro vighnasya nāśe...' describes Gaṇeśa, the elephant-faced son of Śambhu who destroys obstacles; it is an invocation, not a person. 'śambhor nagayom alikhad' perhaps means '(he) wrote at Śambhu's ...'. 'nagayo' may hide a place or temple name, but it cannot be identified. The scribe's name, 'śrī tvimanyākhya bhaṭṭo', is uncertain: it may stand for Abhimanyu, Trimalla or a name in -manyu. 'gatabhūmidaivaḥ' probably contains bhūmideva ('brahmin'). Hanumat, the legendary author ('śrī hanumadviracitā'), is left out as a mythical figure. No date, place or purpose is given.
review: Scribe reading kept (Tvimanya, bhaṭṭa, low confidence); evidence trimmed to the substring that actually names him

Notes expanded: the first half of the verse describes Gaṇeśa, the elephant-faced son of Śambhu who destroys obstacles, and is invocatory, not a person; 'nagayom' may conceal a place or temple of Śambhu; 'gatabhūmidaivaḥ' probably means bhūmideva, i.e. brahmin

The era should be checked against the physical description of the manuscript.

The king reigning in 1888 was Pṛthvī Vīra Vikrama Śāha, and he is not mentioned either. ŚS 1809 + 78 = 1887, but Māgha śukla 10 of that year falls in January/February 1888 CE. It could also be a formulaic invocation of Viṣṇu Padmanābha, so the confidence is medium. The work is a Sauramata (astral) text, the Ratnadīpaka/Ratnadīpikā.

colophon: śrīmannepālavarṣe viśiṣayugaśare phālguṇe māsakṛṣṇe pañcamyāḥ anvabādhe’śvaragurusvadine vajrayoge ‘timukho | rāmāṇāṃ jīvabhūtaḥ kusumaśarasamo bhāti gobhāmadāyāḥ so yaṃ śrīrāmagupto likhitadṛḍhamatiḥ śāstra svarggāvarohaṃ || || ādiṣṭam iṣṭapatreṣu dṛṣṭvā tu tvaritena ca | vṛddhihīnākṣaran tatra bahavas santi patrake || śodhitu naiva śaknomi medhāvī bālyakena ca | śodhyatāṃ vibudhais sarvaiḥ yathāśuddhaṃ tathā kuru || || śubham astu sarvvajagatām iti || || (fol. 41r) rājādhirāja-śrīśrīmajjagajjyotimalladevavijayarājye || mahāmātraśrīrājasiṃhadevaḥ | mahāmātraśrīnāthasiṃhadeva etayoḥ śirobhūtaprastāvakṣaṇe || likhitaṃ saṃpūrṇṇaṃ kṛtam iti || (fol. 41v)
notes: Chronogram 'viśiṣayugaśare' = viśikha (arrow, 5) + yuga (4) + śara (5), read right to left = NS 545 (1424/25 CE), as the catalogue says. 'viśiṣa' is a slip for viśikha. The colophon falls into two parts. The first (verse colophon with the NS 545 date and the scribe Rāmagupta) cannot belong to the reign of Jagajjyotirmalla (Bhaktapur, c. NS 733-757 / 1613-1637 CE), who is named in the second part (fol. 41r-41v) together with the mahāmātras Rājasiṃhadeva and Nāthasiṃhadeva ('etayoḥ śirobhūtaprastāvakṣaṇe'). The likeliest explanation is that the NS 545 colophon of the exemplar was copied over, and that the present Maithili copy was made under Jagajjyotirmalla (c. 1613-1637). In that case Rāmagupta is the scribe of the exemplar, not of this copy, and the scribe of this copy is unnamed. A miscomputed chronogram is less likely. 'anvabādhe'śvaragurusvadine' is corrupt: 'guru' gives Thursday. 'gobhāmadāyāḥ' in the praise of the scribe is unclear and possibly corrupt (a mother's name or a place?). It is left unidentified. The -deva of the two mahāmātras may be honorific rather than part of their names.

title: Bhagavadgītā
subject: Vedānta
date_note: = Monday 10 Apr 1843, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrībhagavatgī(1)tāsūpaniṣatsu brahmavidyāyāṃ yogaśāstre śrī(2)kṣṛṇārjunasaṃvāde mokṣayogonāmāṣṭādaśo(3)dhyāyaḥ || 18 || samāptoyaṃ śrībhagavadgītāśā(4)stram || śrīśubham astu sarvajagatām || (5) tat sat saṃvat || 1900 || caitra śruti(6)vatadaṃśāṃ (!) śubham || (fol. 124r6 &124v1–6)
notes: The colophon names no scribe, commissioner, owner or king. The era is not stated ('saṃvat'). VS is assumed from the Devanagari script, the late date, and the catalogue's 'SAM 1900'. Caitra VS 1900 falls around March–April 1843. The day string 'śrutivatadaṃśāṃ (!)' is corrupt. The most likely reading is '…daśamyāṃ' (tenth tithi), with a pakṣa word (śudi/vadi) garbled in 'śrutiva(ta)'. Another possibility is that 'śruti' is a number word (= 4), which would make the tithi caturthī. The tithi is therefore uncertain and the pakṣa is left blank.
review: No changes to persons, relations, place or purpose: none are named, and the colophon gives no copying place or purpose.
Date kept as VS 1900 Caitra = c. 1843 CE. The era is only 'saṃvat', and VS is inferred. NS 1900 is impossible. ŚS 1900 (= 1978 CE) is unlikely for this manuscript.
Notes expanded on the corrupt tithi string: other readings are possible, and no pakṣa can be recovered.

notes: The colophon gives two dates that agree: Śāka 1752 (+78 = 1830) and '1887 sāla', which is Vikrama Saṃvat (−57 = 1830). This places the copy in about August–September 1830 CE. The scribe's name 'tilocanda' is flagged (!) by the cataloguer. It could be a corrupt form of Tilocana/Trilocana, or a vernacular name such as Tilokcand. 'upādhyā(!)armaṇe(!)' stands for upādhyāya-śarmaṇe. The dative ending would strictly mean 'written for him'. It is taken here, as by the cataloguer, as a slip for the instrumental (written by him), so he is recorded as scribe. The place was a kacaharī (revenue office) village at Rangeli near the Bakraha (Vakrāhā) river, in Vijayapur, Morang.
review: Scribe confidence lowered to medium: the name 'tilocanda(!)' is flagged by the cataloguer (possibly Tilocana/Trilocana), and 'śarmaṇe' is grammatically dative ('for'), not instrumental ('by'). It is read as a slip for śarmaṇā, so the role stays scribe, but this is uncertain.

title: Haritālikāpūjāvidhi
subject: Karmakāṇḍa

colophon: iti haritālikāśivapūjā samāptaṃḥ(!) || aṣṭḥā(!)daśāṃkeṃduśāke māse madhau stathā(!) mūlakṣye(!) bhaṃ || yogavyatiś ca navami(!) asitās(!)tathā bhavanāthadvijaskasya(!) likhitaṃ saumyavāsare || 1 || śubham (fol. 7v8-9
notes: The chronogram aṣṭādaśa (18) + aṅka (9) + indu (1) is to be read left to right as ŚS 1891. With the usual right-to-left rule it would give ŚS 1918 (1996 CE), which is very likely too late for an A-series NGMCP reel. ŚS 1891 checks out astronomically: Caitra kṛṣṇa navamī counted pūrṇimānta (the dark half after Phālguna pūrṇimā, 4 March 1969) falls on 12 March 1969, a Wednesday (saumya = Budha). That day the Moon was in mūla and the yoga was vyatīpāta (sidereal Sun about 327° + Moon about 249° ≈ 216°). This agrees with the catalogue's tentative '1891?'. The pūrṇimānta month naming suggests a Maithili scribe. The scribe's name is corrupt: 'bhavanāthadvijaskasya' is probably for bhavanāthadvijasya, or dvijakasya with a -ka suffix. This does not affect the name Bhavanātha. 'yogavyatiś' = vyatīpāta yoga; 'mūlakṣye bhaṃ' = mūlarkṣe bham (nakṣatra mūla).

notes: The year is in the Śālivāhana Śaka era: ŚS 1806 + 78 = 1884 CE. In the amānta reckoning, Vaiśākha kṛṣṇa 13 falls around late May 1884. In the pūrṇimānta reckoning it falls around late April 1884. Only a rough check was made: the stated Wednesday seems to fit late April better, but neither date has been verified. 'vakṣagotrāya' is probably corrupt for 'vatsagotrāya'. Also, 'gotrāya' is dative while 'kṛṣṇalālaśarmaṇaḥ' is genitive. The phrase can be read as 'book written by Kṛṣṇalāla Śarman' (scribe, which is how the catalogue reads it) or as 'book (written for and) belonging to Kṛṣṇalāla Śarman of the Vatsa gotra' (owner). Both roles are recorded and confidence is medium.

title: Devyāparādhakṣ[a]māpana
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Sunday 7 Sep 1919, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti devyāparādhakṣemāpanam (!) || || || || || || || || samāptaṃ caṃḍikāstavaṃ śubhaṃ bhavatu lekhakapāṭhayoḥ (!) || || śāke rūpayugāṣṭabhūparimite bhādre siterke harau dvādaśyāṃ bhṛguvāsare śaśadhare raudre gate gīṣpatau || puṣye śrīja〈〈ga〉〉daṃbikāstavam idaṃ trivikrame rājake gaurīdattadvijo lilekha matimān bhoraṣṭāreka (!) ? || 1 || śubham bhavatu || || (fol. 92v5–7)
notes: The chronogram is rūpa 1, yuga 4, aṣṭa 8, bhū 1. Read right to left this gives 1841, and the era is stated as śāke: ŚS 1841 = 1919 CE. 'siterke harau' is read as sita (= śukla) + arke harau (sun in Siṃha), which fits Bhādra. In 1919 Jupiter was in sidereal Cancer (Puṣya), which supports the ŚS reading. 'śaśadhare raudre' would put the moon in Ārdrā, which is astronomically odd for śukla dvādaśī; the cataloguer may have quoted it wrongly. 'trivikrame rājake' is taken as a reference to Vāmana/Trivikrama-dvādaśī (Bhādra śukla 12), not to a reigning king. If it did name a ruler (e.g. a Trivikrama Sen), the year would have to be VS (1784 CE), but Jupiter's position argues against that. The catalogue's scribe field 'Gaurīdatta Trivikramarāja' is a misreading of this phrase. 'bhoraṣṭāreka (!)' is corrupt, so its meaning is uncertain (a place name, or the end of a verse).
review: Removed p2 'Trivikrama' as king: Bhādra śukla dvādaśī is Vāmana-dvādaśī, the festival of Trivikrama (Viṣṇu), so 'trivikrame rājake' most likely refers to that day (perhaps a corruption of 'rājati'), not to a ruler. The relation under_reign_of was removed too.
nakshatra_yoga: Puṣya refers to Jupiter (gate gīṣpatau puṣye), not to the moon; the moon is said to be 'raudre' (Ārdrā?). Field rewritten.
Notes: the VS 1784 alternative was dropped as unlikely. In 1919 Jupiter stood in sidereal Cancer (Puṣya); in 1784 it did not. ŚS 1841 = 1919 CE is kept.
Place is now marked as doubtful: 'bhoraṣṭāreka' is corrupt and may not be a place name at all.

date_note: ≈ 1929 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti mārkaṃḍeyapurāṇe sāvarṇike manvaṃtare devimāhātmye (!) surathavaiśyayor varapradānaṃnāma trayadasodhyāyaḥ (!) || 13 || (fol. 53v5–6) uvāca || śrīsāke (!) 1854 śrīsamvat 1986 sāla kauṃḍinye (!) gograsya sadāśivasavarṇaprapautrāyaḥ (!) suta (!) śrīkāṃtasarmaṇa (!) prauyaḥ (!) suta (!) bālakṛṣṇaḥ (!) putrāyaḥ (!) sutaḥ || hariṣṇa (!) sarmaṇa (!) putrāyaḥ (!) suteḥ (!) || devadattapādhyā (!) pyākuralapustakaṃ liṣitaṃ śrīrāmakṛṣṇaḥ subham (!) astu (fol. 53v6–9)
notes: The two dates disagree. Śaka 1854 is about 1932 CE and corresponds to VS 1989. VS 1986 is about 1929/30 CE and corresponds to Śaka 1851. I recorded the VS date. The descent chain is garbled ('prapautrāyaḥ suta', 'prauyaḥ suta', 'putrāyaḥ sutaḥ', 'putrāyaḥ suteḥ'). I read it as Devadatta being the great-great-grandson of Sadāśiva, great-grandson of Śrīkānta, grandson of Bālakṛṣṇa and son of Harikṛṣṇa, which gives a single line of descent. 'devadattapādhyā pyākuralapustakaṃ liṣitaṃ' means Devadatta Upādhyāya Pyākurel either wrote the book (as the catalogue says) or owned it ('Pyākurel's book'). I gave him both roles. 'śrīrāmakṛṣṇaḥ' just before 'subham astu' is most likely an invocation. It could possibly be a separate scribe, but that is unlikely. 'sadāśivasavarṇa' is corrupt; it may stand for 'sadāśivaśarmaṇa'. 'gograsya' should read 'gotrasya'.
review: Removed Rāmakṛṣṇa (p6) as scribe: 'śrīrāmakṛṣṇaḥ subham astu' is most naturally a closing invocation, not a scribe's name; the wrote_for relation went with it

Devadatta: roles changed from owner to scribe + owner. The construction (descent chain, then the name, then 'pustakaṃ liṣitaṃ') presents him as the writer, which matches the catalogue. Confidence lowered to medium
Pyākurala (Pyākurel, a Nepali Brahmin surname) moved into Devadatta's titles/affiliation and removed from as_written

The descent chain is now read as 'X's descendant's son' at each step (prapautra-suta, pautra-suta, putra-suta, suta). This keeps the same five-generation line (Sadāśiva → Śrīkānta → Bālakṛṣṇa → Harikṛṣṇa → Devadatta) but explains the kin terms consistently. Evidence strings updated
Sadāśiva: the 'śarman' title is uncertain because 'savarṇa' is corrupt; confidence set to medium
Notes updated about the date discrepancy and the reading of the name

notes: The two eras in the colophon conflict. VS 1878 is about 1821/22 CE (Phālguṇa vadi 6 falls around Feb/Mar 1822). ŚS 1741 is about 1819/20 CE (Phālguṇa would be early 1820). If they agreed, VS 1878 would be ŚS 1743, and ŚS 1741 would be VS 1876, so one figure is probably a scribal slip. I treat VS as the main era because it is given first. Checking whether Phālguṇa kṛṣṇa 6 fell on a Tuesday in 1820 or 1822 could decide which year is right. The colophon names no scribe, owner or place. review: Notes: spelled out that the two eras conflict. VS 1878 corresponds to ŚS 1743, and ŚS 1741 corresponds to VS 1876, so they are two years apart. They are not just two ways of writing the same year.
Date: weekday given as 'Tuesday (bhaumavā[sara])' because the colophon writes the abbreviated 'bhaumavā'.
Date: kept VS 1878 as the main era because it comes first ('saṃvat'). ce_approx is still 1822, since Phālguṇa kṛṣṇa 6 of VS 1878 falls in Feb/Mar 1822.

The personal name might be Jaivaṃta (Jayavanta), with the final '-na' unexplained. 'alaṃ liṣitaṃ' probably stands for 'idaṃ likhitaṃ'. The era is not named, but 'saṃvat … śudi' in Devanagari points to Vikrama: VS 1684 Āśvina śukla 12 ≈ September/October 1627 CE. The weekday has not been checked. The chapter number 'n(!)naviṃśo' is presumably ūnaviṃśo (19th).

Date fields normalised: month Āśvina (written 'a(!)śvana'), pakṣa śukla (written 'śudi'), weekday Thursday (guruvāra).

notes: The catalogue names Śivarāma as the scribe, but the quoted colophon (fol. 14v1–4) has no personal name. He may be named elsewhere in the manuscript, but he is not listed here because the colophon gives no evidence for him. The date uses the Persian-influenced formula 'sālamiti … roja 5', where roja 5 most likely means the 5th weekday, Thursday. Era is taken as Vikrama (VS): 1932 − 57 = 1875. 'sa〈〈pu〉〉mpurṇam' contains a cataloguer's insertion mark; it means saṃpūrṇam.

title: Yugalakiśorasahasranāmastotra
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Tuesday 4 Oct 1774, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīnāradīyapurāṇe śrīnāradoktaṃ yugalakiśorasahasranāmastotraṃ s(!)māptaṃ śrīr astu savat(!) 1831 varṣe śāke 1697 ā〈〈‥〉〉śvinamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe 13 bhaumavāsare la(!)khitaṃ rāvala〈〈‥〉〉 śaṃbhūrāma(gavaḍa) śrīr astu śrī ❁ śrī ❁ śrī ❁ śrī ❁ śrī ❁ śrī (fol. 10v6–10)
notes: The colophon gives two eras: VS 1831 and ŚS 1697. In Caitrādi reckoning VS 1831 matches ŚS 1696, not 1697. In Kārttikādi reckoning (used in Gujarat), Āśvina of VS 1831 falls in Sept/Oct 1775 and matches ŚS 1697. So the two eras agree, and the date is about Oct 1775 CE. The weekday (Tuesday) was not checked. The text has a lacuna between 'rāvala' and 'śaṃbhūrāma', which may hide part of the name. 'Rāvala' is taken as a title or community name. 'gavaḍa' (in parentheses in the transcript; the catalogue reads 'Gabaḍa') is probably a surname or caste name; it might be Gauḍa, but that is uncertain. The names suggest a scribe from western India (Gujarat or Rajasthan) and not a Nepalese one.
review: Name reduced to stem 'Śambhūrāma'; 'Gavaḍa' (catalogue: Gabaḍa) moved to titles as surname/caste name rather than part of the personal name

ce_approx changed from 1774 to 1775: ŚS 1697 (+78) points to 1775, and Āśvina of VS 1831 falls in 1775 only if the year is Kārttikādi (Gujarati reckoning). This fits the western Indian names Rāvala and Gavaḍa
Notes expanded: explains how the two eras fit together and flags the lacunae in the name

subject: Karmakāṇḍa
