date_note: = Tuesday 15 Feb 1842, weekday verified, nakṣatra not
colophon: iti śrīmahemāde cau(3)sathi lijñeśvara śrīisora samāpta || oṃ namo śrīpaśupataye nama || śubhaṃ || (4) śrī nepālasamvata ritu rasā nava varṣa saṃjña māghase ca śucīpache pañcamyā (5) ca titho pauṣṇe ca nāma nakṣutre śubhe ca yoga maṃgalavārasano minarāsi(6)gate caṃndramasi śrīsūryye udayāta parto ghati 4 saṃpūrṇṇa 〈〈ṛga〉〉 samāpta || (7) śrī śuddhom aśuddho vā mama doṣo na diyate śubhaṃ śapūrṇṇa ....... (b1) śubhaṃm || yā dṛṣṭaka pauṣṭaka lobhānī pāpānī yātya paṃñcamahāpātaka || śū(2)nānaṃ kālasā julo iti cauṣaṣṭilīgāsvara samāpta || || śrīkalījuge (3) bhoga 4942 śrīśakrarājasya śakakāla 1796 śrīsamvata 1898 sā(4)la miti māghaśukrayā paṃñcami reotinakṣetra śūbhayoge aṃgavārasa(5)re ca || śubhaṃ || sarvakālaṃ mama sṛdaya causathi liṃgeśvara namaṣkāro śūbhaṃ || (6) karapūragauaraṃ karuṇāvatāraṃ saṃsārasāraṃ bhujagendrahāraṃ || sa[[dā]]vasatta hṛdayā(7)ravide bhavaṃ bhavāni sahitaṃ namāmi || || || || || || || (exps. 34t2-34b7)
notes: The colophon names no people. It gives two date statements for the same day, Māgha śukla 5, Revatī nakṣatra, śubha yoga, Tuesday. (1) In the first, the NS chronogram ritu (6), rasa (6), nava (9), read right to left, gives NS 966, which is about 1845/46 CE. (2) In the second, Kali 4942 and VS 1898 both point to early 1842 CE. Śaka 1796 (= 1874 CE) contradicts both and is probably a scribal error for 1763. So the NS and the VS/Kali figures conflict by about 4 years. The NS chronogram may be corrupt, e.g. for 962, or the two statements may refer to different events (exemplar and copy). The VS figure is taken as the main date. The text title in the colophon is garbled ('cau(3)sathi lijñeśvara', 'cauṣaṣṭilīgāsvara' = Catuḥṣaṣṭiliṅgeśvara).
review: No persons: confirmed, the colophon names no scribe, patron, owner or king.

Date: the first reading gave era NS with year '966?' and CE 1842, which do not agree (NS 966 + 880 = 1845/46). Changed the main era to VS 1898, the only date written fully in figures that agrees with Kali 4942; CE about 1842.
Chronogram: ritu (6), rasa (6), nava (9), read right to left, gives NS 966. Recorded this in the notes as a conflict, not treated as a corruption of 962.
Śaka 1796 does not match the other eras (VS 1898 implies Śaka 1763); noted as a scribal error.
Weekday: both dates give Tuesday (maṃgalavāra; aṃgavāra for aṅgāravāra).

title: Darśapūrṇamāsī
subject: Kk
date_note: = Monday 15 Sep 1466, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: samvata 586(!) aśukla(!)pañcaṃmyāṃ tithau | jyeṣṭa(!) nakṣatre || somavāsare kātyāyanoktaādhāneṣu suci(!) iṣṭiḥ samāptaḥ|| edāniṃ darśapūrṇṇamāsī samāptaḥ|| likhitam ideṃ || śrīlaḍitabrumā(!) śrīmānīgalake dakṣiṇata(!) || pitho valānihmaṃ yāmagṛhādivāsina|| dvijavara śrīsaśidevātmaja pravoddanārtha(!) svaṃ pvaṣṭakaṃ|| (fol. )
purpose: ātmaja-prabodhanārtham: for the instruction of (the scribe's) son; svaṃ pustakam: his own book
notes: 'śrīsaśidevātmaja pravoddanārtha' is ambiguous. The preferred reading is Śaśideva as scribe and owner, writing to instruct his unnamed son (ātmaja-prabodhanārtham), with 'vāsina' as an instrumental agent. The alternative is that the scribe is an unnamed son of Śaśideva copying for his own study. 'aśukla' is most likely Āśvina śukla: Jyeṣṭhā on śukla 5 implies the Sun is in Kanyā. The cataloguer marked the year 586 with (!), so it may be misread. NS 586 = 1466 CE, but the weekday has not been verified. 'Laḍitabrumā' = Lalitabruma/Lalitapura (Patan); 'Mānīgala' = Maṇigal, the palace area. 'pitho' may be a corruption of 'pīṭha' or of a locality name.
review: Re-segmented 'dvijavara śrīsaśidevātmaja pravoddanārtha': read as 'dvijavara-śrī-Śaśideva[na] ātmaja-prabodhanārtha[ṃ]' ('by the excellent brahmin Śaśideva, to instruct his son'). The instrumental 'vāsina' (= vāsinā) needs an agent noun, and a scribe naming himself only as 'son of X' would be unusual. Śaśideva is therefore the scribe and owner (svaṃ pustakaṃ), not merely the father.
Removed p1 'Śaśidevātmaja' as a person. The son is not named, so he appears only in purpose and notes. The son_of relation is removed as well.
Date: 'aśukla' read as Āśvina śukla. On śukla 5 the Moon in Jyeṣṭhā puts the Sun around Kanyā, which fits amānta Āśvina. Set month Āśvina and pakṣa śukla. NS 586 ≈ 1466 CE is kept.
Purpose rewritten as instruction of the scribe's son; the book is his own.
Place as_written is now the full phrase; Patan is kept (Lalitabruma/Lalitapura, Mānīgala).

title: Kodaṇḍaśāstra
subject: Dhanurveda
colophon: iti śrībhūbhṛddilīpaviracite kodaṇḍasāstre(!) dikpāla…deśādhyāya(!) ṣaṣṭha(!) samāptaḥ || ۞ || samvata 4///śuklatṛtīyāyā(!) bhṛguvāsare punarvaśunakṣatre(!) || || || yambu? Bramāyā(!) śrīcanigalasthāne khāranyamaṃ kāyhastha jayate/// bhīmasyāpi bhatbhaṅga(!) munairapi matibhrama(!) | yadi sudham asudham(!) vā lekhikasya(!) na doṣayet || śubhaṃ bhavatu sarvvalokānām lakṣmīputradve vṛ// (fol. )
notes: The year breaks off after '4' and the month name is lost in the lacuna. The era is not named. 'samvata' with a 4xx year, Newari script and a Kathmandu location point to Nepal Samvat (NS 400–499 = c. 1280–1379 CE), but the century is inferred. Yambu is the old name for northern Kathmandu. Canigala is unidentified, perhaps a tole of Kathmandu. 'Bramāyā(!)' is corrupt. 'khāranyamaṃ' stands before 'kāyhastha (= kāyastha) jayate///'. It is probably the scribe's house or locality name, though it could be part of his name. The scribe's name is cut off after 'Jayate-', so the full form (e.g. Jayateja…) is unknown. The closing 'lakṣmīputradve vṛ//' is unclear and may be a further blessing or a fragment of a name; it has not been treated as a person. The author 'bhūbhṛd Dilīpa' (King Dilīpa) is named only as the text's author, not as the reigning king of this copy.
review: Scribe p2: residence changed from the place-of-copying phrase to 'khāranyamaṃ' (the word right before 'kāyhastha'; probably a house or locality name, reading uncertain); confidence lowered to low because the name breaks off after 'jayate'
Date: weekday normalized to Friday (bhṛguvāsara); era NS kept but flagged as inferred, since the colophon has only 'samvata'; ce_approx filled with the range for NS 400–499
Notes expanded: Yambu/Canigala, the uncertain 'khāranyamaṃ', the lost month, and the unclear closing words

notes: The copy was made in Dalakaulī village, which belongs to Cāuṇṇi tappā (Mithilā region; the modern location is not identified). 'pāṇḍavagrāmīyapaṭhatā' probably means 'pāṇḍavagrāmīya' (from Pāṇḍavagrāma) + 'paṭhatā' (a present participle in the instrumental, 'studying', which agrees with varddhamānena). 'ṭhakuke sārddhaṃ' is unclear. It may be a corrupt or vernacular form, with a Maithili postposition -ke. It could refer to a person named Ṭhakuka, or to an unnamed ṭhakkura (Ṭhākura) with whom, or with whose help, the copy was made. It is not clear whether this person was a co-scribe. The catalogue gives Varddhamāna as Donor, but the colophon says only that he copied it for his own study. The closing verse (pustakalikhanapariśramavettā … hanūmān ekaḥ paraṃ veda) is a stock scribal verse, and 'vidyuj(!)jano' stands for 'vidvajjano'. ce_approx: LS 374 + 1119 = 1493.
review: p1 Varddhamāna: kept as scribe and owner (svapāṭhārthaṃ). The catalogue lists him as Donor, but the colophon does not support that, so donor is not added.
p1 evidence shortened to the exact substring 'śrīvarddhamānena svapāṭhārthaṃ'.

p2 'ṭhakuke': role changed from definite 'scribe' to 'other' and confidence lowered to low. The form is ambiguous: it may be a corrupt personal name, or a vernacular or Maithili form of the title ṭhakkura ('with the Ṭhākura'). 'sārddhaṃ' marks association but does not show that this person was a co-scribe.

title: Kulārṇavatantram
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Tuesday 14 Feb 1662, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: || iti śrīkulārṇavamahārahasye sapādalakṣagranthe pañcamakhaṇḍe nāmavāsanādikathanaṃnāma saptadaśollāsasamāptaḥ || || śrībhavānīśaṃkaraprītir astu || || dvitīyanāgābdhiyute gate nepālavatsare | māghamāsya site pakṣe ekādaśāttithau (!) śubhe || pūrṇṇarājadivjasyājñāṃ dhṛtvāśirapico(?) kutulilekha daivajñaḥ pustakaṃ ca kulārṇṇavaṃ || || samvat 782 māghakṛṣṇa ekādaśyāṃ tithau kutujosina saṃpūrṇṇa coyā || || (fol. 198r4–6 and v1–2)
notes: Chronogram: dvitīya = 2, nāga = 8, abdhi = 7 (the seven oceans). Read right to left this gives NS 782, which matches the prose 'samvat 782' and the catalogue. NS 782 is 1662 CE, Māgha falling in Jan–Feb. The two dates disagree on the pakṣa: the verse has 'site pakṣe' (śukla) and the prose has 'māghakṛṣṇa'. The prose value is recorded here, but the conflict is unresolved. 'divja' is most likely dvija (a brahmin), though daivajña is also possible. 'dhṛtvāśirapico(?)' is corrupt; the sense is probably 'ājñāṃ dhṛtvā śirasi' ('placing his order on my head'), meaning Kutu copied the book on Pūrṇarāja's instruction. 'kutulilekha' = Kutu lilekha. The Newari 'kutujosina' = Kutu Josī with the ergative -na, and josī is the Newari equivalent of the Sanskrit 'daivajñaḥ' used for the same scribe.
review: p1 Pūrṇarāja: title changed from 'daivajña' to 'dvija' ('divja' is most likely a miswriting of dvija); confidence lowered to medium because the epithet and the following 'śirapico(?)' are corrupt
p2 Kutu: shortened the evidence

date: kept NS 782 / 1662 CE. Explained the chronogram: abdhi = 7 (the seven oceans), so reading right to left 'dvitīya-nāga-abdhi' gives 2-8-7 = 782. This is a normal value for abdhi, not a corruption
notes: the pakṣa conflict is now stated explicitly. The verse has 'site pakṣe' (śukla) and the prose has 'māghakṛṣṇa'; kṛṣṇa is kept from the prose
purpose: reworded as a benediction, since it is not a commission purpose

title: Gaurī vivāha pyākhana huyakala vāṅāyā dharoṭa
subject: Vividha
date_note: = Friday 7 Jan 1707, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: thvati śrīśrī jaya Bhūpatīndramalla devasana ñalāyā śrīśrīI(2)ndramalladevasake gaurīvivāha pyākhana huyakala vāṅāyā dharota thvati || || (fol. 32v1–2)
files: A 1218-15=A 0338-38 Gauri vivaha pyakhana huyakala vanaya dharota.doc.html
A 1218-15=A 0338-38 Gauri vivaha pyakhana huyakala vanaya dharota.html
purpose: Record (dharoṭa) of what Bhūpatīndra Malla sent to Indra Malla when the Gaurīvivāha dance-drama was performed
notes: No scribe is named. The quoted colophon contains no date and no place. The catalogue gives NS 827 pauṣa śukla tṛtīyā śukravāra (≈1707 CE) and Bhaktapur, so those details probably come from elsewhere in the manuscript. The text reads as a record of goods 'sent' (vāṅāyā) by King Bhūpatīndra Malla of Bhaktapur (instrumental -sana) to Indra Malla (-sake 'to') on the occasion of the Gaurīvivāha pyākhan. 'ñalāyā' is probably a corruption or misreading of 'yalāyā' ('of Yala', i.e. Patan). That fits Indra Malla, who ruled Patan briefly around NS 826–829. Bhūpatīndra's role is a mix of king and sender/commissioner of the document; Indra Malla is the recipient, not the reigning king of the place where it was copied.

notes: The catalogue names Dharmasena Vajrācārya as the scribe, but the Newari text says the copy was written and given to Vajrācārya Dharmasyaṇa/Dharmasena ('cosyaṃ biyā') and that the writing was done and handed over by Vajrācārya Udayacandra ('likhita ... udayacandrajusyaṃ biyā juro'). So Udayacandra is the scribe. 'Dharmasyaṇa' is a Newari spelling of Dharmasena; this reading is probable but not certain. colophon: (fol. ) iti || || || ❖ śubhaṁ || liṣiṭa karmmacārya dhamendrasiṁha pūtra … deva nihmasyana coyā (6) jula śubhaṁ || jādriṣṭaṁ puṣṭaka vidyā tādrisa li[[ṣi]]ṭa mayā jadi śudhaṁ (7) maśudhaṁ vā mamaḥ dokho niddiyate || (exp. 49b5-7)
notes: The colophon is undated and names no place. 'liṣiṭa … nihmasyana coyā jula' (Newari: 'written … the two of them wrote it') says the copy was made jointly by Karmācārya 'Dhamendrasiṃha' (probably for Dharmendrasiṃha) and his son. Only the ending of the son's name, '…deva', survives; the rest is lost in a lacuna marked by the cataloguer. The colophon gives karmācārya only for the father, though the son probably shared it. It closes with the stock scribe's disclaimer (yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā…: 'I copied it as I found it; whether correct or not, the fault is not mine').

p2: name lost in a lacuna, only '…deva' survives; confidence lowered from medium to low, as_written/evidence kept

title: Jñānārṇavanityātantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_raw: nepāle hāyane jāte dhaneśe nayanārṇṇave | site tapasya sutithau harauvāre vṛspatau
colophon: iti śrījñānārṇave nityātantre pavitrāropana (!) caturviṃśaḥ paṭalaḥ || 24 || || nepāle hāyane jāte dhaneśe nayanārṇṇave | site tapasya sutithau harauvāre vṛspatau || daivajñaviṣṇusiṃhena bhaktāpuranivāsinā (!) || sastaṃ goviṃdanāmārthaṃ saṃpūrṇṇalikhitaṃ tvidaṃ || || || durggā prītri astu || (fol. 60v5–7)
notes: The catalogue names Goviṃda as the scribe, but the colophon names daivajña Viṣṇusiṃha of Bhaktapur as the scribe. He copied the text for someone named Goviṃda. Chronogram: read units first, the words give units = dhaneśa, tens = nayana (2), hundreds = arṇava. Arṇava is 4 or 7. NS 72x is more likely for a Newari manuscript of this kind. Dhaneśa (Kubera) is not a standard number word, so the units digit is uncertain; the year cannot be pinned down without checking the tithi and weekday. 'harau' may name the tithi (ekādaśī/dvādaśī) or stand for the nakṣatra Śravaṇa (ruled by Hari). 'sastaṃ' is probably for 'śastaṃ'. 'durggā prītri (!) astu' stands for 'durgā prītir astu'.
review: Goviṃda: dropped 'commissioner'. 'goviṃdanāmārthaṃ' only says the copy was made for someone named Goviṃda, so the role is beneficiary. Confidence lowered to medium.
Place: as_written changed to the attested form 'bhaktāpuranivāsinā'. This phrase gives the scribe's residence; copying in Bhaktapur is only inferred from it.
Date: year field now gives the number reading. ce_approx is a tentative range. Weekday normalised to Thursday, month glossed as Phālguna. The tithi is given as a possible reading of 'harau'.
Purpose: changed to 'for Goviṃda'. 'durggā prītri astu' is a closing blessing, not a statement of purpose.

title: Devīrahasyam
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Saturday 5 Oct 1929, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrī rudrayāmale taṃtre devīrahasye sarvasiddhi pradāyane utrārdhernāma ṣaṣṭittamaḥ paṭalaḥ60 samāptoyaṃ devīrahasyābhidhastaṃtra saṃpūrṇaṃ siddhi śubha saṃbhavet śrīsaṃvat 1851 ke krāṃ ra śuddhi śrīdurgāttīja 3 śanivāra iti śrī kāśī svakṣetre śrīmaṇI karṇikā varttate śrīgopālamaṃdirasthāne likhitaṃ -------- śrīparmmānaṃda prakāśācāryeṇa ---- oṃ tatsat śubhamastu || (fol. 163v8–11&164r1–6)
notes: The colophon says only 'śrīsaṃvat 1851'. In a Kāśī context with a Hindi-style date ('1851 ke … śuddhi'), 'saṃvat' normally means Vikrama Saṃvat, which gives about 1794 CE. The catalogue's 'ŚS 1851' (= 1929 CE) is not supported by the wording. 'ke krāṃ ra' is probably '[saṃvat 1851] ke kvāra/kuāra', Hindi for Āśvina. That agrees with 'durgāttīja' (Durgā-tṛtīyā, Āśvina śukla 3). The weekday (Saturday) has not been checked. The scribe's name could be read as Paramānanda with the title 'Prakāśācārya', or as the ascetic-style name Paramānandaprakāśa with the title ācārya. The place of copying is the Gopāla temple near Maṇikarṇikā, Kāśī.

title: Tantrasāra
subject: Tantra
date_raw: nepālikābde viyad aśvavāha māsena masye (!) dhavale ca pakṣe
date_note: = Apr 1650, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti mahāmahopādhyāyaśrīkṛṣṇānadabhaṭṭācāryyakṛta (!) tantrasāraḥ samāptaḥ || || śrībhavānī prīṇā (!) tu || || nepālikābde viyad aśvavāha māsena masye (!) dhavale ca pakṣe | anantasiṃho vililekha sarvva anekatantrasya vacaḥ samūhaṃ || tantrasāram idaṃ pustaṃ, lobhāt snehādi kena ca | parebhyo nahi taddeyaṃ gopyaṃ kāryya prayatnataḥ || || śrīcakrarājasya || (fol. 298v4–6)
notes: The chronogram is viyad (0) aśva (7) vāha (7), which gives NS 770 (≈1649/50 CE). That fits the date of Kṛṣṇānanda Āgamavāgīśa (16th–17th century). The value 7 for vāha is the usual one (the horses that draw the sun), but it is not completely certain. The month 'masye' is corrupt: 'matsye' (solar Mīna) is the most likely reading, though 'madhye' or 'māghe' are possible. 'kṛṣṇānada' is a scribal error for Kṛṣṇānanda. The final 'śrīcakrarājasya' most likely refers to the Śrīcakra (a deity or yantra), not a human owner, so no person has been extracted from it. The closing verse forbids giving the book to others, but it names no owner. The catalogue's scribe, Ananta Siṃha, matches the colophon.
review: Chronogram resolved: viyad = 0, aśva = 7, vāha = 7 (horses of the sun, standard value); read right to left gives NS 770, ce_approx ≈ 1650 CE
Year field set to 770; as_written keeps the words of the chronogram
Month: 'masye' (!) is probably a corruption of 'matsye' (solar month Mīna, ≈ Caitra). Noted as uncertain
Author's name kept as Kṛṣṇānanda; 'kṛṣṇānada' noted as a scribal error

title: Saptaśatī
subject: Purāṇa / Stotra
date_note: = Monday 22 Mar 1255, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: mahārājādhirājaparameśvaraparamabhaṭṭārakaśrīmadabhayamalladevasya rājye | || śrībhaktāpurinivāśine jayatarāmasya pāṭhanimittena bhallokaüdayaharṣavarmeṇa likhitam idaṃ | na me doṣa (!) guṇo vāpi anulekhaviparyayaḥ | yathaiva likhitaṃ pūrvaṃ tathaiva likhitaṃ mayā || nepālasamvatsare bāṇaśailaharāṃnukaṃ | māse caitraśuklatrayodaśyāṃ | somavāsare | śubham astuḥ || (fol. 65r1–5)
notes: The chronogram 'bāṇa-śaila-hara' reads 5-7-3 from right to left, giving NS 375. This fits Abhayamalla's reign (c. 1216–1255 CE). Hara is often 11 in bhūtasaṃkhyā, but 3 is the only value that gives a possible year here. 'harāṃnukaṃ' is corrupt, perhaps for 'harāṅkake'. 'nivāśine' is an error for 'nivāsinaḥ' and goes with Jayatarāma; Bhaktapur is his residence. The catalogue's 'Place of Copying: Bhaktapura' is a reasonable guess but the colophon does not state it. The catalogue's 'Donor: Jayatarāma' is not supported; he may have commissioned the copy, but the colophon does not say so. 'bhalloka' = bhāro, a Newar title.
review: p2 Jayatarāma: removed 'commissioner' (no likhāpitam/lekhayāmāsa; colophon only says the copy was made pāṭhanimittena, for his reading); roles now beneficiary + reader. The catalogue's 'Donor' is not supported by the colophon.

p2 residence normalised to stem 'Bhaktāpurī' (Bhaktapur); the place of copying is emptied because the colophon gives Bhaktapur only as Jayatarāma's residence, not as the place where the copy was made.
p3: 'bhalloka' identified as the Sanskritised form of the Newar title bhāro; it stays in titles with varman.
Date: chronogram check added (bāṇa 5, śaila 7, hara 3, read right to left = 375); ce_approx 1255 kept; weekday normalised to Monday.

notes: Copied from an old palm-leaf manuscript (prācīnatāḍapatrapustakāt) by Bhojarāja Śarman for the personal library (Bhāratī Bhavan) of Rājaguru Hemarāja Śarmā.

title: Sārasamudhṛtisaptaśatikā Kuvjikāmata
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: ≈ 1922 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: śrīśrīmat śrīkuvjikāmate sārātsārasamuddhṛtya saptaśatikāntapaddhati samāptam iti śubham śrī 5 mahārājadhirājaśrītribhuvanavīravikramasāhadevasya vijayarājye pradhānam ātyaśrī 3 mahārājacandraśaṃśerajaṅgavarmaṇas tṛtīyaputreṇa janaralakesarasaṃśeravarmaṇānviṣya (!) saṅgṛhītasya saṃvat 092 varṣe likhitasya prācīnatāḍapatrapustakasyādhāreṇa 1979 vaikramīyavarṣe śrīnepālarājagurūhemarājaśarmaṇā lekhakadvārā saṃlekhya samuddhṛtam idaṃ pustakaṃ cirāya sumanasāṃ saumanasyātha kalpeta | (fol. 25v3–7)
purpose: for the lasting delight of the learned (cirāya sumanasāṃ saumanasyāya)
notes: The copy is dated VS 1979, which is about 1922/23 CE. This fits both Tribhuvana's reign (1911–55) and Candra Śamśera's term as Prime Minister (1901–29). It was copied from an old palm-leaf manuscript dated 'saṃvat 092', which Kesara Śamśera (Kaiser Shumsher), third son of Candra Śamśera, had searched for and collected. The era of that date is not given, but it is very probably NS 92, about 972 CE. That is the exemplar's date, not this copy's. The catalogue gives Hemarāja Śarman as scribe, but the colophon says he had the text written out 'through a scribe' (lekhakadvārā saṃlekhya). He is therefore the commissioner/editor, and the actual copyist is not named. 'saumanasyātha' looks like an error for 'saumanasyāya'. 'rājagurū' should read 'rājaguru'. 'kesarasaṃśera' is a spelling of Kesaraśaṃśera.
review: p2: 'varman' moved from the name to titles (name 'Candraśaṃśerajaṅga'). Title normalised to 'pradhānāmātya'. Roles minister + relative_only kept: he was Prime Minister in VS 1979 and is named to identify his son.

p3: 'varman' moved to titles (name 'Kesarasaṃśera'). Role 'owner' removed: the colophon says only that he searched for and collected the palm-leaf exemplar, not that this copy belongs to him. Role 'other' kept (collector of the exemplar).

p4: 'śarman' moved from the name to titles (name 'Hemarāja'). Title given as 'rājaguru' (Nepālarājaguru). Commissioner role kept because he had the copy made through a scribe (lekhakadvārā saṃlekhya).
Added relation p2 under_reign_of p1.
Purpose rewritten as a paraphrase; 'saumanasyātha' is read as an error for 'saumanasyāya'.
Notes: added the exemplar date (saṃvat 092, probably NS = c. 972 CE) and the unnamed hired scribe; recorded that the catalogue's 'scribe' field conflicts with the colophon.

subject: Nyāya
date_raw: abhrevarāvdhi śikharīndumite śake vyorjja śaubhra pakṣa guruvārayutā jajāhe
date_note: = Oct 1818, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śri mahāmopādhyāya śrīyuta jagadīśatarkālaṃkāra bhaṭṭācārya viracitā siddhāṃta lakṣaṇasya ṭippaṇī samāptā || || abhrevarāvdhi śikharīndumite śake vyorjja śaubhra pakṣa guruvārayutā jajāhe || siddhāntalakṣaṇakadīdhiti ṭippaṇīṃ hi śrīlālaratnadharaṇī tridaśo alikhaddhi || 1 || || śrī vārāṇasyāmiti śeṣaḥ || || (fol. 16r5-6)
notes: Chronogram: 'abhrevarāvdhi śikharīndu-' is read as abhra (0) – abdhi (4) – śikharin (7) – indu (1). Read right to left this gives Śaka 1740 (about 1818 CE), which fits a copy of a work by Jagadīśa (about 1600). 'vara' (or 'abhre') is corrupt and does not give a clean digit. It could be emended (e.g. svara = 7), but that would give one digit too many, so the reading is uncertain. The first pāda of the Vasantatilakā verse seems to be a syllable short, which supports corruption here. 'vyorjja' = vā ūrja (Kārttika). 'śaubhra' = śubhra/śukla. 'jajāhe' is probably for jagāhe/jajñe. The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Śrīlālaratnadharaṇī'. The better reading is śrī-Lālaratna, a dharaṇītridaśa ('god on earth', i.e. a brāhmaṇa). The work is Jagadīśa's ṭippaṇī on the Dīdhiti on the Siddhāntalakṣaṇa portion of the Tattvacintāmaṇi ('siddhāntalakṣaṇakadīdhiti ṭippaṇīṃ'). Raghunātha and Gaṅgeśa are not named, so they are not listed.

Scribe p2: confidence lowered to medium. The name division (Lālaratna + dharaṇītridaśa = bhūdeva, i.e. brāhmaṇa) is a reading, not explicit.
Author p1: titles normalized; 'tarkālaṃkāra' kept as a title. 'mahāmopādhyāya' is the colophon's form of mahāmahopādhyāya.

title: Meghadūta
subject: Kāvya
date_note: = Sunday 26 Aug 1601, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīmahākavikālidāsa〈〈kṛto〉〉viracitaṃ meghadū〈〈ha〉〉tā〈〈si〉〉bhidhānaṃ mahākāvyaṃ samāptaṃ || ❖ || itthaṃbhūtaṃ sucaritam idaṃ meghadūtaṃ ca nāmnā kāmakrīḍāvirahitajane viprayukte vinodaḥ | meghasyāsmin atinipuṇatā buddhibhāvāḥ kavīnāṃ natvāryāyāś caraṇayugalaṃ kālidāsaś cakāra 126 || ❖ || ity ākhyāte surapatisakhā śailakulyāpurīṣu sthitvā sthitvā dhanapatipurīṃ vāsaraiḥ kaiścid āpa matvāgāraṃ kanakaruciraṃ lakṣaṇaiḥ pūrvam uktais tasyotsaṃge kṣititalagatāṃ tāṃ ca dīnāṃ dadarśa || 127 tasmād adrer nigaditapathā śīgram etyālakāyāṃ yakṣāgāraṃ galita(vicakaṃ) dṛṣṭacihnair viditvā yat saṃdiṣṭaṃ praṇayamadhuraṃ guhyakena prayatnāt tadgehinyāḥ sakalam avadat kāmarūpī payodaḥ || 28 || || iti śrīmeghadūtakāvyaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || samvat 1658 bhādrapadabahula 14 dine śrī(nāgapurīyatapāgachebhaºº śrīcaṃdrakīrttisūri‥‥‥‥|| śrīmānakīrttisūri ‥‥| śrīharṣakīrttisūribhr lekhitaḥ (!) || samarasiṃhapaṭhanārthaṃ || (fol. 10r7-10v4)
notes: This is a Jain (Śvetāmbara) colophon from the Nāgapurīya Tapāgaccha; 'tapāgachebhaºº' is the cataloguer's abbreviation. The text names a lineage: Candrakīrtisūri, then Mānakīrtisūri, then Harṣakīrtisūri. The connecting words, probably 'tatpaṭṭe' or 'tacchiṣya', are lost in the lacunae (‥‥), so the pupil relations are inferred. Harṣakīrti of the Nāgapurīya Tapāgaccha is a known author active around 1600 CE. Some sources make him a pupil of Candrakīrti directly, which would make Mānakīrti a fellow pupil rather than his teacher, so the exact link is uncertain. 'sūribhr' should be read 'sūribhir'. Grammatically, 'lekhitaḥ' (causative, 'caused to be written') makes Harṣakīrti the commissioner for Samarasiṃha's study; the catalogue's 'Scribe: Harṣakīrtti' is probably loose. The actual copyist is not named. Samarasiṃha's 'reader' role rests on 'paṭhanārthaṃ' ('for the reading of'). The final verse number '28' is an error for 128. VS 1658 corresponds to about 1601 CE (Bhādrapada, August/September).

title: Pavanadūta
subject: Kāvya
date_note: = Friday 2 Feb 1674, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: pūrṇimānta months
colophon: iti pavanadūtaṃ kāvyaṃ samāptaṃ || samvat 794 || māghamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe dvādaśyāṃ tithau śukravāsare thvakahnu saṃpūrṇṇayāphādinajulo || śubha || || ❁ || likhitaṃ śrīdhvakahnathākurajusannam iti || kalyāṇam astu || caturbhis (tvāṃ) hastair ḍamaruparaśuṃ śūlahariṇaṃ dadhānaṃ śubhrāṃśoḥ kiraṇadhavalaṃ pañcavadanaṃ | punā †rātebhaki† pravaṇamanaso harniśam api namsyantaḥ santo yuvatisuta[[yutāḥ santi sukhinaḥ ]] ||
notes: The catalogue gives 'Scribe: ?'. 'thvakahnu saṃpūrṇṇayāphādinajulo' is Newari for '(it) was completed on this day'. The scribal note 'likhitaṃ śrīdhvakahnathākurajusannam' is best divided as 'śrī dhvakahna thākuraju-sanaṃ' ('by Śrī … Ṭhākuraju'). 'dhvakahna' may be a corrupt repetition of 'thvakahnu' ('this day'). In that case no personal name survives and the scribe is identified only by the honorific Ṭhākuraju, which in the Malla period can denote a royal or noble person. If the scribe is royal, that may explain why the name is left out. The name Dhvakahna is therefore very doubtful. NS 794 Māgha falls in early 1674 CE. The verse at the end ('caturbhis … sukhinaḥ') is a benediction added after the colophon and names no persons.

title: Mudrārākṣasa nāṭakam(nepālībhāṣāṭīkā)
subject: Nāṭaka
colophon: iti śrī manmahārājapadabhājaḥ pṛtho sununā śrī viśākhadatta mahā kavinā viracite mudrārākṣasa nāṭake nirvaṃharaṇannāma saptamo arkaḥ || 7 || samāptaśca || (fol. 169v2-3 ) vināmudrāṃ mudrāṃ samalikha dakhinnena ++++=== sasuṃdaryyānadā gana vati vayoṣṭādhika munau || 78 || || || || || || (fol. 169v1-4 )
notes: The scribe's closing verse is corrupt and has a lacuna: 'vināmudrāṃ mudrāṃ samalikhad akhinnena ++++ ...'. It means roughly '[he] tirelessly wrote out the Mudrā[rākṣasa] without mudrā (payment)', a pun on the title. The rest, 'sasuṃdaryyānadā gana vati vayoṣṭādhika munau || 78 ||', seems to say the copy was made at an age of 78 ('vayasi aṣṭādhika-munau' = seventy plus eight, with the numeral 78 confirming it). So 78 is most likely the scribe's age and not a date. Reading it as an abbreviated year (e.g. VS [19]78) is less likely. 'sasuṃdaryyā' might mean 'together with his wife (sundarī)', but this is uncertain. No scribe name can be recovered. Viśākhadatta's father Pṛthu is listed only because the author's standard colophon names him. Since the manuscript has a Nepali commentary, it is probably late (19th–20th c.).
review: Date: '78' is probably not a year. The verse reads 'vayo[='vayasi'?] aṣṭādhika-munau || 78 ||', i.e. at an age of 78, so it most likely gives the scribe's age. Era changed to 'none', year cleared, ce_approx left empty, and the reading is explained in notes.

purpose: for the use of Kaṇṭhānanda (the book became his: saphuli jula)
notes: The era is not stated, but the colophon is in Newari and the catalogue gives NS 882, which is about 1762 CE (August/September). The commentator's name 'taṭṭanāyakamahāsa' is corrupt: the cataloguer's (!) after 'mahāsavi' suggests something like 'mahāśaya-viracite', so Taṭṭanāyaka is a tentative name; a 'bhaṭṭa-' reading is also possible. 'Bheṃkhvāla(na)' has the ergative -na and may be a house or clan name instead of a personal name. The owner could be Kaṇṭhānanda or Śrīkaṇṭhānanda, since 'śrīśrī' is ambiguous. 'bhāju' is a Newari honorific. The colophon says only that the book became his (saphuli jula); it does not say he commissioned it.

colophon: || ityārṣe rāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye śrīmaduttarakāṃḍe svargārohaṇaṃ nāma saptamaḥ kāṃḍaḥ samāptaḥ || || liṣitaṃ rāma upādhyāyena likhitaṃ kavala(!) || || || || (fol. 193r4-5 )
notes: 'liṣitaṃ' = likhitaṃ (ṣ for kh). The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Śrīrāma Upādhyāya'. The colophon reads only 'rāma upādhyāyena', so the 'Śrī' is probably honorific. 'likhitaṃ kavala(!)' is unclear. It is probably a mistake for 'kevalam' or a fragment of a set scribal phrase, not a personal name. The colophon has no date or place. This colophon closes the Uttarakāṇḍa (fol. 193). The reel also contains the Āraṇya- and Kiṣkindhākāṇḍas, which may have colophons of their own that are not quoted here.
review: Persons, roles, date and place are unchanged.

Expanded the notes: the catalogue gives the scribe as 'Śrīrāma Upādhyāya', but the colophon reads 'rāma upādhyāyena', so the 'Śrī' is probably honorific; 'liṣitaṃ' is the usual ṣ-for-kh spelling of likhitaṃ.

title: Vālmīkirāmāyaṇa(sundara&yuddhakāṇḍa saṭīka)
subject: Rāmāyaṇa
date_note: = Friday 20 Sep 1844, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: ityārṣe rāmāyaṇe ādikāvye vālmīkīye uttarakāṃḍe svargārohaṇaṃ nāmaikā daśādhika śatatamaḥ sargaḥ 111 (fol. 376r4-5) iti śrī majjānakī ramaṇapadapaṃkaja paricaraṇa parāyaṇa śivalāla pāṭhaka pādānumāyi bhaṭṭadevarāma saṃgṛhīte śrīmadrāmāyaṇīya viṣamapadavyākhyāne uttarakāṃḍaṃ samāptimagamat samāptam bhādraśudi 9 saṃvat 1901 vārāṇasyāṃ (fol. 376r7-8)
notes: The catalogue gives Rādhākṛṣṇa Dāsa as scribe, but his name is not in the quoted colophon. He may be named elsewhere in the manuscript. Śivalāla Pāṭhaka is called 'śrīmajjānakīramaṇapadapaṅkajaparicaraṇaparāyaṇa'. He is named only as the teacher, or model, of the commentator Bhaṭṭa Devarāma ('pādānumāyin'). He has no part in the 1844 copy. Devarāma 'compiled' (saṃgṛhīte) the Viṣamapadavyākhyāna on the Rāmāyaṇa. This colophon closes the Uttarakāṇḍa (sarga 111, fol. 376r), but the catalogue title gives Sundara- and Yuddhakāṇḍa. Either the title is incomplete or the manuscript covers more kāṇḍas. 'Saṃvat 1901' at Vārāṇasī is taken as Vikrama Saṃvat. Bhādrapada śukla 9 of that year falls in about August–September 1844 CE.
review: Persons, relations, date and place left as they were; all are supported by the colophon.

Notes expanded: Śivalāla is Devarāma's teacher, not the teacher of anyone who produced this copy; the colophon quoted is for the Uttarakāṇḍa, although the title gives Sundara- and Yuddhakāṇḍa; the copy-date pakṣa and tithi were checked.

title: Vaiśākhamāhātmya
subject: Mahātmya
date_note: = Wednesday 16 May 1668, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīpadmapurāṇe pātālakhaṇde vaiśākhamāhātmye yamabrāhamaṇasaṃvāde trayodaśodhyā(2)yaḥ samāptaḥ || 13 || śubhaṃ || || yāte bhujaṃgāṣṭaturaṃgamebde jyeṣṭhe site nāgatithau budhehni | patirggaṇānāṃtara(3)sā dvijo sau vaiśākhamāhātmyamidaṃ lilekha || samvat 788 jyeṣṭhaśukla paṃcamī budhavāra thva kuhnu balānihmayā (4)śrīgaṇapatina thva vaiśākhamāhātmya coya dhunakādina juro || thva velasa rājdhirāja śrī śrī śrīnivāsamallaprabhusana, (5) saptāṅkakaṃsabadhapyāṣaṃadayakaṃ, vokhata voyakaṃ huyakāvala, tavasamadāya, ju va juro || śubham || (fol. 99v1–5)
notes: The verse chronogram bhujaṅga (8), aṣṭa (8), turaṅgama (7), read right to left, gives 788. This matches 'samvat 788' in the Newari prose. nāgatithi = pañcamī (5), also matching the prose. NS 788 + 880 = 1668 CE. That falls within the reign of Śrīnivāsa Malla of Patan (c. 1661–1684), so a Patan setting is likely, but no place of copying is stated. The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Gaṇeśa'. The colophon has Gaṇapati: 'patir gaṇānāṃ' in the verse and 'śrīgaṇapatina' in the prose. 'balānihmayā' = 'the one of Balāni'. This is taken as the scribe's residence or origin, but Balāni is unidentified. The final Newari sentence is garbled: 'saptāṅkakaṃsabadhapyāṣaṃadayakaṃ, vokhata voyakaṃ huyakāvala, tavasamadāya'. It seems to record a contemporary event: King Śrīnivāsa Malla staged a Kaṃsavadha dance-drama (pyākhaṃ), perhaps over seven days ('saptāṅka' might mean 'seven acts'). It does not name any further persons.
review: Place of copying set to empty: 'balānihmayā' ('the one of Balāni') describes the scribe's residence or origin, not where the copy was made. It is kept as p1's residence.

Notes expanded: nāgatithi = pañcamī matches the prose; Śrīnivāsa Malla of Patan reigned c. 1661–1684, which fits NS 788 = 1668 CE; the king's festival or Kaṃsavadha performance is described; Balāni is unidentified.
Evidence strings for the persons shortened.

title: Kuvalayānanda
subject: Alaṇkāra
colophon: iti śrīmatpapramāṇajñatatsadbhāraḥ(!)ma mahātmaja vaidyanāthakṛtā laṃkāracaṃdra(!) kākhyā kuvalayānaṃda ṭīkā || 2 || śrīśubhaṃ || || lekhaka pāṭhakayo śubhaṃ bhavatu (fol.122v4-5 )
notes: This colophon belongs to the text, not to the copy. Vaidyanātha Tatsat wrote the Alaṅkāracandrikā ('laṃkāracaṃdra(!) kākhyā' = alaṅkāracandrikākhyā), a commentary on Appayya Dīkṣita's Kuvalayānanda. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Ṭīkākāra : Vaidyanātha' is wrong: he is the commentator, not the copyist. The father's name is corrupt in 'śrīmatpapramāṇajñatatsadbhāraḥ(!)ma mahātmaja'. It probably stands for śrīmat-pramāṇajña-tatsad-bhaṭṭa-rāma-mahātmaja ('great son of the learned Rāma Bhaṭṭa Tatsat'), but this reading is uncertain. The phrase 'lekhaka pāṭhakayo śubhaṃ bhavatu' is a standard blessing that names no scribe or reader. The copy gives no scribe, date or place.

review: Name reading: 'upādhyāṣadāl' is better read as upādhyāya + Dāhāl (Dahal, a Bahun clan surname), not a corruption of upādhyāya alone. Added Dāhāla to titles and affiliation.

subject: Rāmāyaṇa
date_note: = Monday 26 Oct 1744, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīmadadhyātma rāmāyaṇe umāmaheśvara saṃvāde kiṣkiṃdhākāṃḍe navamaḥ sargaḥ 9 6 || (fol. 39r5-6) iti śrīmatsakala rājavipaduddharaṇa samarthetyādi virudāvalī virājamānasya himmati varmaṇa putrasya śrīsanma(!) varmaṇaḥ kṛtāvadhyātma rāmāyaṇa setau kiṣkiṃdhākāṃḍe navamaḥ sargaḥ 96 śubhamastu saṃvat śrī rāmāyaṇa ṭīkeyaṃ rāmavarmaṇakṛtāśubhā rāmārpaṇaṃ 6 || saṃvat 1801 mītīkātīka vaṃda 5 vāraśomā (fol. 39r2&8-9 )
notes: The catalogue's 'Scribe: Śrīrāma Varmā' is a mistake. Rāmavarman, son of Himmativarman, is the author of the Setu commentary ('ṭīkeyaṃ rāmavarmaṇakṛtā'), not the copyist. No scribe is named. 'śrīsanma(!)' is read as 'śrīrāma'. The figure '9 6' / '96' after 'navamaḥ sargaḥ' looks like a running sarga count. The date 'saṃvat 1801 (mītī) Kārttika vadi 5, Monday' comes straight after the commentary's closing verse. It may therefore date the commentary (or a copy reproduced with it) rather than this manuscript, so treat it as the copying date only with caution. Taking the era as VS gives 1744 CE (October/November). The weekday has not been verified.
review: Merged p2 'śrīsanma(!) varmaṇaḥ' into p3 Rāmavarman. 'sanma(!)' is almost certainly a misreading of 'rāma' (śrīrāmavarmaṇaḥ). The same colophon names the Setu's author as rāmavarmaṇa, so both refer to one commentator, son of Himmativarman. Confidence is now medium.

title: Kārttikamāhātmya
subject: Māhātmya
colophon: iti śrīpadmapurāṇe kārtikamāhātmye ekonatriṃśodhyāyaḥ imāḥ kathā kārttikamāghayo/// śubhaphaṇabhṛmithautra śrīviṣṇututyartham idaṃ purāṇaṃ kuvuddhināśāya gṛhavrata nāma likhitaṃ pahaladaṃ puṃsājñānamuktayabhivāṃchatām jñādigrāmābhidhānaṃ śrīgajādharadvijanmanā || || 1 || śubham astu viṣṇoḥ prasādāt || (fol. 23v8-11)
purpose: For Viṣṇu's satisfaction (viṣṇututyartham = tuṣṭyartham) and to destroy bad thinking (kubuddhināśāya).
notes: The colophon is a corrupt verse. It probably reads: śrīviṣṇutuṣṭyartham idaṃ purāṇaṃ kubuddhināśāya ... likhitaṃ phaladaṃ puṃsāṃ jñānamuktyabhivāñchatām / jñādigrāmābhidhāne śrīgadādharadvijanmanā. 'Gajādhara' is most likely Gadādhara. The as-written form is kept. 'śubhaphaṇabhṛmithautra' follows the lacuna (///) and is corrupt. It contains phaṇabhṛt ('serpent', which can stand for 8 in a chronogram) and may hide a date such as a year name or a chronogram. However, no reading can be made with confidence, so no date is recorded. 'gṛhavrata nāma' is unclear. It could be a corrupt epithet, or part of the place or person description. It is not treated as a person. The place-name Jñādigrāma is not identified.
review: Name normalised to Gadādhara (Gajādhara is almost certainly a mistake for the common name Gadādhara; ja/da confusion). Confidence lowered to medium.
Title changed from 'dvijanman' to 'dvija (brahmin)'.
Place normalised to the village of Jñādi (jñādigrāmābhidhāne). Residence set to the same, but this is uncertain.
Purpose rephrased.
Notes expanded: the corrupt passage and the lacuna.

notes: The colophon gives two dates: śāke 1765 (= 1843 CE) and śrīsaṃvat 1600. As transcribed, 1600 cannot be VS: VS 1600 would be 1543 CE. The catalogue field gives VS 1900, which equals 1843 CE and matches the Śaka year. So '1600' is probably a misreading or scribal error for 1900 (Devanagari 6 and 9 look alike). The catalogue field 'ŚS 1756' does not match the colophon's 'śāke 1765' and is probably a transposition of the digits; this record follows the colophon. The weekday has not been checked against the tithi. Separately, the chronogram 'sukhanipuruṣārthakṣmā 1493 rimitaśaka' (meaning 'measured', i.e. parimita) gives the date the work was composed, Śaka 1493 (1571 CE), not the date of copying. That matches the known date of Nārāyaṇa's Muhūrtamārtaṇḍa. The colophon also refers to the author's own commentary (Mārtaṇḍavallabhā), so Nārāyaṇa is listed as both author and commentator. The concluding verses ('yādṛśaṃ …', 'lagnamāna…') are stock verses, not prosopographical.

'dulitaṃ nhetanī(yā)' seems to be a locality or quarter in Patan, but the reading is uncertain. The colophon ends the 27th sarga (saptaviṃśatimaḥ) of the Adbhutottarakāṇḍa, while the catalogue title says 'Paṃcaviṃśatisarga' (25 sargas). Vālmīki is the traditional author, listed only as author.
review: Scribe p2: as_written now gives both forms (daivajña kṛṣṇavira / josikṛṣṇavīra). Evidence extended to the Newari phrase 'josikṛṣṇavīrana coyājolo' ('written by Jośī Kṛṣṇavīra'). Here coyā means the scribe wrote it, not that someone commissioned it.
Residence of p2 split into a usable form: Yala (Patan), locality 'dulitaṃ nhetanī' as written; the locality is uncertain.
Weekday normalised: vāsare 2 = Monday.
Place: kept 'yaladeśa' = Patan, with the locality phrase flagged as uncertain in notes.
Notes expanded: the catalogue scribe name is truncated; the sarga number in the colophon conflicts with the title; the reading of 'dulitaṃ nhetanī' is uncertain.

notes: The catalogue gives VS 1925, but the quoted colophon reads saṃvat 1915. VS 1915 − 57 = 1858, but Māgha śukla 6 of that year (Caitrādi) falls in Jan/Feb 1859 CE. The ownership statement is in Marathi ('yāce aśe', i.e. 'yāce āhe', meaning 'belongs to'), so the date is only a terminus for the ownership note if that note was added later. The cataloguer writes the name as 'dadhī ca', which probably stands for one word, Dadhīca/Dādhīca. This could be a family name or the Dādhīca brahmin community name qualifying Bāpū Jośī, in which case the personal name would be just Bāpū. 'vāpū' is read as Bāpū (v/b).

title: Bhīmasenapūjāvidhi
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Monday 5 Jul 1751, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: thvatena bhīmasena pūjā vidhiḥ || || (4) ❖ samvat 871 āṣāḍha śudi 12 sidhayakāva vidyāpīthayā vidyācājya 〈〈 maṇiratnadhara〉〉 (5) yatā biyā thva saṃphula sunānaṃ lobha yātasā pañcamāhāpāta julo || || śubham astu || (exp. 11b3-5)
purpose: gift: given to Vidyācārya Maṇiratnadhara of Vidyāpīṭha (yātā biyā)
notes: Newari: 'sidhayakāva' = siddha yānāva ('having completed'); '... yatā (= yātā) biyā' = '(it was) given to ...'; 'thva saṃphula sunānaṃ lobha yātasā pañcamahāpātaka julo' = 'whoever covets this book incurs the five great sins'. The person giving the book (donor, perhaps also the scribe) is not named. The cataloguer puts the name in 〈〈 〉〉, which may mean it was inserted or rewritten, so the recipient's name could be a later addition. vidyācājya = Newari spelling of vidyācārya; a garbled vajrācārya is also possible. 'vidyāpītha' = Vidyāpīṭha, possibly a vihāra or tantric seat; I could not identify it for certain. The date may be the date of completing the copy or the date of the gift. NS 871 + 880 = 1751 CE.
review: Maṇiratnadhara: roles reduced to 'owner' (he is the recipient of the gift, 'yātā biyā'; 'beneficiary' not supported)

Title normalized to 'vidyācārya' (as_written vidyācājya kept in evidence); Vidyāpīṭha kept as affiliation only, residence emptied (yā = genitive 'of', more likely an institution than a stated residence)
Notes expanded: 〈〈 〉〉 around the name, Newari reading of the formula, the curse formula, donor not named

title: Saptamīvratakathā
subject: Kathā
date_note: = Friday 9 Oct 1383, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti saptamīvratakathā samāptāḥ (!) || kīṭalīḍhākṣarāṃ pustīṃ lipidoṣād durakṣaraḥ | asaṃpūrṇṇā samālokya maṇikākhyena pūritā || vahniśūnyaśare yāte nepālābdi vidhīyate | aśunyāś ca site pakṣe tithau kāma bhṛgudine || vīraśiṃhāvidhānena likhitañ ca suśraddhayā | saptamīvratarājeśaṃ dvijāya saṃprabodhitaṃ || śubham astu || ○ || (fol. 10v1–3)
notes: The year is a bhūtasaṃkhyā: vahni = 3, śūnya = 0, śara = 5, read right to left = NS 503. 'aśunyāś' is corrupt, probably for āśvinyāṃ (the month Āśvina). 'kāma' stands for the 13th tithi, as the catalogue also gives. The verse says the book was insect-eaten (kīṭalīḍhākṣarām), badly written, and incomplete, so the one named Maṇika completed it (pūritā). Maṇika may therefore have supplied the missing portions as a scribe, not only corrected them. 'vīraśiṃhāvidhānena' is probably corrupt for vīrasiṃhābhidhānena ('by the one named Vīrasiṃha'), so he is taken as the scribe, which agrees with the catalogue. Read literally as vidhāna ('by arrangement of'), it would make Vīrasiṃha the commissioner instead. It is unclear whether Maṇika's completion happened at the same time as Vīrasiṃha's copy or later. The last line, 'saptamīvratarājeśaṃ dvijāya saṃprabodhitaṃ', seems to say the vrata story was expounded to a brahmin. That refers to the text's content, not to this copy's purpose, and no beneficiary is named.

title: Gītāsāra
subject: Gītā/Purāṇa
date_raw: samvata sāla 60 pradovisā || pusā māsa saṃpurṇa bhayā
colophon: iti śrīkṛṣṇārjunasaṃvāde gītāsāragitā samāpta || rāma rāma || samvata sāla 60 pradovisā || pusā māsa saṃpurṇa bhayā || ❁❁❁❁ || oṃ namo brahmaṇe(!)devāya nama (!) sāmipyasārūpyasālokyasāyāhya || (fol. 6v)
notes: The colophon names no human persons: no scribe, owner, commissioner or king. The date formula is in Nepali ('samvata sāla 60 ... pusā māsa saṃpurṇa bhayā' = 'completed in the month of Pauṣa, year [..]60'). The year '60' is probably an abbreviated year with the century left out. Nepali 'sāla' dating suggests Vikrama Saṃvat (e.g. VS 1960 = c. 1903 CE), but this cannot be confirmed, so the era is left unspecified and ce_approx is left empty. 'pradovisā' is obscure. It may be 'pra[viṣṭa]' (the solar day count used in Nepali dates) followed by a corrupt day numeral, possibly a misreading of 'bāisa' (22); this is uncertain. The final invocation is corrupt ('brahmaṇe(!)devāya ... sāyāhya' for sāyujya) and has no prosopographical content.

place: mānīsake śrī dakṣiṇe vihāre śrī yotho vihāra
colophon: iti uḍḍīsa pārameśvara mahātanumahārṇave caturviṃśatiśārasaṃgrahae śārātsārasaṃgraha uḍḍiśo nāmaḥ(!) paṭala samāptam (abhūt) || ○ || ❁ || śreyostuḥ || samvat (139) kārttika śukla ----- (viśākha) nakṣatraḥ | āyodhānayogeḥ | ravivāre || śrīrājādhirāja parameśvara bhaṭṭārakasya nārāyana(!) śrī śrī jayajyoti mala(!)devānām rājye vijayarāje(!) likhitam idam uḍīsara śāstuṃ śrī ||(mānīsake śrī dakṣiṇe vihāre śrī yotho vihāra kūṭumbaja pradhānāṃga ----- śāstraśrī jayate ------- dvija baruttama śrī manokusośarmanasothe likhitedam śāstraṃ || yadi śuddham aśuddham vā lekhito nāsti dośitaḥ | yathāsāstra tathā likhitaṃ mama doṣo nadīyate || kaṣṭena (lakṣiṇam) ------ (x. 54a5-54b5 )
notes:
The year is read as NS 139 (= 1019 CE), but that is impossible under Jayajyotirmalla, who reigned c. NS 528–548 (1408–1428 CE). The first digit is probably a damaged 5, which gives NS 539 = 1419 CE. This is a conjecture. The tithi is lost in the lacuna. 'āyodhāna' yoga is probably a corruption of āyuṣmān.

On Vijayarāja: 'vijayarāje' could be 'vijayarājye' ('in the victorious reign'). But that would be redundant right after 'rājye', so I followed the catalogue and kept him as the scribe.

The passage in parentheses after '||' looks like a second colophon. It may be secondary, and it is lacunose. It seems to describe a pradhānāṅga of a family (kuṭumbaja) belonging to Yotho vihāra, the southern vihāra in 'Mānīsaka'. That place may be Maṇigalaka (Patan), but this is unconfirmed. The person's name is lost in the lacuna. The phrase may give that person's affiliation rather than the place of copying.

'manokusośarmanasothe' has two possible readings:
- '…śarmaṇaḥ sārthe/syārthe' ('for Manokuso-śarman'): he is the commissioner. This is the reading used in the record.
- '…śarmaṇā svahaste' ('by Manokuso-śarman with his own hand'): he would be a second scribe.

The name may be Manokusuma.
review: p3: removed the brahmin suffix śarman from the name and added it to titles. The name is now 'Manokuso' (perhaps Manokusuma). Confidence lowered to low because the second colophon is corrupt and lacunose.
p3: kept the commissioner role ('-sothe' read as '-sārthe'/'-syārthe'). Notes now give the alternative reading 'śarmaṇaḥ svahaste', which would make him the scribe.
p2: kept as scribe at low confidence. Notes say 'vijayarāje' may be a corruption of 'vijayarājye'; that is redundant after 'rājye', which favours the catalogue's personal name.
Date: year field changed to '139 (as read; perhaps 539)'. ce_approx marked as conjectural. Yoga 'āyodhāna' noted as probably a corruption of āyuṣmān.

Place: left the normalized field empty. Notes say the locative phrase may describe the affiliation of a person lost in the lacuna (a pradhānāṅga of a family of Yotho vihāra) rather than the place of copying. 'Mānīsaka' may be Maṇigalaka (Patan).

title: Kubjikāmata
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Monday 29 Jun 1080, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti kulālikāmnāye śrīkubjikāmate samastājñānāvabodhacaryyo nirddeśo (nāpaś ca) viṃśatiṣaṭ paṭalaḥ || iti caturvviṃśatisāhasre (sārātsāraṃtaraṃ) śrīkubjikāmnāyaṃ śrī(otiyonapīṭhavirnirggataḥ)paścaviṃśatimaḥ paṭalaḥ || ❁ || (sataddevatsare pūrṇṇa paścāvaśām ekādhike tadā āśāmāśe śukladaśaṃyāṃ tithim uttamaṃ viśākhaṛkṣaṃ nāme tu || || likhitaṃ sārasaṃgrahakubjikā) (fol. 200v1-4)
notes: The colophon names no persons: no scribe, patron, owner or king. The date verse is corrupt. 'sataddevatsare pūrṇṇa paścāvaśām ekādhike' most likely stands for 'śatadve vatsare pūrṇe pañcāśad ekādhike', meaning 'when 200 years were complete, plus fifty-one', i.e. year 251. The catalogue gives [NS] 200, which apparently ignores 'pañcāśad ekādhike'. The year should be checked against the manuscript image. The era is not written; NS is assumed from the Newari script and the Nepalese provenance. If the year is 251, NS 251 is about 1131 CE; if 200, about 1080 CE. 'āśāmāśe' = āṣāḍhamāse. Moon in Viśākhā on Āṣāḍha śukla 10 is astronomically plausible. The closing words 'likhitaṃ sārasaṃgrahakubjikā' give a title for the text ('Sārasaṃgraha-Kubjikā'), not a person.

Era set to NS (assumed; not stated in the colophon) instead of 'unspecified', so that ce_approx can be given.
Month normalised to Āṣāḍha; tithi to daśamī; nakṣatra to Viśākhā. Viśākhā on Āṣāḍha śukla 10 is astronomically plausible.

title: Kubjikāmatatantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Friday 13 Feb 1092, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti mahāmudrāpīṭhe śrīkubjikāmate paramarahasye guhyātiguhye aṣṭamaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ || ○ || samvat 212 phālguṇaśuklaaśvanī(!) nakṣatre śukradine śrīmandarathasya rāja (śrīhallapiṅgaviṣaye kāthadhuṭōllakāpicāsinā kulaputravajābhāvokasya pūjārthas puṇyārthinā paramarahasya) pustakam idaṃ khitam(!) iti || ○ ||śivam astu || (fol.39r2-5 )
purpose: pūjārtha, puṇyārtha (for Vajābhāvoka's worship and merit)
notes: 'rāja' probably stands for 'rājye' (under the reign of). No king named 'Mandaratha' is known in Nepal around NS 212 (1092 CE), when Harṣadeva or Śivadeva ruled. He may be a local ruler of the Hallapiṅga viṣaya, or the name may be corrupt (e.g. for 'śrīmad-…'). 'kāthadhuṭōllakāpicāsinā' is probably an error for 'kāthadhuṭollaka-vāsinā' (resident of Kāthadhuṭollaka). The colophon has an instrumental agent ('…vāsinā … puṇyārthinā … [li]khitam') alongside the genitive 'kulaputravajābhāvokasya pūjārtha[ṃ]'. There are two readings: (a) the genitive is a case error for the instrumental, so Vajābhāvoka is the scribe and wrote the copy for his own worship (adopted here); (b) the writer is unnamed and Vajābhāvoka is only the beneficiary. Nothing supports 'commissioner', since the verb is likhitam, not likhāpitam. 'khitam(!)' = likhitam. The name may be a corruption of 'Vajrābhāvoka' or similar. The tithi is not stated.
review: p2 roles: dropped 'commissioner' because the verb is 'likhitam' (written), not 'likhāpitam'. The instrumental agent ('…vāsinā … puṇyārthinā … likhitam') is the writer. Read Vajābhāvoka as that agent (genitive -kasya for instrumental -kena), giving roles scribe + beneficiary ('pūjārthaṃ'). Confidence lowered to low.
p2 residence normalised to 'Hallapiṅga viṣaya, Kāthadhuṭollaka' (kāpicāsinā read as -ka-vāsinā).
p1 confidence lowered to low: no king 'Mandaratha' is known for Nepal c. 1092 (Harṣadeva or Śivadeva). He may be a local ruler of Hallapiṅga, or the name may be corrupt.

purpose: for the benefit of all beings, for long life, and to pacify all evils (sarvasattvopakārārthaṃ āyuṣkāmārthaṃ sarvaduritopaśāntyarthaṃ), commissioned by Jayapati Soma
notes: The colophon names the king as 'jayarājamala⁅deva⁆'. The bracketed part was restored by the cataloguer. NS 481 (1361 CE) falls in the reign of Jayarājadeva (c. 1347–1361), who is usually not styled Malla, so the '-malla' may be a scribal or cataloguer form. The colophon does not say where the copy was made. Patan (Māṇīgala, Lalitāpurī) is inferred from the scribe's residence ('tasmin eva nagaryāṃ'). The catalogue entry 'Donor' really means commissioner (likhāpitam). 'sarvvasatya' stands for sarvasattva. 'śarmmanena' and 'anantarāmanāmnena' are irregular instrumental forms.

title: Sāṃkhyakārikā, Sāṃkhyatattvakaumudī
subject: Sāṃkhya
date_note: = Monday 25 Apr 1825, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: iti śrīvāca(6)spatimiśraviracitā sāṃkhyatattvakaumudī samāptā || || arvābdhyadrīnduśake rādhāsitapakṣagauhasaume ʼhni || svārthaṃ kā(7)śyām alikhad yadolālalaratnākarākhyaḥ || 1 || || śubham astu || || || || || (fol. 27v5-7)
notes: The year is a bhūtasaṃkhyā chronogram: arvan (horse) 7, abdhi 4, adri 7, indu 1. Read right to left this gives Śaka 1747, which is ŚS+78 = 1825 CE. The colophon is a single Āryā verse. 'Gauha' (gau long) is metrically required and means 'belonging to Guha', i.e. ṣaṣṭhī. The scribe's name: the ms has 'yadolālala'. The metre (27 mātrās) works with either 'yadolālala' or the catalogue's 'yādolāla', so the name is probably Yādolāla/Yadulāla with a doubled 'la'. 'Ratnākara' is probably a family name or epithet, so I kept it in the name. A rough calendar check: if 1747 is the expired year, Vaiśākha śukla 6 falls around 22–24 April 1825, which does not give a Monday. If 1747 is the current year (= 1746 expired), it falls around 3 May 1824, which is a Monday and matches 'saume'. So the date could be 1824 rather than 1825. This was checked only with mean new moons and is unconfirmed.
review: p1: name normalized to 'Vācaspati' (miśra moved to titles only, per stem-form rule)
p2: name normalized to 'Yadolāla Ratnākara' (the ms reading 'yadolālala' looks like dittography; the catalogue gives Yādolāla); confidence lowered to medium
date.tithi: 'gauha' is not a corruption. It is the vṛddhi derivative of Guha (the day sacred to Guha/Skanda = ṣaṣṭhī, 6). The Āryā metre needs the long 'gau'
date.weekday: 'saume' read as Monday (sauma < soma); Wednesday (saumya) is possible but less likely
date: chronogram verified (arvan 7, abdhi 4, adri 7, indu 1, read right to left = 1747); added a note on current vs. expired year
purpose normalized to 'svārtha (for the scribe's own use)'

colophon: iti śrīgorakṣaśatakaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || || || saṃ (865) aṣāḍha(śukla) a[[ṣṭamī]] ādityavāro(yurarvva(6)ra) na coyā || śubha || ❁ || (fol. 24v5–6)
notes: The era is not written. NS is assumed because the colophon uses the Newari 'coyā' and the year number is low (NS 865 = c. 1745 CE). 'na coyā' is the Newari agentive 'written by', so the word before it should be the scribe's name. It is quoted as '(yurarvva(6)ra)', running across the break to line 6. That form is corrupt and unidentified, perhaps a garbled personal name. It is also possible that the parenthesis is the cataloguer's report of what the manuscript actually has in place of the normalised 'ādityavāro'. In that case the scribe's name is lost or merged into it. The weekday has not been checked against the tithi. 'Gorakṣa' is part of the title, so it is not listed as a person.

notes: The colophon is undated. The names at the end (Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Rāmacandra, Viśvanātha, Hiraṃvū = Heramba?) are invocations of deities, not persons. 'bhairavanāthabrāhmaṇajyogaḥ' looks corrupt. It may be a Sanskritised form of Nepali 'brāhmaṇa jyū ko' ('of Bhairavanātha brāhmaṇa-jī'), or perhaps 'brāhmaṇena'. Either way Bhairavanātha is the scribe, which agrees with the catalogue. In the verse, 'garbhākṛtānusiṃhādyair' is probably 'garbhīkṛtā nṛsiṃhādyaiḥ' ('incorporating [the views of] Nṛsiṃha and others'). That would point to earlier scholars, not to anyone involved in this copy, so no person record is made for them. 'āditaḥ paṃcalakṣaṇī' describes the portion covered: from the beginning up to the Pañcalakṣaṇī section. Raghunātha, author of the Dīdhiti, is not named; the Dīdhiti appears only as a title.

colophon: iti tarkasaṃgrahaḥ samāptaḥ śake 1758 durmukhābde jyeṣṭhakṛṣṇaikādaśyāṃ (3) kāśyāṃ kelakaropanāmnā sadāśivabhaṭṭena likhitaṃ idaṃ pustakaṃ marāṭhe ity u(4)panāmakasya śrīraṃganāthadīkṣitasya || śrīgaṃgāviśveśvara (!) prasanno stu (fol. 10v2-4)
notes: The era is Śaka: the colophon says 'śake 1758', and 1758 + 78 = 1836 CE. The year name Durmukha agrees: in the 60-year cycle it is 1836/37 CE (Śaka 1758). Jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa ekādaśī would then fall around June 1836. The catalogue's 'SAM 1758' has the right number but a vague era label. Both persons are identified by Maharashtrian surnames (upanāma: Kelakara = Kelkar, Marāṭhe), which points to a Marathi brahmin setting in Kāśī. The colophon only says the book belongs to Raṅganātha Dīkṣita. That it was written for him is an inference, not stated. 'śrīgaṃgāviśveśvara (!) prasanno stu' is an invocation of deities, not a person.

notes: The chronogram nayana-dhanva-aṅka-indu, read right to left, gives indu = 1, aṅka = 9, dhanva = ?, nayana = 2, so the year is 19?2. 'Dhanva' (dhanus) is not a standard number word. Following the cataloguer ('SAM 1952?'), I take it as 5 (bow ~ bāṇa/arrows). If it stands for the 9th rāśi (Dhanus), the year would be 1992 (≈ 1935 CE). The colophon names no era ('śaradi' only). The scribe's name 'ṭoḍarāndenālikhat' is corrupt, probably for ṭoḍarānandena alikhat. 'gnitithu' stands for agnitithau and 'ghasre' for ghasre/vāsare.
review: Scribe confidence lowered from high to medium: the name is corrupt (ṭoḍarāndena), and Ṭoḍarānanda is a reconstruction.
Month normalized to Caitra (madhumāsa), pakṣa to śukla (avadāta), tithi to 3 (agni) and weekday to Wednesday (saumya = Budha).
Notes now flag that the value of 'dhanva' in the chronogram is uncertain. The era is not stated in the colophon, so VS is an inference.

'Koṭa' could also be a Sanskritized form of the Maharashtrian surname Koṭe, in which case the personal name is not given. The invocation 'śrīturajāpuryai namaḥ' addresses the goddess of Tuljāpur (Tulajā Bhavānī), which points to a Maharashtrian scribe. It does not name the place of copying. Date: Śaka 1787 = Krodhana in the southern 60-year cycle (Prabhava = Śaka 1789), so the year is consistent: 1865–66 CE. 'krodhanāvde' is a corrupt spelling of krodhanābde.
review: p1: confidence lowered from high to medium. 'koṭena' may stand for the Marathi family name Koṭe rather than a personal name Koṭa, and 'Aṇṇā/Aṇṇa' is given as an upanāman (by-name or call-name).
Notes: added the ambiguity of the name, the Tuljāpur invocation (a regional pointer, not a place of copying), and a check of the Jovian year.

title: Aṣṭavakragītā
subject: Vedānta
date_note: = Tuesday 22 Jul 1823, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: Kārttikādi, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: ity aṣṭāvakre saṃkhyākramāḥ || ekaviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam || || (fol. 55r6) || iti śrī (aṣṭavakraviśveśvaraviracitāyāṣṭāvakrakālasaṃkramaṇāddivyākhyā)1 samāptaṃ || || || śrīśubhaṃ bhavatu || || śrīrastu || || samvat 1880 āṣāḍhaśukla purṇamāravaudine lī o. bhaṭa raṇachoḍajī śāmajī śrīgoḍajñātīya || śrījīrṇadurga nivāsi || || śubhamastu || || || (fol. 55r7-10)
notes: 'lī o.' probably abbreviates likhitam. Raṇachoḍajī Śāmajī follows the Gujarati pattern of personal name + father's name, both with the honorific -jī; Śāma may stand for Śyāma. The scribe was a Bhaṭṭa of the Śrīgauḍa jñāti living in Jīrṇadurga (Junagadh, Gujarat). The catalogue gives 'Jīrṇadurganivāsī' as the place of copying, but the colophon describes it as the scribe's residence; copying there is likely but not stated. The title passage '(aṣṭavakraviśveśvaraviracitāyāṣṭāvakrakālasaṃkramaṇāddivyākhyā)' is corrupt (the cataloguer flags it with note 1). Viśveśvara seems to be named as the author of a commentary or gloss (vyākhyā), but the reading is uncertain. Date check: in western India VS years start in Kārttika, so Āṣāḍha śukla 15 of VS 1880 falls on about 11 July 1824, a Sunday, matching the colophon. The Caitrādi reading (about 23 July 1823) would fall on a Wednesday.
review: p1 Viśveśvara: confidence lowered to medium; the title in parentheses is garbled, so his exact role (commentator or author of a gloss) is uncertain
p2: as_written widened to include the '-jī' honorific. The name stays Raṇachoḍa and the residence stays as given
p3 Śāma: residence removed. The colophon gives residence only for the scribe, so it should not be carried over to the father. The caste affiliation is kept because it is inherited

date: ce_approx changed from 1823 to 1824. In Gujarat (Junagadh) VS years start in Kārttika, so Āṣāḍha śukla 15 of VS 1880 falls in mid-1824. The full moon of about 11 July 1824 was a Sunday, which matches 'ravau dine'. The Caitrādi alternative, about 23 July 1823, was a Wednesday
date: tithi normalised to pūrṇimā and weekday to Sunday (ravau dine)
place: emptied. 'jīrṇadurga nivāsi' gives the scribe's residence, not the place of copying. Copying at Junagadh is likely but not stated (see notes)

title: Uttaragītā [ adhyāya 1-3 ]
subject: Vedānta
date_note: = Monday 24 Jan 1707, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti uttaragītāyāṃ tṛtīyodhyāyaḥ || (fol. 25r7–8) iti śrīgauḍapādācāryaviracitāyāṃ uttaragītā ākhyātāyāṃ tṛtīyodhyāyaḥ samāptim agamat || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || samvat 1628 vyayasamvatsare māghavadya paṃcamī somavāra taddivase idaṃ uttargītā ākhyāṃ murarīna likhita sadānanda pustakamadaḥ śrīkṛṣṇa jośī || (fol. 25r5,8–10)
notes: The colophon says only 'samvat', which normally means VS. However, the samvatsara name Vyaya matches ŚS 1628 (1706/07 CE) and does not match VS 1628 (1571/72 CE), so I read the era as Śaka. The weekday has not been checked. 'pustakamadaḥ' = pustakam adaḥ, meaning 'this book is Sadānanda's'. 'śrīkṛṣṇa jośī' follows the ownership phrase with no syntax linking it, so his role is unclear. He could be a second owner, Sadānanda's father or family name (Sadānanda [son of] Kṛṣṇa Jośī), or someone who added a later note. Ascribing the Uttaragītā to Gauḍapāda is traditional. The catalogue gives the scribe's name as Murārī; the manuscript has 'murarīna', which I normalised to Murāri.
review: Era changed from VS to ŚS: the samvatsara name Vyaya fits ŚS 1628 = 1706/07 CE exactly (Vyaya, 20th Jovian year), whereas VS 1628 (1571/72 CE) would fall in Prajāpati/Aṅgiras. ce_approx changed from 1572 to 1707 (Māgha kṛṣṇa ≈ Jan/Feb 1707).
Removed the wrote_for relation Murāri→Sadānanda. The colophon only says Murāri wrote the copy and Sadānanda owns it; it does not say the copy was made for him, and the ownership note could be later.
Lowered Kṛṣṇa Jośī to low confidence and expanded the note on his unclear role.

title: Pañcīkaraṇavārttika
subject: Vedanta
date_raw: vasu vāṇavasu kṣoṇī mita varṣe nabhasyamuṃ
colophon: iti śrīparamahaṃsaparivrājakācārya śrīmacchamkarabhagavatpādapūjyaśiṣya śrīmat sudeśvarācārya racitaṃ paṃcīkaraṇavārtikaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || vasu vāṇavasu kṣoṇī mita varṣe nabhasyamuṃ || tāropākhya maṇirāmaṣyaṣyāṃ(!) mamdevyalī | likhat || || śrīḥ || || śrīḥ || śrīḥ || śrīḥ ||
notes: The chronogram vasu (8), bāṇa (5), vasu (8), kṣoṇī (1), read right to left, gives 1858. No era is named. If it is VS, the year is about 1801 CE, which fits a Devanagari manuscript with the name Maṇirāma; if it is ŚS, it would be about 1936 CE. Nabhasya is Bhādrapada; 'nabhasy amum' means 'in Nabhasya, this [book]'. The dating line is an anuṣṭubh: 'vasubāṇavasukṣoṇī-mitavarṣe nabhasy amum | tāropākhyamaṇirāma-ṣyaṣyāṃ(?)maṃdevy alīlikhat'. The verb is alīlikhat, a causative aorist ('had written'), though it is often used loosely for 'wrote', so Maṇirāma may be the scribe rather than the commissioner. 'ṣyaṣyāṃ(!) maṃdevy' is corrupt (the cataloguer marked it with '!') and may hide a further word, such as a form of śiṣya or a female name ending in -devī, but no reliable name can be recovered from it. Śaṅkara is named only as the author's teacher. 'Sudeśvara' is a corruption of Sureśvara.
review: Removed 'Mamdevyalī' as scribe: the line is an anuṣṭubh half-verse ('tāropākhyamaṇirāma- / ṣyaṣyāṃ maṃdevy alīlikhat'), and '-lī likhat' is the verb alīlikhat, not part of a name
Maṇirāma: role changed from owner to commissioner (alīlikhat, a causative aorist: 'had [this] written'), noting he may be the scribe; 'tāropākhya' moved from titles to affiliation as the surname Tāro
Śaṅkara: role changed from teacher to other (he is the author's teacher, not connected with this copy); name normalised to Śaṅkara
Author name changed from Sudeśvarācārya to Sureśvara, with 'ācārya' as a title only; the corruption is noted
Removed the wrote_for relation, which depended on the false scribe
Notes rewritten with the metrical analysis and the uncertainty about the era

title: Pañcadaśī
subject: Vedanta
date_raw: aṅkenduddakadairmite śaka itepatyaudyutīnāṃdhane lakṣmījānidine dale tu dhavale lekhīrajevāsare
colophon: iti śrīviudyāraṇyamunikṛtāyāṃ vedāntapañcadaśyāṃ pañcabhūtavivekonāmā dvitīyaṃ prakaraṇaṃ sampūrṇam (fol. 13r10-11) iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācārya śrībhāratītīrthavidyāraṇyamunivaryaśiṣyeṇa śrīrāmakṛṣṇākhya viduṣā viracitā pañcabhūtavivekatāṭparyadīpikā samāptatāmaglobīt śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ || aṅkenduddakadairmite śaka itepatyaudyutīnāṃdhane lakṣmījānidine dale tu dhavale lekhīrajevāsare vedāntāpi tṛtīyakādikamidaṃ satpañcasadaśyā śubhaṃ śrīkāśyāṃ śivaśarmaṇā prakaraṇaṃ saṅkhyāvatā śrīmatā 1 (fol. 13r12-14)
notes: The date is a śārdūlavikrīḍita verse. Pāda a: aṅkendu-[uu]-dair-mite śake ite patyau dyutīnāṃ dhane. 'duddaka-dair' (two short syllables plus one long) is corrupt, so the Śaka year can only be read as ?19 (units 9, tens 1, read right to left). ce_approx is left empty. Pāda b ends lekhi + [short–long] + vāsare. 'rajevāsare' is unmetrical as a weekday name; indujavāsare (Wednesday) fits the metre, but this is conjecture. 'raver vāsare' (Sunday) does not fit. Pāda c (vedāntāpi tṛtīyakādikam idaṃ sat-pañcadaśyāḥ śubhaṃ) suggests the scribe's verse belongs with prakaraṇa 3 onward, even though it follows the end of prakaraṇa 2 (with Rāmakṛṣṇa's Tātparyadīpikā). Other scribal errors: 'viudyāraṇya' = Vidyāraṇya; 'samāptatāmaglobīt' is corrupt (≈ samāptim agamat). The final '1' is probably a verse number. The catalogue's scribe (Śivaśarmā) and place (Kāśī) agree with the colophon.
review: p4: name 'Śivaśarman' → 'Śiva' with 'śarman' in titles, per the stem rule; residence 'Kāśī' removed, because Kāśī is only stated as the place of copying; epithet saṅkhyāvat ('learned') added to titles; evidence changed to the dated verse.

p2: as_written cut down to Bhāratītīrtha alone. The compound bhāratītīrtha-vidyāraṇya-munivarya-śiṣyeṇa is a dvandva naming two teachers of the commentator. 'munivarya' and the ascetic titles belong to both. The role 'teacher' becomes 'other', since this is the commentator's teacher, not anyone involved in this copy.
p1: Vidyāraṇya kept as author. Noted that he is also named as the commentator Rāmakṛṣṇa's teacher, which is why the pupil_of relation p3→p1 is kept.
p3: the title 'vidvas' kept as an epithet (viduṣā).

Date: month filled in as solar Dhanus (ite patyau dyutīnāṃ dhane = when the sun has entered Sagittarius, ≈ Pauṣa). Tithi read as ekādaśī (lakṣmījāni-dina = Viṣṇu's day). Weekday 'Sunday' rejected: the metre needs two syllables, short–long, before vāsare. The likely reading is (lekh)īndujavāsare, Mercury's day = Wednesday, but this is uncertain.
Year left unresolved. Read right to left, aṅka = 9 (units) and indu = 1 (tens); the remaining figure words are corrupt, so ce_approx is empty.

If 1989 is right, the date is c. 1932 CE; if 1689, c. 1632 CE. The era is not named. VS is assumed because the scribe lived in Rudraprayāga (Garhwal), where Vikrama saṃvat is normal. review: Place: removed 'nepāladdeśe' / Nepal as place of copying. The fragment is cut off ('nepāladdeśe…'), probably opens a new clause and does not say the copy was made there. No place of copying is stated explicitly; the catalogue's Rudraprayāga is only the scribe's residence.

title: Bhagavadgītā
subject: Vedānta
date_note: = Saturday 4 Apr 1693, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrībhagavadgītāsūpaniṣatsu vrahmavidyāyāṃ yogaśāstre śrīkṛṣṇārjjunasaṃvāde śatasāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ śrīmahābhārate bhīṣmaparvvaṇi paramārthanirṇṇaya mokṣayogonāmāṣṭādaśodhyāyaḥ || || śubha || svasti || samvat 813 phālguṇakṛṣṇacaturddaśi utrabhadra (!) nakṣatre ēndrayoga śaniścala (!) vāsare thvakunhu || kāśyapagotra ipalāccha ṭolayā vāsudeva bhārona śrī 3 indrāyaṇīprītina śrī 3 paśupati skeduṃtājuro || śubham astu || (fol. 68v2–5)
purpose: offered to Śrī 3 Paśupati for the pleasure of Śrī 3 Indrāyaṇī (indrāyaṇīprītina)
notes: 'skeduṃtājuro' is probably a corruption, or a word-division error, for '(paśupati)sa deduṃtā juro', 'was offered/dedicated to Paśupati'. That makes Vāsudeva the donor. The colophon does not say he commissioned or wrote the copy. The catalogue calls him the scribe, but the colophon gives no scribe statement. He may have copied it himself, but this cannot be confirmed. 'bhārona' = Bhāro (caste/title) + Newari ergative -na. Ipalāccha ṭola (catalogue: Ipalāttha) is stated as his residence, not explicitly as the place of copying, and its identification is uncertain. NS 813 + 880 gives early 1693 CE: Phālguna kṛṣṇa 14 falls around February–March 1693. The weekday and nakṣatra were not checked by calculation.
review: p1 roles: removed 'commissioner' — no causative verb (likhāpitam/coyakā) in the colophon. 'skeduṃtājuro' is best read as Paśupati-s(a) deduṃtā juro, 'was offered to Paśupati', which supports only 'donor'.
Notes: replaced the 'caused to write' reading of skeduṃtājuro with the dedication reading. Also noted that the catalogue's 'scribe' attribution is not stated in the colophon.
Place of copying: emptied. Ipalāccha ṭola is given only as Vāsudeva's residence (ṭolayā), not as the place of copying.
Purpose: rephrased as a dedication to Paśupati for the pleasure of Indrāyaṇī.
Date: normalized weekday (Saturday), nakṣatra (Uttarabhādrapadā) and yoga (Aindra). Normalized tithi spelling. Refined ce_approx (Feb–Mar 1693).

title: Laṅkāvatārasūtra
subject: Bauddhasūtra
date_note: = Sunday 1 Feb 1789, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: year read as current
colophon: āryyasaddharmalaṃṅkāvatāla nāma mahāyānasūtra sagāthakaṃ samāptam iti || ❁ || ❁ || ye dharmā hetuprabhāvā hetu teṣān tathāgataḥ | h avada teṣāñ ca yo nirodha evamvādi mahāśravaṇaṃ || ❁ || samvat 950 mti māghamāsya śuklapakṣe ṣaṣṭammītithau aśuṇinakṣatre, śubhayogya yathākarṇṇamahātre, ādityavāsare, makrarāsigate śavitre meṣarāsigate candraṃmasi || || dānapati hataṣāde onani, śrībhāju dhaṃsiju tasya bhāryyā vilalakṣmi putra jio dhaṃju tasya bhāryyā jñānalakṣmi putra munirāja, thuti sayāṃ maṅgalajuya māra śubhaṃ || || (fol. 222v)
purpose: Pious gift (dānapati) by Dhaṃsi and family; ends with Newari 'thuti sayāṃ maṅgala juya māra' = may all these (the named family) be blessed
notes: The catalogue gives the year as NS 910, but the quoted colophon reads 'samvat 950'. The colophon reading has been followed, though the catalogue figure may be the correct one. NS 950 + 880 = 1830. However, Māgha falls in January–February, so the actual date is probably early 1831 CE. Sun in Makara with Moon in Meṣa/Aśvinī on śukla 6 fits Māgha. 'hataṣāde onani' is unclear: perhaps a locality (tole) followed by a Newari locative or verb form. It is recorded as the donor's residence, not as the place of copying. 'bhāju' and '-ju' are Newari honorifics, so the stems are Dhaṃsi (also possible: Dhaṃsiju) and Jio Dhaṃ. The split of 'jio dhaṃju' is uncertain; it might be a single name, Jiodhaṃ. 'vilalakṣmi' might be a corruption of Vilāsalakṣmī. No scribe is named.
review: p1 name: removed the Newari honorific -ju, so 'Dhaṃsi' (kept as a variant in notes); titles now bhāju and ju
p3: name read as 'Jio Dhaṃ' (Newari honorific -ju removed) and confidence lowered to medium; the split of 'jio dhaṃju' is uncertain
All five persons get the role 'beneficiary' because of 'thuti sayāṃ maṅgala juya māra' (may all these be blessed); p1 stays donor (dānapati)
place: emptied. 'hataṣāde onani' is given as the donor's residence, not as the place of copying; it stays in p1's residence field
purpose: changed from a fragment of the Newari to its meaning
date: tithi stays ṣaṣṭhī; added yathākaraṇa muhūrta, Sun in Makara and Moon in Meṣa; notes on the CE year and the conflict with the catalogue's 910

title: Subhāṣitamahāratnāvadānamālā
subject: Bauddhāvadāna
date_note: = Friday 17 Jun 1892, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti subhāṣitamahāratnāvadāna [[vasundharāvratakathā samāptā]] 〈〈samāptā 〉〉 śubham astu sarvajagatāṃ sarvadā || . || yo māyābhidhamātṛsundarakarṭibhi(tyā...) yatredaṃ sūtrarājendraṃ prāvartayet kalāvapi bhāṣed yaḥ śṛṇuyād yaś ca śrāvayet yaśca cārayet || eteṣāṃ tatra sarveṣāṃ saṃbuddhāḥ sakalāḥ sadā || kṛpā dṛṣṭyā samālokya kurvantu bhadram mā bhavaṃ || sarvāḥ pāramitā devyas teṣāṃ tatra sadāśivaṃ kurvantyo bodhisaṃbhāraṃ pūrayaṃtu jagaddhite || || anena saddharmarasāmṛtena sarvajñabhāsvadvadanodbhavena || kleśānalaprahvaritāturāsu prajāsu duḥkhapraśamostu nityam || || (śubha samvat 1012 miti jyaṣṭhakṛṣṇasaptami śukravāra ṣunusvālavāhalayā vajrācāryya tejaratna naṃtrelayā paṃditapiniguratnāvadānapustaka thamanaṃ guṇaprakāśayāya pā(!) nimirttinaṃ dakṣaṇā viyāo thao tadayantā thva teyā dharmmanaṃ anūttarapadalokajuyāya thva pustaka sunānaṃ lobhayāta sādvalaṅkipaṃ ca mahāpāpalāyajula thva pustakaguptayāya madu. calaṃyāya māla. jikāya. cṅayā yhupaparyyantadarasaṇtānaṃ caleyāya māla ) (fol.368r8-368v7 )
purpose: for spreading virtues (guṇaprakāśa) and, through this merit, attaining the unsurpassed state (anuttarapada)
notes: The colophon says only 'samvat', with no era named. The catalogue suggests VS with a query, but VS 1012 (about 955 CE) does not fit a Newari-language colophon of this kind. Nepal Samvat 1012 (1892 CE) is much more likely, though the weekday has not been checked. The catalogue calls Tejaratna the scribe. The Newari reads more like this: Tejaratna paid dakṣiṇā to (or through) paṇḍitas, who are not named, to have the Ratnāvadāna book made. The paṇḍitas may therefore be the actual copyists. Two readings are unclear: 'naṃtrelayā' and the prefix 'ṣunu-' in the vihāra name. The closing clause says the book must not be hidden, must be kept in circulation and copied for future generations, and curses anyone who covets it.
review: Removed role 'donor' from Tejaratna: he paid dakṣiṇā to the paṇḍitas for producing the copy, which makes him the commissioner. The colophon does not say he donated the book.
Residence given as written ('ṣunusvālavāhala'), with the reading flagged as uncertain.
Place of copying cleared: the vihāra is Tejaratna's residence, not a stated place of copying.
Purpose rephrased: spreading of virtues (guṇaprakāśa) and merit toward the unsurpassed state (anuttarapada).
Added notes on the unnamed paṇḍitas, who may have done the actual copying, and on the clause saying the book must not be hidden but kept in circulation.
Lowered confidence from high to medium because it is unclear whether Tejaratna was scribe or commissioner.

title: Avadānaśataka
subject: Avadāna
date_note: = Friday 11 Feb 1898, weekday verified, nakṣatra not; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: ity evadāṇasatake(!) dasami(!)uddāṇagāthā samāptaṃ(!)|| || samāptaṃ ca avadāṇasatakatrayaṃ sugatabhāṣitaṃ †yaṃ hīśvarācārya†purvvam(!) idāṇi(!) prakāsitaṃ || || iti samvat 1954 sāla(!) mitiphālguṇavadi 5 roja 6 śubham saṃvat 956 mitiśrāvaṇamāse kṛṣṇapakṣa astamiyā(!) tithau rohiṇīnakṣatre vayoge(!) śaniścaravāsare siṃharāśigate śavitare(!) vṛṣarāśigate candramasi stu(!) śubham || || ❁ || 6 || 6 || 6 (fol.246r8-11 )
notes: The colophon gives two dates. (1) VS 1954 Phālguna vadi 5, roja 6 (Friday), about Feb/Mar 1898 CE. This is probably the copying date of this Devanagari manuscript. (2) NS 956 Śrāvaṇa kṛṣṇa 8, Saturday, Rohiṇī nakṣatra, sun in Siṃha, moon in Vṛṣa, about Aug/Sept 1836 CE (NS+880). This is internally consistent (Janmāṣṭamī conjunction, amānta month) and is probably the date of the exemplar, carried over from it. The two dates are 62 years apart, so they refer to different events rather than conflicting. The passage '†yaṃ hīśvarācārya† purvvam idāṇi prakāsitaṃ' is corrupt. It may hide the name of an ācārya (e.g. '…īśvara-ācārya') who 'formerly' produced or published the text, but it cannot be securely read as a person connected with this copy, so no person is recorded. 'stu' = astu. No scribe, patron or place is named.
review: weekday: 'roja 6' interpreted as Friday (6th day of the week) instead of copying the raw phrase
month normalized to Phālguna (vadi = kṛṣṇapakṣa)
nakshatra_yoga: added the corrupt yoga name 'vayoge(!)'

notes: added that the NS 956 Śrāvaṇa kṛṣṇa 8 date is internally consistent (Rohiṇī + kṛṣṇāṣṭamī = Janmāṣṭamī, sun in Siṃha, so about Aug/Sept 1836); the two eras are 62 years apart, so they are two separate events, not a conflict
persons left empty: the corrupt '†yaṃ hīśvarācārya†' is not clearly a person connected with this copy

title: Sugatāvadāna
subject: Bauddhāvadāna
colophon: iti pūrvvaśrīvasundhārā devī vratasaṃpūrṇṇaḥ asoghoṣo nandimukho avadāna parisamāptaḥ || || ❁ || ye dharmā hetuprabhāvā(!) hetu(!) teṣāṃ tathāgato hevadaṃ(!) teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha yavaṃvādi(!) mahā○śravanaḥ(!) || deyadharmmo yaṃ pravaramahāyānayāyina paramopāsakaparamadhārmika dharmmātmā1 dhyāyamātāpitṛpūrvvagamaṃnaṃ kṛtvā sakarasatvarāśe 'nuttarā samyaksaṃbodhipada prāptayantu || ❖ || svasti || śtīmallabhūupaticaranakamaradhuridhusa (fol. 96v1-5)
purpose: deyadharma; merit dedicated first to mother and father, then to all beings, for supreme enlightenment
notes: The deyadharma formula ('deyadharmo 'yaṃ pravaramahāyānayāyinaḥ paramopāsaka paramadhārmika dharmātmā …') is missing the donor's name: either the scribe left the slot empty or the name dropped out. The colophon breaks off at fol. 96v5 with 'śtīmallabhūupaticaranakamaradhuridhusa…', read as śrī-[…]-malla-bhūpati-caraṇa-kamala-dhūli-dhūsarita(-śiras) 'whose head is grey with the dust of the lotus feet of King […] Malla'. In Newar colophons this formula usually comes right before the name of the scribe or donor, which is lost here. The king's personal name is missing or omitted ('śtī' = śrī), so he cannot be identified beyond 'Malla', which matches the catalogue's '… Malla'. There is no date, so the Malla period (roughly 13th–18th c.) is the only clue to dating. The title 'pūrvvaśrīvasundhārā' is corrupt for Vasundharā, and 'asoghoṣo nandimukho' is probably Nandimukhasughoṣa-avadāna.

'virita' probably stands for 'viracita' ('composed by'), so the person is an author or compiler, not the scribe. 'bhupakamalla' may be a corrupt form of a Malla king's name (for example Bhūpatīndramalla of Bhaktapur, 1696–1722), or 'bhūpa' may be a royal epithet. 'śrīmaṃmunīndra' (= śrīman munīndra) most likely refers to the Buddha, though it could also be read with the following name. 'tapavana vimocano' may be 'tapovanavimocana', part of the title. review: Confidence for Bhūpakamalla lowered from medium to low: the whole passage is in the cataloguer's parentheses and is garbled. The name and the authorship are uncertain.

notes: The author's name is corrupt. 'paṇḍitāvavṛtaśrīmaṅkagadarppaṇa' is taken as paṇḍita-avadhūta śrī Jagaddarpaṇa, the known author of the (Ācārya)Kriyāsamuccaya. In 'śrīvajrācāryyamukuṭānamdana', the final -na is the Newari ergative ending, so the name is Mukuṭānanda. 'sabhūla coya' probably means 'wrote it in full', and 'siddhaya kāgu dina' means 'the day of completion'. The phrase 'ṣūnūsakaumūlabdeyā' before the scribe's name is unclear.
