title: Pratimāpratiṣṭhādaśakriyāvidhi
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Wednesday 14 Oct 1772, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti pratiṣṭhādaśakriyāvidhi samāptaḥ || || śubhaḥ || (30v1) likhiteyaṃ sayava tolake (tarumura)mahāvihārāvasthita raraṃkṛtavihārasya dakṣanadi(2)sagṛhāntavya vajrācāryya śrīhemā〇krana likhyate || yathā dṛṣtaṃ tathā likhitaṃ lekha(3)ko nāsti doṣaṇaṃ | yadi śurddhaṃm aśu〇rddhaṃ〇 〇 vā sodhanīya mahabuddhaiḥ || samvat 892 (4) āśviṇakṛṣṇa tṛtīyā buddhavāra 〇 thvakuhnu sidhu juroḥ || śubhamaṅgalaṃ bhavantuḥ || (fol. 30r6-30v4 / exp. 63b-64t)
notes: The scribe's name is written 'śrīhemā〇krana'. '〇' is probably a string-hole space and not a lost character, and the final '-na' is likely the Newari ergative ending, so the name reads Hemākara (Hemākara-na likhyate). The place is unclear. 'sayava tolake' is a locality (tola) in Newari locative. '(tarumura)' is the cataloguer's uncertain reading of the mahāvihāra's name. 'raraṃkṛtavihāra' may be corrupt. 'dakṣanadisagṛha' means a house on the south side (dakṣiṇadiśā). The city is not identified. The year is in NS with no conflicting era. Thvakuhnu sidhu juro (Newari) means 'completed on this day'.
review: Notes expanded: final '-na' in 'hemā〇krana' read as Newari ergative suffix (Hemākara-na), supporting the reading Hemākara; '〇' is a string-hole/space mark, not a lost akṣara
Affiliation clarified: the scribe's house is on the south side of the Raraṃkṛtavihāra, which belongs to the (Tarumura) Mahāvihāra
Date checked: NS 892 + 880 gives 1772 CE for Āśvina; buddhavāra is Wednesday

title: Vasudhārādisaptadhāraṇī
subject: Bauddhadhāraṇī
date_note: = Wednesday 17 Feb 1790, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: ’’ āryagrahamātṛkānām adhāranīparisamāptā || ye dharmmāhetu prabhāvāhetu 〈〈vā〉〉 heṣāṃ tathāgatahevadatteṣā ca yā nirodha evaṃ vādimahāśravaṇaṃ || ❁ || samvat 910 phārguṇaśuklatṛtiyā buddhavāra kunhu ṅatabhucchayātor ādharadhana ‥‥ siṃyātacosyaṃ viyājuhā … (fol.31v1–5)
notes: The Newari clause after the date is damaged: 'ṅatabhucchayā tor ādharadhana ‥‥ siṃyā tacosyaṃ viyā juhā'. It probably names someone living in the Ṅatabhuccha tol, 'ādharadhana' and a name ending in -siṃ(ha), followed by 'viyā juhā' ('gave'). 'tacosyaṃ' may be a corruption of '(ta)coyā syaṃ' ('having written'), but this is uncertain. Because of the lacuna it is unclear whether these are two persons or one name (e.g. Ādharadhana[…]siṃha), and whether the person was the scribe, the donor or the recipient, so both are recorded with role 'other' and low confidence. Ṅata is probably Nyata (Nardevi area) in Kathmandu, but this is not certain. Date: Phālguna in NS 910 falls in Feb/Mar 1790 CE; the weekday was not checked. Catalogue date NS 910 agrees.
review: p2 role 'commissioner' removed: nothing like coyakā/likhāpita survives; 'viyā juhā' (Nwr. 'gave') suggests giving or donating, but the lacuna makes this too uncertain, so the role is 'other'
p2 name given as fragment '…siṃha' and confidence lowered to low; only the ending -siṃ survives before the genitive -yā
p1 'Ādharadhana' kept but noted that p1 and p2 may be one name split by the lacuna (e.g. Ādharadhana[…]siṃha)
place.normalized cleared: Ṅata (Nyata/Nardevi, Kathmandu) is plausible but not certain, and the phrase gives a residence rather than clearly the place of copying
tithi normalised to tṛtīyā; as_written kept

title: Ugratārānāmadhāraṇī
subject: Bauddhadhāraṇī
date_note: ≈ 1760 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: || āryya eka jaṭānāmadhālanī(!) || mahogratārānāmadhāraṇī parīsamāpta(!) ||❁ || liṣitai (!) śrī 3 āryyāvareokiteśvarasyaṃ(!) caranaśevaka(!) , vajrācāryyaśrīdhatnarājaṃ riṣāyitaṃ|| saṃ 880 || (fol.29r1–3)
notes: The name is written 'dhatnarāja'. That is not a recognisable name, so the most likely reading is Ratnarāja; Dhanarāja is also possible. The catalogue's 'Donor: Śrī 3 āryyāvareokiteśvara' is a misreading. Āryāvalokiteśvara is the deity, and the scribe calls himself his 'caraṇasevaka' (servant at the feet). This may point to a link with a Lokeśvara shrine, but none is named. The verbs 'liṣitai' (likhitam) and 'riṣāyitaṃ' (likhāyitam/likhāpitam) are both tied to the same person. Newar copyists often use the causative loosely to mean 'written', so he may only have been the scribe and not also the commissioner. NS 880 converts to about 1759/60 CE. No month or day is given. The catalogue gives no reigning king, and none is named in the colophon.
review: p1 name: normalized the corrupt 'Dhatnarāja' to the probable 'Ratnarāja'. The written form is kept in as_written, and the doubt is recorded in notes and confidence.
p1 roles: kept scribe + commissioner. The roles rest on liṣitai plus riṣāyitaṃ (= likhāyitaṃ), and notes explain why the causative may be used loosely here.

purpose: For the long life, health, wealth and offspring of the yajamāna (the donor family)
notes: p5: 'likhāpitaṃ' would literally make this person the commissioner. But the sentence opens with 'likhiteyaṃ … avasthita', and the donor (dānapati) is named separately, so p5 is read here as the copyist, a resident of Hemavarṇa Mahāvihāra (Ha Bahā), Patan. The beginning of p5's name is lost: '…rahamaṇi' may be the end of a longer name such as Brahmamaṇi(?). p4 (Jayapati): the cataloguer marks his clause with [[ ]], probably a later or marginal insertion. The donor family lived in Kathmandu (Makhan Tol, Ratnakīrti Mahāvihāra), but the copy was written in Patan, so the catalogue's 'Place of Copying: Makhana Tola' seems to confuse the donor's residence with the place of copying. 'dhala-' is read as Newar l/r for 'dhara-' (perhaps Dharmamaṇilakṣmī?). Date check: NS 825 Kārttika = November 1704, which falls within Bhāskara Malla's reign (c. 1700–1714). This is consistent with the Sun in Tulā and the Moon in Mīna (Revatī).
review: p5: role changed from commissioner to scribe. The colophon says 'likhiteyaṃ … likhāpitaṃ', and the donor is named separately, so 'likhāpitaṃ' is most likely used loosely for the copyist here. Name given as '…rahamaṇi' without the -deva suffix, to match how Jayapati is treated.
p4 (Jayapati): 'beneficiary' removed. The blessing is for the yajamāna in general, and no one is named as beneficiary. Noted that he appears in the cataloguer's [[ ]] insertion.
p2 (Jayarāja): residence and affiliation emptied and confidence lowered to medium. The '...' lacuna separates the vihāra from his name, so they cannot safely be given to him.
p3: confidence lowered to medium because of the 'dhala' = dhara(?) reading. Residence and affiliation kept.
Place of copying changed to Suvarṇapraṇālī (Patan) only. Kāntipura/Makhatvala is the donor's residence, not where the copy was made, so the catalogue field 'Makhana Tola' is probably mistaken.
Date: weekday normalized to Friday (śuklavāsare = śukravāsare). Yoga given as harṣaṇa followed by vajra. ce_approx 1704 (November) confirmed.
Purpose restated briefly in English.

title: Bagalāsāṅkhyāyanatantra
subject: Śāktatantra
date_note: = Wednesday 2 Sep 1840, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīṣaḍvidyāgame śāṃkhyāyaṇataṃtre homavidhiviśeṣakathanam māma catustriṃśaḥ paṭalaḥ samāpta || || saṃvat 1897 sāla miti bhādraśudi 6 roja 4 śubham || || graṃthasaṃkhyā eka hajjāra asī siloka || || 1080 || (fol. 36r1–4)
notes: The colophon gives no era name, and the catalogue's '[ŚS]' is the cataloguer's addition. A weekday check supports VS. In VS 1897 (1840 CE), Bhādrapada śukla 6 fell on Wednesday, 2 Sept 1840: the new moon was on 28 Aug 1840 with the sun in Siṃha, and tithi 6 was current at sunrise on 2 Sept. That matches roja 4 = Wednesday. Under ŚS 1897 (1975 CE), the same tithi falls around Thursday, 11 Sept 1975, which does not match. So: VS 1897 = 2 Sept 1840 CE. The colophon names no scribe, owner or other person. 'graṃthasaṃkhyā … 1080' is the text's length in ślokas, not a date.
review: Normalized paksa 'śudi' → 'śukla' and weekday 'roja 4' → 'budhavāra (Wednesday; roja 4)'.
Set era to VS (was 'unspecified'): verified by computation, see notes.
Narrowed ce_approx to 1840 (2 Sept 1840).

title: Kālītattva
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Friday 16 Nov 1685, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti śrīrāghavabhaṭṭaviracite kālītattve rahasyādipratipādanavidhau ekaviṃśatimamaṃ tattvam || || śubha (!) || ṣaṣṭhadyogajasammite suraguror ghasre[ʼ]site pakṣake kālītatvam alekhayad vijavaraḥ śrīcakrarājaḥ sudhīḥ || māse kārttikike manohararasādevena saṃyatnataḥ pañcamyāṃ śubhayogamiśritabharaṇyāṃ tārakāyāṃ mudā || || || || || (fol. 77r7–9)
notes: The date is a verse chronogram in Śārdūlavikrīḍita: ṣaṣṭha (6), dyo/sky (0), gaja (8), read right to left = 806. No era is written. NS is inferred: it is a Nepalese manuscript, the catalogue gives 'SAM 806', and Rāghavabhaṭṭa is c. late 15th century, which rules out VS 806. NS 806 began in Kārttika 1685 CE, so Kārttika kṛṣṇa 5 of NS 806 falls in Oct/Nov 1685, not 1686. 'ghasre[ʼ]site' = ghasre + asite, i.e. the dark fortnight; 'suraguror ghasre' = Thursday. The date has not been verified. Bharaṇī is hard to reconcile with Kārttika kṛṣṇa pañcamī in either the amānta or pūrṇimānta reckoning; the nakṣatra or the pakṣa may be wrong. 'śubhayoga' may be the named yoga Śubha or a generic phrase. Names: 'vijavaraḥ' is a corruption of 'dvijavaraḥ'. Cakrarāja is the commissioner ('alekhayat'). The scribe is Manohara: 'manohararasādevena' = Manohara + rasādeva, and rasā-deva ('earth-god') is a synonym of bhūdeva, i.e. a brahmin. This agrees with the catalogue's 'Scribe: Manohara' and fits the metre.
review: Scribe: the first reading's 'Deva' is wrong. 'manohararasādevena' = manohara + rasādevena, and rasā-deva ('god of the earth') is a synonym of bhūdeva, i.e. a brahmin. So the scribe is Manohara, with 'rasādeva' (brahmin) as a title. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Manohara' is right. Confidence raised to high.
Author: 'bhaṭṭa' stripped from the name (name 'Rāghava', with bhaṭṭa kept in titles), following the rule on brahmin suffixes.
Cakrarāja: 'vijavaraḥ' marked as a corruption of 'dvijavaraḥ' (not marked by the cataloguer). 'sudhī' added as an epithet.

Date: chronogram confirmed (ṣaṣṭha 6, dyo 0, gaja 8, read right to left = 806). The era is not written and NS is inferred. ce_approx changed from 1686 to 1685, because NS 806 began in Kārttika 1685, so Kārttika kṛṣṇa of NS 806 falls in Oct/Nov 1685.
Yoga: 'śubhayoga' may be the named yoga Śubha or just 'an auspicious yoga'. This is now flagged as uncertain.
Notes rewritten: the rasādeva reading is explained, and the nakṣatra is flagged as a possible inconsistency.

title: Kālītantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Friday 16 Nov 1685, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti śrīrāghavabhaṭṭaviracite kālītattvarahasyādipratipādanavidhau ekaviṃśatimaṃ (!) tattvam || || ❁ || || śubhaṃ || ṣaṣṭhadyogajasammite suraguror ghasre[ʼ]site pakṣake kālītatvam alekhayad vijavaraḥ śrīcakrarājaḥ sudhīḥ || māse kārttikike manohararasādevena saṃyatnataḥ pañcamyāṃ śubhayogamiśritabharaṇyāṃ tārakāyāṃ mudā || || (fol. 94v5–7)
notes:
Chronogram 'ṣaṣ(ṭha)-dyo-gaja': ṣaṭ = 6, dyo (sky) = 0, gaja = 8. Read right to left this gives 806. The era is not named; it is taken as NS from the catalogue's 'SAM 806' and the Newari script. Kārttika of NS 806 falls in October–November 1685, or 1686 if the month is counted after the year's change.

Metre is Śārdūlavikrīḍita, and 'māse kārttikike manohararasādevena saṃyatnataḥ' scans correctly. So the extra syllable 'ra' is metrically needed. It may be a doubled 'ra' in the name: perhaps Manoharasa-/Manohara-deva, which would give 'Manoharadeva'. Alternatively it could be 'manohara-rasāt' plus a name 'Deva'. I follow the catalogue: Manohara.

'ghasre[ʼ]site': the dark fortnight (asita) depends on the cataloguer's avagraha. Read without it, as 'site', it would mean the bright fortnight (śukla). Neither a kṛṣṇa nor a śukla pañcamī in Kārttika fits the Bharaṇī nakṣatra well, so the date details may be faulty. Verify before converting.

Cakrarāja is called a dvija ('vijavaraḥ', missing its 'd'), so he is a brahmin. The text is given in the colophon as the 21st tattva of Rāghavabhaṭṭa's Kālītattvarahasya; the catalogue title is Kālītantra.
review: p1: name changed from 'Rāghavabhaṭṭa' to 'Rāghava'; 'bhaṭṭa' is kept only in titles.

p3: scribe's name changed from 'Deva' to 'Manohara', as in the catalogue. Splitting the word as 'manohara-rasād devena' (Deva, 'out of delight') is less likely than a personal name, and a scribe called just 'Deva' is implausible. Confidence stays medium.
p2: 'vijavaraḥ' recorded as an error for dvijavaraḥ. 'sudhīḥ' added as an epithet.

Date: 'ghasre[ʼ]site' parsed as ghasre + asite (dark fortnight, kṛṣṇa), which depends on the cataloguer's avagraha. The chronogram is confirmed as 6-0-8, read right to left = NS 806. ce_approx widened to 1685/86 because Kārttika falls at the turn of the NS year.
Notes: added the metrical check and a doubt about the nakṣatra, and removed the 'Deva' interpretation.

title: Prapañcasāratantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Sunday 9 Dec 1685, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: || iti śrīprapañcasāre caturtriṃśatiḥ (!) paṭalaḥ saṃpūrṇṇaḥ || 34 || śrīcakrarājyasya || samāptaś cāyaṃ granthaḥ || saṃsārasindhau(!) staraṇaikahetūn vande gurūn mūrddhni śivasvabhāvān rajāṃṣi yeṣāṃ padapaṅkajānāṃ tīrthābhiṣekaśriyam āvahanti || || saṃvat 806 mārgaśira śudi 14 āditya(!)ra saṃpūrṇana coyā dina || (fol. 177v4–6) iti prapañcasāra(!) samāptaṃ || śrīrastu ṣaḍabhravāruṇair yute śake caturddaśītithau pracaṇḍabhānuvāsare sumārgaśīrṣamāsi vai || śuklapakṣamiśrite prapañcasāratantrakaṃ\ sudhīś ca cakrarāja eva lekhayāñcakāraha || (exp. 187b)
purpose: commissioned by Cakrarāja for himself (book is his)
notes: The date is given twice. (1) In prose: NS 806, Mārgaśira śukla 14, Sunday (ādityavāra), the day the copy was finished. This is about Nov/Dec 1685 CE. (2) In a verse with a Śaka chronogram, 'ṣaḍabhravāruṇair yute śake'. Read right to left: ṣaḍ = 6, abhra = 0, then vāruṇa (value unclear). The catalogue's reading ŚS 1606? would need vāruṇa = 16, which is not a standard bhūtasaṃkhyā value. ŚS 1606 Mārgaśira = Nov/Dec 1684 CE, one year earlier than NS 806; the matching Śaka year would be 1607. So the two eras conflict by one year, or the chronogram is misread. NS 806 is taken as primary. The catalogue lists Cakrarāja as scribe, but the colophon only has him commissioning the copy (lekhayāñcakāra, causative) and owning it ('śrīcakrarājyasya', a spelling of śrīcakrarājasya). The scribe is not named; he may have copied it himself, but the text does not say so. 'sudhīḥ' ('learned') is an epithet, not a title.
review: Notes expanded on the Śaka chronogram: 'ṣaḍabhravāruṇair' reads right to left as 6-0-(vāruṇa), and the catalogue's ŚS 1606 needs vāruṇa = 16, which is not a standard value. ŚS 1606 Mārgaśira is about Nov/Dec 1684, but NS 806 Mārgaśira is about Nov/Dec 1685, so the two eras are one year apart. This conflict is now flagged.
Noted the spelling 'śrīcakrarājyasya' for the genitive śrīcakrarājasya. Cakrarāja is kept as commissioner and owner. No scribe is named, so the catalogue's 'Scribe: Cakrarāja' is not supported.

title: Bhūtaḍāmaratantra
subject: Saivatantra
date_raw: śambho rāri śārādharādharārākātithau mitraje | māse māghamaghe ca śobhanayute kuṃbhe ca siṃhe ʼrjune
colophon: iti bhūtaḍāmare mahātantre yakṣasiddhisādhanavidhiḥ pañcadaśaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaś cāyaṃ granthaḥ || śambho rāri śārādharādharārākātithau mitraje | māse māghamaghe ca śobhanayute kuṃbhe ca siṃhe ʼrjune | hantā dānavadāṃbhikāvaraharās sa (śadyukti) /// prādā, siṃhānaktasabhūtadāmaram asau, lekhe (!) mahadbuddhimān || || pustakalikhanapariśrama- vetāvidvajjano nānyaḥ | sāgaralaṃghanakhedaṃ- hanūmān ekaḥ paraṃ vetti || || urasi phaṇipatiḥ śikhī kapālaṃ śirasi vidhuḥ suradhunī jaṭā kailāśe sahacari kathayāmi kiṃ rahasyaṃ puramathanasya rahaḥ sabhā pareṣāṃ || || (fol. 4t5-8)
notes: The date is in verse. Rākā-tithi means the full moon of Māgha, and that fits Maghā nakṣatra and the Moon in Leo. 'Mitraje' most likely means Saturday (son of Mitra = Śani). The year chronogram 'śambho rāri śārādharādharā' is corrupt. Possible number-words include śambhu = 11, ari = 6, śara = 5, dharā = 1 and dharādhara = 7, but the word division is unclear, so no year or era can be fixed. The Newari script suggests NS. 'arjune' may stand for a planet or a corrupt word. In the second half, 'hantā dānava... prādā, siṃhā...' (slayer of the demon, [Pra]hlāda?, siṃha) may be a riddle that encodes the scribe's name, possibly Narasiṃha. This is speculative and not entered as a person. The scribe is otherwise only called 'asau ... mahadbuddhimān', who wrote ('lekhe' (!)) the Bhūtaḍāmara. The rest is stock scribal verses (pustakalikhanapariśrama..., urasi phaṇipatiḥ...).

title: Mntrārādhanadīpikā
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: ≈ 1736 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti śrīkaṃsārimiśrātmajamiśrayaśōdharaviracitāyāṃ maṃdtrārādhanadīpikāyāṃ prathamaḥ prakāśaḥ || || ❁ || || śāle vikramabhūpasya vasviṣu ṣaṭśaśiśu ca || likhitā mādhave naiva maṃtrārādhanadīpikā || ||❁ || || bhavāniśaṃkarābhyāṃ (!) namaḥ | || ❁ || lakṣmīnārāyaṇābhyāṃ namaḥ || ❁ || (fol. 16v6-8)
notes: The chronogram reads vasu (8), iṣu (5), ṣaṭ (6), śaśin (1). Read right to left, that gives 1658. The verse names the era of King Vikrama ('vikramabhūpasya'), so the year is VS 1658, about 1601 CE. 'śāle' is probably a corruption of 'śāke', which is used loosely for the era. The catalogue gives ŚS 1658 (about 1736 CE), which looks like a misreading of 'śāke/śāle'. Neither date can be ruled out completely without palaeographic evidence. 'mādhave naiva' = 'mādhavenaiva', meaning 'by Mādhava alone', so Mādhava is the scribe. The colophon covers only the first prakāśa; the copy may be incomplete. The catalogue title 'Mntrārādhanadīpikā' and the colophon's 'maṃdtrā-' are both garbled forms of 'Mantrārādhanadīpikā'. The author is Yaśodhara Miśra, son of Kaṃsāri Miśra.

purpose: "copied for (or as the property of) the brahmin Jayakalyāṇa"
notes: "The Śaka year chronogram 'vjo bhūpa' is corrupt. 'vjo' might stand for vyoma (0) and 'bhūpa' is 16. But read right to left that gives an impossible Śaka 160, so a word is probably missing. No CE year is given for that reason. Taiṣa = Pauṣa. Moon in Dhaniṣṭhā on Pauṣa śukla 4 is astronomically plausible. 'nav saṃyute' is unclear: it may hide a yoga name or a number. The scribe's name 'paḍmanārāyaṇakhaḥ' (!) is probably 'padmanārāyaṇākhyaḥ'. Jayakalyāṇa is described as a brahmin honoured by kings ('nṛṇāṃ rājñāṃ saṃmānitasya'). The genitive marks the copy as his, but the colophon does not say outright that he commissioned it. Place: Kāntipura (Kathmandu), on the Bāgmatī near Paśupati."

title: Lalitārahasyasārabhāṣyam
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Thursday 2 May 1907, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: || iti śrīmatpadavākyapramāṇapārāvārapārīṇa (!) dhuriṇā sarvataṃtraśrīmadgaṃbhīradīkṣiasūrisununā (!) bharatyupākhāne bhāskarayrāyeṇa bhāsurānaṃdanārthot (!) dīkṣānāma śālinā praṇītaṃ saubhāgyabhāskarākhyaṃ vrahmāṃṇdapurāṇīyaśrīlalitārhasyam sāhasraṃ bhāṣyaṃ samāptaṃ || || śubham || || śrīsaṃvat || 1027 caitrakṛṣṇaroja. 5..se śrī lalitāpuramahāvuddhavodhimadayasa vijyākalaśrīmarendranandanaṃ coyā sidhayakā jula śūbham || || (fol. 240r10–12, v1–3)
notes: The colophon is in Newari ('coyā sidhayakā jula' = written and completed), so the era is Nepāla Saṃvat: NS 1027 = c. 1907 CE. VS or ŚS 1027 would fall before Bhāskararāya (18th century), so neither is possible. 'roja. 5' is unclear: 'roja' (day) may mark 5 as the tithi or as a weekday number (5 = Thursday). Here 5 is taken as the tithi. The scribe's name 'śrīmarendranandanaṃ' is probably a slip for śrī-Narendranandana, as on the catalogue card. The word before it, 'vijyākala', is unclear: it may be a corrupt epithet or title, or part of the name. The place is the Mahābuddha (Mahābauddha) area/vihāra in Lalitpur (Patan), written 'mahāvuddhavodhimadaya-sa' with the locative -sa. Bhāskararāya is the author of the Saubhāgyabhāskara commentary on the Lalitāsahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa). The colophon gives his surname as Bhāratī (corrupt 'bharatyupākhāne') and his dīkṣā name as Bhāsurānandanātha (corrupt 'bhāsurānaṃdanārthot'). The text title is corrupt in the catalogue ('lalitārhasyam sāhasraṃ').

notes: The colophon gives two dates in saṃvat 1754: Kuāra (Āśvina) śuklapakṣa and Kārttika kṛṣṇapakṣa. In pūrṇimānta reckoning, which is normal at Kāśī, these are consecutive fortnights, so they probably mark the progress or completion of the copy. The catalogue reads the year as ŚS 1754. However, a plain 'saṃvat' in a North Indian (Kāśī) colophon is normally Vikrama, which gives VS 1754 ≈ 1697 CE; ŚS would give 1832 CE. 'samaai/samai nāma' is unclear; it may stand for samaya or a garbled saṃvatsara name. 'gaṃgā (!)' before the first saṃvat is probably part of the invocations rather than an era name. The scribe Nāthurāma Kāyastha is said to be 'of Nizāmābād' (nījāmāvāda ke). This is probably the Nizamabad near Azamgarh, UP, but the identification is not certain. The catalogue's 'Date of composition: SAM 1550' is the date of Rāghavabhaṭṭa's commentary (Padārthādarśa, c. VS 1550 ≈ 1493/94 CE) and is not stated in this colophon. The deity invocations (Gopāla, Viśveśvara, Rāma, Gaṇapati, Govinda, Gaṅgā, Nārāyaṇa, Śaṅkara, Mahādeva, 'manumāna' = Hanumān?) are not persons.
review: Kept both persons; only minor refinements.
p2 residence normalized to 'Nizāmābād' (nījāmāvāda ke), with the identification marked as probable; evidence shortened.
Date notes: the two dates are probably consecutive fortnights in pūrṇimānta reckoning (Āśvina śukla, then Kārttika kṛṣṇa), so CE 1697 (c. Sept.–Oct.). Added that 'samaai/samai nāma' is unclear.
Notes: the catalogue's composition date (SAM 1550) is the commentary's own date, not the copying date; 'gaṃgā saṃvat' is probably an invocation run together with the date.

title: Nānauṣadhakalpa
subject: (Tantra)Āyurveda
date_note: = Wednesday 11 Nov 1857, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīherambāecanavidhi saṃpūrśubhma (!) || |samvat 1914 sāla miti mārgavadi 11 roja 4 śubhma || || huṃ || (aṭala) || robhayānā kāladhālā paṃcamahāpāpa (!) thosaphu dhirjavīrasiṃha yāgu (exp.23.b:4-7)
notes: The phrase 'robhayānā kāladhālā paṃcamahāpāpa' is a Newari curse against theft. It reads as lobha yānā kāla dhāla(sā) pañcamahāpāpa(ka), 'if anyone takes [this book] out of greed, [may he incur] the five great sins'. So 'kāladhālā' is not a place of copying, and the catalogue's 'kāladhārā' is a misreading. 'thosaphu dhirjavīrasiṃha yāgu' means 'this book belongs to Dhirjavīrasiṃha'. He is the owner, and nothing in the colophon says he copied it, so the catalogue's 'Scribe' label is unsupported (he may be scribe-owner, but that cannot be shown). The name may stand for Dhīrajavīrasiṃha / Dhīra-Javīra Siṃha. The colophon's title is 'śrīherambāecanavidhi' (= Herambārcanavidhi), not Nānauṣadhakalpa, so this colophon may close a sub-text in a composite MS. '(aṭala)' after 'huṃ' is unclear (possibly a seal or a closing word). VS 1914 Mārgaśīrṣa ≈ Nov/Dec 1857 CE.
review: Place removed: 'kāladhālā' is not a toponym but part of the Newari curse formula 'robhayānā kāladhālā' = lobha yānā kāla dhāla(sā) 'if anyone takes [it] out of greed'; the catalogue's Place of Copying 'kāladhārā' and the normalization 'Kathmandu' are both wrong
Residence of Dhirjavīrasiṃha cleared (it came from the same misreading)
Weekday rendered as Wednesday (roja 4)
Notes rewritten: the curse formula is explained, owner-only role kept, colophon title Herambārcanavidhi noted

title: Vaidyajīvana
subject: Āyurveda
date_raw: śāke 1714 saṃvat 18〈〈8〉〉90āśvī dvitīyā 2 mamgalavāra , [ṭikā: VS khaṃ vahni siṃdubhir (!) jeṣṭakṛṣṇa 7 bhṛguvāra] (!)
date_note: = Tuesday 1 Oct 1833, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīman manohara sūnunā gosvāminā harinātha kṛtāyāṃ vaidyajīvanaṭīkāyāṃ praṃcamo (!) vilāsaḥ || śrīmad bhūpati vikramādgaṇanā khaṃ vahni sindhubhisindubhi(!)r || māse jeṣṭa (!) asi saptamī tithai (!) vāre bhṛguśoriyaṃ || ṭīkā || vaidyajivanasya(!)racī || śrīnātha gosvāmibhīr cautastvaṃṭamārithe śarayure dhāryā bhiṣagbhiḥ || sadā || likhiṃ[[ta]] puruṣottama bhrāmhana (!) paṃḍītasya (!) chaganajīvrane pustakalītaṃ (!) pustakaṃ || miti āsvī dvitīyāṃ 2 maṃgalavāsare || || saṃvat || || 1890 || || vṛṣe śākha || || 17 || 14 || || śubhaṃ bhūyāt || śrī mutharaśa (!) || ❁ || ❖ ❁ śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ || ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ (fol.67r1–67v3)
notes:
The copy is dated VS 1890 (c. 1833 CE). The following 'vṛṣe śākha 17 14' would be ŚS 1714 (c. 1792 CE). That conflicts with the VS year, which corresponds to ŚS 1755. 'vṛṣe' may be the name of the Jovian year (Vṛṣa) rather than part of the era. The Vikrama year is preferred here.

The verse 'śrīmad bhūpati vikramād gaṇanā khaṃ vahni sindhubhi sindubhir ... jyeṣṭha asi saptamī ... bhṛgau iyaṃ ṭīkā ... racī(tā) śrīnātha gosvāmibhiḥ' gives the date when the ṭīkā was COMPOSED (Jyeṣṭha, dark half, day 7, a Friday), not the copy date. The chronogram is uncertain. Read right to left, kha=0 and vahni=3 give a year ending in -30. The doubled 'sindhu' (4 or 7) looks like dittography, so a reading such as VS 1730 cannot be secured.

The commentator is 'harinātha' in the prose colophon but 'śrīnātha gosvāmibhiḥ' in the verse; this is probably 'śrī[hari]nātha'.

'cautastvaṃṭamārithe śarayure dhāryā bhiṣagbhiḥ' is garbled, roughly 'to be kept by physicians'. A place name (Sarayū?) is possible but uncertain.

'chaganajīvrane' is probably a corruption of Chaganajīvana (+ -ena/-sya). The book is said to be his ('paṇḍitasya ... pustakaṃ'). 'paṇḍita' could instead belong to Puruṣottama.

The final 'śrī mutharaśa (!)' is unclear: it may be Mathurā (the place) or a personal name. It is not recorded as either.

notes: The catalogue gives ŚS 1789, but the colophon reads 'śrīśāke 1719' (= 1797 CE, Mārgaśīrṣa, so Nov./Dec. 1797). The 1719 reading fits the Gorkha occupation of Kumaon (1790–1815), when a Subbā (governor) Prabal Rāṇā would be plausible, so the catalogue figure is probably a misprint. 'Pravala' is probably Prabala/Prabal. 'Yogyeṣu likhitam' means 'written for (the use of)': it makes him the owner/beneficiary and probably the commissioner. The colophon does not support the catalogue's 'Donor'. Gaṃgāvālī = Gaṅgolī in Kumaon. The colophon gives it as the scribe's residence ('nivāsinā'), not explicitly as the place of copying. Paṃta = Pant, a Kumaoni brahmin surname. Vaṅgasena (son of Gadādhara) is the author of the text.

colophon: samvat 713 jeṣṭha kṛṣṇa tṛtīyāyāṃ utrāṣāḍha (!) nakṣatra budhavāra thva kvahnu jayadatta nāma śāḍaṃyā śāstra coya dhuṃṅa dina juro || thva pustaka śrī śrī jayanārāyanāvatāra parameśvara paramabhaṭṭāraka rājādhirāja śrī śrī jagajjyotirmmalladeva prabhu ṭhākuras taṃ śrī jayantarājadevana coyā juro || e || śrī bhavānīśaṃkarābhyāṃ namaḥ || śubham astu || || [[❖śrī śrī sumati jayajitāmitramalladevasana thva ustaka dalavārayā kayaña gadāṅa guli dukā syaṃta yā juro || bhāgīrāma paramāna yā varasa || samvat 808 śrāvaṇa vadi 13 śubah ||]] (fol. 56v1–6)
notes:
The main colophon says that in NS 713 (c. 1593 CE), Jayantarājadeva copied Jayadatta's treatise on horses (Aśvaśāstra) for the lord Jagajjyotirmalla. The reading of 'prabhu ṭhākuras taṃ' is unclear: it could mean 'for the lord' or 'by the lord himself'. Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur reigned c. NS 734-757 (1614-1637 CE), so in NS 713 he could only have been a prince. Either the regnal titles were added later or the year is miscopied (perhaps 733?).

The bracketed later note is dated NS 808 Śrāvaṇa vadi 13 (c. 1688 CE). That date fits the reign of Jitāmitramalla of Bhaktapur (c. 1673-1696). The note records that the king acquired this book from the son of Dalavāra by paying a sum of money (gadāṅa; 'dukā syaṃta'). Bhāgīrāma acted as witness (paramāna = pramāṇa). 'varasa' is unclear. title: Devībhāgavatapurāṇa

date_note: = Friday 7 May 1529, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: current year, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrīdevībhāgavate mahāpurāṇe ṣṭādaśasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyyāśikyāṃ dvādaśaskaṃdhe trayodaśo dhyāyaḥ || || samāptaś cāyaṃ skandhaḥ || lekhakapāṭhakayo śubham astu bhūpaṃ ca parjanyayuteṣu śāke śukrākhyamāsāsitapakṣake ravau śaṃbhos tithau vipravaro lilekha triśaktimāhātmyayutaṃ kathānakam || 1 || (fol. 22v3–5)
notes: 'Vipravaro lilekha' most likely means 'an excellent brahmin wrote [this]', which hides the scribe's name. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Vipravara' takes the epithet as a name, so it is doubtful. The chronogram 'bhūpaṃ ca parjanya-' appears corrupt; the catalogue reads it as bhū-pañca-parjanya. Parjanya is not a standard number word. If it stands for Indra (= 14), reading right to left gives ŚS 1451 = c. 1529 CE. That is only a guess, and other values for parjanya would change the year. Śukra is the old name for Jyeṣṭha. 'Śambhos tithi' is most probably caturdaśī (Śiva's tithi; kṛṣṇa 14 = Śivarātri), but ekādaśī (Rudra = 11) or aṣṭamī cannot be ruled out. The colophon ends Skandha 12, adhyāya 13, and includes a stock blessing for the writer and reader (lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ śubham astu).

Tithi changed from ekādaśī to caturdaśī (probable). 'Śambhos tithi' names the tithi whose deity is Śiva, which is the 14th; kṛṣṇa caturdaśī is Śivarātri. Ekādaśī (Rudra = 11) and aṣṭamī are noted as alternatives.
Year: added a tentative reading of parjanya as Indra = 14, read right to left with bhū 1 and pañca 5 to give ŚS 1451 (≈1529 CE). It is marked as uncertain.

purpose: kṛṣṇaprīti (for Kṛṣṇa's pleasure); closing benediction: śrī 3 nārāyaṇaprītir astu
notes: The chronogram bāla(=bāṇa, 5)-vahni(3)-vasu(8), read right to left, gives 835. The era is not written; Nepal Saṃvat (NS) is assumed, giving NS 835 = c. 1715 CE (Caitra amāvāsyā). After the colophon comes a separate Newari note, 'samvat 1013 kārttikavadi 11 maṅgalavāla' (NS 1013 = c. 1892/93 CE, a Tuesday). It names Maheśvarānanda (written maheśavarānanda) of Ukubahāḥ, Patan, and breaks off ('///-') before saying what he did. The catalogue gives both scribes and both dates. Two readings are possible: (a) the NS 1013 note is a later owner's or reader's entry, or (b) Maheśvarānanda copied the manuscript in NS 1013 and carried over Harinārāyaṇa's NS 835 verse colophon from his exemplar. In case (b), Harinārāyaṇa would be the scribe of the exemplar, not of this copy. A look at the folio, its script and its hands is needed to decide. title: Matsyapurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Tuesday 14 Oct 1890, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīmatsyapurāṇe pāramasaṃhitāyāṃ anukramaṇikākhyaṃ matsyapurāṇaṃ samāptaṃ || 275 || liṣitaṃ tat tu kṣeyā(!) śrīvajrācāryye machindraviranāthanatho śāstra coyā julo || || samvat 1010 miti āśvinaśudi 1 roa 3 sasaṃpūrṇadhikādina julo || || maganāpuratamadhitolayā śrīupādhyāyahaladhāyānacoyā vaviyā julaḥ || yādṛśa ... doṣaka(!) || || śubhm || || (fol. 243v3–5)
notes: The colophon contains two Newari statements about writing. (1) 'śrīvajrācāryye machindraviranātha-na tho śāstra coyā julo' means 'Vajrācārya Machindravīranātha wrote this śāstra'. The verb is 'coyā' (wrote), not the causative 'coyakā', so he is the scribe, not the commissioner. (2) 'maganāpura tamadhi tola-yā śrī upādhyāya haladhāyāna coyā vaviyā julaḥ': 'haladhāyāna' is probably Haladhara-na (ergative), and 'vaviyā' is probably biyā ('gave' / 'wrote for someone'). The catalogue takes Haladhara as the scribe. If the ending is really -yāta, the sentence would mean the book was written and given TO Haladhara, making him the recipient or owner. So the relationship between the two men is unclear: they may be two scribes, or one may be the scribe and the other the recipient. The opening 'liṣitaṃ tat tu kṣeyā(!)' is corrupt. Maganāpura with Tamadhi ṭol is given as Haladhara's locality; it is not identified, and it is not stated as the place of copying. The era is read as NS: 1010 VS would be impossible for a Newari-language Devanagari colophon of this kind. That gives NS 1010 = c. 1890 CE. 'sasaṃpūrṇadhikādina' = the day of completion.
review: p1 Machindravīranātha: role changed from commissioner to scribe. Newari 'coyā' means 'wrote' (the causative would be 'coyakā'), and 'machindraviranātha-na tho śāstra coyā julo' means 'Machindravīranātha wrote this śāstra'. Confidence lowered to medium.

p2 Haladhara: kept as scribe, following the catalogue, but confidence lowered to medium. The phrase 'haladhāyāna coyā vaviyā' is corrupt, and Haladhara could instead be the person it was written for. Residence normalized to Tamadhi ṭol, Maganāpura.
Removed the wrote_for relation. The colophon gives no clear basis for saying p2 wrote for p1.
Date: pakṣa normalized to śukla and weekday to Tuesday (roa 3 = roja 3). NS 1010 = c. 1890 CE confirmed.
Place: kept, but the notes now say it is stated as Haladhara's locality, not explicitly as the place of copying.

The verse names the month as Jyeṣṭha (pūrṇimānta), while the prose has Vaiśākha kṛṣṇa (amānta). These are the same new moon (kuhū), so the two do not conflict. 'ujhā' (Ojhā, Maithil brahmin surname/title) with honorific -ju and dative -yatā: Kālidāsa received the book. The giver is not named explicitly but is presumably the scribe. 'vāravāhlācake(!)' is corrupt and unclear; it could be a place or a verb phrase, so it is not used as the place of copying. 'līlādāsa vayusmata(!)stutikathāmahātmyayustaṃ(!)' is corrupt. Līlādāsa could be a personal name, but it is more likely part of a description of the text, so it is not entered as a person. 'jagatsvāmine' refers to the deity, not a person.

notes: The colophon is in Nepali. It says Sardār Candravīra had the Brahmottarakhaṇḍa copied at Śrīnagara through (mārphata) Mahānanda Paṇḍita. Mahānanda may have been the actual copyist, or only the paṇḍita who arranged the copying. The text does not say which. Candravīra is probably Candravīra Kũvar, a Gorkhali sardār in Garhwal during the Gorkha occupation (1804–1815). That fits Śrīnagara = Srinagar in Garhwal, but the identification is not certain. The date is VS 1863 Phālguna kṛṣṇa 4, a Thursday, which is about Feb/Mar 1807 CE; the weekday was not checked against an ephemeris. The catalogue fields do not match the colophon. No Hariścandra appears in the quoted text; he may be named elsewhere in the manuscript. King Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa Śāha died in 1775, so he cannot be the reigning king; in 1807 the king was Girvāṇayuddha Vikrama Śāha, who is not named here.

The ending -jī in Kānhajī may be an honorific (stem Kānha), but it is kept because it works as the name in this western/central Indian usage. The colophon's 'dvivedī' stands before the father's name; giving it to the son as well is inferred from shared family status and the catalogue's 'Someśvara Dvivedī'. The catalogue names only Someśvara as scribe, but the colophon names both men. VS 1775 = c. 1718 CE (Bhādrapada, probably August–September 1718). Avaṃtīnagara = Ujjain. This is a non-Nepalese (Mālwā) manuscript.
review: Added 'owner' to both scribes: 'svavācanārthaṃ' means the copy was made for their own reading ('paropakārārthaṃ vā' = or for others' benefit).
Added the title 'dvivedī' to Someśvara as well. The family surname covers father and son, which matches the catalogue's 'Someśvara Dvivedī'.
Normalised the weekday 'caṃdravāsara' to 'Monday' and the tithi to 'kṛṣṇa 4'.
Changed the purpose field to a short normalised form.
Expanded the notes: the -jī ending, the ubhābhyāṃ correction and the word division.

title: Itihāsasamuccaya
subject: Itihāsa
date_note: = Monday 10 Apr 1679, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: || itihāsasamuccaye nāradapuṇḍarīkasaṃvādo nāma dvātriṃśatitamoʼdhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || || lasannākanāthā layenopamāne, mahīmaṇḍāsmin pure bhaktasaṃjñe | nṛpe śāsati śrījitāmitra malle, kaniṣṭhogramalle virājatpratāpe || nepāle hāyanesmin grahanidhi turage caitramāse tamiśre, vaidhṛtyāṃ revatī divasakara śaśina saṃgame somavāre | devīprītyā sudhīmān śivahari dharaṇī daivatoyetihāsaṃ, vyāsoktaṃ pustakātryāṃ vitarāte śivasiṃhaḥsma daivajñe dhīraḥ || (fol. 161r2–5)
purpose: for the pleasure of the Goddess (devīprītyā)
notes: Chronogram graha (9), nidhi (9), turaga (7), read right to left, gives NS 799 = 1679 CE. This falls within Jitāmitramalla's reign at Bhaktapur (1673–1696), with his younger brother Ugramalla named beside him. The catalogue's 'NS 997' reads the chronogram left to right and is wrong. 'divasakara-śaśina-saṃgame' means the sun–moon conjunction, i.e. Caitra amāvāsyā. Revatī as the nakṣatra fits this, since the sun sits at the end of Mīna. The second verse is corrupt ('daivatoyetihāsaṃ', 'pustakātryāṃ' perhaps for pustakākhyaṃ/pustakārthaṃ, 'vitarāte' for vitarate, 'śivasiṃhaḥsma'). It has two nominative agents: Śivahari, a learned brahmin (dharaṇīdaivata), who 'gives' (vitarate) the Itihāsa spoken by Vyāsa, and Śivasiṃha, the daivajña. The verse does not say who wrote and who gave. Treating Śivahari as donor and Śivasiṃha as scribe follows the catalogue and the order of the verse, but it is not certain. Śivasiṃha could also be the donor/giver, with Śivahari as a person or exemplar source in another case.
review: p3 Śivahari: role changed from 'commissioner' to 'donor'. The verb is vitarate ('gives, bestows'), and no likhāpita or lekhayāmāsa appears. Confidence stays medium.
p4 Śivasiṃha: confidence lowered to medium. The verse has no explicit 'likhitam'. The scribe role rests on the catalogue and on his being named last as the daivajña.

Date confirmed: graha 9, nidhi 9, turaga 7, read right to left, gives NS 799 = 1679 CE. Caitra kṛṣṇa amāvāsyā, Revatī, Vaidhṛti and Monday all agree with each other. The catalogue's NS 997 is a misreading (read left to right).
Purpose clarified as 'for the pleasure of the Goddess (devīprītyā)'.
Notes expanded on the syntactic ambiguity of the second verse.

title: itihāsasamuccaya
subject: Itihāsa

colophon: || itihāsasamuccaye nāradapuṇḍarīkasaṃvādo nāma catvāriṃśatitamoʼdhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || 40 || || aṣṭāṃkasvarasaṃyāte mārggakṛṣṇe śubhetvadaḥ | caturddaśyāṃ gurorvvāre likhitāʼntakrśariḥ || || saṃpūrṇṇa (fol. 144v5–6)
notes: The chronogram is aṣṭa = 8, aṅka = 9, svara = 7. Read right to left, this gives 798. The colophon does not name the era. 'śubhetvadaḥ' is corrupt, probably for something like śubhe 'hani. The scribe's name is corrupt. 'likhitāʼntakrśariḥ' probably stands for 'likhito 'nantakeśarī' (ananta- with the syllable 'na' lost, and krśari for keśarī). This matches the catalogue's reading, Anantakeśarī. review: Notes expanded: the era is not named and NS is inferred; the right-to-left reading of the chronogram is spelled out; the corrupt name segment is explained.

title: Viṣṇupurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Friday 6 Nov 1693, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīviṣṇupurāṇe ṣaṣṭhaṃśe ṣṭamo dhyāyaḥ ṣaṣṭhāṃśaś ca samāpta iti || śrīśrīśrīviṣṇuprītir astu || ... saṃ 814 kārttikaśukla 9 thvakunhu śrīśrīsumatijayajitāmitramalladevasanabhāgirāmapradhānāṅgayā velasathva viṣṇupurāṇamahāyatnanadayakā ana helāya yamateva ... yāya māla || || (fol. 177v1–3)
purpose: for the pleasure of Viṣṇu (viṣṇuprītir astu)
notes: The catalogue gives the date as SAM 818, but the quoted colophon reads 'saṃ 814' (NS 814 = 1693 CE). The year 814 fits the reign of Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur, who ruled until about NS 816 (1696). By NS 818 the king was Bhūpatīndra Malla, so 818 is probably a catalogue error. The catalogue also names the scribe as 'Bhāgīmāna Pradhāna', which looks like a garbled form of 'Bhāgirāma Pradhān(āṅga)'. In the colophon, Bhāgirāma appears only in a time phrase: 'pradhānāṅgayā velasa' means 'in the time of (minister) Bhāgirāma'. Nothing marks him as the scribe, and no scribe is named in the quoted text. The king is in the ergative case ('-sana') and is the agent of 'mahāyatnana dayakā' ('had it made with great effort'), so he is the commissioner. colophon: || iti śrīmahābhārate śatasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyāśikyāṃ śāṃtiparvaṇi uttamānuśāsike dānadharme bhīṣmasvargārohaṇaṃ nāmo ʼdhyāyaḥ || 166 || || || || śubham || sarabhaśaka (!) ....................ntisattaḥ (!) || ❁ || śubham astu || ❁ || sampūrṇaṃm (fol. 204r9–12)
notes: The only colophon is the chapter colophon: adhyāya 166, Bhīṣmasvargārohaṇa, in the Dānadharma section. The text calls it 'śāṃtiparvaṇi uttamānuśāsike', but this is the final chapter of the Anuśāsanaparvan. After it comes a corrupt passage with a lacuna, 'sarabhaśaka (!) .... ntisattaḥ (!)'. This might once have held a date, perhaps with 'śaka', or a scribal statement, but no name, era, year or place can be recovered from it. The physical manuscript should be checked at fol. 204r9–12.
review: No persons, date or place added; notes expanded on the damaged line 'sarabhaśaka ... ntisattaḥ', which may be a garbled date or scribe statement (e.g. a Śaka year) but is not recoverable

title: Mahābhārata
subject: Mahābhārata
date_note: = Sunday 26 Feb 1769, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīmahābhārataśataāhasryā vaiyāsakyāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ānuśāsanike parvaṇi bhīṣmaniryāṇaṃ || 155 || || samāptam idaṃm ānuśāsanikaṃ bhāratasya trayodaśaṃ parvaṇi || || 13 || śubhaṃ bhavatu || śrīr astu || samvat 1825 miti phā. va 6 (fol. 172v4–5)
notes: The era is not stated. 'samvat ... miti' in a Devanagari manuscript points to Vikrama Saṃvat, so 1825 VS gives about 1768 CE; Phālguna vadi 6 would most likely be in Feb/Mar 1769 CE. The catalogue field says SAM 1872 (about 1815 CE), which does not match the 1825 quoted from fol. 172v (Anuśāsanaparvan end). The 1872 date may come from another part of the multi-part reel B 260/2, or it may be a catalogue error. The colophon names no scribe, patron or other historical person. 'vaiyāsakyāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ' is part of the title formula, so Vyāsa is not recorded as a person.
review: Era kept as VS, but the notes now say it is inferred: the colophon has only 'samvat' plus 'miti', which is the usual pattern for Vikrama dates in Devanagari manuscripts from Nepal.
ce_approx stays 1768 (1825−57). The notes add that Phālguna kṛṣṇa 6 of VS 1825 most likely falls in February/March 1769 CE.
Expanded the note on the catalogue's SAM 1872: it may belong to another part or another dated colophon of reel B 260/2, so it does not have to be a misreading.

colophon: || iti śrī mahābhārate virāṭaparvaṇī satasahāśvā. Saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyāsikyāṃ dvisaptatitamo dhyāya (!) || 72 || || samāptaṃ śubham || || kāyaṇavāca………………….. doṣo na diyate (!) || svasti śrīśāke 1796 || śrīvikramādi 1931 śrīnepālī śrayos tu samvat 994 sālam iti naṣṭa āṣāḍhavadi 8 roja 3 mā liṣitaṃ śubham || likhāpaītvā (!) sakodeśe jalaṣu tola vāgvatuthikṣeyānhulakṣanārāṃyā (!) manasa dharmacitta utpattijuyā bhvate bhāṣasaphulatokātayā jula śubhaṃ (fol. 128v12–21)
purpose: merit: copy had made because a pious mind arose (dharmacitta utpatti juyā)
notes: The three eras agree: ŚS 1796 + 78 = VS 1931 − 57 = NS 994 + 880 = 1874 CE. The word 'naṣṭa' before āṣāḍhavadi is unclear. It may be a scribal word, or it may mark a kṣaya/irregular month; this has not been checked. The catalogue names Lakṣyanārāyaṇa as the scribe. However, likhāpaītvā (= likhāpayitvā, 'having caused to be written') together with 'dharmacitta utpattijuyā' suggests he was the patron who had the copy made. He may also have done the writing himself, but the colophon does not say so. His name is corrupt (lakṣanārāṃyā with Newari genitive -yā; possibly Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa). The 'nhu' before it and the string 'vāgvatuthikṣe' are unclear and may be part of a locality or a corrupt word, so they are not treated as an affiliation. The closing Newari phrase 'bhvate bhāṣasaphulatokātayā jula' is obscure.

title: Satyanārāyaṇakathā
subject: Kathā
date_note: = Monday 17 Jan 1848, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: pustakam etat stynārāyaṇasya śrīmajajagddhara (!) paṃtebhyo kurmāṃcalasthe[[bhyo]] kurmācalīya hutahut (!) [[te]]bhyo svahastena saṃpūrṇīkṛty smvt vedābhrāṅkabhūmimite pau[[ṣe]] māsi śukla[[pa]]kṣe trayodaśyāṃ somo samrpiteti śubham || (fol. 10r8–10)
purpose: gift: copy completed in the giver's own hand and presented (samarpitā) to Jagaddhara Paṃta of Kurmācala
notes:
The chronogram vedābhrāṅkabhūmi reads 4-0-9-1; read right to left this gives 1904. The colophon has only 'saṃvat', so the era is not stated. In Kumaon this almost certainly means VS, which gives Dec 1847 or Jan 1848 CE (Pauṣa śukla 13). The weekday (Monday) has not been verified.

Jagaddhara Paṃta (Pant, a Kumaoni brahmin family name), of Kurmācala, is named in the honorific plural dative as the person who received the book. He is not the scribe, so the catalogue's Scribe field is a misreading. The person who completed the copy 'with his own hand' (svahastena saṃpūrṇīkṛtya) and gave it away is not named. 'kurmācalīya hutahut[te]bhyo' is corrupt. It is probably a further honorific description of Jagaddhara, for example something built on hutabhuj ('fire-priest' / agnihotrin). It could also be a second recipient, but this is uncertain. Kurmācala is Jagaddhara's residence; the colophon does not explicitly give it as the place of copying, although the copy was probably made there.
review: p1 Jagaddhara: role 'beneficiary' replaced by 'other' (recipient of the gift); 'owner' kept because the book was handed over to him. He is not the scribe, so the catalogue's Scribe field is wrong.
Evidence shortened to the dative phrase plus samarpitā.
Place of copying emptied: the colophon gives Kurmācala only as Jagaddhara's residence ('kurmāṃcalasthebhyo'), not as the place where the copy was made.
Purpose changed from 'parārtha' to a specific gift statement.
ce_approx explained: Pauṣa śukla 13 of VS 1904 falls around Dec 1847 or Jan 1848.
Notes extended to cover the unnamed copyist/donor and the corrupt word 'hutahut[te]bhyo'.

colophon: iti śrīmadrāmeśvara(20r1)bhaṭṭasutanārāyaṇabhaṭṭaviracitāyāṃ śakuṃtalaprākṛtavivṛtau saptamokaḥ (!) samāptaḥ || || saṃvat 1885 miti (vaiiśapya) vadī (!) 10 saṃmaye (!) bhādrapada || śuklā tṛtīyā ravau ṣubhadine †yapurvehinaṇepīnāpya† brāhmaṇena liṣitam idaṃ pustakaṃ || (fol. 19v9-20r2)
notes: 1) Date: the catalogue gives 'ŚS 1848', but the colophon reads 'saṃvat 1885'. 1848 may be a misreading or a digit swap. The era is not named. In this context saṃvat with miti/vadī most likely means VS 1885, about 1828 CE. If it were ŚS 1885, the date would be 1963 CE, which is unlikely. 2) The colophon has two day-dates that don't agree: 'miti (vaiiśapya) vadī 10' (perhaps Vaiśākha kṛṣṇa 10) and 'bhādrapada śuklā tṛtīyā ravau'. The Bhādrapada date is recorded here. 3) Scribe: the cataloguer marks the text before 'brāhmaṇena' as corrupt (†yapurvehinaṇepīnāpya†). It may not be a personal name. It could, for example, contain a garbled place or ethnic word (…nepālīya?). The only certain point is that the scribe was a brāhmaṇa. 4) Nārāyaṇa, son of Rāmeśvara, wrote the Prākṛta commentary on the Śākuntala; he is not connected with this copy.

p3: the scribe's name is in the cataloguer's crux (†…†) and may not be a name at all. It could be a garbled place or descriptive word before 'brāhmaṇena'. The string is kept as written, with low confidence and a note.

notes: The era is not named, but NS is implied by the reign of Nṛpendramalla of Kathmandu (c. NS 794–800 / 1674–1680 CE). The chronogram navavivaravāha gives nava = 9, vivara = 9 (the nine openings of the body) and vāha = 7 (the horses of the sun). Read right to left, that is 799, so NS 799 ≈ 1679 CE. The catalogue's NS 709 is probably a misreading of the chronogram, since 709 would fall outside his reign. Nepāla is given as the scribe's residence (nepālādhirvāsinā, read nepālādhivāsinā); the place of copying is not stated separately. 'dijanmanā' should read dvijanmanā. 'naipāyikavāraṇapaṃcānana' should read naiyāyikavāraṇapañcānana, an epithet of the author Murāri. The weekday (Monday) has not been checked against the tithi.

title: Mālatīmādhava
subject: Nāṭaka
date_note: = Wednesday 3 Nov 1694, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīmālatīmādhavaṃ nāma nāṭakaṃ sampūrṇam || || saṃvat 1616 mārgaśira vadi 1 dine budhavāsare śrīmad †vṛ(14) varatadagacchebha 0 † śrījinaharṣasūriguruṇāṃ saṃāne śrīmānakīrtimahopādhyānaṃ śiṣya paṃ. śrīdevakalaśamunipaṇḍitapravara (15) /// śiṣya vinayasāgaramunilibhir likhitaṃ || śrīdillīnagaramadhye || śubhaṃ bhavatu lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ (fol. 31v13–15)
notes: This is a Jain (Śvetāmbara, apparently Kharatara) colophon written in Delhi, not a Nepalese one. Era: 'saṃvat' in a western Jain colophon is normally Vikrama, so VS 1616 = 1559 CE. The catalogue's 'ŚS 1616 ?' is probably wrong, and the weekday has not been verified. The gaccha name is corrupt (†vṛ(14) varatadagacchebha 0†), and 'bṛhatkharataragaccha' is a conjecture. Caution: the best-known Kharatara pontiff called Jinaharṣasūri flourished c. VS 1856–1892 (I am recalling this, not checking a source). If that is the man meant, it would fit a date of VS 1916 better than 1616, so the numeral may have been misread. The point needs checking against the photographs. 'saṃāne' should read 'santāne' (lineage), and 'mahopādhyānaṃ' should read 'mahopādhyāyānāṃ'. The '///' before 'śiṣya' marks damage, so there may be intermediate pupils between Devakalaśa and Vinayasāgara. 'munilibhir' is probably a mistake for 'munibhir' or 'muninā'. The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Sāgaramuni', but the colophon reads Vinayasāgara(muni).
review: p1: name stripped to 'Jinaharṣa' (sūri is a title); affiliation given as conjectural Bṛhatkharataragaccha for the corrupt 'vṛ varatadagaccha'; confidence for the gaccha lowered
p1: role changed from 'teacher' to 'other'. 'santāne' (written saṃāne) means 'in the lineage of', so he is the head of the lineage, not the direct teacher
p2→p1 relation changed from pupil_of to other (lineage, santāne)
p3: titles reduced to paṇḍita and muni (paṃ. = paṇḍita; paṇḍitapravara is an epithet)
p4: confidence lowered to medium and p4→p3 relation flagged, because the lacuna (///) before 'śiṣya' may hide one or more intermediate names
Date: ce_approx refined to 1559 (Nov./Dec.); era VS kept
Notes expanded

notes: The chronogram reads bhū 1, kha 0, parvata 7, śaśāṅka 1; read right to left, this gives 1701. 'vikramakṣitipateḥ ... abde' is the normal way of naming the Vikrama era, which gives VS 1701 = c. 1644 CE. This conflicts with the catalogue, which gives ŚS 1701 (= 1779 CE). The catalogue may be right. The patron Trivikrama could be Trivikrama Sen of Tanahun (later 18th century), and he fits 1779 better than 1644. Also, 'tri' was added as a correction (〈〈tri〉〉), so the scribe first wrote 'śrīvikramanṛpasya'; the 'vikrama' in the date verse may therefore be loose usage. Verses 1–2 are marked 'yugmam', meaning they form one sentence. Check the weekday to decide between the two eras. 'rājña yā' is a corruption of 'rājñājñayā' or 'ājñayā', so 'by order of the king'. 'pakṣaklakṣe' is probably 'pakṣe valakṣe' ('in the bright fortnight', i.e. śukla). 'medinītridaśakaḥ' is obscure; it may encode the tithi (13?). Māṇikyamalla and Manohara belong to the history of the Subodhanī commentary, not to this copy.

title: Nītisaṃgraha
subject: Nītiśāstra
date_note: = Sunday 21 Oct 1629, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: || iti mahārājādhirāja śrīśrījagajjyotirmmalladevaviracito nītisaṃgrahaḥ samāptaḥ || || samvat 750 kārttikaśukla paṃcamyāṃ tithau, muraṇakṣatra (!) śubhajoga, āditya vārasa, dvija śrīdhanarāja devaṇa, likhitam saṃpūrṇṇaṃ, || śubhamastu || sadā sarvvadā, || idaṃ pustakaṃ svapāṭhārthaṃ likhitaṃ || nepālavatsare jāte vyomakhādahayāmite kārtikasya site pakṣe paṃcamyām ca tithau dine mūle vā śubhamyoje ca ravivāreṇa saṃyute vipraśrīdhanarājena likhyate nītisaṃgrahaḥ || ❁ || ❁ || (fol. 44v3–45r1)
notes:
The prose date is NS 750 Kārttika śukla 5, a Sunday, with nakṣatra mūla. That corresponds to about Oct/Nov 1629 CE, because Kārttika śukla opens the NS year.

The verse chronogram 'vyomakhādahayāmite' seems corrupt. Reading vyoma = 0, kha = 0, haya = 7 from right to left gives 700, and '-āda-' has no clear numerical value. So it matches neither 750 nor the catalogue's '760'. The catalogue's '750 pauṣaśukla 15' also does not appear in the quoted colophon and may come from another part of the manuscript or be an error.

The scribe's name is 'dhanarāja devaṇa' in the prose and 'dhanarājena' in the verse. 'deva' may be part of the name (the catalogue gives Dhanarājadeva) or an honorific, followed by the Newari agentive -ṇa.

Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur, the author, ruled in about NS 734–757, so this copy was probably made during his reign. However, the colophon does not name him as the reigning king.
review: p1 Jagajjyotirmalladeva: removed role 'king'. He is named only as author of the Nītisaṃgraha ('-viracito'), and the colophon has no reign formula for this copy. NS 750 does fall within his Bhaktapur reign (c. NS 734–757), which is now recorded in notes.

p2: name changed from 'Dhanarājadeva' to 'Dhanarāja'. 'devaṇa' looks like deva + Newari agentive -ṇa, and the verse gives only 'vipraśrīdhanarājena'. The -deva form is kept as a possible variant in notes. Confidence lowered to medium for the name form; roles scribe + owner unchanged (svapāṭhārtham).
Date: ce_approx changed from 1630 to 1629. Kārttika śukla 5 falls at the very start of NS 750, about Oct/Nov 1629 CE.
Date: nakshatra written as mūla in standard form.
Notes rewritten: the chronogram 'vyomakhādahayāmite' as transmitted gives 0-0-7, read right to left = 700, which matches neither 750 nor the catalogue's 760. The prose figure 750 is preferred.

title: Hitopadeśa
subject: Nītiśāstra
date_note: = Friday 16 Jul 1660, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: || iti hitopadeśa ----- rnāma caturthaḥ kathā samāptaḥ || samvat 780 ākhāḍha śuklanavamyāntithau likhitaṃ ------ kāyasya devarobhena nājo ----- midaṃ || || śubhamastu || || śubhānisantu || (fol. 76v5-7 )
notes: The colophon does not name an era. I read 'samvat 780' as Nepāla Saṃvat because the script is Newari, which gives about 1660 CE. Read as Vikrama Saṃvat, the year would be about 723 CE, which is implausible for this script. 'kāyasya' is probably an error for 'kāyastha'. 'devarobhena' is probably a corrupt name; possible readings are Devaśobha or Devarāma. There is a lacuna before the name, so a fuller name or more titles may be missing. 'nājo ----- midaṃ' is broken off and unclear. 'nājo' could be a title or Newari word (cf. nāyo), or part of a phrase like 'pustakam idaṃ', so a possible owner or commissioner may be lost there. The ending 'caturthaḥ kathā samāptaḥ' has grammatical errors as quoted.
review: Title normalized from 'kāyasya' to 'kāyastha'; the reading as written is recorded in notes
Scribe confidence lowered to low: the name is probably corrupt and is surrounded by lacunae
Month normalized to āṣāḍha, with the as-written form kept in date.as_written
Notes expanded: the era is inferred, not stated, and the role of the fragment 'nājo' is unclear

title: Nānārthapañcadaśagīta
subject: Saṅgīta
colophon: thvate nepālabhākhāna nānārtha paṃcasdaśakam gītaṃ saṃpūrṇam || || śubham astu sarvvadā || e || (fol. 4r6)
notes: The colophon is in Newari: 'thvate nepālabhākhāna nānārtha paṃcasdaśakam gītaṃ saṃpūrṇam' means 'these fifteen songs on various topics, in the Nepal language, are complete'. 'paṃcasdaśakam' is a corrupt form of pañcadaśakam. The quoted colophon names no scribe, owner, king, date or place. The catalogue's King field (Jagajjyotimalla) is probably there because he is thought to have composed or patronised the songs (Jagajjyotimalla of Bhaktapur, who wrote Newari songs). It may come from the song signatures (bhaṇitā) in the body of the text, not from this colophon. It is not recorded here as reigning king or author because the colophon gives no evidence for either.
review: No changes to persons, relations, date or place: the colophon names no person, era or place.
Expanded the notes: the Newari wording, the corrupt reading paṃcasdaśakam, and the likely reason the catalogue names Jagajjyotimalla.

date_note: = Thursday 28 Jul 1836, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīrāgalakṣaṇaṃ samāptaṃ || vaśviṣu ṣvaṃgeṃducyute ca śāke māse śucau saṃsthita paurṇimāsu giridharākho likhanoṣu dakṣo hyalī likhadādarataḥ suvegāt || 1 || || || || || || || || || rāmo jayati śubham || (fol. 15r5–7)
notes: The verse is corrupt. The intended text is probably 'vasv-iṣv-aṅgendu-yute ca śāke māse śucau saṃsthita-paurṇamāsyām giridharākhyo likhaneṣu dakṣo hy alīlikhad ādarataḥ suvegāt'. The chronogram words are vasu (8), iṣu (5), aṅga (6) and indu (1). Read right to left (aṅkānāṃ vāmato gatiḥ), they give ŚS 1658 = c. 1736 CE. The catalogue's ŚS 1758 would need a 7 in the hundreds place, for example aśva/muni instead of aṅga, which the text as quoted does not support. Either the catalogue is wrong or the cataloguer read the manuscript differently, so check the original if possible. Śuci is normally Āṣāḍha (sometimes Jyeṣṭha). 'hyalī likhad' = hy alīlikhat ('wrote').
review: Chronogram re-read: 'vasv-iṣv-aṅgendu-yute śāke' = vasu 8, iṣu 5, aṅga 6, indu 1; read right to left this gives ŚS 1658 (≈1736 CE), not the catalogue's 1758 (≈1836 CE). Year and ce_approx changed, and the conflict with the catalogue is noted.
Month normalised to Āṣāḍha (śuci); pakṣa śukla is implied by pūrṇimā.
Scribe evidence string shortened. Scribe's confidence lowered to medium because the name sits in a corrupt verse.

title: *Jālandharopākhyānanāṭāka
subject: nāṭaka
date_note: = Friday 1 Jun 1703, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: saṃ 823 jyaṣṭakṛṣṇa dvitiyā śuklavāra thvakuhnu si(exp.24b4)rdha yāṅā || jadi sūrdhaṃ masūrdhaṃ vāmamadva ..na hieta || || śubha || || (5)
notes: The colophon is in Newari: 'thvakuhnu sirdha yāṅā' = 'completed on this day' (sirdha for siddha). It names no scribe, patron or owner. The closing line 'jadi sūrdhaṃ masūrdhaṃ vāmamadva ..na hieta' is a corrupt form of the usual scribe's apology verse ('yadi śuddham aśuddhaṃ vā...'). The catalogue gives King Bhāskaramalla and Kathmandu, but neither appears in the quoted colophon. They fit the date, since Bhāskaramalla ruled Kathmandu c. 1700–1714 CE. The cataloguer probably inferred them, or took them from a part of the manuscript that is not quoted here, so they are not recorded as persons or place.
review: month normalized from 'jyaṣṭa' to 'jyeṣṭha'
weekday normalized: 'śuklavāra' is a scribal slip for śukravāra (Friday), which agrees with the catalogue
added notes on 'sirdha yāṅā' (= siddha yāṅā, 'completed') and the corrupt closing verse; date and ce_approx (NS 823 = 1703 CE) confirmed

title: Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa (ṭīkāsetuḥ)
subject: Rāmāyaṇa
date_raw: nepālena vanaṃ danaṃ damilite pauṣesite pūrṇimā nakṣatre ca punarvasu vudha dine yoge tathā eiṃdrake
date_note: = Monday 16 Jan 1775, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: || iti śrīmad adhyātmarāmāyaṇe umāmaheśvara saṃvāde uttarakāṇḍe navamaḥ sargāḥ || 9 || || ❖ || || ❁ || || ❁ || uttarakāṃḍa samāptaṃ || adhyātmottara kāṇḍe ------------ tvārthataḥ || || śubham || graṃtha saṃkhyā 4200 (fol. 228v2-6 ) || iti śrīmatsakala rāja vipaduddharaṇa samarthetyādi virudāvalī virājamāna himmativarmaṇaḥ putrasya śrī rāma varmaṇa kṛtāvadhyātma rāmāyaṇe setau uttarakāṇḍe navamodhyāyaḥ || 9 || || samāptacāyamadhyāya rāmāyaṇa ṭīkā || || nepālena vanaṃ danaṃ damilite pauṣesite pūrṇimā nakṣatre ca punarvasu vudha dine yoge tathā eiṃdrake || śrī viprottamarājako haladharohyatyātma rāmāyaṇaḥ ṭīkā pustaka lekhitaṃ śubhadine śrīrāmasu prītaye || || śubham || || (fol. 228v1,7-8)
purpose: for the pleasure of Śrī Rāma (śrīrāmasuprītaye)
notes: The catalogue lists Śrīrāma Varmā as the scribe. The colophon shows he is the commentator: he wrote the Setu commentary and is the son of Himmativarman. He is not the copyist. Haladhara had the copy made ('lekhitaṃ', causative). It is possible he also wrote it himself, but the colophon does not say so. 'viprottamarājako' is unclear. It could be viprottama ('excellent brahmin') plus a word ending in -rājaka (a surname or place?), or a corruption. The year chronogram is corrupt. It might read 'nepāle bāṇa-nanda-danti-milite', i.e. 5, 9, 8 read right to left, giving NS 895 ≈ 1775 CE. This reading is tentative and has not been checked against the weekday or nakṣatra. A full moon in Pauṣa normally falls in Puṣya, not Punarvasu. 'adhyātmottara kāṇḍe ------------ tvārthataḥ' is a lacuna in the cataloguer's transcription.
review: Haladhara: removed 'scribe'. 'lekhitaṃ' (causative participle, 'caused to be written') supports only 'commissioner'. Confidence lowered to medium because 'viprottamarājako' is unclear. Title normalised to 'vipra' (with 'viprottama' kept as written).

Date: proposed reading of the corrupt chronogram 'vanaṃ danaṃ damilite' as bāṇa(5)-nanda(9)-danti(8) → NS 895, giving ce_approx 1775 (tentative; the year field shows it as a reading, not a certainty).
Purpose normalised to 'for the pleasure of Śrī Rāma (śrīrāmasuprītaye)'.
Notes updated: the earlier 'NS 99x' guess is replaced and the uncertainties are listed.

title: Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa, Adhyātmarāmāyaṇaṭīkā
subject: Rāmāyaṇa
date_note: = Sunday 24 Jul 1853, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīmad adhyātmarāmāyaṇe umāmaheśvara saṃvāde uttarakaṃḍe navamaḥ sargaḥ || 9 || rāmāyaṇa mahākāvyaṃ likhitaṃ pustakaṃ śubhaṃ śrāvaṇokṛṣṇapakṣevai pūrṇajātaṃ śubhapradaṃ || 1 || (fol. 62r6–8) iti śrīmatsakalarājyavipaduddharaṇa samarpyetyāde virudāvalī virājamānasya himativarmaṇaḥ putrasya śrīrāmavarmaṇaḥ kṛtāvadhyātmarāmāyaṇasetau uttarakaṃḍe navamaḥ sargaḥ || 9 || saṃvat || 18 9 ||(!) śāke || 17 || 75 || rattākṣanāma || ā. | tṛ. | (fol. 62r2–10)
notes: The colophon has two eras. The VS figure '18 9' is corrupt; it is probably VS 1910, which equals ŚS 1775 and 1853 CE, so the two eras agree. The saṃvatsara is 'rattākṣa' = Raktākṣa/Raktākṣī. In the southern 60-year cycle, Raktākṣī falls in ŚS 1786 (1864/65), not ŚS 1775, so either the year or the cycle name is doubtful. 'ā. tṛ.' is read as Ādityavāra and tṛtīyā, but this is uncertain: 'ā.' could also abbreviate a month. The month and fortnight (śrāvaṇa kṛṣṇa) come from the verse after the mūla colophon. Rāmavarman, son of Himativarman (possibly Himmatavarman), wrote the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa-setu commentary. His birudāvalī suggests he was of royal or noble rank. He is not the reigning king of this copy. The catalogue's 'Scribe' field gives the ṭīkākāra. No scribe is named in the colophon.
review: Date: tithi/weekday from 'ā. | tṛ.' kept as tṛtīyā / Ādityavāra, but flagged as uncertain. 'ā.' could also abbreviate a month (Āṣāḍha/Āśvina).
Date: the month śrāvaṇa kṛṣṇa comes from the verse after the mūla colophon ('śrāvaṇe kṛṣṇapakṣe'), not from the dated line.
Notes: the corrupt 'saṃvat 18 9' is explained as probably VS 1910, which agrees with ŚS 1775 (= 1853 CE). The two eras do not conflict.
Notes: the Raktākṣa saṃvatsara does not obviously fit ŚS 1775 in the southern 60-year cycle (Raktākṣī falls in ŚS 1786 = 1864/65). This is flagged.
Notes: the catalogue's 'Scribe' field actually names the ṭīkākāra (Rāmavarman). No scribe is named. Himativarman may stand for Himmatavarman.

title: Rasikaraṃjanī
subject: Sāhitya
date_note: = Wednesday 5 Feb 1772, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śri bhānudatta miśra viracitā rasamaṃjarī samāptā śrīrāmovijayate tarāma śubhaṃ (fol. 54r8 ) tāta śrī harivaṃśa bhaṭṭaika caraṇaśaraṇa gopāla bhṭṭakṛtā rasika raṃjanī ṭīkā samāptā śubhamastu leṣaka pāṭhayo(!) netrāṃkabhūpa pramite śāke māghe gurau dvikegatyā(!) śrīnagarabhye likhatsvayama 1693 śubhaṃ likhitā viṣṇu vallabhena śubham (fol. 54r8-10 )
notes: The chronogram 'netrāṅkabhūpa' read right to left gives bhūpa 16, aṅka 9, netra 2, i.e. Śaka 1692. The figure written in the colophon is 1693. The text says 'śāke', so the era is taken as ŚS, even though the catalogue just has 'Saṃ. 1693(!)'. If it were VS, the date would be 1636 CE. ŚS 1693 + 78 = 1771, but Māgha falls in January–February, so Māgha of Śaka 1693 is early 1772 CE. If the chronogram's 1692 is right, it is early 1771 CE. 'dvikegatyā(!)' is corrupt. It probably hides the 2nd tithi ('dvitīyāyāṃ'?), but this is uncertain, and the pakṣa is not stated. 'śrīnagarabhye' is probably 'śrīnagarākhye' or '-madhye'. Which Śrīnagara is meant (Garhwal, Kashmir, etc.) is not certain. 'leṣaka pāṭhayo(!)' is the stock blessing 'lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ śubham' and names no one. 'likhat svayam' just means the scribe wrote it himself.
review: Removed 'Śrīnagara' as Viṣṇuvallabha's residence: the colophon gives it only as the place of copying ('śrīnagarabhye likhat').
Cleared purpose: 'likhat svayam' says the scribe wrote it himself, not that he wrote it for himself. No svārtha or owner role is stated.
Emptied place.normalized: 'Śrīnagara' could be Srinagar in Garhwal, Srinagar in Kashmir or another place, so the identification is not certain.
Lowered confidence for tithi 2 (read from corrupt 'dvikegatyā') and explained it in notes.
Expanded notes on the chronogram (1692) vs the figure (1693), the CE conversion for Māgha, and the 'leṣaka pāṭhayo' formula.

'Saṃvat' with Prabhava fits VS 1734 = 1677 CE: in the northern Bārhaspatya reckoning 1677 was Prabhava (the southern-cycle Prabhava was 1687). Kārttika śukla 9 falls on about 24 Oct 1677 Julian (= 3 Nov 1677 Gregorian), which was a Wednesday. That matches budhavāsara, and the moon was about 8 days past new moon. Scribe name: 'vyāsodaya kṛṣṇena' is read as Vyāsa Udayakṛṣṇa, son of Vyāsa Madhusūdana. The catalogue's 'Kṛṣṇavyāsa' takes only the second element, so 'udaya' might not be part of the name. 'sūnūnā' should be sūnunā. The invocation 'śrīviśveśo vijayatetarām' may point to a Vārāṇasī (Viśveśvara) milieu, but no place of copying is stated.
review: Lowered p3 (scribe) confidence from high to medium: 'vyāsodaya kṛṣṇena' could be read either as Vyāsa Udayakṛṣṇa or as Kṛṣṇa (the catalogue gives Kṛṣṇavyāsa). Udayakṛṣṇa is kept as the preferred reading.
Lowered p2 confidence to medium because the case form 'sūnūnā' is corrupt (for sūnunā).
Added a check of the samvatsara: Prabhava matches VS 1734 = 1677 CE in the northern (Bārhaspatya) reckoning.
Specified that 24 Oct 1677 is a Julian date (= 3 Nov 1677 Gregorian). Moon-phase and weekday checks agree with śukla 9 and Wednesday.
Expanded the notes.

title: Kautukacintāmaṇi
subject: Tantrā-yurveda
date_note: = Sunday 8 May 1808, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: || iti śrīmahāerājādhirājapratāparūdradeva gajapatipādāravindaṣaṭpadāyammānasenasakalavidvajjanacaraṇa(9)sampāditaprajñāvibhavena caturacārarika (!) śvetanāgabhāyābhāṇḍāradhūrttakarttavividhavirūḍhavidhitena viśveśva(10)ramahāprasādisutena kadambeśvarāddhanyāsyānamahāprasādena sunṛtavādināviracite kautukacintāma(1) ṇīgraṃthe kautukanirūpanaṃ (!) nāma tṛtīyādīptiḥ samāptaṃ śubham astu || || śrīvikramādityasaṃvat 1865 sāla (2)vaiśāṣa śukla 13 ravivāsare liṣitaṃ kṛṣṇānanda sarmanaḥ (!) || kāṣṭhamaṃḍapasthāne || śubham || || || || (fol.59v8–11:60r1–2)
notes: The first part of the colophon (iti ... tṛtīyā dīptiḥ) is the author's own closing statement. It names Gajapati Pratāparudradeva of Orissa (16th century) as the author's patron. The work is often attributed to that king himself. Here it is written by a court servant, son of Viśveśvara. The servant calls himself 'sunṛtavādin' ('speaker of truth'), which is probably an epithet. The servant's name is corrupt. 'kadambeśvarāddhanyāsyāna' may hide a place or temple name ('Kadambeśvara') plus a name, so treat the name as uncertain. 'mahāprasādi/mahāprasāda' probably stands for mahāpātra. Pratāparudradeva is not the reigning king of this copy: the catalogue's King field takes him from the author's statement. The scribe's own colophon names no ruler. The copy was made by Kṛṣṇānanda Śarman at Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa (Kathmandu) in VS 1865 (c. 1808 CE), Vaiśākha śukla 13, on a Sunday. The weekday has not been checked.
review: p2 Pratāparudradeva: role changed from 'king' to 'other'. He is the Gajapati of Orissa who sponsored the original work (the author calls himself a bee at his lotus feet). He is not the reigning king of this VS 1865 Kathmandu copy, so the catalogue's King field is misleading.
p1 Kṛṣṇānanda: residence cleared. Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa is given only as the place of copying.
p3 and p4: confidence lowered. 'mahāprasādi/mahāprasāda' is probably a corruption of the Orissan office title mahāpātra. The author's personal name is uncertain.
Weekday normalized to ravivāra (Sunday).
Notes expanded.

title: Golādeśa
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Wednesday 6 Sep 1826, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti dāmo(22)darīye golādeśe kālanirddeśo daśamaḥ || || nakhapurusūraghana 1748 śāke nabhasyeśajanya ho golādeśaṃ lālaratnākaro ʼlikha drameṭpure || 1 || || śrīśo ʼvatu lekhakaṃ paṭhantam || (fol. 20r21–22)
notes: The colophon gives the year 1748 in figures, Śaka era, which is 1826 CE (Bhādrapada falls in Aug–Sep 1826). The word-numeral chronogram 'nakhapurusūraghana' is corrupt or unusual and could not be checked digit by digit. 'nabhasyeśajanya ho' is read as 'on the day of Īśa's son (Gaṇeśa) in Nabhasya', which most likely means Bhādrapada śukla 4 (Gaṇeśa-caturthī). This is tentative. 'ʼlikha drameṭpure' should be divided as (a)likhad + rameṭpure, so the place is Rameṭpura. The name looks corrupt. The catalogue's suggestion of Umeśapura = Kāśī is speculative, so the place is left unnormalized. The scribe's name appears as 'lālaratnākara' and the catalogue gives 'Ratnākaralāla'. Lāla is probably a name suffix of the Kāyastha type, so the person may be catalogued as Ratnākaralāla. 'śrīśo ʼvatu lekhakaṃ paṭhantam' is a blessing formula and names no other person.
review: Scribe: name given as 'Ratnākara' with 'lāla' kept in titles, instead of 'Lālaratnākara' plus a duplicated title. The catalogue's 'Ratnākaralāla' is the same person with the parts reversed (lāla is put first in the verse).
Scribe: residence removed. Rameṭpura is where the copy was made, not a stated residence.
Date: tithi added as a tentative reading. 'īśajanya' (Gaṇeśa) probably points to Gaṇeśa-caturthī, Bhādrapada śukla 4. The chronogram could not be fully checked.
Notes: the sandhi of 'ʼlikha drameṭpure' is explained, and the Umeśapura/Kāśī idea is marked as the cataloguer's guess.

title: Bṛhajjātaka(caramādhyāyantam)
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Saturday 29 May 1824, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: year + 1, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrī varāhamihirakṛtau vṛhajjātake caramādhyāyaḥ || || rasa nigamagahayendu śākakerke hyanaḍuhiśukrasitādirmeke jenhi || trinayana purilālaratna śarmmā likhadidamadhyayanāya bhūsurolam || 1 || || śubhamastu || || śrī viśveśvarāya namaḥ || || || (fol. 19v7-9)
purpose: adhyayanāya (for study, presumably the scribe's own)
notes: The chronogram, read right to left, is rasa 6, nigama 4, haya 7, indu 1, giving ŚS 1746 (about 1824 CE). 'gahaya' is a corruption of 'haya'. I take the corrupt date phrase as 'śākake 'rke hy anaḍuhi śukra-sitādime (?) jñe 'hni': the year in the Śaka era, the sun in Taurus, the month Śukra (= Jyeṣṭha), the first day of the bright fortnight, a Wednesday. The tithi and weekday readings are conjectural; I have not checked them against an ephemeris. Trinayanapurī ('city of the three-eyed one', i.e. Śiva) means Kāśī/Vārāṇasī, which fits the closing invocation to Viśveśvara. It could equally be the scribe's home rather than the place of copying. 'bhūsuro 'lam' marks Lālaratna as a brahmin. The catalogue's scribe field (Lālaratna Śarmā) agrees.
review: Lālaratna: roles changed from scribe+beneficiary to scribe+owner (he copied it 'adhyayanāya', for (his) study; no separate beneficiary)
Date: 'hy anaḍuhi' read as sun in Taurus (Vṛṣa); month 'śukra' = Jyeṣṭha; paksa normalised to śukla; tithi pratipad from 'sitādime' (tentative); weekday Wednesday from 'jñe 'hni' (written 'jenhi')
Purpose corrected: colophon has only 'adhyayanāya'; the 'bhūsurāṇām' in the first reading is not in the text ('bhūsuro 'lam' describes the scribe)
Notes expanded on the corrupt date phrase

title: Itihāsasamuccaya
subject: Itihāsa
date_raw: nobhranaya (!) munivarṣe māsasyaśrāvaṇastathā śitapakṣe tṛrodaśī (!) samāptaṃ kuca dinena
colophon: || itihāsasamuccaye puṇḍarīkopākhyānaṃ cāliśodhyāya samāptaṃ || || nobhranaya (!) munivarṣe māsasyaśrāvaṇastathā śitapakṣe tṛrodaśī (!) samāptaṃ kuca dinena || likhita śrīvāṣṭaka (!) kāyasta (!) hedayasiṃhena yadi śuddhaṃmaśuddhaṃmvā sodhanīyāmahatvudhai (!) || (fol. 115r2–4)
notes: The chronogram 'nobhranaya munivarṣe' is best read as nabho (0) + nayana (2) + muni (7). Read right to left, this gives 720. The colophon states no era. NS 720 (c. 1600 CE) is assumed because the manuscript is in Newari script; VS or ŚS 720 would be far too early. 'śrīvāṣṭaka' is a corruption of Śrīvāstavya/Śrīvāstava, a Kāyastha subcaste. 'kuca dina' stands for kujadina, i.e. Tuesday. The scribe's name 'Hedayasiṃha' (as in the catalogue) probably represents Hṛdayasiṃha. The tithi is śukla 13 (śitapakṣe = sitapakṣe). The weekday has not been verified against an ephemeris.
review: Chronogram resolved: 'nobhranaya' read as nabho- (nabhas = 0) + nayana (2), with muni (7); read right to left this gives 720, not the two alternatives the first reading offered

Year field normalized to '720'
Title 'śrīvāstaka' normalized to Śrīvāstavya (the Kāyastha subcaste); note added that Hedayasiṃha probably stands for Hṛdayasiṃha

notes: The colophon names no persons. The final dating is Śaka 1793 Bhādra vadi 11, roja 7 (Saturday), which is 1871 CE. The 'saṃvat 1871' that comes earlier, inside the text, does not agree with this date if it is read as Vikrama: VS 1871 would be about 1814 CE, while Śaka 1793 is VS 1928. It agrees only if it is read as the Christian year 1871, which is unusual but possible in a late manuscript. The catalogue's 'SAM 1871' and 'ŚS 1793' therefore point to the same year only if SAM means CE. I took the Śaka date as authoritative.

title: MuhūrttacintāmaṇI(ṭīkā piyuṣadhārā)
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_raw: śakepuṇa(!) bhrarasemāse ca māghasite || titherekādaśī scavye
colophon: iti śrī vidvadvaivajñayuk(!) murālekāranīkaṃ ṣjyoti(!)vidatputra(!) goviṃda jyotirvīdvaracitājyaṃ(!) muhūrttaciṃtāmaṇI ṭīkāyāṃ pīyūṣadhārābhidhāyāṃ śubhāśubhaprakaraṇaṃ samāptimagāt || || śubhamastu || || śrīḥ || || śakepuṇa(!) bhrarasemāse ca māghasite || titherekādaśī scavye likhitāṃ yugajmavataiḥ || 1 || śubhaṃ || ❖ || (fol. 49r6-8)
notes: The colophon is badly corrupt. The commentator Govinda of the Pīyūṣadhārā (composed ŚS 1525 = 1603 CE) is the son of Nīlakaṇṭha jyotirvid and nephew of Rāma Daivajña, author of the Muhūrtacintāmaṇi. So 'murālekāranīkaṃ ṣjyoti(!)vidatputra' probably garbles '...nīlakaṇṭhajyotirvitputra', not Murāri. The Śaka chronogram 'puṇa(!) bhrarase' may stand for pūrṇa(0)-abhra(0)-rasa(6), which gives 600 when read right to left. A thousands digit seems to be missing; it may be ŚS 1600 = 1678 CE, but this is unverified. The copy must postdate 1603 CE. 'scavye' probably stands for 'saumye' (Wednesday). 'likhitāṃ yugajmavataiḥ' may hide the scribe's name or may be a further corrupt chronogram/phrase. The text author Rāma is not named in the colophon.
review: Commentator's father: the standard Pīyūṣadhārā colophon calls Govinda the son of Nīlakaṇṭha jyotirvid (grandson of Ananta). The garbled 'murālekāranīkaṃ ṣjyoti(!)vidatputra(!)' most likely hides '...nīlakaṇṭhajyotirvitputra'. p2 is re-identified from Murāri to Nīlakaṇṭha, with low confidence; the 'daivajña' title is dropped as unsupported.

Date: 'puṇabhrarase' is not a valid year form. The chronogram probably reads pūrṇa(0)-abhra(0)-rasa(6), giving 600 when read right to left, so a digit is probably missing. The year is left uncertain and ce_approx stays empty.
Weekday: 'scavye' is probably a corruption of 'saumye' (Wednesday).
Scribe name 'yugajmavataiḥ' kept as low-confidence. The given name is now the form as written, not a reconstructed stem.
Notes rewritten to match.

notes: The catalogue's King field ('Ṭoḍarānanda Malla') is wrong. Ṭoḍaramalla (Rājā Todar Mal, d. 1589) is named as author or patron of the Ṭoḍarānanda, of which the Horāsaukhya is a part, and 'Ṭoḍarānanda' is the work's title. He is not the reigning king of this copy, and no reigning ruler is named. 'saṃvat 1639' in this Devanagari, North Indian setting is taken as Vikrama, giving 1582 CE; this also fits Todar Mal's lifetime. The tithi is irregular: a bright fortnight normally ends at 15, so 'śudi 30' plus 'the following pratipad' may be a slip for vadi 30 (amāvāsyā), or it may mean the full moon followed by pratipad. 'praohita' is read as purohita. 'alīliṣat' stands for alīlikhat ('wrote / caused to be written'). The catalogue gives Devadatta as scribe, and that is accepted here. 'lleṣakapāṭhakayoḥ' (for lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ) is a standard blessing on scribe and reader, not a named person.
review: p2 (Rāma): confidence lowered to medium because 'praohita' is a corrupt spelling, read as purohita (a title, not part of the name).

p3 (Devadatta): kept as scribe only, confidence set to medium. 'alīliṣat' stands for alīlikhat. That form is formally causative, but here it goes with the instrumental 'devadattena' and is loosely used to mean 'wrote'. There is no separate commissioner, so no commissioner role was added.
