title: Meghamālā
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Friday 3 Apr 1587, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: amānta months, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: śāka 1 kuśa2 kroṃca3 śālmalī 4 na cet 5 puṣkara 6 jaṃbūdvī 7 || śrīkṛṣṇāparṇam astu || || śubhaṃ bhavatu || || kalyāṇaṃ || (7) || saṃvat 1644 varṣe | śāke 1509 pravarttamāne | ṣaṣṭyābdamadhye manmathanāmasaṃvatsare | | mālapakakṣetre || mudgala(vā)ta(8)sāha śrīakabararājye | ūcanudasamīpe sonakachagṛāme | śrīsādhu pūrṇimā gache | bhaya śrīsādhu suṃdarasūri tatpa(9)hebhaya śrījayasāgarasūribhir meghamālāgaṃtha likhitam asti || || śubhaṃ bhūyāt sarvvadā || prathamavaiśāṣavadi 11 ravi(9)vāsare liṣitaṃ || || maṃgalaṃ lekhikāṇāṃ tu | pāṭhakāṇāṃ tu maṃgalaṃ | maṃgalaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ | bhaūmau bhūpatimaṃgalaṃ || || śri || (fol. 36v5–9)
notes: VS 1644 and ŚS 1509 agree: both give 1587 CE. The text also names the year as 'manmathanāmasaṃvatsara' in the 60-year cycle. In the standard southern reckoning, 1587/88 is Sarvajit, not Manmatha. The name may follow a northern Bārhaspatya reckoning or may be an error; this has not been verified. 'prathamavaiśāṣa' means the first (intercalary) Vaiśākha. 'vadi' means the dark fortnight (pūrṇimānta reckoning). 'mālapakakṣetre' probably stands for Mālavakṣetre (Malwa). 'ūcanuda' is unidentified. 'sonakacha' may be Sonkatch near Dewas (Madhya Pradesh), but this is uncertain. 'bhaya' is probably the abbreviation 'bha°' for bhaṭṭāraka. 'tatpahe' stands for tatpaṭṭe: Jayasāgara succeeded Sundara(sūri) on the paṭṭa, which may not mean a direct teacher–pupil link. The name could also be read Sādhusundara, but 'śrīsādhu' more likely repeats the gaccha name. 'meghamālāgaṃtha' stands for meghamālāgrantha. The opening list (śāka, kuśa, krauñca, śālmali, ...) names dvīpas from the text and contains no persons.
review: Names given without the Jain title sūri: Jayasāgarasūri → Jayasāgara and Sundarasūri → Sundara, with 'sūri' moved to titles.
Read 'bhaya' as an abbreviation of bhaṭṭāraka and added it to the titles of p2 and p3.
Changed the affiliation from Pūrṇimāgaccha to Sādhupūrṇimāgaccha, a known branch: 'śrīsādhu pūrṇimā gache' is the gaccha name, so 'sādhu' is not a title of Sundara. Removed 'sādhu' from p2's titles.
Changed Akbar's title reading to 'mudgalapātasāha' (Mughal pādśāh); the 'vā' is the cataloguer's doubtful reading.
Moved 'manmatha' out of nakshatra_yoga: it is the name of the 60-year (Jovian) year, not a nakṣatra or yoga. It is now recorded in notes.
Cleared place.normalized: identifying Sonakacha with Sonkatch is plausible but not certain.
The pupil_of relation is kept but annotated: tatpaṭṭe means successor on the pontifical seat (paṭṭa), not necessarily a direct pupil.

colophon: || || iti śrībhāskarīye siddhāntaśiromaṇau līlāvatīsaṃjñā pāṭī samāptā || || ❁ || rāmāya namaḥ || || śrībhāskarāya namaḥ || ❁ || śrīśāke 1699 saṃvat 1834 likhitam idaṃ pustakaṃ †laṃtarjuge† padmanābhopādhyāyena || || ❁ || || rāma || || śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ || alikulasya ṣaḍbhāgo dvādaśabhāgā hataḥ || mālatyāṃ mūle dve ṣaḍbhramarāś caṃpake kati te || || ❁ || || || 1 || rāmo jayati || << in another hand >> imāme ʼ agnaiṣṭakā dhenavaḥ... muṣmiṃ loke || 1 || (fol. 35r1–6)
notes: The colophon gives two eras, Śaka 1699 and saṃvat 1834. Read as Vikrama Saṃvat, they agree: both are 1777 CE. The cataloguer marked '†laṃtarjuge†' as corrupt. It probably names the place of copying (a locative). Reading it as Lamjung is only a guess, so no modern place is given. The verse after the colophon (alikulasya ṣaḍbhāgo...) is a mathematical riddle. The Vedic mantra added in another hand (imāme 'gnaiṣṭakā dhenavaḥ...) names no one, and neither tells us anything about who made or owned this copy.
review: No substantive changes. Scribe Padmanābha (title upādhyāya) and author Bhāskara are both kept.

title: Lagnacandrikā
subject: Jyotiṣa

colophon: iti śrīkāiśāthakṛtau lagnacaṃdrikāyāṃ daśamaparicchedaḥ samāptaḥ || (fol. 55r2–3) << After the coliphon>> atha rohiṇīcakraṃ || || lagnākāraṃ likhec cakraṃ tatra bhānī likhet sudhīḥ || dvayaṃ dvayaṃ samedresu śeṣasthāne tathaikakaṃ || 1 || ... ativṛṣṭiḥ samudreṣu taṭe vṛṣṭis tu madhyamā || saṃdhau ca khaṃḍavṛṣṭiḥ syād anāvṛṣṭis tu parvate || lakṣite vikramābde ca vedāṃbaramuniṃdubhiḥ || pauṣaśukladvitīyāyām alekhī chrīpatis tv adaḥ || (fol. 55r3–4, 8–9) << on the exp. 57, with a diagram >> auṣadhe vāhanārohe vivāhaśayane [ʼ]śane || vidyāraṃbhe vījavāpe†kṣutaṃ† saptasu śobhanaṃ || 1 || (fol. 55r8–55v1)
notes: The author's name is corrupt: 'kāiśātha' is taken as Kāśīnātha, the known author of the Lagnacandrikā. The year is a chronogram read right to left: veda 4, ambara 0, muni 7, indu 1, giving VS 1704 (agrees with the catalogue). Pauṣa śukla 2 of VS 1704 falls about Dec 1647 / Jan 1648 CE. 'alekhī chrīpatis' is the sandhi of alekhīt śrīpatiḥ. The scribe's verse comes after the end-colophon, in the appended rohiṇīcakra material, so strictly it may refer only to that appendix. It most likely dates the whole copy.

notes: The colophon gives no scribe, patron or place. The date formula 'mahārājādhirāja cakravartti śrīvikramāditya-sat (= saṃvat) 1861' names the Vikrama era, not a reigning king. VS 1861 is about 1804/05 CE. The catalogue fields name a Malla king ('Kīrtivamamalla', probably corrupt) and a donor 'Yuvarājanṛsiṃhavikramamalla', with Kāntipura as the place. None of these are in the quoted colophon, and Malla rulers do not fit VS 1861, which falls in the Shah period. These fields are probably carried over from another record or come from another part of the MS, and should be checked against the manuscript. The colophon closes the 11th adhikāra (vyatīpāta) and the pūrvakhaṇḍa. The '(!)' marks the cataloguer's flag on the corrupt 'ātmajya' for ātmaja.

If that word is 'dyumaṇi' (the sun, 12), the year would be ŚS 1200, about 1278 CE. That is speculative, so ce_approx is left empty. 'ravikṛya rāśyai' is probably 'ravau kriyarāśau', the sun in Kriya (Aries), which gives the solar month Meṣa. The scribe copied it for his own study (nijapaṭhanārtham), so the unnamed scribe would also be the owner, but no person record is made because no name is given.

title: Sūryapakṣaśaraṇakaraṇam
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: ≈ 1608 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: śrīsūryapakṣaśaraṇe karaṇetijña sudaivajñacittaharaṇebhinavaprakāre || daivajñaviṣṇuracite khacarāgamesminyāta sphuṭa prakaraṇaṃ paripūrṇamāsīt || ❖ || śāko nakhāgnīṣubhuvaḥ samaughaḥ sūryā hatau saugatamāsamīhaḥ || (fol. 10v10–11r2)
notes: 1) The date verse probably belongs to the text, not to this copy. Viṣṇu Daivajña's Sūryapakṣaśaraṇa karaṇa is known to use Śaka 1530 (c. 1608 CE) as its epoch. This verse comes right after the text's own closing verse, so it most likely gives the composition/epoch year. If so, Śaka 1530 is only the earliest possible date (terminus post quem) for the copy, and the catalogue's 'Date of Copying: ŚS 1530' may be wrong. 2) The chronogram does not work out exactly. Reading 'nakhāgnīṣubhuvaḥ' right to left with nakha = 20 gives bhū 1, iṣu 5, agni 3, nakha 20, which is more than four digits. 1530 only works if nakha is taken as 0 (or the compound is read loosely). 1530 does agree with the known epoch of the work. 3) 'samaughaḥ sūryā hatau saugatamāsamīhaḥ' is corrupt or obscure. It does not clearly give a month, so no month is recorded. 4) The catalogue names the scribe as Rudradevadvija (probably Rudradeva, titled dvija), but no scribe appears in the quoted colophon. That name must come from somewhere else in the manuscript and could not be checked here.
review: Removed month 'saugata': it is not a month name. The phrase 'sūryā hatau saugatamāsamīhaḥ' is corrupt or obscure and gives no reliable month.
Added a caveat in notes: the Śaka 1530 verse is probably the author's epoch (the date of the text's composition), not the date this copy was made.
Added a note on the chronogram reading (nakha = 20 does not fit four digits).
Kept Viṣṇu (daivajña) as author, Śaka 1530 = c. 1608 CE, and the remark about the scribe Rudradeva.

title: Līlāvatī
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Thursday 10 Apr 1659, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrībhāskarācāryaviracite siddhāṃtaśiromaṇau pāṭīnāmādhyāyaḥ prathamaḥ || samvat 1716 śake 1591 vaiśāṣakṛṣṇatṛtīyā gurau lkhitam idaṃ pustakaṃ bhaṭavidyādharamoḍha (!) nivedinā || śubhaṃ bhūyāt || (fol. 26r12–13)
notes: The two eras conflict. VS 1716 is c. 1659 CE and should correspond to ŚS 1581, but the colophon gives ŚS 1591, which is c. 1669 CE (equal to VS 1726). One of the two years is probably a slip; this record follows VS 1716, so 1669 is also possible. Checking the weekday (Thursday) against Vaiśākha kṛṣṇa 3 in each candidate year could settle it. The scribe's designation is corrupt: 'bhaṭavidyādharamoḍha (!) nivedinā' is best read as bhaṭṭa-vidyādhara-moḍha-trivedinā, i.e. Bhaṭṭa Vidyādhara, a Moḍha brahmin and Trivedin. Moḍha is a Gujarati brahmin community, so the copy may come from western India and not Nepal. The colophon names no place.

title: Grahalāghava
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Sunday 13 Jan 1704, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti ---- vāsādhikāraḥ samāptaḥ || iti grahalāghava siddhānta samāpta || || (fol. 19v2) ❖ samvat 824 pauṣaśukla satami(!) thvakunhu bhorānātha golamaṃ dhīyā bhājuyā ------ dhanarāma || śubha || (fol. 19v3-4)
notes: The Newari text reads 'bhorānātha golamaṃdhīyā bhājuyā': 'of Bhāju Bhorānātha of Golmadhi'. The genitive probably went with a noun that is now lost in the lacuna, perhaps pustaka (making him the owner) or kāya (making Dhanarāma his son). Because of the lacuna, his role and any relation to Dhanarāma cannot be fixed. Bhorānātha may be a variant of Bholānātha. Bhāju is a Newari honorific for laymen, not a caste name. Dhanarāma is taken to be the scribe only because his name stands in the closing position. Date: NS 824 + 880 = 1703/04; Pauṣa śukla 7 falls around late Dec 1703 to Jan 1704. This matches the catalogue's NS 824.
review: Place of copying cleared: the colophon does not say where the copy was made. Golamaṃdhī (Golmadhi ṭol, Bhaktapur) is only Bhorānātha's residence and stays in his record.
Dhanarāma's scribe role lowered to low confidence: the name comes straight after a lacuna and there is no verb of writing (coyā/likhitam).
Bhorānātha's confidence lowered to low and the name noted as possibly Bholānātha. His role stays 'other' because the lacuna hides what he did.
Tithi normalised to saptamī. ce_approx kept at 1704, with a note that Pauṣa śukla of NS 824 falls around Dec 1703 to Jan 1704.

colophon: iti śrīmahābhārate śatasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyāśikyāṃ strīparva samāptim agāt asyānaṃtaraṃ | rājadharmmasyāyam ādya ślokaḥ kṛco(!)dakās te suhṛdāṃ sarvveṣāṃ pāṃḍunaṃdanāḥ | viduro dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca sarvvāś ca ta(!)ratastriyaḥ śuta(!)m astu śaṃ(!)vat 1696 samaye mā(‥)vadi trayodaśi vāra(!) maṃdavāsareḥ(!) jā(!)dṛśaṃ pustakaṃ kṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ liṣ(!)yate mayā ja(!)di su(!)dha(!) asudha(!)ṃ vā mama doṣo na dīyate likhyate paramānaṃdkāstha(!) | (fol. 20r3–6)
notes: The colophon gives only 'śaṃvat 1696' with no era name. VS is assumed, following the usual convention for an unqualified saṃvat in Devanagari manuscripts, which gives about 1639 CE. If it were ŚS, the date would be about 1774 CE. The month is damaged: mā(‥) could be Māgha or Mārgaśīrṣa. The scribe's name and caste are written run together as 'paramānaṃdkāstha', read here as Paramānanda kāyastha (the cataloguer reads 'Pramānanda kāyastha ?'). The catalogue's 'King: Kamari Datta Sen ?' does not appear anywhere in the quoted colophon, so no king is recorded. It may come from another part of the manuscript, or it may be a mistake. The verse 'jā(!)dṛśaṃ pustakaṃ kṛṣṭvā(!) ...' is the standard scribe's disclaimer (yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā) and says nothing about who owned or commissioned the copy.

purpose: royal copy (śrīrājapustakaṃ), made for the king or the royal library
notes: 'rāmabhadradvuja' is corrupt. It most likely stands for 'rāmabhadradvija', meaning the brahmin Rāmabhadra, which is how the catalogue reads it too. It could also hide a kinship word such as '-tanuja' or '-ātmaja'. In that case the phrase would mean 'Rāmakṛṣṇa, son of Rāmabhadra', and Rāmakṛṣṇa alone would be the scribe. The relation between the two men is therefore left unrecorded. 'śrīrājapustakaṃ' marks the book as royal property, but no king is named. In ŚS 1688 (1766–67 CE) the Kathmandu Valley was being conquered by the Gorkhā ruler Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa Śāha, but nothing in the colophon says which court is meant. If 'month 12' is counted from Caitra it is Phālguna, which falls in early 1767 CE. If it is counted from Mārgaśīrṣa it is Kārttika, which falls in 1766 CE.

p3 Rāmakṛṣṇa: kept as possible co-scribe (low); possible son_of reading added to notes
purpose: changed from the bare word to an explanation: rājapustaka marks the copy as belonging to the king or royal library, which is an ownership statement and not a named beneficiary
date: month 12 read as Phālguna (counting from Caitra) and weekday 7 as Saturday; ce_approx refined to 1766–67, since Phālguna ŚS 1688 falls in Feb–Mar 1767

The verse also gives mādhava = Vaiśākha, rasa (written raṣa) = 6, bhṛgudina = Friday and tiṣya = Puṣya. NS 317 is about 1197 CE, so the king must be Lakṣmīkāmadeva II of the late 12th century, not Lakṣmīkāmadeva I of the 11th century. 'lakṣī' is an error for lakṣmī. 'jasa brahmaṇā' in the verse is probably a corruption of jayabrahmaṇā. 'lekhakapipra' stands for lekhaka-vipra. Both 'hastalikhāyitaṃ' and 'likhāyitaṃ' are causatives. Here they probably just mean 'written', because Jayabrahman calls himself lekhaka and the copy is for his own use. A commissioner role cannot be ruled out entirely, though. 'paṇḍitācāryaśrīśrī vaccharūdrācāryakṛtvā' is unclear: it may name a teacher, a reviser or the person who arranged the copy, and the name may be Vatsarudra. I have not checked the weekday against an ephemeris.

title: Bhāgavata(daśamaskanda)
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Monday 14 Feb 1724, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: … haribhaktir astu śubhaṃ || sambat 844 māghakṛṣṇāpaṃcamī citrānakṣatra bhājudevanathavatāro cakāvatayā || (ṅākṣa 1036 vida) || (fol. 203v4-5)
notes: The Newari passage is corrupt. 'cakāvatayā' is most likely coyakā(va) tayā, 'had it written and kept'. That would make the named person the commissioner rather than the scribe; no scribe is named. 'bhājudevanathavatāro' is read here as bhāju (an honorific) + Devanātha (written 'devanatha'). The remainder, 'vatāro', is unclear. It could be a corruption, a genitive/ergative ending, or 'va tāro' ('and Tāro'), which would mean a second co-commissioner named Tāro/Tāra. The name, the title 'bhāju' and the role are therefore only medium confidence. The bracketed '(ṅākṣa 1036 vida)' appears to be a separate, later note: NS 1036 is about 1916 CE, and 'vida' may be Newari biyā, 'given'. It may record a later transfer of the manuscript and does not date this copy. The date itself, NS 844 Māgha kṛṣṇa 5, falls in about Jan–Feb 1724 CE.

title: Kāmandakīyanītisāra
subject: Nīti
date_note: = Sunday 17 Mar 1247, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: nītisāre rājopadeśe kāmandakīye ekaviṃśatamaḥ sargaḥ || ○ || śribhadrākhyaṃ samastāṅgaḥ | makāmādivṛddhaye | śrīmaddevadhareṇedaṃ samāptaṃ guṇinām prabho || ○ || śrī śrī śrī śrī śrīkaṇṭhāya namaḥ || samvat 367 caitraśukladaśamyāṃ śrīphaṇapiṅgasthāne viṣayādhipati mahāsāmanta śrījetamalla [[likhitasvapustakabhā]]veṣu vijayarājye .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. (fol. 110v2–5)
purpose: dharmakāmādivṛddhaye (for the increase of dharma, kāma, etc.)
notes: The era isn't named ('samvat 367'). Reading it as NS (as the catalogue suggests) and the 'viṣayādhipati mahāsāmanta' formula, which fits the 13th century, NS 367 Caitra falls in spring 1247 CE. The bracketed '[[likhitasvapustakabhā]]veṣu' looks like a later or corrupt insertion into the vijayarājye formula. It might mean 'written as [my/his] own book', but it is unclear whether 'sva' refers to the scribe Devadhara or to Jetamalla, so no owner role was assigned. 'makāmādivṛddhaye' is probably a damaged 'dharmakāmādivṛddhaye'. 'śribhadrākhyaṃ samastāṅgaḥ' is corrupt. It may hide a name or an epithet, but it was not extracted as a person. 'guṇinām prabho' is a vocative/epithet, not a person. Jetamalla was the feudatory ruler of Phaṇapiṅga (Pharping).
review: Removed 'owner' from Jetamalla: the inserted, bracketed '[[likhitasvapustakabhā]]' is corrupt and doesn't clearly name him as owner. It could equally mean the scribe's own book. Explained in notes.
Purpose normalised to the probable reading dharmakāmādivṛddhaye.
Notes expanded: the interpolation, the NS conversion, and the identification of Jetamalla.

title: Vyavasthārṇava
subject: Dharmaśāstra
date_note: = Tuesday 23 Jun 1778, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti gauḍadeśīya raghunāthasārvabhaumaviracito vyavasthārṇavaḥ samāptaṃ saṃpūrṇam śrīśāke || 1700 || || śrīsaṃvat || 18 || 35 ||| miti dutīā āṣānhavaditerasī || †ke prasataka puraṇa bhaye ena somaradeṣyā somaralīṣyā ||† (fol. 71r3-5)
notes:
The colophon gives two dates, Śaka 1700 and Vikrama Saṃvat 1835. They agree: both are 1778 CE, and the catalogue fields match. 'dutīā āṣānha' probably means the second Āṣāḍha, which would make it an intercalary month. This has not been checked against an ephemeris.

The closing note is vernacular and corrupt: †ke prasataka puraṇa bhaye ena somaradeṣyā somaralīṣyā†. A likely reading is '[yah] pustaka pūraṇa bhaye; Somara dekhyā, Somara likhyā' ('the book was completed; Somara saw/checked it, Somara wrote it'). On that reading Somara is the scribe, and possibly also the checker of the copy. The name may also be Somāru, or the text may be a garbled 'somavāra' (Monday), so confidence is low.

'Gauḍadeśīya' describes the author Raghunātha Sārvabhauma, not the scribe.
review: p2 Somara: removed residence 'Gauḍadeśa'. That belongs to the author Raghunātha, not the scribe.
p2 Somara: still scribe, low confidence. Read the vernacular note as 'pustaka pūraṇa bhaye … Somara dekhyā, Somara likhyā'.
date.month normalized to 'Āṣāḍha (dvitīya, i.e. second/intercalary)'. Paksa normalized to 'kṛṣṇa (vadi)' and tithi to '13 (trayodaśī)'.

title: Mukundavijaya
subject: Tantra
date_note: = Thursday 3 Aug 1780, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: svasti śrīnepālasamvatsaragate 900 śrāvaṇaśulkatṛtīyāyāṃ tīthau (!) uttarabhadraṇakṣatre (!) dhṛtiyoge śukravāsare ttaddine (!) sampūrṇam iti || śubham astu || || || śrīdivākarāya rastu (!) || || ❖ kṛttikānva viśākhānva bhaumavāreṇasaṃyutaṃ taddine ghaṭitaṃ śastraṃ saṃgrāme jayadāyakaṃ || iti sva[[rodaye]] || (fol. 38v6-8)
notes: 'śrīdivākarāya rastu (!)' is probably 'śrīdivākarāyāstu', a dative blessing meaning '[may it] be for Divākara'. That would fit a human owner or beneficiary named Divākara. It could also be a garbled invocation to the Sun god (Divākara), possibly a corruption of '...namo 'stu'. If it is the deity, delete p1, which is why its confidence is low. The colophon names no scribe or place. After the completion formula the copy adds a Svarodaya verse about weapons made on a Tuesday with Kṛttikā or Viśākhā; the cataloguer supplied '[[rodaye]]'. That verse's nakṣatras and weekday are not part of the copying date. 'ttaddine' is a corruption of 'taddine'. The colophon agrees with the catalogue date (NS 900).
review: No substantive changes. Persons, date, era and ce_approx (NS 900 + 880 = 1780; Śrāvaṇa of NS 900 falls in mid-1780) are correct.
Notes expanded: the uncertainty about Divākara is explained in more detail, and the nakṣatra and weekday terms in the appended verse are marked as not part of the copying date.

title: Dīkṣāpaddhati
subject: Tāntrika Karmakāṇḍa
colophon: iti mahāmahopādhyāya rāmajīvanatarkālaṃkārabhaṭṭācāryyātmajaśrīvāgīśvarabhaṭṭācāryyaviracitāyāṃ dīkṣāpaddhatyāṃ paṃcamapaṭalaḥ || || †turārke† sitapakṣe vai tṛtīyāyāṃ śanau sudhīḥ śrīnārāyaṇaśarmāhaṃ vyalikhad īśvarechayā || 1 || samāptam || || śubham || (fol. 56r6-8, exp. 42b)
notes: The cataloguer marks '†turārke†' as corrupt. The probable reading is 'tulārke' ('when the sun is in Tulā'), which would give the solar month Tulā, roughly October–November. The colophon gives no year and no era, so the copy cannot be dated from it. The scribal verse mixes persons: 'nārāyaṇaśarmāhaṃ' is first person, but 'vyalikhad' is third person (as is 'sudhīḥ'); it is a metrical, ungrammatical verse, and the scribe is still clearly Nārāyaṇa. The colophon names the author as Vāgīśvara Bhaṭṭācārya, son of Mahāmahopādhyāya Rāmajīvana Tarkālaṃkāra Bhaṭṭācārya. The Bhaṭṭācārya title probably points to a Bengali scholarly family. The catalogue's scribe field (Nārāyaṇa Śarmā) agrees with the colophon.
review: p3: name changed from 'Nārāyaṇa Śarman' to 'Nārāyaṇa'. 'śarman' is a brahmin suffix, so it stays only in titles.
purpose: emptied. 'īśvarechayā' (by the will of God) is a pious formula, not a statement of purpose (svārtha/parārtha etc.).
notes: added remarks on the grammar of the scribal verse and on the tulārke reading.

'tatchāsanika' = tacchāsanika, 'his (the king's) officer/appointee'. 'rāuta' is a rank title (from rājaputra). 'surahi' is read as Sura plus the vernacular instrumental ending -hi, the agent of 'likhāpitam'; the name Surahi is less likely. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Sura Rāuta' is wrong: Sura had the copy made for himself (commissioner/owner). The actual scribe is not named; 'lekhaka' appears only in the closing benediction. review: p2 name normalized from 'Surahi' to 'Sura': '-hi' is the vernacular (Apabhraṃśa/Old Hindi) instrumental/agentive ending governing 'likhāpitam'. This agrees with the catalogue's 'Sura Rāuta'. Confidence lowered to medium.
Added a servant_of relation from p2 to p1. 'tacchāsanika' (written tatchāsanika) means 'his officer, one under his command', and 'tat' refers back to Jayacandradeva.

title: Pūrvāmnāyanityakarmadevārcanavidhi
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Friday 17 Aug 1714, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīpūrvvāmnāyanityakarmmadevārccanavi(4)dhi samāptaṃ || || saṃvat 834 śrāvana śuklasaptamīkuhnu saṃpurṇṇa yā(5)ṅā juro || liṣiti vidyāpiyā karmmācarya, lakṣmīdharana saṃpurṇṇa yāṅā ju(6)ro || || saṃvat 832 vakādharaṃ dāṅāyā hlāṣa || || || (7) yā diṣṭi | puṣṭakaṃ dṛsṭā, tā dṛṣṭi likṣitaṃ mayā, jadi śuddhaṃ maśurddhaṃ vā liṣā(8)ko dāṣa(!) nāṣṭidaṃ || || yadakṣala pabhṛṣṭaṃ māṭrāhinaṃ tathaiva ca ta(33b1)t sarvva kṣammatā māta kṣamaśva parameśvarī || || iśvarī prītrīrastu || || (exp. 34t3-34b1)
notes: The Karmācārya Lakṣmīdhara finished copying this manuscript on Śrāvaṇa śukla 7, NS 834 (c. 1714 CE). His residence or affiliation 'vidyāpiyā' is unclear. It is a Newari genitive ('of Vidyāpī-') and could be a place, a lineage, or something corrupt. A separate line reads 'saṃvat 832 vakādharaṃ dāṅāyā hlāṣa', dated NS 832 (c. 1712 CE). It probably records something done by or with a person Vakādhara (perhaps Bakādhara). This could be the start of the copying, the handover of the exemplar, or a gift. The wording is obscure, so both the name and the role are uncertain. The two years 832 and 834 are both Nepāla Saṃvat and do not conflict. The colophon ends with the usual scribal verses ('yādṛṣṭaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā…', 'yad akṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ…').
review: Purpose: 'iśvarī prītrīrastu' is a closing benediction (īśvarī prītir astu, 'may the Goddess be pleased'). It does not say who the copy was made for. Recorded it as a benediction and gave a normalised form.
Lakṣmīdhara's residence 'vidyāpiyā' kept, but the notes now flag it as uncertain. It is a Newari genitive ('of Vidyāpī-') and could be a place, a lineage or a corruption.
Notes expanded on the NS 832 entry. Also noted that the 832/834 years are not two conflicting eras.

title: Śabdalakṣaṇavivaraṇapañjikā
subject: vyākaraṇa
date_note: ≈ 1034 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: /// yāmi praṇīta sabdalakṣaṇavivaraṇapañjikāyāmācārya pūrṇṇacandra viracitāyāḥ vachyokhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || || ....... (a hṛ pta) (59v1) dvayorddhi ....... punarvasunakṣatre || rajādhirāja parameśvara paramabhaṭṭārakaḥ śrīlakṣmīkāmadevasya vijayarājyeḥ | śrīkopravalabhya || || somara…… (2) .. lekhikena likhitanna itti || || ۞ ||
notes: The year is written in letter-numerals (a hṛ pta). The value 154 comes from the catalogue: no era is named, and the value of each sign could not be checked independently. NS 154 = 1033/34 CE, which fits Lakṣmīkāmadeva's reign (c. NS 144–160 / 1024–1040 CE). 'somara……' follows the place name and comes just before '.. lekhikena', so it is probably the start of the scribe's name (e.g. Somarāja…). It could also be the start of a weekday (somavāra), though. In that case the scribe's name is lost in the lacuna. 'śrīkopravalabhya' is a corrupt toponym (perhaps a vihāra or locality) and cannot be identified. 'dvayorddhi' is fragmentary, possibly part of the tithi. Pūrṇacandra wrote the pañjikā, a commentary on the Śabdalakṣaṇavivaraṇa, so his role is given as commentator.
review: p3 (scribe 'Somara…'): kept at low confidence, with a note that 'somara' may instead be the start of a weekday (somavāra) and the scribe's name may be lost in the lacuna
Date: era NS is only inferred, since no era is written; noted that the letter-numeral reading a-hṛ-pta = 154 rests on the catalogue
ce_approx left as 1034 (NS 154 = 1033/34 CE); fits Lakṣmīkāmadeva's reign
Notes expanded: corrupt place name and the uncertain letter-numeral values

title: Pratimālakṣaṇasamuccaya
subject: vāstuśāstra
date_note: = Friday 25 Feb 1684, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: saṃ 804 phālguṇa śikla pakṣe navamyāntithau śukravāra thvakuhnu coya dhunakāvaṃ lānihma vāsinā śrītri(30r6)vikrameśādaṭa puṣṭakam iti || ||(7) gaṃgāya dhyana rudra jāmale || devīñcattrar.. joṃ gaṃgā trinetrāṃ mukta ṭo..lāṃ | padma daryyaṇahastāñcavaradā bhaya hastakāṃ || (30v1) divya vastra vṛtāṃ kāntāṃ sarvvābharaṇa bhūṣitāṃ || praṃcaṇḍa vadanāṃ dhyāyachi cotsaṃge ca comatāṃ || || gajuli(2)yā cosa luna thva yāvate thvani rañjana mūrtti || pustaka, padma, vara, abhaya, padmāsana || thvate juro || (3)
notes: 'śrītrivikrameśādaṭa' is corrupt. It most likely reads Trivikrama(-īśa/-datta?) plus the Newari dative -ṭa (= -yāta), meaning 'the book for Trivikrama...'. If so, he is the recipient/owner and the scribe is unnamed. 'lānihma vāsinā' is obscure: it could be '(the) resident of Lāni' or a Newari verb phrase. It is not taken as the place of copying. Everything after 'iti || ||' is a later addition: a Gaṅgā dhyāna 'from the Rudrayāmala' and Newari iconographic notes. These do not name anyone connected with this copy. 'śikla' = śukla.
review: p1: the final -ṭa in 'śrītrivikrameśādaṭa' is most likely the Newari dative ending ('for/to'). The book is therefore for Trivikrama..., not written by him. Roles changed from scribe+owner to owner. The scribe is not named.
p1 name: best reading is 'Trivikrama' (stem uncertain: perhaps Trivikrameśa or Trivikramadatta). Confidence lowered to low.
Residence/place: 'lānihma vāsinā' is unclear. It may be a Newari verb form ('handed over'?) and not a toponym. Removed 'Lānihma' as residence and as place of copying; explained in notes.
Purpose set to: book for Trivikrama (dative).
Date confirmed: NS 804 phālguṇa śukla 9, Friday, about 1684 CE (Feb/Mar).

colophon: iti śrībhīmasya pavitrārohanavidhiḥ samāpta | ḥ || || ❁ || saṃ 787 caitra śukla pratipadā kūnhu śuklavāra coyedhu naka | cokahma śrībhākūtunacoā yāvaviyā śrīvakhanihmaṃ śrīsudarśanabhāju yātacoyā (x11b:8- x12a:3 )
notes: The era is not written ('saṃ 787'). NS is assumed from the script and the catalogue. Caitra NS 787 falls in March/April 1667 CE. The weekday (Friday) has not been checked. The Newari phrase 'cokahma śrībhākūtunacoā yāvaviyā śrīvakhanihmaṃ' is hard to parse, and the cataloguer may have split the words wrongly. It roughly means 'the writer, Vakhani, living (coā) at Bhākūtuna, of Yāvavi'. 'yāvaviyā' could be a genitive giving the scribe's father, house or locality (for example Yā Bahi), so it is not recorded as an affiliation. The scribe's name 'Vakhani' is uncertain: it could be a garbled personal name or an occupational term. Sudarśana's title 'bhāju' is an honorific, often used for brahmins or gentlemen. He was probably also the commissioner and owner, but the colophon only says 'written for' him.
review: p1 Sudarśana: roles changed from commissioner+owner to beneficiary. 'yātacoyā' (yāta coyā) only says the copy was written for him. Commissioning and ownership are likely but not stated.
p2 scribe: name changed from 'Vakhanihma' to 'Vakhani'. '-hmaṃ' is the Newari agentive classifier (-mhaṃ), not part of the name. Confidence lowered to low.
p2: 'yāvavi' taken out of affiliation and put in notes. 'yāvaviyā' may be a genitive ('of Yāvavi'), giving a kin or locality link, rather than a vihāra name.
place: emptied. 'bhākūtuna coā' describes where the scribe lives, not where the copy was made.
purpose reworded.

title: Śīghrabodha
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: doubtful: Saturday 19 Dec 907 is too early for a paper manuscript (an abbreviated or misread year, or the exemplar's date)
date_doubtful: doubtful: Saturday 19 Dec 907 is too early for a paper manuscript (an abbreviated or misread year, or the exemplar's date)
colophon: iti śrīkāśināthakṛtau śīghrabodhāyaḥ (!) prakaranaṃ samāpta (!) || || || 591 || || || ||❖ samvat. 28 pauṣaśukla 12 roja 7 vāla || || thva saphūlasidha yakā dina juro || || dai iba bhe || keśavasiṃhana juro || || || || śubha || (fol. 40v)
notes: The catalogue gives NS 591 (= 1471 CE), probably from the bare number '591' right after the text's closing words. That number has no 'samvat' and could instead be a grantha/verse count. The full date with tithi and weekday is 'samvat 28 pauṣa śukla 12, Saturday', which seems to have the century left out (e.g. NS 728 = 1608 CE or NS 828 = 1708 CE). The Persian loan 'roja' (day) and the Newari wording suggest the later Malla period rather than 1471, so ce_approx is left empty. If 591 is the year, the copy dates to 1471 CE. A weekday check of Pauṣa śu. 12 against NS 591 and 728/828 could settle this. 'thva saphū lasidha yakā dina juro' = 'this is the day the book was completed'. 'dai iba bhe' is unclear (perhaps corrupt; maybe a title like daivajña, or a place or a relative). Keśavasiṃha is taken as the scribe on the strength of the instrumental 'keśavasiṃhana juro', as the catalogue also has it.
review: Weekday normalised: 'roja 7 vāla' = 7th day, i.e. Saturday (roja = day); recorded as '7 (Saturday)' rather than 'roja 7'.
as_written for Kāśīnātha trimmed to the form as it appears (kāśinātha-), without śrī; stem normalised to Kāśīnātha.
Scribe confidence lowered to medium because the instrumental keśavasiṃhana stands next to the unclear 'dai iba bhe' and the clause only says the book was completed by him.
Date: the dated clause is still read as NS (century omitted) 28. The notes now explain the conflict with the catalogue's NS 591 (= 1471 CE) and give possible ce values.

notes: The scribe's name, 'Jayarūndrasiṃha', is probably a corrupt spelling of Jayarudrasiṃha. The catalogue gives a chronogram: durggā(9) aginī(3) vasu(8). Read right to left this gives 839, which matches the colophon's Saṃbat 839, so NS 839 = 1718 CE (kārttika). The catalogue also gives a bracketed second date, 'saṃvat 831', with the same month, pakṣa, tithi, nakṣatra, yoga and weekday. This conflicts with 839. It may come from a second colophon or be a misreading; 831 would be 1710/11 CE. The quoted colophon does not name the king (Mahīndrasiṃha) or the place (Kathmandu); they appear only in the catalogue fields, so they are not listed as persons or place. The date fits the reign of Mahīndrasiṃha (Mahīndra Siṃha Malla) of Kathmandu, c. 1714–1722.

notes: Chronogram 'gaṃdharvvajaivātrikasarpyamāne' (corrupt for -sarpa-māne): gandharva = horse = 7, jaivātrika = moon = 1, sarpa = 8. Read right to left this gives 817. No era is named. NS is assumed from the Newari script, so 817 + 880 ≈ 1697 CE. This is not certain: read as VS 817, the year would be impossibly early for Mallinātha, who lived in the 14th–15th century. Calendar check, not done: Svātī on a kṛṣṇa caturthī with the sun already in Meṣa looks astronomically awkward, so the date details may be garbled. Bhūmideva wrote the copy 'cirāya' (to last) after bowing to Maheśa's lotus feet. The opening invocation is to Nārāyaṇa, Nara and Śiva. The scribe matches the catalogue field 'Bhūmideva ?'. Kolacala is Mallinātha's family name.
review: Chronogram decoded: gandharva (= horse, aśva) = 7, jaivātrika (moon) = 1, sarpa (nāga) = 8; read right to left this gives 817. The era is not stated, but a Newari-script copy points to NS, so year 817 ≈ 1697 CE. The first reading left the year undecoded and guessed 'NS 81x'.
Era left 'unspecified' because the colophon gives none; ce_approx set to 1697 on the NS assumption.
Mallinātha: 'Kolacala' moved to notes as a family/clan name rather than an institutional affiliation (kept in the affiliation field as a lineage marker).
Notes extended with the astronomical caveat and the invocation.

title: Mahāmatasāra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Friday 18 Oct 1929, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: || iti caturviṃśatisahastraśrīmahāmatasāraśrīmahālakṣmīmatabhaṭṭārake katipayasādhanakathano nāma daśama ānandaḥ || || samāptaḥ śrīmahālakṣmīmatabhaṭṭāraka iti || aśītyadhikasaṃyāte samvatsaraśatatraye || māsi caitreʼ site pakṣe pañcamyāṃ bhṛguvāsare || … mahārājādhirājaparameśvaraparamamāheśvaraparamabhaṭṭārakaśrīmajjayabhīmarājye || || iti maṅgalamahāśrī. ity attra lekhayutāt prācīnabhujavalākṣaralikhitatāḍapatrapustakād uddhṛtya śrīrājagurūhemarājapaṇḍitavarāṇām ājñayā 1986 vaikramāvde āśvinapūrṇimāyāṃ pūrṇaprasādaśarmaṇā vilikyā samāpitam idaṃ pustakam iti. (fol. 46r1–7)
purpose: copied by order of Rājaguru Hemarāja Paṇḍita
notes:
This is a modern transcript (VS 1986, about 1929 CE). Hemarāja is almost certainly the well-known Rājaguru Hemarāja Śarmā (Paṇḍita).

The transcript was taken ('uddhṛtya') from an old palm-leaf manuscript written in Bhujimol script ('bhujavalākṣara'). It reproduces that exemplar's colophon: 'aśītyadhikasaṃyāte samvatsaraśatatraye' = year 380, Caitra śukla 5, a Friday, in the reign of Jayabhīma(deva). The exemplar's date names no era, but it is presumably NS 380 (about 1260 CE). That fits Jayabhīmadeva's reign, roughly NS 378–391.

For this reason Jayabhīmadeva has role 'other' rather than reigning king of this copy, so the catalogue's King field refers to the exemplar. 'vilikyā' stands for vilikhya. 'lekhayutāt' is unclear and may stand for lekhayuktāt.
review: p1 Jayabhīmadeva: role changed from 'king' to 'other'. He reigned when the palm-leaf exemplar was copied in (NS) 380, about 1260 CE, not when this copy was made in VS 1986 (1929 CE).
p3: name changed from 'Pūrṇaprasāda Śarman' to stem form 'Pūrṇaprasāda'; śarman stays in titles only.
Date: paksa filled as śukla, which pūrṇimā implies.
Purpose: shortened to a plain description.

Notes: the exemplar's date was left without a stated era; it is now given as an inferred NS 380 with a check against Jayabhīmadeva's reign. Added notes on the exemplar's script and the corrupt word 'vilikyā'.

title: Kūlārṇava
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Wednesday 17 Aug 1791, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīkulārṇave mahārahasye īśvarapārvatīsaṃvāde dūtīsapādalakṣagranthe paṃcamakhaṇḍe dūtīyāgārccanaṃ nāmāṣṭādaśollāsaḥ || 18 || || śubhaṃ bhavatu sarvadā || || [after the sub colophon of the 17th chapter, on the exp.70 is given:] iti śrīkulārṇave mahārahasye sarvvasāre sapādalakṣagranthe tattvasāre paṃcamakhaṇḍe gurunāmāditattvapadārthannāmaḥ samāptaḥ || saṃvat 1713 bhādraṅṛṣṇatṛtīyāṃ(!) budha (!) revatyāṃ daivajña〈〈‥ ‥〉〉varmaṇā likhitaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || yādṛśī pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā... kṣamyatāṃ parameśvari | ... manu || tīrthe maṃtre tathā deve daivajñe āiṣadhe tathā| yādṛśī bhāvanā yasya siddhir bhavati tādṛśī |\ bhāvena cuṃbite- (!) 1yuādśī bhāvanā yasya īśvarapārvatīsaṃvāde sapādalakṣagranthe tatvasāre paṃcamakhaṃḍe || gurunāmāditatvapadārthannāma saptadaśollāsaḥ samāptaḥ || saṃvat 1713 bhādrakṛṣṇatṛtīyāṃ vudharevatyāṃ daivajñavarmmaṇalikhitaṃ saṃpūrṇṇaṃ || (fol. 62r5–6)
notes:
Scribe: the name is given twice. On exp. 70 it reads 'daivajña〈〈‥ ‥〉〉varmaṇā', with a marked lacuna or insertion between daivajña and varmaṇā. On fol. 62r it reads 'daivajñavarmmaṇalikhitaṃ'. The full name may therefore be '…varman', with only the ending surviving. 'Daivajña' is taken as a title (astrologer). The catalogue's 'Varmmaṇa' is an inflected form.

Era: the colophon says only 'saṃvat'. The catalogue gives ŚS 1713, which would be 1791 CE. A rough mean-lunation check (amānta Bhādrapada, kṛṣṇa 3) gives these results:
- VS 1713: kṛṣṇa 3 falls on about 6 Sept 1656, a Wednesday, with the Moon in about Revatī. This agrees with 'budha revatyāṃ'.
- ŚS 1713: kṛṣṇa 3 falls on about 15–16 Sept 1791 (Thursday/Friday), with the Moon near the Revatī/Aśvinī boundary. This fits less well.
VS 1713 (c. 1656 CE) is therefore preferred, but this has not been checked with an exact pañcāṅga.

Text: the same dated colophon closes the 17th ullāsa (gurunāmāditattvapadārtha), apparently in two copies. The 18th-ullāsa colophon has no date. The passage '...bhāvena cuṃbite- (!) 1yuādśī bhāvanā yasya...' is corrupt in the catalogue quotation.
review: Scribe evidence now uses the fuller form 'daivajña〈〈‥ ‥〉〉varmaṇā likhitaṃ'. Confidence lowered to low because the marked lacuna may hide the first part of the name (…varman).

Date: added a rough check of the weekday and nakṣatra. VS 1713 (6 Sept 1656 CE, a Wednesday, Moon in Revatī) fits better than the catalogue's ŚS 1713 (c. 15–16 Sept 1791, Thursday/Friday). ce_approx set to 1656 while the era stays 'unspecified'.
Notes expanded: the catalogue's ŚS attribution is questioned, the two colophon copies are listed, and the corrupt passage is flagged.

title: Netrajñānārṇavatantra
subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: ≈ 1419 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti netrajñānārṇave mahātantre sutantrabhāvane śrīmata (!) kailāsamukhanirgate śrīprāpṛcchābhidhāne śrīguhyāmṛtīśārcano nāma ekaṣaṣṭipaṭalaḥ sapāptam iti | || samvat 439 māghakṛṣṇadvitīyātithau uttarāphālgunīnakṣatre mūlayoge ādityavāsare lalitapattane purādhivāsinā †śrīmāniglake† śrīdakṣināvihāraśrīyothāvihārāddhavanāyakamūrtyaṅgapradhānāṅgapātraśrījayadevavarmaṇā naḥ svārthahetunā svahastena śrīnetrajñānārṇavatantraṃ daityanārāyaṇayuvarājaśrīśrījagajjyotirmalladevānāṃ vijayarājye likhitam. ityantalekhayutāt śrīdaºº.kaºº janaralakeśaravarmasaṃṅgṛhītāt prāyaśo .śuddhatāḍapatrapustākād uddhṛtya śrīmanmānyavarapravbalagorakhādakṣīṇabāhurājaguruhemarājaśarmavidvadvarākhyayā 1991 vaikramābde nepālakāṣṭhamaṇḍaparājadhānyāṃ pūrṇaprasādaśarmaṇā likhitam idaṃ pustakaṃ śubhāya bhavatu || || (fol. 89r5–8)
purpose: no purpose stated for this copy; ends with the benediction 'śubhāya bhavatu'
notes: This manuscript is a paper transcript made in Kathmandu in VS 1991 (1934/35 CE). Pūrṇaprasāda copied it on the order of Rājaguru Hemarāja from a palm-leaf manuscript collected by General Keśara (Kaiser Shumsher Rana); the colophon calls that source largely corrupt ('prāyaśo .śuddha'). The transcript reproduces the source's own colophon ('ityantalekhayutāt'). In that colophon, Jayadeva(varmā) of Lalitapattana (Māniglaka), attached to Dakṣiṇāvihāra and Yothāvihāra, says he wrote it with his own hand for his own purpose ('svārthahetunā svahastena'). He did so on Māgha kṛṣṇa 2, under Uttaraphālgunī, in yoga Mūla, on a Sunday, in the reign of Yuvarāja Jagajjyotirmalla. Because of this, Jayadeva and the king are recorded with role 'other', not as scribe and king of this copy. The year of the source is a problem. The quoted colophon reads 'samvat 439' (1319 CE), but the catalogue gives NS 539 (1419 CE). 539 fits Jyotirmalla, son of Jayasthitimalla, who ruled about 1408–1428. 439 fits no known Jagajjyotirmalla. So 539 is probably correct and the '439' in the quotation is probably a typo; it needs checking on the reel. Several readings are uncertain: '†śrīmāniglake†' is marked corrupt by the cataloguer; 'āddhavanāyakamūrtyaṅgapradhānāṅgapātra' is an unclear string of office titles; and 'śrīdaºº.kaºº' is an abbreviated title of Keśara.
review: p1 Jayadeva: his role changed from 'scribe' to 'other'. He wrote the palm-leaf exemplar in NS 439/539, not this 1934 copy. Name stripped to 'Jayadeva' with 'varmā' moved to titles. Affiliation split into the two vihāras.
p2 Jagajjyotirmalladeva: role changed from 'king' to 'other'. He was reigning when the exemplar was copied, not when this VS 1991 transcript was made.
p3 Keśara (General Kaiser Shumsher): role changed from 'owner' to 'other'. He collected the exemplar, not this copy. Name stripped to 'Keśara' with 'varmā' moved to titles.
p4 Hemarāja: 'śarmā' moved from the name to titles.
p5 Pūrṇaprasāda: 'śarmā' moved from the name to titles.
Added a relation from p5 to p3 (copied from the exemplar in p3's collection).
Notes: added the exemplar's full date and flagged the NS 439 vs NS 539 problem. 539 fits Jyotirmalla's reign; 439 does not.
Purpose: 'śubhāya bhavatu' is now labelled as a benediction. Jayadeva's 'svārthahetunā' (for his own purpose) applies to the exemplar, not this copy.

notes: The date uses the Persian-style formula 'śālamiti … roja 3' (year-date … weekday 3 = Tuesday). Caitra śukla 4 of NS 977 falls in March/April 1857 CE. The date is followed by a lacunose Newari note, 'saṃni saṃsthiti coyā ... svarggavāsa lāyu'. It appears to record that someone died (went to heaven) on this date, but the name is lost in the lacuna. So the date may be the date of that death note rather than the date of copying. The catalogue gives the date of copying as NS 977, which suggests the cataloguer took this as the copying date. The catalogue's king, Bhūpālendra(malla), is not in the quoted colophon. He reigned in Bhaktapur c. 1687–1696 CE, which does not fit 1857 CE, so the catalogue field is probably wrong or comes from elsewhere in the manuscript.

title: Amarakoṣa: avyaya- liṅgādisaṅgrahavarga, saṭīka
subject: Koṣa
date_note: ≈ 1780 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: (mūla:) samvat 1837 || yasya likhitar kalyāṇar sarvadā || || (fol. 3r) (ṭīkā:) iti śrīvaghelavaṃśodbhavaśrīmahīmahīyara(!)viṣayādhipatiśrīkīrttisiṃhadevājñayā śrī bhaṭṭojidīkṣitātmajaśrībhānujidīkṣitaviracitāyām amaraṭīkāyām vyākhyāsudhākhyāyām tritīya(!)kāṇḍaḥ sampūrṇṇatām agāt || || śivaḥ || śubha || barhirkhanagarharervārarādityaryukte || likhitam ida granther ddharmmaddhajosya kīrtte || 1 || (fol. 3v)
notes: The year is given only as 'samvat 1837'. VS (= c. 1780 CE) is assumed because the script is Nagari and the text is Bhānuji Dīkṣita's 17th-century commentary. NS is impossible. ŚS 1837 (= 1915 CE) cannot be strictly ruled out. The final verse is corrupt; a probable reading is 'barhirkhanagare harer vāre ādityayukte likhitam idaṃ granthaṃ dharmadhvajo 'sya kīrteḥ': 'in Barhirkha-nagara, on Hari's day (ekādaśī) falling on a Sunday, Dharmadhvaja wrote this book …'. Dharmadhvaja as scribe is therefore probable but not certain, and the place name is uncertain. The date 1837 stands at the end of the mūla text (fol. 3r); the scribe verse comes after the ṭīkā colophon (fol. 3v). Kīrttisiṃhadeva, the Vaghela ruler of 'Mahīmahīyara(!)', ordered the original commentary; he is not the reigning king of this copy. 'yasya likhitaṃ kalyāṇaṃ sarvadā' is a blessing formula and names no one.
review: Kīrttisiṃhadeva: role changed from 'king' to 'other'. He ordered the commentary itself (ājñayā … viracitāyām), so he is the patron of the original text, not the reigning king of this 1837 copy.
Bhaṭṭoji and Bhānuji: 'Dīkṣita' taken out of the names and kept only in titles (names now 'Bhaṭṭoji', 'Bhānuji').

Date: tithi filled in as ekādaśī (harer vāra = harivāsara) and weekday normalised to Sunday (ādityavāra). The year has no era name; VS 1837 = c. 1780 CE is kept as the likely reading and the assumption is stated in notes.
Place as_written changed to the actual colophon substring 'barhirkhanagar[e]'.
Notes rewritten: the verse is parsed and the doubts about the era and the scribe are flagged.

The date is a bare 'śrīsaṃvat 1877' with no era named. The copy was made in Kāśī in Nagari script, so Vikrama Saṃvat is the likely era (VS 1877 ≈ 1820 CE). The catalogue gives ŚS 1877, which would mean c. 1955 CE; that reading is not supported by the colophon. Rudradeva's role as owner is inferred from 'pāṭhārtham'; the colophon does not say the book is his.
review: p2 Rudradeva: dropped 'reader'. The colophon has 'rudradevasya pāṭhārtham', which says the copy was made for his study; it does not say he read it. Kept 'beneficiary' and added 'owner', following the svapaṭhanārtham rule for a copy made for someone's study.
Notes: made clear that the era is a bare 'saṃvat', so VS is an inference, and that the catalogue's ŚS 1877 would mean c. 1955 CE.

title: Kāraṇḍavyūha
subject: Bauddhasūtra
date_note: = Sunday 28 May 1899, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīśakhyakā(!)buddhamāyājālatatre(!) aṣṭā.itisahaśraṣaṇḍe paṭale śrīkāla(!)vyūhaśrīāryyāvalokṛteśvara(!)varṇakāra(!)vyūha(!) samāptaṃm(!) || || ye dharmmā hetuprabhāvā hetu(s) teṣāṃ tathāgata(!) he(!) vartta(!) te(ṣ)ā(!) ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaṃ || || || samvat 1019 miti vaiśāṣavadi 3 ro 1 sathosā(pu)tadhukṣeyāmachindravajrācāryye | tadhukṣayāvajrācāryye kāruyāta coyāvaviyājulo || || || || samvat 1956 sālamiti jyeṣṭavadi 3 ro 1 māsi ‥ganyā || || śubhm(!) || (fol. 63v3–7)
purpose: written and given to Kāru Vajrācārya of Tadhukṣe
notes: The colophon has two dates. The first is NS 1019, Vaiśākha vadi 3, Sunday, which falls in April/May 1899. The second is VS 1956, Jyeṣṭha vadi 3, Sunday, also in 1899. VS 1956 begins in April 1899, so the two eras do not conflict. The dates could be the same day: Vaiśākha vadi in the amānta month system (common in Newar dating) is called Jyeṣṭha vadi in the pūrṇimānta system (common in Gorkhali dating). They could also be one month apart. The garbled 'māsi ‥ganyā' after the VS date is unclear. It may be a later note or another name, so it was not recorded as a person. 'sathosā(pu)' before 'tadhukṣeyā' is also unclear; it might be a place or household name. Tadhukṣe is probably a Kathmandu locality or household, but this is not certain. The scribe's name 'Machindra' probably stands for Matsyendra. The reading 'Kāru' is uncertain.
review: Second person added: 'kāruyāta' is the Newari dative 'to/for Kāru'. So Kāru (Vajrācārya of Tadhukṣe) is the person who received the copy. The first reading took the word for a corruption of 'kāryayāta'.
Sentence read as Newari 'coyā va viyā julo' ('having written, [he] gave it'): Machindra is scribe and donor, Kāru is recipient (beneficiary). Relation added: Machindra wrote_for Kāru.
'tadhukṣayā vajrācāryye' is not a dittography. It describes the recipient, not the scribe.
Place of copying emptied: Tadhukṣe is only given as residence. The colophon does not say the copy was made there.
Date fields: weekday normalised to Sunday (ro 1). The notes now explain how the NS and VS dates relate (they may not be the same day). ce_approx 1899 kept.

(5).. śrīpadmasiṃha utrāpantha hlāsanāmasiddhakṣetrasa prakṣānti śrīśrīśrīcoramūci triratnamuttivajrāsana akṣobhyasyāgrasa coṅāva verasa manasa dharmacitta utpatti juyā(1)na oyāva, thva kāraṇḍavyuha aparamitā durggatipariśodhana tribhiḥ pustakāḥ kṛṣṇakāgatapatre kanakarupyād akṣaleṇa likhāpitaṃ || tat pu
purpose: Commissioned in Lhasa while inspired before the Akṣobhya statue; for the longevity, health, wealth, progeny, and attainment of Sukhāvatī for Padmasiṃha and his family.
notes: Padmasiṃha commissioned three manuscripts (Kāraṇḍavyūha, Aparimitā, Durgatipariśodhana) written in gold and silver ink on black paper while on business/pilgrimage in Lhasa (utrāpantha hlāsanāmasiddhakṣetrasa). The scribe Dhanamunideva wrote it at Tarumūla Mahāvihāra (Sikhamū Bāhā) in Kathmandu.

title: *Ghaṭakarpara
subject: *Sāhitya
date_note: = Tuesday 23 Dec 1800, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti kālidāsakṛtaṃ ghaṭakrpparaṃ samāptaṃm(!) || || śubham astu || iti śamvat 1857 śāla paṣṭa śudi 8 roja 7 śāke 1722 liṣītam edam postakam || || || || || || || (fol.4v1-3 ) śloka || dvijarājamukhī mṛgarājakaṭī tarurājavirājitajṃghaṭī || yadi śā vanitā hṛdaya(!) vasati kva japaḥ kva tapaḥ kva samādhividhiḥ || 1 || || || || || || || || || ||
notes: The two eras agree: VS 1857 − 57 = 1800 and ŚS 1722 + 78 = 1800. The date uses Persianate formulas: śāla (sāl, 'year') and roja (roz, 'day'), so roja 7 is probably the 7th weekday, Saturday. The month 'paṣṭa' is corrupt; Pauṣa is the most likely reading. If it is Pauṣa śukla 8, the date would fall around late December 1800 or early January 1801. That does not fit the catalogue's guess of 24 November 1800, which would point to Mārgaśīrṣa. The scribe is not named ('liṣītam edam postakam'). The attribution of the Ghaṭakarpara to Kālidāsa is traditional. The verse after the colophon is a stray śloka (dvijarājamukhī…) with no prosopographical content.
review: weekday: 'roja 7' read as the 7th day of the week, i.e. Saturday (if Sunday is counted as day 1)
notes: VS 1857 and ŚS 1722 agree (both give 1800 CE), so there is no conflict between eras; added the Persianate terms śāla/roja; added a note on the month and on the catalogue's date
Kālidāsa kept as author: the colophon gives him as author, though the attribution is traditional; the person list is otherwise confirmed

notes: The colophon gives only the author's statement and the date. It names no scribe, commissioner or owner. 'dhṛtakauśika' is probably an error for the gotra Ghṛtakauśika. The epithet akhaṇḍapaṇḍitamaṇḍalāgraṇī most naturally describes the father Makaranda, but it could be meant for the author. 'samāptatām ahaiṣīt (!)' is the cataloguer's marked error. The kings in the catalogue fields, Pratāpasiṃha (r. 1775–77) and Bahādura Śāha (regent c. 1785–94), do not appear in the colophon and do not fit VS 1919 = 1862 CE (the reign of Surendra Vikrama Śāha). review: Lineage name: 'dhṛtakauśika' is very likely a scribal error for Ghṛtakauśika, a known Brahmin gotra. Affiliation changed to 'Ghṛtakauśika gotra' for both persons, with the error flagged in notes.
Moved the epithet 'akhaṇḍapaṇḍitamaṇḍalāgraṇī' from Śivaśarman to Makaranda. Grammatically it heads the chain of epithets ending in makarandasūri, so it describes the father.
Notes now say that the kings in the catalogue fields (Pratāpasiṃha r. 1775–77; Bahādura Śāha was regent c. 1785–94) do not fit a copy dated VS 1919 (1862 CE).
Noted that the colophon names no scribe, commissioner or owner.

title: Guhyasamāja
subject: Bauddha Tantra
date_note: = Sunday 18 Apr 1847, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrī sarvva tathāgatakāyavākcittarahasyāṅguhyaśrīsamāje sarvvaguhyanirdeśaḥ || ❁ || vajrajñānādhiṣṭhāno nāmāṣṭādaśaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ || || ye dharmmāhetu prabhāvā he⟨n⟩tu teṣān tathāgato hyavadatteṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādi || ❁ || mahāśramaṇaḥ || ❁ || śubham astu sarvvadāt || ❁ || śreyo stu samvat 967 adya vaiśāṣamāse śuklapakṣe tṛtīyāyāṃ mahāpuṇyatithau rohiṇīnakṣatre śau(!)bhana yoge yathākarṇṇam udgate ādityavāsare meṣarāsigate savitare vṛṣarāsigate candramasi || etat dine likhāpitaṃ śubhaṃ || dānapati śrīlalitāpuramahānagarayā ekuṣe vakaṃ vahālayā kāyaṣṭa jyeṣṭa naravīrasiṃhabhāryyā tejalakṣmījyeṣṭaputra mānavīrasiṃ dvitīyaputra kṛṣṇamānasiṃ tṛtīyaputrakṛṇamānasiṃ tṛtīyaputra kulamānasiṃ caturthaputra gajamānasiṃ thvati sakala parivārayā dharmacitta utpatti juyāo thva pustaka dayakā jula śubhaṃ || lekhaka śrī cakravāhālayā śrītejadattena coyā jula śubhaṃ || (fol. 146r2–v5)
purpose: Pious donation by Tejalakṣmī and her sons (dharmacitta utpatti juyāo thva pustaka dayakā jula)
notes: 'tṛtīyaputrakṛṇamānasiṃ' is a dittography of the second son's name and is not a separate person. The real third son is Kulamānasiṃ. The dānapati is Tejalakṣmī, named as the wife of the senior kāyastha Naravīrasiṃha, together with her four sons ('thvati sakala parivāra'). Naravīrasiṃha may also count as part of the donating family, but the syntax makes him an identifying relative. The donor family lives at Ekuṣe Vakaṃ Vahāla, Lalitāpura (Patan). The scribe belongs to Cakravāhāla, which is probably Cakra Mahāvihāra in Patan. Neither is stated as the place of copying, so it was probably Patan, but that is not certain. The date details agree with each other: Sun in Meṣa, Moon in Vṛṣabha with Rohiṇī, Vaiśākha śukla 3. NS 967 is about April/May 1847 CE.

Tejalakṣmī is the dānapati. The phrase 'naravīrasiṃhabhāryyā tejalakṣmī' names her as the wife of Naravīrasiṃha, and the sons follow her. Naravīrasiṃha is changed to relative_only (medium confidence). He is named to identify her, and he may have been dead.

'śāke bhikṣu' = śākyabhikṣu. 'pustakadajinā viyā' probably = pustaka dayakā biyā. 'dharmmaraṃja jamānayā' probably = dharmarāja yajamānayā. p2: evidence cleaned up; 'pustakadajinā viyā' read as 'pustaka dayakā biyā' ('made the book and gave it'), which supports both commissioner and donor.
p3: confidence lowered to medium, since 'pramukha' shows he heads a group whose other members are not named.

title: Bhajagovindastotra
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Monday 27 Apr 1863, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti saka(!)rācayaviracitau bhajagovindastā(!)traṃ samāptaṃ || ❁ || iti samvat 1920 sāla vaisākha sudina 9 roja 2 (fol. 3r4–5) iti indrākṣistotra(ṃ) samāptam ❖ (fol. 4v3)
notes: 'saka(!)rācaya' is a corrupt spelling of Śaṅkarācārya, the traditional author of the Bhajagovindastotra. The era is not named ('samvat … sāla'), but year 1920 with Nepali date words (sāla, roja) points to Vikrama Saṃvat: Vaiśākha VS 1920 = about April–May 1863 CE, which agrees with the catalogue's 'SAM 1920'. The manuscript also contains the Indrākṣīstotra (colophon on fol. 4v3), which has no date. No scribe, commissioner or owner is named.
review: weekday rendered as 'Monday (roja 2)' (roja 2 = second day of the week, counting from Sunday)
paksa normalized to 'śukla' (sudina = sudi = bright fortnight)
notes expanded: second colophon (Indrākṣīstotra) has no date or scribe; scribe and owner are not named

title: Bhajagovindastotra

notes: The corrupt 'sakarācaya' stands for Śaṅkarācārya, the traditional author of the text. 'sudina 9' means sudi 9, the 9th day of the bright half (śukla). 'roja 2' is Monday. The era is not named. Reading 'samvat 1920 sāla' as VS fits the Devanagari script and the Nepali wording (sāla, roja), giving roughly April/May 1863 CE. The catalogue gives SAM 1920. No scribe, commissioner or owner is named. The manuscript also contains the Indrākṣīstotra (fol. 4v), which has no date.
review: Weekday 'roja 2' read as Monday (Nepali count: roja 1 = Sunday); the original wording is kept
Month normalised to Vaiśākha

notes: The phrase 'padmā ānandarāmaja?' most likely means Padmā, son of Ānandarāma (ānandarāma-ja, 'born of Ānandarāma'). The cataloguer marked the final syllable as doubtful, so the son_of relation is uncertain. It is also possible that the whole string is one person's name, as the catalogue field 'Padmā Anandarāma ?' suggests; in that case there is a single scribe and no relation. 'Padmā' looks feminine, but '-ja' is masculine, so the true form may be Padma. The colophon does not name the era. VS is assumed because the script is Devanagari and the year is 1838; this gives about 1781 CE. Mārkaṇḍeya is left out because he is the mythical speaker of the stotra.

title: Dharmasaṅgraha
subject: Bauddha Darśana

colophon: iti śrīnāgārjuṇaviracitaṃ (!) dharmmaśāśtraṃ samāptaṃ || ❁ || mai. bhā. || śubham || ○ || saṃ 1013 jyeṣṭha śudi 4 sakyebhi tiṣṭhage vātārayā śrīvajrācāryya jñānandanaṃ dayakā thao saphalikhao niścaya || || śubham || (fols. 12v5–6, exp14)
purpose: copied by the scribe for himself ('thao saphalikhao', wrote his own book)
notes: Name: 'jñānandanaṃ' is read as Jñānānanda + Newari agentive -naṃ (haplography of -ānanda- is possible). The catalogue gives 'Jñānanandan', which takes -naṃ as part of the name. 'sakyebhi tiṣṭhage vātārayā' before the name is unclear. It may be a corrupt locality, vihāra or residence (perhaps '-yā' as a genitive or residential ending), but no identification is safe. 'mai. bhā.' after the text colophon is also unexplained. The colophon calls the text 'dharmmaśāśtraṃ' (!) although the catalogue title is Dharmasaṅgraha. Date: NS 1013 + 880 = 1893 CE (Jyeṣṭha śukla 4).
review: p2: name read as Jñānānanda. 'jñānandanaṃ' is best read as Jñānānanda plus the Newari agentive ending -naṃ, not as a stem Jñānanandana; confidence lowered to medium. The catalogue's 'Jñānanandan' is noted.
p2: role 'commissioner' removed and 'owner' added. 'dayakā thao saphalikhao' means he wrote his own (thao) book (saphū); nothing says he had it copied by someone else.
purpose rewritten in plain words: copied by the scribe for himself.
paksa normalized to śukla.
Notes expanded: the unclear words before the name may be a locality or an affiliation; 'mai. bhā.' is left unexplained; the NS date has been checked.

title: Śivamānasapūjā
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Wednesday 17 Apr 1861, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti vyāsakṛtam | mānasīpūjā samāptam || śubham || || śrī śāke 1783 madhisita 7 vāsare 7 śubham (fol. 9v5–9)
notes: 'madhisita' is probably a corruption of madhu-sita (Madhu = Caitra, sita = śukla). Caitra śukla 7 of ŚS 1783 falls around March/April 1861 CE. The weekday number 7 is taken as Saturday. The colophon credits the text to Vyāsa (vyāsakṛtam), although the Śivamānasapūjā is usually attributed to Śaṅkarācārya. No scribe, owner or place is named. The date matches the catalogue field (Śāke 1783).
review: date.month: 'madhi' read as Madhu (= Caitra); 'madhisita' is most likely madhu-sita, i.e. Caitra śukla. Dropped the Māgha alternative.
date.weekday: vāsare 7 read as Saturday (Śanivāra).
notes: explained the readings and the attribution to Vyāsa.

title: Mṛtyuñjayastotra
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Apr 1931, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīpārameśvarataṃtre caturaśīti sāhasre śrīmṛtyuñjayastotraṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ śubham || 1988 vaiśāṣa gate roja taddine likhitam || (exps. 6b7–7t3)
notes: The colophon names no era. VS is the only plausible reading of 1988: it is far too high for NS and lies in the future for ŚS. The 'gate roja' solar-day formula is also typical of VS dates, and the catalogue agrees. Vaiśākha VS 1988 falls in about April–May 1931 CE. The day number after 'gate roja' is missing: the text has only 'taddine', so the day of the solar month is not given. The catalogue lists Bhuvaneśvara as scribe, but no personal name appears in the quoted colophon. The name may come from elsewhere in the manuscript, perhaps another part of the composite reel A 1149/12. I have not added him as a person.
review: weekday: removed 'roja'. Here roja (Persian rōz, 'day') belongs to the solar day count 'vaiśāṣa gate roja N', so it is not a weekday
month: written as vaiśāṣa; normalised in notes as Vaiśākha
notes: the colophon gives no era and no day number; the era was inferred

colophon: śatasāhasrāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ dvādaśaḥ parivarttaḥ | prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ samāpta iti || || ye dharmā hetu prabhāvā hetu teṣāṃ tathāgataḥ | ye vada yo nirodhī evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ || || anena saddharmarasāmṛtena sarvajñananto dharaṇītalena | kleśānalo prajvalitaḥ na tasmai lokasya duḥkhaṃ praśamo stu nityaṃ || || śrīmadrājādhirājaparameśvaraparamabhaṭṭārakaśrīmacchrī siddhinarasiṃhamalladevasya vijayarājye || śrīlalitacchūmāyāṃ śrīmānībālakādhisiro deyadharmāyaṃ pravaramahāpārayāminaḥ paramabrahmopāsakajayamuni bauddhācāryanāmn yadatra puṇyan te bhavatu mātāpitṛpūrvaṅgamaṃ kṛtvā satvarāśer anuttaraṃ dhyānaphalāptaye iti || samvat .. .. .. prathamāṣāḍhe śukladvitīyāyāṃ śanaiścaradine punarvasunakṣatre yoge vṛddhi śatānukūle śrījayamunibauddhācāryeṇa likhita samāpta kṛtam iti || anena cāhaṃ kuśalena karmaṇā bhaveya buddho na vināyaloke | deśeya dharmaṃ jagato hitāya | māneya satvāṃ bhavaduḥkhapīḍitāt || anena puṇyena tu sarvadarśitā sa vāpyanirjitya pradoṣavidviṣaḥ | jarānuja mṛtyumahormi taṃ kulāt samuddhareyaṃ bhavasāgarāj jagat || || śrī śrīnivāsena na devarājā mābhūt prajānāṃ pratipāladakṣaḥ | tasya prasādāc ca vijitya mārāṃl lilekha prajñāṃ sakalāṃ salakṣāṃ || yacchrīnivāso nayadharmacārī dadau vinocchrīṃ likhanāya yuddhāṃ | anena puṇyena sukhaṃ sarājyaṃ tuṣṭas ciraṃ gacchatu śaivalokaṃ || lakṣmyādinārāyaṇavāsudevau yajjitya gopiṃ dadataś ca prajñāṃ | taddharmamuṇyena tayoḥ savaṃśā jayantu nandantu viśantu śaivaṃ || abde naipālike khyāte grahaṣaḍgirisaṃyute | māse tu prath

title: Śatasāhasrikāprajñāpāramitā
subject: Bauddha Sūtra
date_note: = Wednesday 8 May 1715, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: śreyo ʼstu samvat 835 vaiśākhamāse śuklapakṣe pañcami pravaṣṭamyān tithau punarvasunakṣatre śūla joge jathākarṇṇamuhūrte budhavāsare mekharasigate savitari muthunarāsigate candramasi thva kuhnu saṃpūrṇṇa padhiṣṭhāyāṅā o siddhayāṅā juro śubham astu || || ata paran tadeśabhāṣā || || dānapati śrīkāntipurimahānagare ṅaṃ tatorake somavāhārasannidhāne ṅatapithyāmūgalayautānāmagṛhādhivāsikaturādharavakhāsiṃhayāmana saatidharmmacitte utpatijñasya o yā o śrī śrī rakṣā bhagavati pustaka vāvakā juro || etatpuṇyena yadapuṇya tadbhūtvā cāryyopādhyāyas tato pitṛpūrvvagamaṃ kṛtvā śakalasatvarāśīnāmanuttarajñānaphalaṃ prāptam astu || || lajjā bhagavatī pustakamaprameyaphalaṃ lekhaṃ sumerupramāṇarajaṃ saṃkhyā śakyaṃ mayā kṛtaṃ || lajjā bhagavati pūstaṃ lekhaṃ puṇyena sakyate aprameya asaṃkhyekhyayā phalaṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate || || liṣitaṃ śrīgvapūrcchati miliṣūnyakṣatra śrīsākyaṃ sumahāvihārladhiṣṭhita śākyavaṃśodbhava śākyabhikṣu śrīdharmmachriṃ putra jñānachriṃ thva pariniptasyana saṃpūrṇṇa siddhayakā juro || || yathā dṛṣṭa tathā liṣita lekhako nāsti doṣa taṃ yadi śuddhaṃ maśuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo na vidyate || || śubha maṅgalaṃ bhavatu sarvvadā śubha || || ❁ || || (fol. 429v1–6)
purpose: Donation by Vakhāsiṃha. The merit goes to teachers (ācāryopādhyāya), to parents and ancestors, and to all beings, so that they may reach supreme knowledge.
notes: The era is not named, but the Newari script and Newari language fit NS: 835 + 880 = 1715 CE, which agrees with the catalogue. 'pañcami pravaṣṭamyān' is corrupt. It probably means pañcamī followed by ṣaṣṭhī ('parā ṣaṣṭhyām'), less likely aṣṭamī. Other date details: sun in Meṣa, moon in Mithuna, muhūrta 'jathākarṇṇa' (corrupt). The donor's name sits inside a run-together string: 'turādhara' = Tulādhara, a caste title; 'yāmana' is probably the genitive -yā plus mana ('mind'), going with 'ati dharmacitte'. The place of copying is not stated clearly. The scribe's phrase 'śrīgvapūrcchati miliṣūnyakṣatra śrīsākyaṃ sumahāvihār(a)' is corrupt, and the vihāra cannot be identified for certain. Kāntipura (Kathmandu) is named only as the donor's residence. The colophon gives the śākyabhikṣu title only to Dharmaśrī. It is extended to his son Jñānaśrī by inference.

The surname Śejvalīkara and the name 'Bāpūjī Pant' point to a Maharashtrian brahmin milieu. The catalogue's scribe and date fields agree with the colophon.
review: p3: 'bāpūjīpatayāṃ sadattam' read as a corruption of 'bāpūjīpaṃtāya (saṃ)dattam', meaning 'given to Bāpūjī Pant'. Roles changed from beneficiary to owner + beneficiary, since he received the book. 'paṃta' added to titles.

title: Śivagīta
subject: Stotra
notes: The colophon is undated. Viśveśvara is read with the cataloguer's reconstructed syllables 'vi(sveśva)rena(!)', standing for viśveśvareṇa. 'kāśīnāthāya maṃgalaṃ' most likely invokes Śiva as lord of Kāśī, but it could also be a blessing for a person named Kāśīnātha. That person is not recorded. The place name is illegible and unmetrical. It comes inside a closing verse of praise ('palāśapatrīkṛta... nivāsinaṃ tāṃ ... īḍe'), so it may name the deity's home, not the place of copying. The catalogue says 'Place of Copying: illegible'. The colophon calls the work 'śivāṣṭapatiḥ(!)', probably a corruption of śivāṣṭapadī, while the catalogue title is 'Śivagīta'.
review: Viśveśvara: confidence lowered from high to medium, because the cataloguer put the middle syllables '(sveśva)' in parentheses as uncertain and marked the form with (!).
Place: kept the illegible reading but added a note that it sits inside a closing stuti verse ('...nivāsinaṃ ... īḍe'). It may describe where the praised deity lives, not where the copy was made.
Notes: added that 'kāśīnāthāya maṃgalaṃ' could also be a blessing for a person named Kāśīnātha, such as an owner or recipient. It is not recorded as a person because the reading is uncertain.
Owner role not added: 'svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca' is a stock formula, and it does not say the scribe kept the book.

purpose: possibly offered to the goddess Sarasvatī (thva sarasvati deva yā ...); uncertain
notes: The cataloguer could not understand the Newari clause after the stanza: 'thva sarasvati deva yā śiro kathavagvastikadhani karmmā cājye yo kekāyāva devyandrakarmmā cājyena thava āṣalasena vavamacātośene yātāhleyājulo śubha'. A tentative reading: 'This [book] belongs to the goddess Sarasvatī; Devendra Karmācārya, son (kāya) of ...dhani Karmācārya, wrote it in his own letters (thava ākhalasena) and offered it (?)'. 'devyandra' = Devendra; 'karmmā cājye/cājyena' = Karmācārya with the instrumental case. 'yo kekāyāva' may be a corruption of 'yā kāya va' (son of), but that is uncertain. The son_of relation p1→p2 is therefore low certainty. The father's name (?) is corrupt: 'śiro kathavagvastikadhani' could hide a name ending in -dhana/-dhani, perhaps with an honorific such as śiromaṇi. Sarasvatī is a deity and is not listed as a person. The colophon has no date and no place.

Added p2: a low-confidence Karmācārya named in the clause ('...gvastikadhani karmmā cājye yo kekāyāva'), possibly Devendra's father, given the role relative_only

title: Avadānaśataka
subject: Bauddha, Avadāna
date_note: = Monday 20 May 1669, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: ity avadānaśataka(!) daśamī uddāra(!)gāthā samāptā || ○ || samāptaṃ ca (ava)dānaśa(taṃ) .. .. yaṃ (suga)tabhāṣitaṃ thaṃdīśvaracāryapūrvam idānīṃ prakāśitaṃ || ye dharmā hetuprabhāvā hetu teṣāṃ tathāgataḥ | hy avadad yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśrama[ṇa]ḥ || || śreyo stu saṃvat 789 vaiśāṣakṛṣṇa paṃcamyāṃ śrīviradevavajrācāryena likhitā saṃpūrṇṇā jātā śubha || ○ || (fol. 236v1-3)
notes: The era is not named ('saṃvat 789'). NS is assumed because the script is Newari, the scribe is a Vajrācārya and the catalogue says NS; NS 789 + 880 = 1669 CE, which matches the catalogue. 'viradeva' is read as Vīradeva. The phrase 'thaṃdīśvaracāryapūrvam idānīṃ prakāśitaṃ' is corrupt. It is probably a statement about how the text was handed down (perhaps something like 'sthavirācāryapūrvam', meaning 'formerly [taught] by the elder teachers, now made known'), not the name of someone connected with this copy, so no person was extracted from it. The ye dharmā verse is garbled, which is common.
review: Notes expanded: 'thaṃdīśvaracāryapūrvam' is probably a corrupt formula rather than a person's name, and the spelling 'vira' was normalized to Vīradeva.

title: Ahorātravratakathā & Kārttikavratakathā
subject: Avadāna, Bauddha
colophon: (18r5)iti śrīkā[r]ttikavra⟨rt⟩takathā samāptaḥ || ❁ || śubha || || ye dharmmā hetuprabhāvā, hetus teṣāṃ ⟪ca⟫ tathāgata, hy evadat teṣāṃ ca yo niro(6)dha evaṃvādi mahāśravaṇaṃ || ○ || likhitaṃ, talamuramahāvihāre, (jontā)vāhārakhalucuka etāgṛhā(va)sthita(?), śrī 3 vajradevīprasādena, vajrā (The colophon continues to fol. 18v. The letters in the six lines on the last page cannot be deciphered with certainty, since the page is dark and the exposure is blurred.)
notes: The colophon breaks off on fol. 18r at 'vajrā…'. The cataloguer could not read the six lines on fol. 18v because the page is dark and the exposure blurred, so no scribe, donor or date survives in the transcription. 'vajrā…' probably begins the title vajrācārya (a priestly title) followed by the scribe's name, which is lost. 'śrī 3 vajradevīprasādena' invokes a deity's grace and does not name a person. Vasubandhu, Indrapṛṣṭa and the jinaśārdūla on fol. 9v are characters in the vratakathā, not people connected with this copy. talamuramahāvihāra = Tārumūla Mahāvihāra (catalogue: Taramula-Mahāvihāra). It is identified here as a vihāra in Kathmandu, but this identification is not fully certain. '(jontā)vāhāra' and 'khalucuka' are uncertain local names, probably a bāhāl and its courtyard (cuka/chowk).

purpose: svādhyāya (copied by the scribe for his own study); merit and prosperity for the patron's family, and liberation hereafter
notes: The catalogue's 'NS 391' is a slip for NS 931, as the colophon itself reads. NS 931 Kārttika śukla pūrṇimā falls in about Oct./Nov. 1810 CE, inside Gīrvāṇayuddha's reign (1799–1816). The weekday has not been checked. The Moon in Meṣa and the Sun in Tulā both fit Kārttika pūrṇimā. 'jayomāna' is read as a corrupt 'yajamāna' (the patron), not a personal name; if it were a name ('Jayamāna'), that person would be a beneficiary. 'coyā' is read as 'wrote' (compare 'coyakā', 'had written'), so Nāmasaṃgati is the scribe and not a commissioner. Suvarṇapanāri = Suvarṇapraṇālī; the modern town is left unidentified. The word 'dānapati' is quoted before the place and the person's name.
review: p2 Nāmasaṃgati: 'thamanaṃ coyā jula' means he wrote it himself for his own study (svādhyāyanimitta), so the roles are now scribe + owner, plus donor because he is called dānapati. The residence is split from the affiliation.
p2: 'dānapati' is a role, not a title, so it is removed from titles.
p3 'Jayamāna' removed: 'jayomāna jyeṣṭapramukhādi sagaṇaparivārāṇāṃ' is almost certainly a corrupt 'yajamāna' ('the patron, with the eldest and the rest of his family'), not a personal name.
Removed 'jyeṣṭhapramukha' as a title.
King's name normalised as 'Gīrvāṇayuddhavikrama Śāha'. Honorifics trimmed to real titles.
Purpose reworded. Date fields normalised (nakṣatra Bharaṇī, yoga Varīyas). Notes expanded.

title: Cāmuṇḍāpūjāpaddhati
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Tuesday 1 Oct 1754, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: śubha || saṃmvat 874 ā(3)śuna śuddhi 15 maṃgalavārakuhnu coyā dina || juro (4) kṛṣṇa siṃhana coyā juro || (exps. 8b3-9t4)
notes: The catalogue gives Kathmandu as the place of copying and Jayaprakāśa Malla as the king, but the quoted colophon names neither. NS 874 (about 1754 CE) does fall within Jayaprakāśa Malla's reign in Kathmandu (c. 1736–1768), so the catalogue's attribution is plausible, but it comes from the catalogue, not the colophon. 'coyā juro' is Newari for 'was written', so Kṛṣṇasiṃha is the scribe. It is not 'coyakā' ('caused to be written'), which would make him a commissioner. The colophon does not give the weekday separately, so Tuesday was not checked against the tithi.
review: No substantive changes. Added a note that the date fits the catalogue's king, and a note on how 'coyā' was read.

colophon: samvat 802 vaiśākha śuddhi || || śrīśrī sumati jaya jitāmitramalladevasana dayakā || || śubha || oguli chātasa hleyā || (fol. 54v109/run fol. 110v)
notes: The colophon reads samvat 802 (NS, about 1682 CE). The catalogue gives NS 815 (about 1695 CE). Both years fall within Jitāmitra Malla's reign in Bhaktapur (about 1673–1696). This is item (2) of a multi-text reel, so the catalogue's 815 may come from another colophon in the same bundle. 'śuddhi' is taken as the bright half (śukla). 'sumati jaya' is read as part of the king's royal style (epithets), not as his personal name. The commissioner role rests on Newari '-sana dayakā' ('made by'). It does not say whether he commissioned only this copy or the ritual it records. 'oguli chātasa hleyā' is unclear. It may mean 'written/offered on these leaves' or refer to the occasion. The final line 'oguli chātasa hleyā' is unclear; it may be an instruction about where the text or offerings are to be placed.

notes: The chronogram is yugala (2), śūnya (0), aṅka (9). Read right to left, that gives 902. The colophon does not name the era. NS is inferred from the Newari script and the period of the Vratāvadānamālā literature, and the catalogue puts [NS] in brackets. On that basis the date is Mārgaśīrṣa śukla 6, a Wednesday, NS 902, which is about November/December 1782 CE. The weekday has not been checked. The catalogue names Amṛtānanda as scribe, but the quoted colophon fragments name nobody, only 'likhitaṃ'. So no person is extracted. The attribution may come from elsewhere in the manuscript, e.g. from the hand, and should be checked against the catalogue description.

title: Kriyāsaṅgraha
subject: Bauddhakarmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Sunday 24 Mar 1715, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti mahāpaṇḍitarecārya(!) kuladattaviracitāyāṃ kriyāsaṃgrahanāmapañjikāʼṣṭamaprakaraṇaṃ samāpta(!) || ❁ || (yoʼstu) samvat 835 phāguṇa kṛṣṇa 4 śrībhāskaladeoca(!) saṃskārita(!) || ❁ || śrīkāntipuri(!)mahāgare pārāvatamahāvī(!)hāre śrī‥‥‥‥‥‥‥‥‥‥‥‥‥‥‥‥‥‥ śrīcakrapatidevena likhāyitaṃ || ❁ || || śubhamaṅgalaṃ bhavaṃtu || (fol. 168r3–6)
notes: 'śrībhāskaladeoca saṃskārita' belongs to the full name of the monastery: Bhāskaradeva-saṃskārita Pārāvata-mahāvihāra (Itum Bāhā, Kathmandu). It refers to the 11th-century king Bhāskaradeva, who restored the monastery. He is not the reigning king of this copy. That king would have been Bhāskara Malla of Kathmandu (c. NS 834–842), who is not named. There is a long lacuna (śrī‥‥) after the vihāra name, which may have held other names, possibly the scribe's. Cakrapatideva's link to the vihāra is therefore inferred and may be wrong. 'mahāpaṇḍitarecārya(!)' probably stands for mahāpaṇḍitācārya.
review: p2 Bhāskaradeva: confidence raised from low to medium. 'bhāskaladeoca saṃskārita' is clearly the standard epithet of the Pārāvata-mahāvihāra (Itum Bāhā), so the reading itself is secure; role 'other' kept.

title: Saddharmapuṇḍarīka
subject: Bauddha Sūtra
date_note: = Saturday 31 Jan 1852, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: samāptaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sūtrāntaṃ mahāvaipulyaṃ bodhisattvāvabādhaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ sarvabuddharahasyam sarvabuddhanigūḍham sarva||❁||buddhajāti || sarvabuddhaguhyasthānaṃ || sarvabuddhabodhimanda[la]ṃ || sarvabuddhadharmacakra⟨ṃ⟩pravarttanaṃ || sarvabuddhaikaghanaśarīraṃ sarvopāyakauśalyam ekayānanirddeśaṃ paramārthanirahāranirddeśam iti || ❁ || ye bhyāgatā iha surāsuranāgayakṣā gandharvakinnaranarāśravaṇāya dharma[ṃ] rakṣantu te jagad idaṃ jinasāsanaṃ ca dharmmaṃ munīndra kathitañ ca caraṃ|| ||tu nityaṃ || … ye dharmā hetuprabhā(!)vā hetu[s] teṣāṃ tathāgata hyavadat teṣāñ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaṃ || śubham astu jagat || ❁ || śubhaṃ bhūyāt || || svasti śrīgirirājacakracḍāmaṇinaranārāyaṇētyādi vividhavirudāvalīvirājamānamānonnatamahimaṇḍalanepāleśvaranarapatisahasrasaṃsevyamānacaraṇakamalavividhyandanīlamaṇihemapadmarāgavajravaiḍūryamuktāratnasamūhasamaukṛtayakṣādhī(!)pavibhavavidyādharasahasrāṅgīyamāṇakīrttisarvāṅgasundaraśrīmahārājādhirāja śrī3 surendravikramasāha samrajayī mahāsamaravijayī vijayarājye || … bhāṣā śubhaṃ saṃvat 972 miti māghamāse śuklapakṣe daśamyāṃ tithau kīrttikāpra(!)rohininakṣetre (!) śaniścaravāsare || || etaddine dānapati nepāladeśe kāntipuranagare bhāskaradevasaṃskārita keśavacandrakṛta pārāvātamahāvihāramāricidevyācaraṇasevaka ā o acche nāmā gṛhavāsita śākyabhikṣu bhāju vīra bhrātṛ candravīra … saptaratnaṃ bṛddhir astu || ❁ || prajñāpāramitā[ṃ] namāmi satataṃ gandhādivyūhaṃ daśa- bhūmīkaṃ ca samādhidhirājasahitaṃ
notes: The donor Bhājuvīra resided in Kāntipura (Kathmandu) at Itum Bāhā (bhāskaradeva-keśavacandra-kṛta pārāvāta-mahāvihāra), while the manuscript was copied in Lalitapura (Patan) at Cuka Bāhā (mānadeva-saṃskārita cakra-mahāvihāra).

title: Saundaryalaharī
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Friday 27 Sep 1776, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīmacchaṃkaracāryaviracitaṃ sauṃdaryyalahrīstotra<nowki>[ṃ]</nowiki> saṃpūrṇaṃ ⟨jagya⟩[yajña]nāthayoḥ śubhaṃ bhūyāt ❁ ❁ ❁ śubha[ṃ] sujñai[r] †jñativiracitam† itīdaṃ vilikhitaṃ sadbhūtajñānaṃ bhavajalanimagnoddharaṇakaṃ murāreḥ pāṭhārthaṃ girir iti sunāmnaḥ stavanakaṃ sukhaṃ gopālenāvataritamahśaṃkarakṣataṃ 1 vi⟨s⟩[ś]ve⟨s⟩[ś]varāya namaḥ saṃvat 1833 samayanāmabhādramāse site pakṣe pūrṇavāśyāyāṃ (!) bhṛguvāsare jagya(!)nāthena vipreṇa pustakaṃ likhitaṃ śubham dheyaṃ sadā paribhavagnam abhi(!)ṣṭadohaṃ tīrthāspadaṃ śivaviraṃcinutaṃ saraṇyaṃ | bhṛtyārtihaṃ praṇatapāla bhavābdhipotaṃ vaṃde mahāpurukha(!) te caraṇāraviṃdaṃ 1 ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ (fol. 12v5–13r3)
purpose: for the reading of Murāri Giri (murāreḥ pāṭhārthaṃ)
notes: The scribe's name is written 'jagyanātha', a spoken form of Yajñanātha. The cataloguer corrected it to Yajñanātha, which matches the catalogue field. 'yajñanāthayoḥ śubhaṃ bhūyāt' is a dual genitive, which is odd. It may be a scribal error for the singular yajñanāthasya, or it may mean two people (Yajña and Nātha?). It is taken here as the scribe alone. 'girir iti sunāmnaḥ' most likely means that Murāri carried the Daśanāmī name Giri, but this is inferred. The verse 'sukhaṃ gopālenāvataritamahśaṃkarakṣataṃ' is corrupt. Gopāla might be an earlier copyist, the composer of the verse, or a word play (an epithet of Kṛṣṇa), so this entry has low confidence. 'samayanāma' before Bhādramāse is unclear: perhaps a corrupt year name, or meaning 'in the month named'. 'pūrṇavāśyāyāṃ' is read as pūrṇamāsyām. The weekday (Friday) was not checked against an ephemeris. VS 1833 Bhādrapada falls in August/September 1776 CE. The closing verse 'dheyaṃ sadā ... mahāpurukha te caraṇāraviṃdaṃ' is a quoted stotra verse (Bhāgavata 11.5.33) and contains no persons.

p2: 'yajñanāthayoḥ śubhaṃ bhūyāt' added as further evidence for the scribe; the odd dual genitive is now flagged in notes
p3: role 'reader' dropped; the colophon only says the copy was made for his reading (pāṭhārtham), so he stays beneficiary. Affiliation changed from 'Daśanāmī' to 'Giri (Daśanāmī order, inferred)'
p4: kept as 'other' with low confidence, and the possible readings are now explained in notes
