title: Tārārahasyavṛtti
subject: Tantra
date_note: = Thursday 30 Oct 1698, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti gautranivāsiśaṅkarāgamācāryyeṇa viracitāyāṃ tārārahasyavṛttau nityapūjānirṇṇayaḥ prathamaḥ paṭala(!) || || (fol. 53r4-5) iti gautrabhūminivāsiśrīśaṅkarācāryyaviracitāyāṃ tārārahasyavṛttau dīkṣānirṇṇayo dvitīyao paṭalaḥ || || (fol. 54v2-3) iti śrīśaṅkarācāryyaviracitāyāṃ tārārahasyavṛttau puraścaraṇanirṇṇayas tṛtīyaḥ paṭalaḥ || || (fol. 59v5-6) iti tārārahasyavṛttau naimittikavidhiś caturthaḥ paṭalaḥ || || (fol. 64r8) etc. etc. iti gautrabhūminivāsiśrīśaṅkarācāryyaviracite tārārahasyavṛttau dvādasaḥ paṭalaḥ || || (fol. 123v5-6) iti śrītārārahasyavṛttau nityapūjāvidhirṇṇayo(!) nāma trayodaśaḥ paṭalaḥ || || (fol. 132v3) iti tārārahasyavṛttau homasya vidhin nāma caturddaśaḥ paṭalaḥ || || || (fol. 141v3-4) || iti gautrabhūminivāsimahāmahopādhyāyaśrīśaṃkarācāryyaviracitā vāsanarahasyavṛttikā pañcadaśaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ || || samvat 818 āśvinakṛṣṇadvādaśī bṛhaspativāra kuhnu karmmacāryyaha(riśa)ṅkarabhārotasaṃpūrṇṇayāḍājuro || (fol. 146v6-8)
notes: The author is Śaṅkara Āgamācārya, described as living in 'Gautra(bhūmi)'. This is probably a corruption of Gauḍa(bhūmi), i.e. Bengal, but that is not certain, so the residence is left as written. The syllables 'riśa' in the scribe's name are in brackets in the catalogue (supplied or unclear), so the reading Hariśaṅkara is likely but not certain. The Newari phrase 'saṃpūrṇa yāṅā juro' means 'completed (the copy)'. The final colophon names the work 'vāsanarahasyavṛttikā' instead of Tārārahasyavṛtti, probably a scribal error. The era is not stated, but the Newari wording and the karmācārya title point to Nepal Saṃvat: NS 818 = 1698 CE, which matches the catalogue.

title: Kalpalatikā
subject: Darśana
date_note: = Tuesday 13 Aug 1771, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīkavikairavenduśrījāṣarājaviracitāyāṃ kalparatikāyāṃ vedāntamatasaṃgraha(ścāntimaḥ) || || || ... it śrīkavikairavenduśrījāṣarājaviracitā kalpalatikā samāptā || || saṃvat 891 śrāvan śuddhi tṛyā(!) (‥ ‥ ‥) nakṣetra(!) taddine śrīvakjrācārya hṛdayānandena liṣita⟪(‥ ‥)⟫ m iti || || yadi śuddham aśuddhaṃ vā śodhanīyaṃ mahadbudhaiḥ || śubham astu sarvadākālaṃ || || śubhaṃ || || (fol. 96r5–7)
notes: The colophon says only 'saṃvat 891', with no era named. NS is the right reading: the scribe is a Newar vajrācārya, and VS 891 (c. 834 CE) or ŚS 891 (c. 969 CE) would be far too early for a Devanagari paper manuscript. The catalogue also gives NS 891, i.e. 1771 CE. The nakṣatra name is lost in the lacuna before 'nakṣetra(!)'. 'vakjrācārya' is a corrupt spelling of vajrācārya, 'liṣitam' stands for likhitam, 'tṛyā' for tṛtīyā, and 'kalparatikā' in the first colophon is a slip for kalpalatikā. In Newar Devanagari ṣ often stands for kh, so the author's name may really be Jākharāja. 'kavikairavendu' is an epithet ('moon to the lotus of poets'), not part of the name.
review: Persons, roles, titles and date confirmed as they were

notes: The copy was made during the 'increasing victorious reign' of the Pāla king Madanapāladeva of Bihar/Bengal (c. 1143–1161 CE). The passage after 'abhilikhya' is lacunose ('(patrāṅke vāsi)....bhū....tyā'). It may have contained a regnal year or other date, but none can be read. The scribe's compound reads 'śrīmanto..nagaravāstavyaśaulekhakamahīpati(putrena(!))'. Most likely this is '…-nagara-vāstavya-[gauḍa?/śau-]lekhaka-Mahīpati-putreṇa', 'by the son of the scribe Mahīpati, resident of Śrīmanto..nagara'. The son is not named. The other parse, with Mahīpati himself as scribe, is less likely. It is also unclear whether 'lekhaka' describes the father or the son. 'śau-' may be a misreading (perhaps 'gauḍa-' or 'kāyastha'-type designation). The town name (residence of the scribe) is only partly legible. It is not explicitly stated as the place of copying, and the catalogue gives the place as illegible. The catalogue's '12th century' fits Madanapāla's reign. The figure 129 after chapter 4 is a cataloguer's or scribe's count, not a date.

The cataloguer's (!) marks only the dental -n- (for putreṇa), not an intrusive word. So the scribe is an unnamed son (new p3: scribe, lekhaka, residence), and Mahīpati (p2) is changed to relative_only.

title: Kāraṇḍavyūha
subject: Bauddha, Bauddhasūtra
purpose: deyadharma: merit transferred to teachers (ācāryopādhyāya…, standard formula, cut off) and all beings
notes: The donor appears twice: as Jayakīrttika in the Sanskrit deyadharma clause and as Jasakīrttiju (Newari form) in the dānapati clause. They are treated as one person; if they are two, split them. The king's name is lost in the lacuna before '...nasya vijayarāje'. Only the ending -na survives, so no king is recorded. The cataloguer says the king is illegible. The place is given as the donor's residence and vihāra (Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa = Kathmandu, Rañjanatvalaka, Kīrtipuṇyamahāvihāra; 'Vajradhātumahāvihārāvasthita' is ambiguous). The place of copying is inferred from this, as in the catalogue. The scribe is not legible in the quote. The cataloguer notes that 'a number of names follow' on fol. 94v5–95r1, probably the donor's family or co-donors, but they are not quoted. The manuscript is written in gold and silver letters (suvarṇarajatākṣareṇa). No date survives in the quoted colophon.
review: Merged p1 and p2 into one person. 'Jayakīrttika' (in the Sanskrit deyadharma clause) and 'Jasakīrttiju' (Newari jasa = jaya, honorific -ju, in the dānapati clause) are almost certainly the same donor. The stem is given as Jayakīrti, since the -ka is pleonastic. Confidence is set to medium because the identification is inferred.
Added the role commissioner: the gold-and-silver copy was made for him as his deyadharma.
Split location data: Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa and Rañjanatvalaka are now his residence; Kīrtipuṇya and Vajradhātu mahāvihāras are his affiliation.
Purpose rewritten as a summary of the merit-transfer formula instead of a raw quotation.
Notes expanded: the king's name is lost, the place of copying is not stated directly, more names follow, and the book is written in gold and silver letters.

title: Āryavidyāsudhākara
subject: Dharmaśāstra
date_note: = Monday 10 Sep 1866, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: śālivāhanīyaśāke ʼsmin nāgebharṣidharāmite śuklanabhasye pūrṇo ʼbhūd grantho ʼyaṃ pratipat tithau || vedādigranthapāthodhimanthanena samudhṛtaḥ vidyāsudhākaraḥ so ʼyam ānandayatu sajjanāt || || iti śrībhaṭṭayajñeśvaronnīte āryavidyāsudhākare pañcama prakāśaḥ samāpto ʼyaṃ granthaḥ || ❁ || (fol. 150v11-151r2)
notes: The chronogram nāga (8), ibha (8), ṛṣi (7), dharā (1), read right to left, gives Śaka 1788, i.e. c. 1866 CE (Bhādrapada śukla 1). The verse says 'pūrṇo ʼbhūd grantho ʼyam' ('this work was completed'), together with a closing verse by the author. So it most likely records when Yajñeśvara Bhaṭṭa finished composing the work, carried over from the exemplar, not when this manuscript was copied. The catalogue's 'Date of Copying ŚS 1788' probably comes from this verse, so the actual copy may be the same date or later. No scribe, commissioner or place of copying is named.
review: Date: chronogram checked (nāga 8, ibha 8, ṛṣi 7, dharā 1, read right to left = 1788); ŚS 1788 = c. 1866 CE confirmed

title: Bodhicaryāvatāraṭīkā
subject: Bauddhadarśana
date_note: doubtful: Tuesday 31 Jul 1078 is too early for a paper manuscript (an abbreviated or misread year, or the exemplar's date)
date_doubtful: doubtful: Tuesday 31 Jul 1078 is too early for a paper manuscript (an abbreviated or misread year, or the exemplar's date)
colophon: bodhicaryāvatāre prajñāpāramitāparichedaṭīkā samāptā || kṛtir iyaṃ paṇḍitabhikṣuprajñākaramatipādānāṃ || || likhāpiteyam anavadhiguṇagaṇavividharatnarāśiparivyāptagaṃbhīraprajñāpratānajalasāgaraiḥ kleśa…. ṭīkeyaṃ paramā suyaṃtritapadā śuddhā manolhādinī saṃsārārṇavapāragāmini jane nauyānapātropamā || āśuprāptakarī jinasya padavī soʼ yaṃ likhitvā mayā prāptaṃ yat kuśalaṃ sasaṃpadi padaṃ tenāstu buddho janaḥ || aṣṭānavatisaṃyukte śate śaradi vatsare | kṛṣṇe śrāvaṇapañcamyāṃ vāsare kujam āhvaye || śrīmacchaṃkaradevasya rājye vijayaśālinaḥ | bodhicaryāvatārākhyaṃ ṭīkālekhyam idaṃ śubhaṃ || śrīlalitapure ramye śrīmāṇiglasasṃjñake || yacchrīraghavanāmasthavihāre sugatālaye dhanyasthavirabhikṣos tu buddhacaṃdrasya pustakaṃ | tatpuṇyād bodhisatvasya labhate paramaṃ padam iti || (fol. 148v7–11)
purpose: Merit transfer: the scribe dedicates the merit of copying so that people may become buddhas ('tenāstu buddho janaḥ'); the owner's merit leads to the supreme state of a bodhisattva ('tatpuṇyād bodhisatvasya labhate paramaṃ padam').
notes: Era: none is named, but 'aṣṭānavatisaṃyukte śate' = 198. This fits NS 198 (c. 1078 CE) and the reign of Śaṅkaradeva (c. 1067–1080 CE, NS c. 187–200). The catalogue's 'VS 1989?' is wrong. 'kujam āhvaye' = Tuesday. Commissioner: 'likhāpiteyam' is followed by a long string of plural epithets and then a lacuna ('kleśa….'), so the commissioner's name is lost. subject: Bauddhatantra
date_note: = Tuesday 21 Jun 1689, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: iti dvādaśasahasrādihbuddhoddhṛte śrīlaghukālacakrajñānapaṭalaḥ samāptaḥ || 50 || ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetu[s] teṣān tathāgato hy avadat teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ || || śreyo ʼstu || saṃvat 809 āṣāḍhaśuklapañcamyāṃ tithau bhaumadine vidūyati devācāryena(!) lekhayet(!) sampūrṇa[ṃ] karomi || etat puṇyānubhāvena mama saparivārāṇāṃ kalyāṇam astu || || śubham astu sarvajagatāṃ || (fol. 113r3-6)
purpose: merit transfer: for the welfare of the scribe and his family (mama saparivārāṇāṃ kalyāṇam astu)
notes: The era is not stated. NS is assumed from the Newari script and the catalogue; year 809 gives c. 1689 CE. The phrase 'vidūyati devācāryena(!) lekhayet(!) sampūrṇa[ṃ] karomi' is corrupt. 'vidūyati' is unclear: it could be a garbled verb or epithet, perhaps 'viduṣā', and is probably not a place name. 'lekhayet' looks causative, but 'sampūrṇaṃ karomi' (I complete it) and 'mama' (my) are in the first person, which marks Devācārya as the scribe. Devācārya might also be read as the personal name Deva with the title ācārya (possibly a Vajrācārya). It is kept here as a single name, matching the catalogue.
review: Removed the title 'ācārya' from Devācārya: the name is kept whole as Devācārya, so listing 'ācārya' as a separate title counted it twice. The alternative reading (Deva + title ācārya) is mentioned in notes.

colophon: iti śrīdhanajayasya kṛtau nighaṭaṃ(!) samaye śabdasaṃkīrṇayaṃ nirūpaṇaṃ nāma(fol. 13r3) prathamaḥ paricchedaḥ || || ۞ || || samāpto dhanaṃjayakokhaḥ || || || saṃvat 1654 || āṣā(4)ḍhaśudi 13 bhṛguvāsare liṣitam idaṃ virātbhaṭṭātmajeva naraharibha<<>>ṭṭena || || śubham astu (5) || || ۞ || || śubhaṃ bhūyāt || ۞ || (6) yādṛśaṃ pustake dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ liṣitaṃ mayā || yadi śu<< >>ddham aśudho vā mama doṣo na dīyate || || || || śubhaṃ (fol. 15v3-6)
notes: 'virātbhaṭṭātmajeva' is a miswriting of 'virāṭabhaṭṭātmajena', 'son of Virāṭa Bhaṭṭa'. 'kokhaḥ' stands for 'kośaḥ' (dhanaṃjayakośaḥ). The colophon says only 'saṃvat 1654'. In a Devanagari manuscript dated by śudi and a weekday this is most likely VS, which gives about 1597 CE. 17 June 1597 (Julian) is a Friday, which fits bhṛguvāsara, but I did not check that the tithi falls on that day. The catalogue gives ŚS 1654 (= 1732 CE), and that remains possible. The colophon has no internal evidence for Śaka, so I am keeping VS, but this should be checked with a calendar calculation.

notes: The era is not named, but 'saṃvatra 958' in a Newari colophon means NS 958 (1838 CE), which matches the catalogue. 'yanyāpuhnī 4 līsa' = 4 days after Yaṃlā punhi (the Bhādra full moon), so about Bhādra kṛṣṇa 4. 'coyāgu gītā siṃmanalasiṃ nāpāvana' is roughly 'the written Gītā went with (nāpā vana) Siṃmanalasiṃ'. This could mean he received or owned it, or took it with him. It does not clearly make him the scribe, commissioner or owner, so his role is left as 'other'. The name may be a phonetic form of Siṃhanarasiṃha (Newari l/r and h/m variation), or it may be two words. The 'rāva,' before 'subha' at line 6 is unclear: it could be a fragment of a word or name, or of the weekday (e.g. -vāra). The scribe is not named.

Notes: added the stray 'rāva,' and a fuller explanation of the Newari phrase.

title: Raghuvaṃśa and Sañjīvinī
subject: Kāvya
date_note: ≈ 1554 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti śrīraghuvaṃśe mahākāvye kālidāsakṛtau vaśiṣṭāśramagamano nāma prathamaḥ sargaḥ || ❖ || (fol. 27r5–6) || iti śrīmahopādhyāya kolamalamallināthasūriviracitāyāṃ raghuvaṃśasamākhyāyāṃ saṃjīvinyāṃ prathamaḥ sargaḥ || ❖ || (fol. 27r7–8) || dviṣaṇnagendrasaṃmite śakeṅganāgateruṇe | lilekhakāvyapustakaṃ saṭīkakaṃ dvijāgraṇīḥ śāstreṣu bhraṣṭā kavayo bhavaṃti tatrāpi naṣṭā tu purāṇyabhaṭṭāḥ | tatrāpi naṣṭā kṛṣim āśrayaṃti kṛṣīcyutā bhāgavatā bhavaṃti || 1 || malayācalasaṃbhūte madaṃ vahati mārute || niniṃda kāmini kāmin vānarān yāminimukhe || 1 || śrīrāmacandraya namaḥ | śrīsarasvatyai namaḥ || śrīgurubhyo namaḥ || (fol. 27r8–11)
notes: The scribe is called only 'dvijāgraṇīḥ' (foremost of the twice-born, i.e. a brahmin) and is not named: 'lilekha kāvyapustakaṃ saṭīkakaṃ dvijāgraṇīḥ'. The year is uncertain. The chronogram reads dvi(2)-ṣaṭ(6)-naga(7)-indra. Indra usually stands for 14, which gives an impossible number when read right to left. Taking 'indra' as a slip for 'indu' (1), which fits the pañcacāmara metre equally well, gives ŚS 1762 ≈ 1840 CE, which suits Devanagari on Nepali paper. The catalogue's ŚS 1476 (≈1554 CE) can only be reached by reading indra=14, naga=7, ṣaṭ=6 and dropping dvi, so it looks doubtful. 'aṅganāgate 'ruṇe' means the sun had entered Kanyā (solar month around Bhādra/Āśvina). The verses after the date ('śāstreṣu bhraṣṭā…' and 'malayācalasaṃbhūte…') are stock subhāṣitas, not colophon data. The colophon is for sarga 1 only.
review: Date: the chronogram 'dviṣaṇnagendra' does not give ŚS 1476. Read right to left, dvi=2, ṣaṭ=6, naga=7 and indra (normally 14) gives an impossible 14762. Reading indra as a slip for indu (=1) gives ŚS 1762 (c. 1840 CE). This is the proposed reading and is flagged as uncertain, against the catalogue's 1476.
Date: 'śake 'ṅganāgate 'ruṇe' = in the Śaka year, when the sun (aruṇa) had entered Virgo (aṅganā = Kanyā). Month field set to solar month Kanyā.
Mallinātha: 'Kolamala' is not an institution. It is moved out of affiliation and marked as a corruption of the family name Kolācala.
Notes expanded: unnamed scribe, the verses that follow, and the date conflict.

title: Vāsavadattā
subject: Kāvya
date_note: = Sunday 3 Jul 1808, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīmahākavisubaṃdhuviracitā vāsavadattākhyā ākhyāyikā samāptim agāt śrīmanmahāgaṇapatiśāradābhyāṃ namaḥ śrīviśveśvarāpanamanaḥ || khavahniśailadharaṇī saṃmite pramāthināmni samvatsare āṣāḍamāsya(!) site raviyutadaśamyāṃ likhitam idaṃ śrīvinodaśarmaṇākāśyāṃ (fol. 32r4‒6)
notes: The chronogram 'khavahniśailadharaṇī' read right to left gives kha 0, vahni 3, śaila 7, dharaṇī 1, so 1730. The colophon names no era. The catalogue reads it as Śaka 1730 and dates it Sunday 3 July 1808, which I have kept. The year name is a problem, though. Under the southern 60-year cycle, Śaka 1730 is Vibhava, and Pramāthin would be Śaka 1741 or 1801. Read as VS 1730 (1673 CE), the year would be Pramādin, not Pramāthin. The year name may follow the northern Jovian reckoning, or it may be a scribal slip, so the era is somewhat uncertain. 'āṣāḍamāsya(!)' is a corruption of āṣāḍhamāse. 'śrīviśveśvarāpanamanaḥ' is corrupt, probably for '(śrī)viśveśvarārpaṇam astu'. 'site' = śuklapakṣa; 'raviyuta' = Sunday; 'kāśyāṃ' = Kāśī (Vārāṇasī).

title: Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇatantra
subject: Bauddha Tantra
date_note: = Saturday 22 Aug 1896, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: year + 1, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: itya(!) kallavīrākhyaśrīcaṇḍamahāroṣaṇatantre devatāsādhanapaṭalaḥ pañcaviṃśa⟨|| ||⟩titamaḥ || ❁ idam avocad bhagavān śrīvajrasattvas te ca yoginīgaṇā bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti || itya(!) kallavīraṃ nāma śrīcaṇḍamahāroṣaṇatantraṃ samāptam || || ye dharmā hetu prabhavā hetu[s] teṣāṃ tathāgata[ḥ]⟨||⟩ hy avadat teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādi(!) mahāśramaṇaḥ || naipāladeśe sthitakāṃtipuryāṃ śrīratnakīrttivihāranāmnā || śrīvajrācāryayogamānvilāsāt likhāpi (!) tantraiḥ (!) kallavīrākhye || dānapati asaṃṭolahiti maṃgala jeyā tulādhara dhijamān siṃha bhātṛ buddhimān siṃhayāta thva pustaka coyā viyā jula || śubha saṃvat 1016 śrāvaṇaśukla 14 roja 4 sasidhayakā || (97v3–98r5)
purpose: written and given to the dānapati Buddhimān Siṃha (brother of Dhijamān Siṃha)
notes: The era is not named, but 'saṃvat 1016' with Newari phrasing and a Tulādhara patron fits NS: 1016 + 880 = 1896 CE. 'likhāpi' (!) usually means 'caused to be written', but the Newari line 'coyā viyā jula' ('wrote and gave') points to Yogamān as the scribe, which agrees with the catalogue's tentative 'Scribe: Yogamān Vajrācārya ?'. The verse is corrupt and unmetrical. 'asaṃṭolahiti maṃgala jeyā' is unclear: Asaṃ Ṭol is Asan in Kathmandu, and 'hiti' (water conduit) may be a locality, but 'maṃgala jeyā' cannot be resolved; it may be part of a name or a locality. The grammar leaves it open whether the dānapati is Dhijamān Siṃha alone (giving the book to his brother), both brothers, or Buddhimān Siṃha. The tulādhara title for Buddhimān Siṃha is inferred from the family. 'sasidhayakā' is probably a slip for 'siddhayakā' (completed). Ratnakīrtivihāra is Makhan Bahal, Kathmandu.
review: Names kept in their attested Newari forms: Yogamān, Dhijamān Siṃha, Buddhimān Siṃha (not a Sanskritised 'Yogamāna').
Buddhimān Siṃha is the person the book was written and given to ('-yāta thva pustaka coyā viyā jula'). As the likely dānapati he gets commissioner + donor + owner instead of plain beneficiary.
Dhijamān Siṃha: the colophon is unclear whether he is a co-dānapati or is named only to identify his brother. He keeps commissioner + donor, but at medium confidence.
Residence: 'Maṃgala jeyā' is not part of a place name. The residence is reduced to Asaṃ (Asan) Ṭol, and the unclear words are explained in notes.
wrote_for relation now runs from the scribe to Buddhimān Siṃha, the recipient. A wrote_for link to Dhijamān Siṃha is kept at lower certainty.
Weekday: roja 4 is given as Wednesday.
Place: Ratnakīrtivihāra is identified as Makhan Bahal, Kathmandu.

colophon: ityāgneye mahātantre pratiṣṭhātantraṃ mohacūḍottaram || || saṃpūrṇam || śubham || śivam bhūyāt || || samvat 806 phālguṇavadi 10 bhaume śrīmadbhogaleśvaramaṭhāvasthita paṇḍitācāryabhaṭṭāraka śrīsarvagaṇena likhitam idaṃ puṣtakaṃ puṣpikāntalekhayutasya prācīnadevākṣaralipimayasya prācīnatāḍapatrapustakasyādhāreṇa 1982 vaikramavarṣe jyeṣṭhamāse śrī5mahārājādhirāja tribhuvanavīravikramaśāhadevavijayarājye pradhānasaciva śrī3mahārājacandraśamśerajaṅgabahādūrarāṇāpratipālite nepāladeśe kāṣṭhamaṇḍaparājadhānyāṃ śrīmadrājagurumānyavarahemarājavidvadvarair gaṇeśadattaśarmadvārā likhitam idaṃ pustakaṃ || asyādhārabhūtatāḍapatrapustakasya prācīnatayā tatpratilipikṛtasya pustakāntarasyāpi triśatābdapūrvaprācīnatā darśanena tadullikhita 806 samvatsaro nepālasaṃvatsarād bhinno vaikramādiḥ saṃbhāvyate || (fol. 47r2–7)
notes: This is a modern Devanagari copy, made in Kathmandu in VS 1982 Jyeṣṭha (c. May–June 1925 CE). Gaṇeśadatta wrote it for Rājaguru Hemarāja. The ruler was King Tribhuvana and the prime minister was Candra Śamśera. It was copied from an old palm-leaf manuscript that the colophon describes as written in old Devanagari ('prācīnadevākṣaralipimaya'). The palm-leaf colophon is reproduced: 'samvat 806 phālguṇavadi 10 bhaume', written by Paṇḍitācārya Bhaṭṭāraka Sarvagaṇa of Bhogaleśvaramaṭha. Sarvagaṇa is therefore the scribe of the exemplar, not of this copy, and the catalogue's 'Scribe: Sarvagaṇa' refers to the exemplar. The year 806 has no era. The 1925 note itself argues that it is Vikrama rather than Nepāla saṃvat, because the palm-leaf and an intermediate copy look more than 300 years old. Read as VS, 806 would be c. 749 CE; read as NS, it would be c. 1686 CE. Neither reading is confirmed (the catalogue also queries it: '806 ???'). The record's main date is VS 1982. Hemarāja is presumably Rājaguru Hemarāja Paṇḍita, the well-known collector, though the colophon does not say he owned the copy.

title: Śyāmārahasyatantra
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti śrīpūrṇānaṃdaparamahaṃsena viracite śyāmārahasye dvāviṃśatitamaḥ paricchedaḥ samāptaḥ || śubham astu || || ○ || śailāgnighanage śāke taiṣe māse site dale || saptamyāṃ ravivare ca viśvānaṃdoʼ likhaj jinaḥ || 1 || || śubham || (fol. 153r3–5)
notes: The chronogram is unresolved. śaila = 7 and agni = 3, but 'ghanage' (the catalogue field has 'dhanage') matches no standard number word with certainty; it may be a corruption of e.g. naga = 7. Read right to left, three digits would give Śaka 737, which is too early for Pūrṇānanda (16th century). The year probably needs four digits, e.g. Śaka 17x7, roughly 1800 CE, but no CE date is given. taiṣa = Pauṣa. 'likhaj jinaḥ' is odd: 'jinaḥ' may be a misreading (e.g. of 'janaḥ') or an epithet of the scribe, and it is not treated as a separate person. The catalogue's 'Vīśvānaṃda' is a misspelling of Viśvānanda.

title: Saubhāgyaratnākara
subject: Tantra
date_note: = Sunday 16 Jul 1662, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīsaccidānaṃdanāthacaraṇāraviṃdadvaṃdvānte vā siro śrī śrī vidyānaṃdanāthena kṛte saubhāgyaratnākare ṣaṭtriṃśas taraṃgaḥ || ❁ || samvat 782 śrīvaṇa śuklapratipadyān tīthau puṣyānakṣatre yakṣe yoge ādityadine thva kuhnu coye dhunakā tho saṃphuli co yāthaṃ puṇyaṃ thivaṃ tāyā brāhmaṇa śrībhākuṃtuna coyā va śrī caravanihma śrī upādhyā śrīviśvanāthaṃ jūyāta viyā juro || ❖ || śubha sarvvadāmastu || (exp. 240t8–b4)
purpose: for merit (puṇya); the copy was given to Upādhyāya Viśvanātha
notes: The catalogue names Viśvanātha Upādhyāya as the scribe, but the colophon says the Brahmin Bhākuṃtu wrote the copy and gave it to Viśvanātha ('brāhmaṇa śrībhākuṃtuna coyā va ... śrīviśvanāthaṃ jūyāta viyā juro'). 'caraṇāraviṃdadvaṃdvānte vā siro' is a corruption of '-dvandvāntevāsinā' ('pupil at the lotus feet of'). 'śrī caravanihma' probably means 'the one of Caravani/Carava', perhaps a locality or a quarter; this is uncertain. 'yakṣe yoge' does not match any standard yoga name and is probably corrupt. Bhākuṃtu is an unusual name form ('-na' is the Newari ergative). NS 782 = c. 1662 CE.
review: Saccidānandanātha: role changed from 'teacher' to 'other'. He is the author's guru, not a teacher connected with this copy. The corrupt 'caraṇāraviṃdadvaṃdvānte vā siro' is read as '-dvandvāntevāsinā' (pupil), so the pupil_of relation stays.
Bhākuṃtu: 'donor' added, because he wrote the copy and gave it away ('coyā va ... viyā'). Confidence lowered to medium because the name form is unusual.
Viśvanātha: 'caravanihma' recorded as a possible residence or locality (low certainty). Kept as beneficiary and owner, since he received the copy.
Added a relation: Bhākuṃtu gave the book to Viśvanātha ('other').
Notes: the corrupt passage, the odd yoga name and the catalogue's scribe error are now recorded.

notes: No scribe, commissioner or owner is named. 'bhagatpatnanagare' could be Bhaktapattana (Bhaktapur), but 'harikṣatre' (= harikṣetre) is more typical of Harihara-kṣetra (Sonpur, near Patna, Bihar), so the place is left unidentified. 'dharyanārāyaṇavatāse' is unclear. It may be '(Dhairya/Dharma)nārāyaṇa-āvāse', 'at the residence (or temple) of ...nārāyaṇa'. The '(2)?' after 801 may be the cataloguer's line-number marker, or it may mark a doubtful last digit (802 = c. 1682 CE). The catalogue gives 801. 'Haripatidevana' is the ergative ('by Haripatideva'). The -deva ending is kept as part of the name, but no king of this name is known, so it is not treated as a regnal name. 'coyā juro' means 'was written', so the role is scribe, not commissioner. After the colophon comes a vernacular (Hindi/Bhojpuri-coloured) mantra invoking Kāmākhyā Devī of Kāmarūpa (kāmarideśa kaṃmacchādevi), with a jogī and a list of gifts. title: Guhyakālīpratiṣṭhā
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Sunday 5 Apr 1626, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti guhyakālīpratiṣṭhā ahorātrayajñaṃ samāptaṃ || || samvat 731 kārttikakṛṣṇa tṛtīyāyāntithau rohinī(!) nakṣatre budhavāra kvahnuṃ guhyakālīpratiṣṭhā yāṅā dina śrī upādhyā uddhavarājena sañcitam idaṃ pustakaṃ || caparitale satayā pratibhārapratiṣṭhāṃthama yāṅā || śubhaṃ || || saṃvat 746 caitra śukla navamyāntithau puṣyanakṣatre ādityavāsare śrī3guhyakālīpratiṣṭhālikhitadinaṃ śrīuddhavanāthaguro(!) prasādācchrīkālīdāsenalikhitam idaṃ pustakaṃ || śrīśrīśrīdevīprītir astu || tasmai gurave sadārādhane rato ʼhaṃ bhavāmi || || śubham astu sarvvadā bāndhavādīnāṃ || ❁ || (fol. 31v5–9)
purpose: for the pleasure of the Goddess (śrīśrīśrīdevīprītir astu)
notes: The colophon gives two dates. Both are in NS and they do not conflict. (1) NS 731 kārttika kṛṣṇa 3, budhavāra, Rohiṇī nakṣatra (about 1610 CE): the day the Guhyakālīpratiṣṭhā was performed and a pratiṣṭhā held at the sattal of Caparitale. On that day Upādhyāya Uddhavarāja compiled (sañcitam) the book. This is probably the exemplar or the original compilation of the ritual manual. (2) NS 746 caitra śukla 9, Sunday, Puṣya nakṣatra (1626 CE): the date this copy was written by Kālīdāsa, through the grace of his guru Uddhavanātha. Uddhavarāja and Uddhavanātha are very likely the same person (Uddhava-), so the guru would be the compiler. They are not merged because the names differ. Another possible reading of 'sañcita' is 'collected/acquired', which would make p1 an owner of the exemplar. Caparitale is the place of the pratiṣṭhā; the place of copying is not stated.
review: p1 Uddhavarāja: role changed from 'owner' to 'author' (compiler). 'sañcitam idaṃ pustakaṃ' means he compiled the book at the NS 731 pratiṣṭhā, not that he owned it. Confidence lowered to medium.
p1 title normalised from 'upādhyā' to 'upādhyāya'.
Note added that p1 Uddhavarāja and p2 Uddhavanātha are probably the same person, Kālīdāsa's guru. They are kept as separate records.
Place stays empty: Caparitale (a sattal) is where the pratiṣṭhā was performed, not where the copy was made. The notes now say so.
Notes now give the CE date of the first date (NS 731, about 1610 CE).

title: Durgāprāsādaśāntibalyarcanavidhi
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
colophon: iti gṛhe pratiṣṭhā śāntibalyarccanavidhiḥ samāptaḥ || || || yādṛṣṭaṃ puṣṭakaṃ(!) dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ liṣitaṃ mayā | yadi śurddha(!) maśubddhao(!) vā mama doṣo na dīyate || śrīśrījayabhūpatīndramalladeva prabhuthākurasana kvātha pratiṣṭhāyā śānibalyarccanavidhiḥ sāphuli dayakā juro || || śubhaṃ bhavatu sarvvadā || || || || ❁ || ❁ || (fol. 134r3–134v2)
purpose: made by order of King Bhūpatīndra Malla for the consecration of a kvātha (fort/citadel)
notes: The colophon gives no date and names no scribe: the copyist only says 'mayā' in the stock verse yādṛṣṭaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā. Bhūpatīndra Malla was king of Bhaktapur, reigning about NS 816–842 (1696–1722 CE), so the copy probably dates from that period and comes from Bhaktapur. The colophon does not state the place, so the place field is left empty. In the Newari sentence the agentive -sana with 'sāphuli dayakā juro' ('the book was made') makes him the commissioner. The final rubric says 'gṛhe pratiṣṭhā' (consecration of a house), while the Newari sentence says 'kvātha pratiṣṭhā' (consecration of a fort). Corrupt spellings: puṣṭakaṃ for pustakaṃ, liṣitaṃ for likhitaṃ, śurddha maśubddhao for śuddham aśuddhaṃ, śānibalyarccana for śāntibalyarcana.
review: Split the title 'prabhuthākura' into two titles, 'prabhu' and 'ṭhākura' (Newari thākura).
Shortened the evidence to the substring that supports both roles: the agentive -sana with 'sāphuli dayakā juro' means the book was made by him, so he is commissioner as well as king.
Reworded purpose: the book was made for the consecration (pratiṣṭhā) of a kvātha, i.e. a fort or citadel.
Added notes on his reign dates, the likely place, the rubric variant and the corrupt spellings.

title: Dīkṣāvidhi
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Thursday 26 Feb 1682, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti dīkṣāyāṣukuṭhi coya yāyārātayā vidhi samāptaḥ || || śubhaṃ || vaiṣākha kṣemalābhas tu jyeṣṭhe ca maraṇaṃ dhruvaṃ | ākṣāḍhe bandhunāśaṃ ca śrāvaṇe ca samāyutaṃ || … dīkṣāyā māsaphalaśubha aśubha saye juroṃ || || saṃ 776 jyeṣṭha vadi 8 goyacchoyā dina || digaprāśana || vāraprāśana || pūrvva || ḍāḍiṃvi || āditya || gvāla || dakṣiṇa || surāpāna || … abde yogaukhanāge tvasitaphaṇitithau phāluṇe māsyalekhi | sthūlāṃ dīkṣābhidhāyāṃ vividhavidhimayīṃ paddhatīṃ sūjñalabhyāṃ | saṃpūrṇnaṃ śrībhavānyāḥ padakamalatare bhāvanaikāgracittaḥ kātyāyanyāḥ kṛpāvān sumatijayajitāmitramallo mahīndraḥ || || śrī nepālasamvat 802 vikramāditya saṃvat 1738 kaligatasaṃvat (4772) śake samvat 1603 phālhuṇamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe paṃmyāyā(!)tithau svātinakṣatre dhruvayoge kathākalanamuhutake(!) bēhapati(!)vāsare kūharāśigate savitari turārāśigate candramasi || || thva kuhnu śrīśrījayajitāmitramallavarmanā svakarena likhitaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || || jitāmitrasya bhūpasya tvāṃ vinā nāsti me gatiḥ | tvadbhakti tvatparāśaktir matirbhūyāt kulāmbike || || śrī3 siddhilakṣmīprīnātu || (exp. 35b7–37t4) exp. 37b contains two graphs of Yantra.
notes: The scribe is King Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur (reigned c. NS 793–816). He wrote this copy himself ('svakarena likhitaṃ'; 'alekhi' in the verse). The verse might also mean he compiled the paddhati, but this is uncertain, so 'author' is not given. In the verse the name is given as 'sumatijayajitāmitramallo'; 'sumati' is an epithet. The chronogram yoga(2)-kha(0)-nāga(8), read right to left, gives 802, and asita-phaṇi-tithi gives kṛṣṇa pañcamī. Both agree with NS 802 Phālguna kṛṣṇa 5, VS 1738 and Śaka 1603, i.e. about Feb/March 1682 CE. The sun in Kumbha and the moon in Tulā (Svāti) are consistent with this. Kali 4772 is about 10 years too low (expected c. 4782); the cataloguer has already put it in parentheses. The catalogue's 'NS 776' comes from 'saṃ 776 jyeṣṭha vadi 8 goyacchoyā dina'. That is part of the text's dīkṣā-month section (c. 1656 CE, before the king's reign), not the copying date. The place is not stated; Bhaktapur is likely, given the king. Muhūrta 'kathākalana(?)' is corrupt.
review: Removed role 'author': 'alekhi' and 'svakarena likhitaṃ' say the king wrote out this copy. They do not clearly say he composed the paddhati.
Titles: removed 'sumati', which is an epithet ('wise') inside the verse. Kept mahīndra, bhūpa, varman.
Date: checked the chronogram 'yoga(2)-kha(0)-nāga(8)', read right to left = 802, and 'asita-phaṇi-tithi' = kṛṣṇa pañcamī. Both agree with the prose date.
Notes: Kali 4772 does not match. The expected Kali year is about 4782 for CE 1681/82, so the first reading was wrong to say it matches.
Notes: NS 776 belongs to the text (the dīkṣā māsaphala section), not to the copying.
Purpose: reduced to the benediction, since no svārtha/parārtha statement is given.
Muhūrta and sun/moon rāśi added to the notes.

subject: Karmakāṇḍa
colophon: iti śrīmat trimallaṃvināviracitaṃ śrīmadbhāṣyakārakṛtanityārādhanavidhivyākhyānaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ samāptaṃ śrīmate rāmānujāya na (fol. 15r10)
notes: The commentator's name is corrupt: 'trimallaṃvināviracitaṃ' (fol. 15r10). Possible readings are 'trimallakavinā viracitaṃ' or 'trimallena viracitaṃ', or a Sanskrit form of a Tamil name such as Tirumala/Tirumalai. 'Trimalla' is a best guess. Rāmānuja is the author of the root text (the Nityārādhanavidhi), not of this commentary. He is identified by the epithet 'bhāṣyakāra', and his name also appears in the final invocation 'śrīmate rāmānujāya na(maḥ)', which is cut off. The colophon gives no scribe, date or place.
review: Lowered p1 (Trimalla) confidence to low: the form 'trimallaṃvinā' is garbled, and the stem could be Trimalla or a Sanskrit form of a South Indian name (e.g. Tirumala/Tirumalai).
Added p2 Rāmānuja as author of the root text (Nityārādhanavidhi), given as 'bhāṣyakāra' and named in the closing invocation 'śrīmate rāmānujāya na(maḥ)'.
Expanded the notes.

title: Revantamahābhairavapūjāvidhi
subject: Tantrik Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Wednesday 6 Dec 1713, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīśrīśrī revantamahābhairavapūjāpaddhatiḥ pūjāparddhati vidhi samāptaḥ || || śubha || ❖ samvat 834 mārgaśiravadi 4 budhavāra puṣyanakṣatra aidra yoga sā+rapāṭhapratiṣṭhā yāṅā dina || || (fol. 37r3–6)
notes: The era is not named ('samvat 834'), but the Newari script and the Newari phrase 'yāṅā dina' make it Nepāla Saṃvat. NS 834 begins in autumn 1713, so Mārgaśira kṛṣṇa 4 of NS 834 falls in Nov/Dec 1713 CE. NS+880 would give 1714, which is too late for this month. The closing phrase 'sā+rapāṭhapratiṣṭhā yāṅā dina' means 'the day on which the pratiṣṭhā of sā+rapāṭha (sārapāṭha?) was performed'. It marks the date as the day of a ritual, not the purpose of the copy. The word is damaged ('+'), so the reading is uncertain. No person is named in the colophon. The catalogue's king, Jaya-Bhūpatīndra Malla of Bhaktapur (r. c. 1696–1722), fits the date, but he is not named in the quoted text, so he is not added.
review: purpose cleared: 'sā+rapāṭhapratiṣṭhā yāṅā dina' gives the date as the day a pratiṣṭhā was performed, not the purpose of the copy; moved to notes
nakshatra_yoga normalized: 'aidra' read as aindra yoga
ce_approx 1713 kept; added a note on why it is not NS+880 = 1714
notes expanded: catalogue king not named in colophon, but consistent with the date

notes: The colophon names no people. The catalogue gives Bhūpatīndra Malla as king, but he is not in the quoted colophon. The catalogue probably took him from the date: NS 836 = 1716 CE falls within his Bhaktapur reign (c. 1696–1722 CE). title: Śuṇṭhīvratavidhāna
subject: Tantrik Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Friday 3 Dec 1751, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: amānta months, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śuṭhāyīvrata samāptaṃ || śubham astu || ❁ || a || saṃvat 1808 pauṣa kṛṣṇa patipade (!) ādityavāra thva kuhnu śuṭḥāyai vrata likhitaṃ śubhaḥ || thva verasa makvāṃpura mahākumāraju śrījoganara (exp. 11b5–7)
notes: The era is not stated ('saṃvat'). NS 1808 is impossible. ŚS 1808 (1886 CE) would fall after the Gorkhā conquest of Makwanpur (1762), which does not fit a 'mahākumāra' of Makwanpur. VS 1808 = 1751/52 CE fits the late Sen period, so VS is assumed. Pauṣa kṛṣṇa pratipad falls around Dec 1751 / Jan 1752. The weekday was not checked. The colophon breaks off after 'śrījoganara', so the name may be incomplete. 'thva verasa (= velasa) …' ('at this time …') is the usual formula for naming the ruling authority at the time of copying. So Joganara is probably a Makwanpur prince (mahākumāra) in power, or the heir apparent, in whose time the copy was made. Whether he also commissioned it cannot be determined from the text as quoted. No scribe is named.
review: Joganara: title normalized to 'mahākumāra' (-ju is a Newari honorific suffix); confidence lowered to low because the colophon breaks off and the name may be incomplete (e.g. Joganarasiṃha / Joganārāyaṇa)
Joganara: role kept as 'other', with a note that the 'thva velasa …' formula usually names the authority in power at the time of copying
Tithi normalized to pratipad (written 'patipade')
Date: noted that the copy falls in Dec 1751/Jan 1752 and explained why VS is the era
Notes rewritten: the Sen identification is now presented as a guess

title: Śambhavanirūpaṇasaṅketavidhi
subject: Tantrik Karmakāṇḍa
date_raw: śrīsaṃvat 1772 bhādre māsi site ( pakṣe ) pūrṇā ca kujavāsare
date_note: = Friday 13 Sep 1715, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: Kārttikādi, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrīrudrayāmale śrīcakravāsanā antaryajana niskalaśāmbhavanirūpaṇasaṃketavidhi samāptā || || śrīsaṃvat 1772 bhādre māsi site ( pakṣe ) pūrṇā ca kujavāsare udite yāmale rudra śrīcakrārcanavāsanaṃ || | śrīmatkāmeśvarī bhakto kāmeśvarasya sevakaḥ || lalitā…tmena likhitaṃ madhusūdanaśarmaṇā || || (fol. 10v6–10)
notes: The colophon gives the year only as 'śrīsaṃvat 1772' and names no era. The record assumes Vikrama Saṃvat (VS 1772 ≈ 1715 CE). If the era were Śaka, the date would be ≈ 1850 CE. The weekday (Tuesday) has not been checked against either option. 'śrīmatkāmeśvarī bhakto kāmeśvarasya sevakaḥ' most likely describes the scribe as a devotee of the goddess Kāmeśvarī and her consort, the god Kāmeśvara, not as the servant of a man named Kāmeśvara. The words before the scribe's name ('lalitā…tmena') are damaged. They could be 'lalitātmajena' ('son of Lalitā[...]'), which would name a parent, but they are too uncertain to record as a person.
review: No substantive changes. Added to notes: the era is uncertain (VS assumed), 'kāmeśvarasya sevakaḥ' most likely refers to the deity, and 'lalitā…tmena' may hide a kinship term.

title: Nārasiṃhapurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Sunday 10 Feb 1669, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīnārasiṃhapurāṇe ādye dharmmārthakāmamokṣapradāyini parabrahmasvarūpiṇi idam ekaṃ suniṣpannaṃ dhyeyo nārāyaṇaḥ sadā na vāsudevāt param asti kiñcit śrīnārasiṃhapurāṇaṃ samāptaṃ || || || nidhivasumunivarṣe māghamāse valakṣe śiśirakiraṇaṛkṣe bhānuvāre daśamyāṃ| svakulakamalabhānuḥ pūrṇasiṃhaś ca prītyā naraharipadabhakto vāsudevo lilekha || agryaḥ satāṃ praṇayināṃ kuladevatāyāḥ prītyai sadārppitamanāḥ sa tadaṅghriyugmo dātā dadau ravikulodbhavavāsudevaḥ, pustīmimāṃ kulamaṇidvijalakṣmaṇāya || śrīvāsudeva śrīkṛṣṇa śrīrāma śrīpadmanābha śrīgaruḍadhvaja || jaya dīnadayāla || śubham astu sarvvadā || śiva śiva śiva || rāma rāma rāma || kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa jaya dīnadayāla || śivaṃ || ❖ gaṃgādharāhitamanodvijalakṣmaṇākhyo, pādhyāya(śarmaṇa) idaṃ jananarmadasya| saṃsāragharmaśamanadvijavarṣma(varṇaṣ) (ṣaṭkarma)śarmakaradharmasunirmalasya || (fol. 144r2–7)
notes: Chronogram: nidhi (9), vasu (8), muni (7) = NS 789. The scribe Vāsudeva, claiming descent from the solar lineage (ravikulodbhava), gifted the manuscript to Upādhyāya Lakṣmaṇa.

title: Bhāgavatapurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
date_note: = Sunday 31 Oct 1683, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrībhāgavate mahāpāramahaṃsyāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyāśikyāṃ dvādaśaskaṃdhe saṃkhyāvarṇṇanaṃ nāma trayodaśodhyāyaḥ || || śubham astu || || ❖ sumati jitāmitramalla kaniṣṭhogramallavicakṣaṇe nṛpatau | śāśati bhaktagrāmaṃ manojñaviśrāmaramanīyasthānaṃ || rājñaḥ pradhāno jayakīrttināmā tadātmajo viṣṇur iti pratītaḥ || kāśīti nāmā jasasābhirāmas tasyātmajo dhārmmikapūrṇṇarāmaḥ || bhakte pauryyavacapratosti lalitaśrīmanmahābhairavasthāne caṇḍigaṇe suvarṇṇaracitāṃ yatra praṇālāṃ śubhāṃ || tatra kṣoṇipate ramātyapurago rāmeti candrānvitaḥ tejasvīraṇajitvaro surasamaḥ pūrṇṇeti rāmas tataḥ || vedadyauvasuvarṣage sitagate viṣṇos tithau kārttike uttrebhadrayute dineśadivase harṣeti yogānvite | skandhair dvādaśabhir mu .. .. racitaṃ rāmeti candrātmajaḥ śrīmadbhāgavataṃ saṃpūrṇṇam alikhal lakṣmīdharaḥ śāstradhīḥ || || ❖ samvat 804 kārttika su(!)kla dvādaśi utrabhadrakṣatre harṣanayoge ādityavāra thva kuhnu dhunakā śrī 3 bhāgavata ādiṃ nisya antaṃ sampūrṇṇa na coyā likhiti kūla .. tra lakṣmīdharaḥ || || yā vireṣakapāṭhakayo kasya śubha śubham astu śubham bhūyāt || || thavatā nimīrtti cayā kṛṣṇaprītir astu || śubha || (fol. 483r1–7)
notes: The date is given both metrically in Sanskrit (vedadyauvasuvarṣage = 804) and in Newari prose. Lakṣmīdhara copies the text for his own use ('thavatā nimīrtti cayā'). Jitāmitramalla rules Bhaktapur along with his younger brother Ugramalla ('kaniṣṭhogramallavicakṣaṇe nṛpatau').

title: Mahābhārata Virātaparva
subject: Mahābhārata
date_note: = Tuesday 2 Oct 1866, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: || iti śrīmahābhārate satasāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyāsikyāṃ virāṭaparvaṇI dviśaptatitamodhyāyaḥ || 72 || iti samvat 1923 sāla miti āśviṇa (!) vadi 9 roja 3 tasmīn (!) dine likhitaṃ līṣanārthe (!) padmadāsabhaktānāṃ sampūrṇa śubham (fol. 107v12–14)
notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Padmabhāsabhakta', but the colophon as quoted reads 'padmadāsabhakta-'. The colophon reading is used here. 'līṣanārthe' is corrupt. It could stand for 'likhanārthe' or 'lekhanārthe', or be a garbled 'paṭhanārthe'. If it means 'paṭhanārthe', the genitive plural (honorific) would mark Padmadāsabhakta as the person the copy was made for (owner/reader), not the writer. The first reading's roles 'commissioner' and 'owner' are not supported by any explicit formula, so only 'scribe' is kept, following the catalogue. 'bhakta' may be a name element rather than a title, so it stays in the name. The date is VS 1923, dark half of Āśvina, 9th tithi, Tuesday (roja 3), which falls around September–October 1866 CE.
review: Roles for Padmadāsabhakta cut to scribe only. No causative verb such as likhāpitam supports 'commissioner', and no possessive formula supports 'owner'. The genitive after 'likhitaṃ' is read as naming the writer, which agrees with the catalogue's scribe field.
Purpose left empty. 'līṣanārthe' is corrupt and its meaning is uncertain; the possible readings are given in the notes.
Weekday changed to plain 'Tuesday'; the 'roja 3' form stays in as_written.
Notes expanded: the name as read differs from the catalogue's spelling, and the alternative reading is explained.

subject: Mahābhārata (Itihāsa)
date_note: = Sunday 30 Sep 1990, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīmatpadavākya pramāṇaamaryādā dhuraṃdhara caturdhara vaṃśāvataṃsa śrīgoviṃdasūri sūnu śrīnīlakaṃṭha viracite bhāratabhāvadīpe sabhāparvārtha prakāśaḥ samāptimagamat śrīkṛṣṇāya vāsudevāya namaḥ ❖ śrīrāmāya rāmacandrāya namaḥ ❖ rāmarāma rāmaḥ || (fol. 172v1&9) || iti śrīmahābhārate śatasāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyyāsikyāṃ sabhāparvaṇI anudyūtaṃ samāptaṃ80 adyāyaḥ saṃkhyā 7233 svasti śrīsamvat 1912 sālamiti āśvinaśukla 11 ravivāsare saṃpūrṇaṃ idaṃ pustakaṃ tejadattena likhitaṃ śubham śrīrāmarāmarāmarāmarāmarāmarāma (fol. 173v2–3&173r5–6)
notes: The catalogue gives the date as ŚS 1912. But 'saṃvat 1912 sāla miti' is the usual Vikrama Saṃvat formula in Nepal, so VS 1912 = c. 1855 CE. Śaka 1912 would be 1990 CE, which is not plausible. The weekday (Sunday) was not checked against an ephemeris. 'Caturdhara' is Nīlakaṇṭha's family name (vaṃśa), not a place. Nīlakaṇṭha, son of Govinda, wrote the Bhāratabhāvadīpa commentary. He is not connected with this copy. Govinda is listed only as his father.

notes: The two people named appear in the standard deyadharma formula, which makes them donors. The colophon does not say they wrote the copy, and no scribe is named. The closing formula 'yathā dṛṣṭaṃ tathā likhitaṃ lekhako nāsti doṣaḥ' is generic. The catalogue's 'Scribe' field is therefore doubtful. 'Paranirvāṇamahāvihāra' is the donors' affiliation (-vihārīya), not an explicit place of copying, so the catalogue's Place field is an inference; the vihāra is not identified. The second syllable of the nun's name is lost (so+matī), and 'Somamatī' is the cataloguer's restoration. Era not stated ('samvat'), but NS fits Ānandadeva's reign (c. 1147–1167 CE). The cataloguer's folio references are inconsistent: the colophon is cited as fol. 216v6–217r4, while ch. 31 ends at 217v6.

notes: The colophon has no date or place. syedaṃ(!) is most likely asyedaṃ with the first syllable lost: 'this book belongs to King Trivikramasena'. Trivikramasena was a king of one of the Sena lines; Tanahun and Makwanpur are both possible, but the colophon names no kingdom, so the identification is unconfirmed. The wrote_for relation (the scribe copying for the king) is inferred because the scribe statement and the ownership statement stand next to each other; the colophon does not say it directly. 'Pantha' (Panta/Pant) is read as a brahmin family name or title of the scribe. The author's name is also written paḍita(!)rājajagaṃnnātha(!) in the first vilāsa colophon.

title: Raghuvaṃśaṭīkā
subject: Kāvya
date_note: = Saturday 30 Apr 1667, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: iti | śrīraghuvaṃśamahākāvye syonaviṃśatisarggasya ṭīkā samāptā || || sindhunāgamunināmayutābde mādhave himaruci(dyu)tiṣasṭhyāṃ sūryyaje ca divase raghuṭīkā vīrabhadrariṣitāstu mude vaḥ || sam 787 || vaiśā ṣaṣṭhi śanivāra kunhu coyā || śubham astu || (fol. 93v6–8)
notes: The chronogram is read right to left: muni 7, nāga 8, sindhu 7 (the seven seas; sindhu can also mean 4). This gives 787, which matches 'sam 787' and the catalogue's NS 787 (about 1667 CE). Mādhava = Vaiśākha. Sūryaja (Saturn) = Saturday, which matches 'śanivāra'. The śukla pakṣa is only inferred from 'himaruci(dyu)ti' (the moon's brightness); the Newari line just says 'vaiśā ṣaṣṭhi'. 'vīrabhadrariṣitāstu' is probably corrupt for 'vīrabhadralikhitā astu' ('may the Raghu commentary written by Vīrabhadra be for your joy'). That makes Vīrabhadra the scribe, not the author of the ṭīkā. A reading 'racitā' would make him the commentator instead, but that is less likely in a dated copy colophon followed by 'coyā'. The ṭīkā itself is not attributed to anyone here. Other corrupt spellings: 'syonaviṃśati' stands for 'ekonaviṃśati' (19th sarga), and 'ṣasṭhyāṃ' stands for 'ṣaṣṭhyāṃ'.
review: Vīrabhadra: role changed from commentator to scribe. 'vīrabhadrariṣitā' is best read as 'vīrabhadralikhitā': ri stands for li, and ṣ for kh, as often in Newari scripts. The dated verse is the copyist's colophon, and 'coyā' (wrote) in the Newari line goes with it.
Purpose emptied: 'mude vaḥ' is a blessing on readers, not a stated purpose of the copy.
Notes: chronogram explained (sindhu = 7 seas here), pakṣa inference explained, and corrupt spellings flagged.

title: Meghadūta
subject: Kāvya
date_note: = Monday 20 May 1652, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti mahāmahopādhyāyaśrījagaddharaviracitā rasadīpinī meghaṭīkā samāptā || || netragotragirau varṣe mādhave prathame site | dvādaśyāṃ śanivāre śrīkṛṣṇena likhitā mudā || samva(!) 772 naṣṭavaiṣākhaśu(kla)dvādaśī kuhnusvanihmaśrīdevadāsadevayākāṃ śrīkṛṣṇa na coyā śubha || (fol. 74v7–9)
notes: The chronogram 'netragotragirau' gives 772 when read right to left: giri = 7, gotra (the seven kulaparvatas) = 7, netra = 2. This matches the numerals 'samva 772' and the catalogue's NS 772, which works out to 1652 CE. The verse calls the month 'prathama mādhava' (first Vaiśākha), so this was probably a year with an intercalary Vaiśākha. The Newari colophon calls it 'naṣṭavaiṣākha', and the exact meaning of 'naṣṭa' there is unclear. The Newari passage 'kuhnu svanihma śrīdevadāsadevayākāṃ' is obscure. 'kuhnu' means 'on that day'. 'svanihma' might be a garbled 'svanigahma', meaning 'a person of Svanigaḥ (Kathmandu)', but this is uncertain, so it is not recorded as a residence. I read '-yākāṃ' as marking the person for whom the scribe wrote, which gives Devadāsadeva the role of commissioner or beneficiary with medium confidence. Jagaddhara is the author of the commentary Rasadīpinī on the Meghadūta, not of the Meghadūta itself.
review: p2: name normalized to 'Kṛṣṇa'. The 'śrī' is an honorific and is now left out of the name, as the rules require. Confidence set to medium, because 'Śrīkṛṣṇa' as a full name cannot be ruled out.
p2: evidence now also cites the Newari 'śrīkṛṣṇa na coyā'.
date: month field now gives Vaiśākha, with mādhava, prathama and naṣṭavaiṣākha noted.
notes: the chronogram check is restated: read right to left, giri 7, gotra 7 (kulaparvata), netra 2 = 772. Also added a possible reading of 'svanihma' and a remark on '-yākāṃ'.

It is unclear whether the ownership note ('mukuṃdasyedaṃ pustakaṃ .. khāvī saṃ 1691') belongs to the scribal colophon or is a separate note; 'khāvī' is unexplained. notes: The two eras in the colophon conflict. Śāke 1614 = c. 1692 CE, but saṃvat 1852 (taken as VS) = c. 1795 CE, which would be Śāka 1717. The record uses VS 1852 because 'saṃvat 1852' comes directly after 'likhitaṃ'. The Śāka figure '1614' may be a scribal or cataloguing error (for example for 1714 or 1717), though the Śāka date could also be the true one. The weekday (bhaumavāra, Bhādrapada śukla 7) has not been checked against either year; doing so would settle which date is right. The catalogue gives both dates. No scribe, commissioner or place of copying is named.
review: Date: the first reading paired era ŚS / year 1614 with ce_approx 1795, which does not match (ŚS 1614 = c. 1692 CE). Changed to era VS, year 1852, ce_approx 1795, so the fields agree; the conflicting Śāka year is kept in as_written and explained in notes.
Notes: removed the claim that Bhādrapada śukla 7 of VS 1852 fell on a Tuesday, because it was not checked; the weekday still needs to be checked in a pañcāṅga.
Lakṣmīpati as author confirmed. The colophon names no scribe, commissioner or place.

notes: The colophon has only completion formulas for a section and for the whole text (puṣpikā). There is no scribal colophon, so nobody involved in making this copy is named. The author's name appears in two forms: 'śrīśrīdatta-' (honorific śrī + Śrīdatta) at fol. 115r9, and 'śrīpadatta-' at fol. 115r5–6, which is probably a miscopy of the same name. He is identified as the Maithila Śrīdatta Upādhyāya (c. 13th–14th century). 'Upādhyāya' is not written in the colophon, so it is not entered under titles.
review: Added Śrīdatta as author (role 'author'). 'śrīdattapaddhatau' means 'in Śrīdatta's paddhati'; this is the Maithila Śrīdatta Upādhyāya, author of the Ekāgni(dāna)paddhati. So the name is an authorship attribution, not merely a word inside a title.
Everything else confirmed: there is no scribe, date, place or purpose.

title: Kheṭapīṭha
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Tuesday 11 Jun 1867, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīvasiṣṭādivākyānusārālasadvāsanāṃ kheṭasatpīṭhamālāṃ | cakārāśrugoviṃda yo hekarādyair dvijai(!) nodito deva āpābhidhānaḥ 24 || (fol 7v7–8) || iti kheṭapīṭhaḥ samāptaḥ saṃvat 1924 jyeṣṭa śukla 10 bhaume | lam vyāsādīnā nāthena śubhaṃ || (fol. 7v13)
notes: The author verse is corrupt. A likely reading is 'cakārāśu govinda-[...]-ādyair dvijair nodito devāpābhidhānaḥ': '[the one] named Āpā(deva) quickly composed [this], urged by Govinda and other brahmins'. 'yohekara' may hide a second name or a surname, so Govinda's role is uncertain. The author's name could be Āpā, Āpādeva, or Devāpā. 'lam' is probably an abbreviation of likhitam. The scribe's name is written 'vyāsādīnā nāthena', probably Vyāsa Dīnanātha/Dīnānātha. The colophon does not name the era. VS is assumed from the Devanagari script and the year 1924, giving about 1867 CE. If the year were ŚS, it would be about 2002 CE, which is impossible. The weekday was not checked.
review: The first reading made Goviṃda the author. In the verse ('cakārāśu ... dvijair nodito deva āpābhidhānaḥ'), the subject of cakāra is the one 'named Āpā', who wrote at the urging of brahmins (dvijair nodito). The author is therefore Āpā/Āpādeva (added as p1, role author). Govinda is one of the brahmins who urged him (p2, role other).
Govinda's name is now the IAST stem 'Govinda', not 'Goviṃda'. Confidence lowered because the string 'goviṃda yo hekarādyair' is corrupt.
Scribe's name normalised to Dīnanātha (as written: 'vyāsādīnā nāthena'), with Vyāsa kept as a title/surname. Confidence lowered to medium because the word division is corrupt.
Added a 'wrote at the urging of' relation (type other) from the author to Govinda.
Notes: the era of 'saṃvat' is not stated. VS is assumed (1924 VS ≈ 1867 CE).

title: Gaṇeśacaturthīpūjāvidhi
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_raw: śāke 1806 saṃvat 1942 sāle miti bhādrasudirarojaha śubham
date_note: = Sep 1885, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti bhaviṣyottarapurāṇe siddhivināyakapūjāvidhi(!) samāptaṃ śubham || || śāke 1806 saṃvat 1942 sāle miti bhādrasudirarojaha śubham likhitaṃ ciraṃjīviśarmaṇā ||❁ || || || || || || || || || || (fol. 12v2–3)
notes: The colophon gives two eras. VS 1942 − 57 = 1885 CE, so Bhādra śukla falls in about August–September 1885. Śaka 1806 + 78 = 1884, which is one year earlier: Śaka 1807 is the year that matches VS 1942. A one-year slip like this is common, for example when an expired year is confused with a current one. VS is taken as the main era. 'bhādrasudirarojaha' is probably garbled. 'roja' is Nepali for 'day', so the 'ra' may be a misread numeral (tithi) or an abbreviated weekday. This text is the Siddhivināyaka/Gaṇeśa caturthī pūjā, so the date may well be Bhādra śukla 4 (Gaṇeśacaturthī), but the text does not confirm this. The weekday was left blank.
review: Weekday 'rarojaha' removed: 'roja(ha)' is the Nepali word for 'day'. Reading 'ra' as ravi (Sunday) is only a guess. Weekday and tithi are now blank and the possibilities are explained in notes
Date as_written now includes 'śubham', as in the colophon
Notes: added the one-year mismatch between Śaka 1806 and VS 1942, with an explanation

The catalogue fields are empty.

title: Tvaritarudrajapavidhi
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Sunday 23 Jul 1797, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti rudrajapavidhiḥ || śake 1719 piṃgalānāmasaṃvatsare śrāvaṇaṃ vaya 14 taddinīdevopanāmakagopālabhaṭṭātmajaśrīpatine(!) lekhitaṃ || svārthaṃ paropakārārthaṃ ca || bāṇabhaṭṭajām akhaṇḍakarasya dattaṃ || (fol. 9r3–7)
purpose: svārthaṃ paropakārārthaṃ ca (for himself and for others); afterwards given to Akhaṇḍakara
notes: The catalogue names Akhaṇḍakara as the scribe. The colophon, however, says the copy was written (lekhitaṃ) by Śrīpati, son of Gopālabhaṭṭa of the Deva family, and then given (dattaṃ) to Akhaṇḍakara. So the catalogue's scribe field looks wrong. 'śrīpatine(!)' stands for the instrumental śrīpatinā. 'taddinī' = taddine. 'vaya' = vadi/vadya (kṛṣṇa pakṣa). 'bāṇabhaṭṭajām' is unclear. It may mean 'son of Bāṇabhaṭṭa' (-ja + stray m) or be an abbreviated jāmātre ('to the son-in-law of Bāṇabhaṭṭa'), so the son_of relation is uncertain. It is also unclear whether the upanāma Deva qualifies only Gopāla or the whole family; it is assigned to both. Date check: Śaka 1719 = 1797 CE. Piṅgala is year 51 of the 60-year cycle ((1719+12) mod 60 = 51), so the saṃvatsara name agrees with the year.
review: Śrīpati: role changed from commissioner to scribe (+owner, donor). 'śrīpatine(!) lekhitaṃ' is a corrupted instrumental (for śrīpatinā), so it means 'written by Śrīpati'. The scribe's svārtham makes him the owner, and 'dattaṃ' makes him the giver.
Gopālabhaṭṭa normalized to Gopāla with title bhaṭṭa. Bāṇabhaṭṭa normalized to Bāṇa with title bhaṭṭa.
Upanāma Deva recorded in the titles of Gopāla and Śrīpati (family surname).
Akhaṇḍakara kept as recipient (owner, beneficiary). His relation to Bāṇa is kept as son_of but flagged as uncertain, because 'bāṇabhaṭṭajām' is unclear (-ja 'son' or a truncated jāmātṛ 'son-in-law').
Added relation: Śrīpati wrote_for Akhaṇḍakara (gave the copy to him).
Purpose and notes expanded. The saṃvatsara name has been checked and agrees with the year.

subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_raw: śāke 1733 māse vaiśāṣadinagae 17 ādityavāsare śuklapakṣe tithu || citrabhānunāmasaṃvatsa[re]
date_note: = Apr 1811, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: svastiśrīśāke 1733 māse vaiśāṣadinagae 17 ādityavāsare śuklapakṣe tithu || citrabhānunāmasaṃvatsa[re] maye(!) likhitaṃ daśakarmmarāmapaddhatipustakaṃ likhitaṃ nakurājye tāhnugrāme brahmasthāne li(!) upādhyāyaḥ śūbhaṃ || śūbhaṃ śubhaṃ bhūyāt yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭā tādṛśa[ṃ] li[khi]taṃ mayā || yadi śūddaṃ aśuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo nadi(!)yate || (fol. 190v6–11)
notes: The scribe is anonymous. The colophon reads 'li(!) upādhyāyaḥ', probably 'likhitam upādhyāyena' ('written by the Upādhyāya'), and also uses 'mayā'. The phrase 'daśakarmmarāmapaddhati' could hide a personal name (Rāma, as author or owner?). More likely it is part of the title, so no person record was made for it. Date: Śaka 1733 + 78 = 1811 CE. 'Dinagate 17' is the 17th solar day of Vaiśākha, so roughly late April 1811. 'Tithu' has no number, so the tithi is not given. 'Citrabhānu' is the name of the 60-year Jovian saṃvatsara. Under the southern (luni-solar) reckoning, Śaka 1733 would be Prajāpati, not Citrabhānu. Under the northern (Bṛhaspati) reckoning, about 11 years ahead, it would be Citrabhānu. So the name fits if the northern reckoning is used, and the era is consistent. Place: 'nakurājye' is unclear. It may be a corruption, e.g. of a local rājya name, possibly 'Tanahũ-rājya'. 'Tāhnugrāma' may be Tanahun (Tanahũ) in central Nepal, but this is uncertain, so the place is not normalized. 'Brahmasthāne' = at the Brahmin settlement or temple site.
review: p1: 'Upādhyāya' is a title, not a personal name. Name left empty; upādhyāya kept in titles only.
p1: residence cleared. The colophon gives the place of copying, not the scribe's home; the place stays under 'place'.
p1: evidence shortened and confidence raised to medium. The person is clearly the anonymous scribe; only the name is missing.
date: 'dinagate 17' is a solar day count (17th day of Vaiśākha), not a tithi. Tithi left empty, and this is explained in notes.
date: 'Citrabhānu' is the name of the Jovian year (saṃvatsara), not a nakṣatra or yoga. Removed from nakshatra_yoga and discussed in notes.
date: month normalized to 'Vaiśākha', paksa to 'śukla' and weekday to 'Sunday (ādityavāra)'.
notes expanded: the place reading, the possible personal name 'Rāma' in the title, and the saṃvatsara check.

The phrase 'sahasi māsike caturthīsaṃjñakatithau some saṃkaṣṭanāśanaṃ' says when the vow is kept (caturthī in the month Sahas/Mārgaśīrṣa, on a Monday). It is not the copying date. The prefix 'bhīmapuropa' before Rāmagovinda probably reads Bhīmapure + upa(nāmaka), 'surnamed Bhīmapure', which looks like a Marāṭhī-type family name. It could instead mean origin from a place called Bhīmapura. Either way it is not stated as the place of copying, so residence and place are left empty. The catalogue gives the scribe as Sarvottama Bhaṭṭa; the colophon attaches bhaṭṭa explicitly only to the father, and the title is inferred for the son.
review: Place of copying set to empty: the colophon does not say where the copy was made. 'bhīmapuropa-' is part of the scribe's family description.
Residence 'Bhīmapura' removed from both persons. 'bhīmapuropa' most likely means Bhīmapure + upa(nāmaka), 'surnamed Bhīmapure'; see notes.
Added 'owner' to Sarvottama's roles because of 'svārthaṃ' (for himself), as well as for others.
Confirmed ce_approx 1703: VS 1760 − 57 = 1703 and ŚS 1625 + 78 = 1703, so the eras agree.
Confirmed weekday stays empty: 'sahasi māsike caturthīsaṃjñakatithau some' describes when the vow is kept, not the date of copying.

notes: The colophon says only 'saṃvat'. VS is assumed because the script is Devanagari and the owner appears to be from a Maharashtrian brahmin family (Pāṭhaka, Kārkheḍakara). title: Saundaryalaharī
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Friday 27 Sep 1776, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīmacchaṃkarācāryaviracitaṃ sauṃdaryyalaharīstotraṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ jagyanāthayoḥ (!) śubhaṃ bhūyāt || ❁ ❁ ❁ śubhasujñaijñativiracitam itidīdaṃ vilikhitaṃ sadbhūtajñānaṃ bhavajalanimagnoddharaṇakaṃ murāre pāṭhārthaṃ girir iti sunāmnaḥ stavanakaṃ sukhaṃ gopālenāvataritamahāśaṃkarakṣataṃ 1 viśvesarāya namaḥ saṃvat 1833 samaya nāma bhādramāse site pakṣe pūrṇavāśyāyāṃ bhṛguvāsare jagyanāthena vipreṇa pū(!)stakaṃ likhitaṃ śubham dhe(!)yaṃ sadā paribhavagnam abhi(!)ṣṭadohaṃ tīrthāspadaṃ śivaviraṃcinutaṃ saraṇyaṃ | bhṛtyātmahaṃ praṇatapāla bhavābdhipotaṃ vaṃde mahāpurukha(!) te caraṇāraviṃdaṃ 1 ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ (fol. 12v5–13r3)
notes: The scribe's name 'jagyanātha' is a phonetic spelling of Yajñanātha. It also appears as 'jagyanāthayoḥ (!) śubhaṃ bhūyāt', a dual genitive that makes no grammatical sense. The stanza before the date is badly corrupt and has metrical errors. 'śubhasujñaijñativiracitam' may hide a name, possibly the scribe's (Yajña-?), but this is not certain. The stanza seems to say the copy was written for the reading of Murāri, whose proper name is given as '... Giri' (perhaps Murārigiri, a Daśanāmī ascetic). 'gopālenāvataritamahāśaṃkarakṣataṃ' names a Gopāla in an unclear role: he might be a co-copyist or the one who transmitted the text. There is no explicit wording saying he commissioned the copy, so his role is set to 'other'. 'samaya nāma' after the year is unexplained; it may be a corrupt saṃvatsara name. The date is taken as Vikrama era (VS) because VS 1833 fits Devanagari paper manuscripts and matches the catalogue: Bhādra śukla pūrṇimā, Friday, which is about Aug/Sept 1776 CE. The weekday has not been checked. The closing stanza is from Bhāgavatapurāṇa 11.5 and has nothing to do with who produced the copy.

subject: Bauddhasūtra

colophon: āryā mahāpratisarāyā mahāvidyārājñāḥ prathamaḥ kalpaḥ samāptaḥ || ❁ || athāto vidyādharasyāryarakṣāvidhānakalpaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi sarvasatvānukampayā | yena rakṣāvidhānena mahāsiddhi bhaviṣyati | (fol. 18v1) āryamahāpratisarāyāṃ mahāvidyārājñī samāptam || ○ || ye dharmmā hetuprabhāvā(!) hetu ⟪prasā⟫ teṣāṃ tathāgato hy avat(!) teṣāṃs(!) tathāgato yo niyodha(!) evaṃvādī mahāsravaṇaḥ || ○ || ❖ namo bhagavatyai āryamahāsāhasrapramarddanyai || (fol. 22v4-23v1) || ❁ || mahāsāhasrapramadanī(!)nāma mahāyānasūtraṃ samāptam || e(!) dharma(!) hetuprabhavā hetu(!) teṣāṃ tathāgato hy avat(!) teṣā(!) ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśrāvana || ○ || śubham astu || ❁ || ❖ namo buddhāya | namo dharmmāya | namaḥ saṅghāya || namaḥ saptānāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ sasrāvakasaṃghānāṃ namo (āke)(?) arhatānāṃ(!) namo maitreyapramukhānāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ namo anāgāmināṃ namas sakṛdāsināṃ namaḥ srotaāpannānā namo lokasamyagnatā⟪tā⟫nā namaḥ samyakpratipannānām || teṣān namas kṛtvā imāṃ ma+māyūrī vidyārājñī pramocayāmi | sā me vidyā sam(ṛ)ddhyantu sṛṇvantu me bhūtagaṇā ye ke cit pṛthithivī(!)carāḥ | khecarāḥ jalacarāḥ | devāḥ nāgāḥ asurāḥ | marutāḥ garuḍāḥ gandharvāḥ kinnarāḥ mahoragāḥ | yakṣāḥ | rā⟪kṣasā⟩⟩kṣasāḥ || pretāḥ pisācāḥ bhūtāḥ kumbhāṇḍāḥ pūtanāḥ kaṭapūtanāḥ skandhāḥ unmādāḥ chāyāḥ | apanmārāḥ ostārakāḥ sṛṇvantu me | ojohārāḥ bhūtagaṇāḥ gabhāhārāḥ | rudhirāhārāḥ | vasāhārāḥ | mānsāhārāḥ medāhārāḥ | majjāhārāḥ | jātāhārāḥ | jīvitāhārāḥ | balyāhārāḥ | gandhāhārāḥ | puṣpāhārāḥ | pūpāhārāḥ | phalāhārāḥ | sasyāhārā
purpose: for the complete prosperity (sarvasampati) of the dānapati Ḍhoṣṇanaka and his wife Jyantanalakṣmī
notes: The colophon writes the king as 'jagatsthitirājamalla'. This is a corruption of Jayasthitirājamalla (Jayasthiti Malla, r. c. NS 502–515 / 1382–1395 CE), which fits NS 507. The catalogue gives him as 'Sthitimalla'. The phrase 'vijasya vijarājasmaye' is a corrupt form of vijayarājye/samaye. The place, 'haṭhakhāchyaṃ vikraṇichyaṃ gṛhanāmadheyam', is literally the name of a house (Newari chẽ, 'house'). It most likely names the donor's house, which may also be where the copy was made; the locality is not identified. The '-ka' at the end of both lay names (Ḍhoṣṇanaka-sya, Jyantanalakṣmī-ka-sya) may be a suffix: Ḍhoṣṇana and Jyantalakṣmī/Jayantalakṣmī are possible readings. 'vajrārya' stands for vajrācārya. The colophon has no causative verb for having the copy made, so the dānapati is recorded as donor and beneficiary only. The date is NS 507 Kārttika śukla 1, Wednesday, Viśākhā nakṣatra, Śobhana yoga, which is October/November 1386 CE. Viśākhā is a plausible nakṣatra for Kārttika śukla 1, but the weekday has not been computed.
review: King's name corrected to Jayasthitirājamalladeva: the colophon's 'jagatsthiti-' is a corruption of Jaya-, the king who reigned c. NS 502–515. Confidence lowered to medium.

Ḍhoṣṇanaka: dropped 'commissioner' because no causative verb (likhāpitam etc.) appears; kept 'donor' (dānapati) and added 'beneficiary' (sarvasampatihetunārthaṃ). Confidence lowered to medium because the name is odd and the '-ka' may be a suffix.
Jyantanalakṣmī: dropped 'donor' and 'relative_only' and gave her 'beneficiary', since she is named only as the dānapati's wife and the merit is for both of them. Confidence medium.
Added the relation Ḍhoṣṇanaka under_reign_of the king.
Notes expanded: the king's name corruption, the reading of the place as the donor's house, the -ka endings and the date check.

notes: Era not stated, but taken as NS: the catalogue says so, and Vijayakāmadeva's reign (c. NS 312) fits. Month and pakṣa are partly restored (vai⁅śā⁆〇⁅kla⁆). 'bhallāka' is the title bhalloka (later bhāro); the catalogue writes 'Lakṣmīpālavarmabhalloka'. 'prasiddhanāma śrī (buauvarman)' gives the donor's popular name. The cataloguer marked the reading as uncertain; it could be something like Bubuvarman. It is not counted as a separate person. No scribe is named.
review: p2: name normalized to 'Lakṣmīpālavarman'; 'bhallāka' (= bhalloka, later bhāro, an honorific/office title) moved to titles
p3 '(buauvarman)' removed as a separate person: 'prasiddhanāma' introduces the popular name of the donor himself, so it is an alias of p2 and is now recorded in notes
weekday normalized to Thursday (bṛhaspatidina)

title: Gajendropākhyānabhāṣā
subject: Stotra
date_note: ≈ 1849 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti śrībhāgavate mahāpurāṇe aṣṭamaskandhe gajendropākhyāne caturtho dhyāyaḥ 4 || || śrīśāke vidhuśailameghabhuvi yad rājendrabhūmaṇḍale nepālendrapade bhṛtau harasutaprakhyas tithau lekhitam (fol. 22r5–7)
notes: Chronogram: vidhu (1) śaila (7) megha (?) bhū (1). 'Megha' is not a standard number-word; it is taken as 7 only to match the catalogue's ŚS 1771, so the year is uncertain. ŚS 1771 = ca. 1849 CE. That is after King Rājendra Vikrama Śāha was deposed (1847 CE, succeeded by Surendra). Either the scribe still named the old king, or 'megha' should be read differently. 'Bhṛtau' is probably a corruption of 'bhṛgau' (Friday). 'Harasutaprakhya tithi' is probably caturthī (Gaṇeśa); ṣaṣṭhī (Skanda) is also possible. Month and pakṣa are not given. No scribe, commissioner or place is named.
review: Weekday added: 'bhṛtau' is probably a corruption of 'bhṛgau' (bhṛguvāra), which would make it Friday.
Tithi changed to caturthī (4th). 'Harasuta' (son of Hara) here most likely means Gaṇeśa, whose tithi is caturthī. 'Harasutaprakhya' is not a name.

Chronogram check: vidhu=1, śaila=7, bhū=1. 'Megha' is not a standard number-word and is taken as 7 only to match the catalogue's 1771. Read right to left this gives 1771; because the figure reads the same both ways, the reading direction does not matter.
King's confidence lowered to medium. Rājendra Vikrama Śāha was deposed in 1847 CE, so ŚS 1771 (1849 CE) falls after his reign. This is now stated in the notes.
'Nepālendra' kept as an epithet/title. The note's guess that the tithi phrase might hide a person's name has been dropped.

notes: The colophon names no scribe, commissioner, owner or patron. The era isn't stated in the text. Reading the year as VS fits the catalogue field and the Nepali wording ('sāla miti ... roja'). VS 1939 Jyeṣṭha śukla 6 falls around 23 May 1882, which was a Tuesday, so it agrees with 'roja 3'. After the date the scribe added two corrupt subhāṣita stanzas ('dhanyās te vītarāgāḥ ...'), of the kind attributed to Bhartṛhari's śatakas. Neither stanza contains a personal name. 'vighnaṃ vināsanāye namaḥ' is an invocation.

title: #Stotrasaṅgraha
subject: Stotra
colophon: iti śrīskandhapurānya vihnunnārāyaṇāya samāpta || śubham astu || jādṛṣṭaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛṣṭaṃ likhitaṃ mayā jadda śuddha asudhaṃ vā mama doṣo na diyate || thva sarasvati devayā śirokaḥ thava gvaṃ stikadhanikarmmācājyayāke kāyāvaḥ devyandrakarmmācājyena thava āṣalasena vavamacāto śenayātā hleyā julo śubha || ❖ || (exp. 50b3–7)
notes: The Newari note says roughly: 'this Sarasvatī-deva hymn (śirokaḥ = ślokaḥ), taken from [Gvaṃ]stikadhani Karmācārya, was written by Devendra Karmācārya in his own hand (thava āṣalasena) to teach the children (macā … śenayātā)'. 'vava' may be a corruption of 'thava' ('own'), giving 'his own children'. p2 only supplied the exemplar. The name is corrupt: 'gvaṃ stikadhani' could also split as a place or epithet 'Gvaṃ' plus the name 'Stikadhani', or hide some other form. The end title ('śrīskandhapurānya vihnunnārāyaṇāya', i.e. a Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa piece from the Skandapurāṇa) does not match the Newari note's 'sarasvati devayā śirokaḥ'. This is probably because the manuscript is a Stotrasaṅgraha and the note covers the whole collection or one hymn in it. The colophon is undated.

title: Āhnikatattva
subject: Dharmaśāstra
date_raw: sūcahāṣṭa varṣeṣu cāravān asite phaṇi | tatra bhadrā
colophon: iti vajraghaṭīha /// ryyātma mahāmahopādhyāya śrīragh⌠u⌡nandanabhaṭṭācāryyaviracitam āhnika⌠ta⌡ttvaṃ samāptaṃ || ❖ || yādṛṣṭā pusṭakaṃ dṛ.. .. .. .. .. .. likhitaṃ mayā jadi śuddham aśuddhaṃ vā mama doṣa na dīyateḥ || || sūcahāṣṭa varṣeṣu cāravān asite phaṇi | tatra bhadrā ... kulānandena lekhitaṃ || ❖ || ❖ || ❖ || śubham astu || (fol. 98v1–3)
notes: The date verse is corrupt. 'sūcahāṣṭa' may be a word-numeral chronogram read right to left, e.g. sū(nya)=0, ca(ndra)=1, aṣṭa=8, giving 810. If the era is NS, that would be c. 1690 CE. This fits a Newari-script copy of Raghunandana, who wrote in the 16th century, but the reading is speculative, so ce_approx is left empty. 'cāravān' is unidentified: it may be a garbled month name or weekday (vāra). 'asite' = dark fortnight. 'phaṇi' (snake) = 8 by bhūtasaṃkhyā convention; the Nāgapañcamī association (5) is less likely in a numeral context. 'Bhadrā' is the karaṇa Viṣṭi. The colophon line 'vajraghaṭīha ///ryyātma' is damaged and probably held the author's family and lineage epithets. Kulānanda is taken as scribe: 'lekhitaṃ' is used loosely in Nepalese colophons, and the 'likhitaṃ mayā' verse supports scribal agency.
review: Tithi: 'phaṇi' as a word-numeral stands for nāga/sarpa = 8 (aṣṭamī), not 5. Changed to '8 (phaṇi), uncertain'.
nakshatra_yoga: bhadrā is the karaṇa Viṣṭi (Bhadrā), not a nakṣatra. Labelled as a karaṇa.
Month: 'cāravān' cannot be identified as a month name. Marked as unidentified; it may be a corrupt month or weekday.
Notes: added a tentative decoding of the year chronogram; the commissioner doubt is resolved in favour of scribe because of the 'likhitaṃ mayā' verse.

colophon: mātā sā pārvatī sā janaka iti mataḥ śrīghanaśyāmadevo deśas tā kammaśailaḥ kṣitijasurataroḥ śrī[ma]laivammasaṃjñā yasya prajvālakaḥ śrī dvijakulasujani premanidhyāhūyoyaṃ prāyaś cittapradīpe tata udita/// ṣaṣṭhaḥ prakāśaḥ || || subhadrākhyā mātā śikhari vanakhāṃcī nagapatiḥ pitā yasyāḥ karṇād api ca dalasāhaḥ parataraḥ | malaivammaḥ svāmī kṣitipatirumeśorcyacaraṇāś cakāraiṣā graṃthaṃ hi mahalavasaṃtābhidhaṃ /// mā || śrīmanmalaivammanṛpātmajeṣu kanīyasā svīyaguṇair garīyasāḥ | ramenāmallena nijaprasūpitṛprakīrttayedīyakṛtipracāritā || yasyodyotamatī satī guṇavatī /// tomāpatir nāmapremanidhīpaṃthaṃ ta (exp. 418t2–8) kulabhūḥ kūrmmācalo janmabhūḥ bhūpālakṛtajāpyajā /// sīvam || soyaṃ tvālakabhāvabhayātaraha graṃthaṃ yadīyasya tu || || rājārājñī dvijoyaṃ natirapi sabhā .. .. .. .. .. guruś ca .. varaṃ || .. .. .. .. dhayaghaṭito niṣyadoṣye ṣamūkaḥ || vācālaḥ paṇḍitānāṃ sadasi trikāladhī harṣada .. .. .. vijayaś cittapradīpo bhuvi jayatutarāṃ kopyapūrvo hi putraḥ || || śāke vedaśararttubhūparigate māse .. .. site pakṣe rāmatithau guroś ca divase mātaḥ prapūrttiṃ gataḥ gaṃḍakyāḥ savidhe hi dānapadataḥ khyāte tu deśe vare /// yāvaśādamalatāṃ graṃthe samāga .. .. .. || iti śrīgaganagirirājacakracūḍāmaṇi/// di vividhavirudāvalīvirājamānamānonnataśrīmahādhirājamalaivammakṛtaḥ prāyaścitta /// pa saṃpūrṇaḥ || || saṃvat 1855 miti .. .. .. śudī 5 śata 1205 || || ❖ || || ❖ || ❖ || || (exp. 418t2–8)
notes: The colophon contains two dates: the text composition date in Śāka 1654 (veda-śara-ṛtu-bhū = 1654, approx. 1732 CE) on Gandaki river, and the manuscript copying date VS 1855 (approx. 1798 CE). Premanidhi Pantha composed the Prāyaścittapradīpa under King Malaivamma of Parbat (Kammaśaila/Gaganagiri). King Malaivamma's unnamed queen was the daughter of King Dalasāha of Khāñcī and Subhadrā. Malaivamma's younger son Ramenāmalla popularized or patronized the work. 'śata 1205' designates the grantha count (1205 slokas).

title: Yājñavalkyasmṛti and Ṛjumitākṣarā
subject: Dharmaśāstra
colophon: iti śrībhāradvājapadmanābhabhaṭṭopādhyāyātmajasya śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakaśrīviñāneśvarabhaṭṭakasya kṛtā(!) ṛjumitākṣarāyāṃ yājñavalkyadharmaśāstravivṛttau tṛtīyaḥ prāyaścittaprapaṃcādhyāyaḥ samāptāḥ | ❁ || || (266v3–5) || saṃvat 2825 phālgunakṛṣṇaṣaṣṭīravivāre liṣikṛtaṃ brāhmaṇabālūprakaraṇājñātībhūṇakṛṣṇalalāṭamadhye | śubhaṃ bhavatu || || kalyāṇam astu || || śrīr astu || || śrīkṛṣṇo vijayati || || śrī[ḥ] || (267v7–8)
notes: The colophon reads 'saṃvat 2825', which is clearly a slip for VS 1825. The catalogue field says SAM 1825, which agrees. VS 1825 − 57 = 1768 CE, but Phālguna of that year would fall in Feb/Mar 1769 CE. The scribal phrase 'brāhmaṇabālūprakaraṇājñātībhūṇakṛṣṇalalāṭamadhye' is badly garbled. The best guess is a brahmin named Bālū as scribe. Other readings are possible: 'Bālū' might be part of a longer name (e.g. Bālūpra-…), 'jñātī' may mean caste/kin group, and '…kṛṣṇalalāṭamadhye' may name a place of copying, but none of this can be identified with confidence. Vijñāneśvara's father, Padmanābha (Bhāradvāja gotra), is named only in the author's colophon and has nothing to do with this copy.

subject: Dharmaśāstra

colophon: iti śrīmatpadavākyapramāṇapārāvārapārīṇadhurīṇamīmāṃsādvaitasāmrājya-dhuraṃdharabhaṭṭaśaṃkarātmajabhaṭṭadāmodaronnītaṃ kaliyuganiṣedhyaniṣedhakavākyavivaraṇaṃ samāptaṃ śubham || || śāke ʼṣṭanaṃdasaptaike nabhasyaikadine gate || alikhad giridharnāmā kṣityāṃ vai narabhūpake || 1 || kā(lo)tattve || mokṣārthī raktavastre ca bhogārthī śvetavāsasī(!) || māraṇe kṛṣṇavāsas tu vaśye raktaṃ sadā vaśet || uccāṭe vyāghracarmaṇi vṛkṣatvak staṃbhakarmaṇi || paridhāya tato maṃtrī yāgabhūmiṃ samāviśet || || kulārṇave || puṇyakṣetre nadītīre mahāparvatamastake || tīrthapradeśe siṃdhūnāṃ saṃgame pāvane vane || udyānāni vicitrāṇi vilamūle taṭe gireḥ || devatāyatane kūle samudrasya nije gṛhe || sādhakānāṃ praśastāni sthānāny etāni maṃtriṇāṃ || (fol. 7r6–10)
notes: The chronogram aṣṭa(8)-nanda(9)-sapta(7)-eka(1), read right to left, gives Śaka 1798 = 1876 CE, which matches the catalogue. Nabhasya is Bhādrapada. 'ekadine gate' (one day having passed) is ambiguous: it could be the 1st (solar) day of the month or the day after it. No pakṣa is given. 'giridharnāmā' is a corrupt form of Giridhara-nāmā. 'kṣityāṃ vai narabhūpake' is probably a generic reference to the ruling king, not a name, so no king is recorded. The verses after the colophon (from the Kālottara and Kulārṇava) are unrelated extracts written into the same manuscript, and they name no people.

title: Kātantradhātuvṛtti
subject: Vyākaraṇa
date_note: ≈ 1546 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: vasūrasabhuvanagaṇite śāke dharmmadravīti rekātaṃtradhātuvṛttiṃ nirmitevān ramānāthaḥ || na vyabhāṣata mimanoramāyāṃtīdamīdṛśaṃ nāvamarṇamanuvarṇamīśatāṃ || sadhavaḥ kim iti saṃśrayād vidviṣaṃti śatapaurvāmauktikaṃ || || iti vedagarbhatarkācāryān navāpi kulaprasūtaśrīramānāthaśarmanirmmitāyāṃ kātaṃtradhātuvṛttau curādivivaraṇaṃ samāptaṃ || ❖ || śubham || ❖ || (fol. 133r5–9)
notes: This is the author's colophon, not a scribal one. The date, Śaka 1468 (about 1546 CE), is when Ramānātha composed the text; this manuscript is not dated, and no scribe or owner is named. The year comes from the chronogram read right to left: vasu = 8, rasa = 6, bhuvana = 14, giving 1468. If bhuvana is taken as 3, the year would be 368, which is not plausible. 'navāpi kulaprasūta' is probably a corruption of 'anvavāya/anvaye kulaprasūta', meaning 'born in the family line of Vedagarbha Tarkācārya'. That makes Vedagarbha an ancestor, though the exact relation is unclear. The phrase 'dharmmadravīti re' is corrupt; it may hide a name or epithet, but it cannot be read with confidence. The verse after it is also corrupt.

title: Kātantravistara
subject: Vyākaraṇa

notes: 'karṇadevopādhyāya' is most naturally read as an epithet of Vardhamāna ('teacher of Karṇadeva', probably a king). The end of the colophon has only invocations (śāradāyai namaḥ; bhavānyai prītir astu) and a corrupt formula 'kṛtohaṃ yas teno bhūyāḥ'. The copy names no scribe, owner, date or place. Moved the title 'upādhyāya' from Karṇadeva to Vardhamāna.
Karṇadeva: role changed from relative_only to other (a king or patron the author taught; not the reigning king of this copy), confidence set to low.
Replaced the son_of relation with Karṇadeva pupil_of Vardhamāna (medium).
Purpose cleared: 'bhavānyai prītir astu' is a blessing, not a statement of why the copy was made. It is now recorded in notes.

title: Viṣṇupūjākalpalatā
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: = Friday 12 Jan 1596, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: śrīmadbhairavasiṃhasya tīrabhuktimahībhṛtaḥ | bhūyā(!) kalpavatī viṣṇupūjākalpalatākṛtiḥ || iti samastaprakriyāvirājamānamahārājādhirājaśrīnarasiṃhātmajasamastaprakriyopeta mahārājādhirāja śrīmaddhṛdayanārāyaṇānuja samastaprakriyālaṅkṛta mahārājādhirāja haricaraṇaparāyaṇa śrīmadbhairavasiṃhadevakṛtau śrīviṣṇupūjākalpalatā paripūrṇṇam iti || || śrījagajjyotirīśena viṣṇupūjāratātmanā | vinā purāṇavākyāni santoṣo naiva jāyate || viṣṇupūjakalparatā tasmāt tena likhāpitā | śake mate pakṣabāṇa titibhir lakṣate gate || dvādaśyā pauṣaśuklasya vinodo vyalikha cūtā | budhā vilokyatām śuddhāṃ yuktāḥ santu sadā mudā || || (fol. 114v4-115r4)
purpose: Copy commissioned by King Jagajjyoti, who was devoted to Viṣṇu worship and found no satisfaction without the words of the Purāṇas
notes: Chronogram: pakṣa (2), bāṇa (5), tithi (15). Read right to left this gives Śaka 1552 ('titibhir' = tithibhiḥ; 'lakṣate' is probably lakṣite). Śaka 1552 is 1630 CE; Pauṣa śukla 12 falls around Dec 1630 or Jan 1631. The colophon says Śaka explicitly. The catalogue's 'VS 1652' (= c. 1595 CE) conflicts with this: the cataloguer probably misread the era or the digits. 1595 also falls before the reign of Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur (r. c. 1614–1637), while Śaka 1552 falls within it. Jagajjyoti ('jagajjyotirīśa') is taken to be Jagajjyotirmalla, but the colophon gives no -malla and names no place, so the place field is left empty. 'vyalikha cūtā' is corrupt, perhaps for 'vyalikhac chubhām' or similar; the scribe's name Vinoda is clear. Bhairavasiṃha(deva) of Tīrabhukti is the author, the Oinavāra king of Mithilā. His father Narasiṃha and elder brother Hṛdayanārāyaṇa are named only in the author's praśasti, so they are not connected with this copy.
review: Chronogram checked: pakṣa 2, bāṇa 5, tithi 15, read right to left, gives Śaka 1552 (1630 CE); era and year kept
Purpose rewritten: 'viṣṇupūjā' was not a copying purpose. It is now the king's devotion to Viṣṇu worship as the motive for commissioning the copy
Notes expanded: the corrupt passages are discussed, the clash with the catalogue's VS 1652 is explained, and Jagajjyoti is identified as Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur (place of copying not stated)
Bhairavasiṃha's residence changed to empty and Tīrabhukti moved to affiliation: Tīrabhukti is his kingdom as author, not a stated residence
Evidence fields shortened
