title: Sārasvatavyākaraṇa
subject: Vyākaraṇa
date_note: = Friday 8 Jul 1763, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīparamahaṃsaparivrājakānubhūtisvarūpācāryaviracitāyā sārasvatīprakriyā samāptā || || ❁ || āṣāḍhakṛṣṇapakṣe caturarāsigate raviravaśuravigate samvat, samāptim agamas tadā || yātaḥ śrīupamanyuvaṃśatilakaḥ bhakto bhavāṇi priyaḥ | nāmnā śrībhavānidāsarabhavat, praddyotakirtti bhuvi | tatputro hi priyamvadaḥs tu parabhūt tadd hi kūre sādhavaḥ || jyāyān | vīro hi bhadro, tadanu hariḥ saṅkaro sarvvavettā | tattrātā śivapūrvvanāma hi abhūt jñāniḥ satāṃ sādhavaḥ || tatsunu jyatyavat kriyāparipūto, satsaṃpradāyakaviḥ || (fol. 241r6–241v6, exps. 242b–243t) … samvat 883 miti jyeṣṭhakṛṣna, tradasi, kuhnu āṣāḍhasya śrī vidyānaṃ dayā kabho cā bhāju nasya ṅā juroḥ || ❖ || ❖:(exp. 246b)
notes: The catalogue names Chatrasiṃha as scribe, but the name does not appear in the quoted colophon. The colophon has two dates. The verse date reads 'āṣāḍhakṛṣṇapakṣe caturarāsigate raviravaśuravigate samvat'. It is garbled: perhaps a corrupt chronogram, perhaps a weekday such as ravivāra, but it cannot be read. The prose date reads NS 883 jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa 13 (trayodaśī), followed by 'āṣāḍhasya'. The two month names do not conflict: kṛṣṇapakṣa āṣāḍha in the pūrṇimānta reckoning is the same fortnight as jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa in the amānta reckoning. NS 883 = c. 1763 CE (May–June). The verse is a genealogy of the Upamanyu lineage: Bhavānīdāsa; his son Priyaṃvada ('priyaṃvada' could also be an epithet, 'sweet-speaking', of an unnamed son); in that family the elder Vīrabhadra, then Hari(-)śaṅkara (one person or two); a brother whose name begins with Śiva ('tattrātā śivapūrvvanāma' = tadbhrātā); and his unnamed son ('tatsunu ... satsaṃpradāyakaviḥ'). That unnamed son is probably the scribe or the person behind this copy. The final Newari line ('vidyānaṃ dayā kabho cā bhāju nasya ṅā juroḥ') is corrupt. 'Vidyānandayā' looks like a genitive. 'nasya ṅā juro' might be nyāṅā julo ('was bought'), which would make this a sale or ownership note, but that is uncertain. Kabhocā could also be a place or a misreading. The roles of Vidyānanda and Kabhocā are therefore left as 'other'.

title: Taddhitakośa
subject: Vyākaraṇa
date_note: ≈ 1787 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: śāke vā saptatithibhir bhūyevājabahādure || prayogāḥ katicit proktā bhavadeve va taddhite || || iti bhavadevapaṇḍitakṛtastaddhitakoṣaḥ || || saṃvat 1844 || śubham astu maṃgalam astu rāma rāma rāma rāma rāma rāma rāma rāma (fol. 61v6–8)
notes: The opening verse is the author's statement of when the text was composed, not a statement about this copy. It reads 'śāke vā saptatithibhir bhūye vājabahādure', probably for '... bhūpe Bājabahādure' ('when Bājabahādura was king'). This is probably Baz Bahadur Chand of Kumaon (r. c. 1638–1678), so he is recorded with the role 'other', not as the reigning king of this copy. The Śāka chronogram is corrupt. One possible reading, right to left: 'vā' as a garbled word for 5 (bāṇa?), sapta = 7, tithi = 15, giving Śāka 1575 = c. 1653 CE. This is not certain. The copy date 'saṃvat 1844' gives no era; VS is assumed (c. 1787 CE). The catalogue's 'SAM 1695' (VS 1695 = c. 1638 CE) does not appear in the quoted colophon. It may come from the cataloguer's reading of the composition verse, and it conflicts with the copy date saṃvat 1844. The catalogue's place, Vārāṇasī, also does not appear in the colophon. No scribe or owner is named.
review: p2 (Vājabahādura): role changed from 'king' to 'other'. He is named in the author's verse about when the text was composed, not as the king reigning when this copy was made in saṃvat 1844. Confidence lowered to medium because the verse is corrupt.

'paṇḍitaikaśeṣaśeṣau' probably calls the two ancestors leading paṇḍits of the Śeṣa family, the well-known Banaras lineage. That reading is uncertain and may be corrupt. No scribe is named in the copying statement 'likhitam idaṃ kāśyām', so the copyist is unknown. The author may have written this copy himself, but the colophon does not say so. The year 'saṃvat 18' looks cut short, perhaps an abbreviated 18xx, probably VS since the copy was made in Kāśī; no CE date is given. 'roja 4' is read as Wednesday, counting Sunday as day 1. This matches the catalogue place (Kāśī, Cauleśvaraghaṭṭa).

colophon: iti śrīgorakṣaśatakaṃ yogaśāstraṃ sampūrṇaṃ || śubham || vaiśāṣe kṛṣṇapakṣe tu parvaṇi budhavāsare rajasthāne ca vāstavyaṃ likhitaṃ rāmaśarmaṇā || śrīsamvat 1756 || (fol. 26r2–6)
notes: The catalogue gives '(ŚS) 1756'. The colophon says only 'śrīsamvat', and the script is Devanagari with a North Indian context, so Vikrama Saṃvat is more likely: VS 1756 ≈ 1699 CE. If it were ŚS, the year would be ≈ 1834 CE. 'rajasthāne' (for rājasthāne) is read as the place where the scribe lived/copied, 'rajasthāne ca vāstavyaṃ' (the neuter 'vāstavyaṃ' should be 'vāstavyena', agreeing with rāmaśarmaṇā). It may mean 'at the royal seat/capital' rather than the region of Rajasthan, so the place is not normalized. The scribe's name is given as Rāma, with -śarman moved to titles under the stem-form rule ('Rāmaśarman' in full). 'parvaṇi' in the kṛṣṇapakṣa points to the new-moon day; the weekday has not been checked.
review: place.normalized cleared: 'rajasthāne' (= rājasthāne) may mean 'at the royal seat/capital' and need not be the modern region of Rajasthan, so the identification is not certain
date.tithi: noted that 'parvan' in the dark fortnight is presumably the amāvāsyā
notes expanded: the ambiguity of rājasthāna, and the era judgement (VS over the catalogue's ŚS)

colophon: iti śrīnityanāthasiddhaviracitāyāṃ siddhasiddhāntapaddhikāyāṃ piṇḍasamatir nāma tṛtīyopadeśaḥ || || samāpraś cāyaṃ granthaḥ || || ❁ || khaṣaṭ iṃdvātmake āke vibhavābdde ca phālgune || tithau pratipadi some hṛdayarāmo vyalīlikhat || || catvāro vihitā loke puruṣārthā svayaṃbhuvā kāraṇaṃ cānupūrveṇa yatteṣām antagodhikam || jñātvā pṛthvīpati rājā kāraṇaṃ mokṣasādhanam || sāṃkhyāpātañjalenoktaṃ yogaṃ saṃyuktavān svayaṃ || atas tasya vinodāya kiṃcid arthapradarśakam || likhitaṃ tuṣyatāṃ devau siddhidau dhanadau hi tau || || sītāpataye namaḥ || (fol. 18r1–8)
notes: The chronogram 'kha-ṣaṭ-indv-ātmake' yields only three digits (160), with 'āke' being an error for 'śāke'. King Pṛthvīpati is likely Pṛthvīpati Śāha of Gorkha (r. late 17th to early 18th century), which aligns with the jovian year Vibhava (Śaka 1610 = 1688 CE), suggesting a missing fourth digit.

title: Yogasūtra
subject: Yoga
date_note: = Thursday 17 Dec 1863, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: itiśrī(dhū)reśvaviracitāyāṃ pātañjalayogaśāstravṛttau kaivalyapādaś caturthaḥ 4 saṃvat 1920 li❁khā va||nā❁rasa ||mai śu❁bham || || miti mārga śudi 7 roja 5 śubham (exp. 30t7–30b2)
notes: The cataloguer's '(dhū)reśva' is almost certainly a mistake for 'dhāreśvara', the epithet of King Bhoja of Dhārā, author of the Rājamārtaṇḍa commentary on the Yogasūtra. He appears only as commentator, not as a person connected with this copy. No scribe, commissioner or owner is named. 'likhā vanārasa mai' is Hindi/Nepali for 'written in Banaras'. The era is not stated, but saṃvat 1920 with miti/roja fits VS, so the copy dates to Mārgaśīrṣa śukla 7, a Thursday, around November–December 1863 CE. The ❁ marks in the colophon are decorative.
review: Commentator identified: '(dhū)reśvaviracitāyāṃ' is a corruption of 'dhāreśvaraviracitāyāṃ'. Dhāreśvara ('lord of Dhārā') is the usual epithet of Bhoja, whose Yogasūtra commentary is the Rājamārtaṇḍa (a pātañjalayogaśāstravṛtti). Name changed from 'Dhūreśva' to 'Bhojadeva' and confidence raised to medium.
Weekday: 'roja 5' now glossed as Thursday.
Notes expanded.

notes: Only a 60-year Jovian year is given: Īśvara, the 11th year of the cycle. No era year appears, so the CE date can't be fixed. In the southern reckoning, Phālguna of Īśvara would fall in early 1818, 1878, 1938 and so on, 60 years apart. Devanagari script and the Jovian-year dating may point to a South Indian or Daśanāmī context. The scribal phrase 'hastākṣaraprahlādasarasvatīmahādevakara' is unclear. It most likely means 'handwriting of Prahlāda Sarasvatī', a Daśanāmī renunciant of the Sarasvatī order. 'mahādevakara' could be: part of the same person's name or an epithet; a second person, Mahādeva, possibly a co-writer; or 'kara' (hand) repeating 'hastākṣara'. For that reason Mahādeva is kept at low confidence with role 'other'. The catalogue fields are empty.

purpose: dharma (religious merit) of the commissioner; merit transferred so that all beings attain Sukhāvatī
notes: The catalogue gives the place of copying as Kathmandu. That is where the commissioner lived (yadesa kyalatora = Keltol, Kathmandu). The colophon itself says the copy was written in Lhasa, at Mudariṃgā ('hlāsa mudariṃgāsa coyā jula'), by a Mānandhar scribe from Kirtipur (kipudesa). This fits the Newar merchant communities in Lhasa. 'Jiodhanaṃ' is read as Jīvadhana. 'Cakanāsiṃ' is read as Cakanāsiṃha, though it could also be a Newari personal name such as Cakanā Siṃ. The book is called 'vasudhārādeviyā pustaka' (the book of the goddess Vasudhārā) and was made 'dharmmacesnā svacita' (out of religious intent, by his own wish). This may mean Cakanāsiṃha offered it as well as commissioning it, but the colophon does not say so explicitly, so the role is kept as commissioner only. Dates: Dillā = Āṣāḍha; NS 959 = 1839 CE.

title: Dattātreyataṃtra
subject: Vaiṣnavatantra
date_note: = Wednesday 17 Jul 1850, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti śrīdattātreyataṃtre īśvaradattātreyasaṃvāde prathamaḥ paṭalaḥ || 1 || (fol. 3v3–4) || iti śrīdattātreyataṃtre īśvaradattātreyasaṃvāde vyāghrādinivāraṇaṃ nāma dvāviṃśatitamaḥ paṭalaḥ || 22 || || śubham astu sarvadā || giryantarikṣāṃkasomair mite vikramavatsare || śuci māse tīladale durgāyāṃ bhaumavāsare || 1 || dattātreyyābhidhaṃ taṃtraṃ pārvatīpatinoditaṃ || viśvaharṣo ʼlikhad vaṃdyo padmādāsamude mudā || 2 || śubham || (fol. 59v1–5)
notes: Chronogram read right to left: giri 7, antarikṣa 0, aṅka 9, soma 1 = VS 1907 (about 1850 CE), which matches the catalogue. Śuci usually means Āṣāḍha. 'tīladale' is probably corrupt; the paksa (bright or dark half) cannot be settled. Durgā is taken as navamī (the 9th tithi); aṣṭamī is less likely. 'vaṃdyo' can be read as 'venerable', describing the scribe, or as the Bengali surname Vandya/Bandyopādhyāya; if it is a surname, it belongs among Viśvaharṣa's titles. The name Padmādāsa is cut out of the compound 'padmādāsamude' and is not certain.
review: p1: added a note that 'vaṃdyo' may be a surname (Vandya / Bandyopādhyāya) rather than the epithet 'venerable'. The name itself is unchanged.
p2: confidence lowered to medium; 'padmādāsamude' is a compound and the name boundary is not certain (it could be Padmādāsa or a feminine Padmā-based name).
date: month glossed as śuci = Āṣāḍha; tithi given as navamī (Durgā); weekday normalised to Tuesday; paksa left uncertain.
purpose: rewritten in plain English instead of the bare compound.

colophon: iti tatra buddhānāṃ buddhānubhāvena | devatānāṃ devatānubhāvena mahatī vyupaśānteti || mahārakṣāmahāmantrānusāriṇīnāmamahāyānasūtraṃ rakṣākalpaṃ samāptaḥ 〇 || ۞|| āryamahāpratisarā || ārya〇 mahāsāhasrapramarddanī || āryamahāmāyurī || āryamahāśītavatī || āryamahāmantrānusāriṇī ||〇 etāni pañcamahārakṣāsūtrāṇi parisamāpta〇m iti || ۞ || ye dharmmā hetuprabhāvā hetun(!) teṣān tathāgato hyavadat teṣā(!) ca yo niro〇dha evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ || ۞ || de〇ya[ṃ] dharmmo ʼyaṃ pravaramahāyānayāyinaḥ paramopāśaka-vajrācārjye(!) śrījayarāja-yad atra pūṇyaṃ tat bhavatv ācāryopādhyāya-mātāpitṛpūrvaṅgamaṃ kṛtvā sakalasatvarāśair anuttarajñānaphala-samyak saṃbodhipadaṃ prāpto ʼyam iti || ۞ || svasti śrīmatpaśupaticaranākamaladhuridhusaritasiroruha(!), śrīman mānyaśvābhīṣṭa devatābalarabdhaprasādadedipyamānamānonnata-ravikuratiraka-harumarddhajanepāreśvala(!) māhārājā〇 dhirājarājendrasakarajājacakrādhiśva〇la śrīśrījayabhāskalamallaparamabhaṭṭārakadevānāṃ sadā samalavijayināṃ(!) prabhuthākulasya(!)〇 vijayarājye || ۞|| dānapati[ḥ], kānti〇pulamāhānagare(!) makhanatvolake, śrīśrīśrīratnakī[r]timahāvihāra, duthurivi, otāche, grīhāvasthita-divaṃgata-vidhakapitā, vajrācārjye śrījasirāja | jaśirājasya putra vajrācārjye śrījayalathaṃ tasya bhājyā(!) mandharīlakṣmī, tasya prathamaputra, vajrācārye śrījayaratna dvitiyaputra vajrācārye śrījayadhana, tṛtiyaputra vajrācārye śrījayarāja tasya bhājyā ratnamuṇilakṣmī | jayadhanasya prathamaputra vajrācārye śrīdhanasiṃha || dhanasiṃhasya prathamaputra, vajrācārjy
notes: The catalogue lists Jasirāja as donor, but Jasirāja is the deceased grandfather; the commissioner is Jayarāja, who had the manuscript made while trading in Tibet (Trāsilumbu / Tashilhunpo). The scribe Ratnamunideva copied it at Suvarṇapraṇālī (or was resident at Hemavarṇamahāvihāra in Suvarṇapraṇālī).

title: Jayadrathayāmala, ṣaṭka IV
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti śrībhairavasrotasi vidyāpīṭhe śiracchede jayadrathayāmale mahātaṃtre caturviṃśati〇sāhasre caturthaṣaṭke mudrācadre (!) prathamaḥ paṭalaḥ || ○ || (fol. 5v4–5) iti bhairavaśrotasi vidyāpīṭhe śiracchede jayadrathayāmale mahātaṃtre caturviṃśatisāha〇sre caturthaṣaṭke rāviṇīcakre unmanodayakulāvatāraḥ paṭalaḥ || ❁ || (fol. 103v1–2) iti jayadrathe jīvapra〇tyānaghapurakṣobha unmodayaḥ (!) paṭalaḥ || ○ || (fol. 122r2) iti jayadrathayāmale caturviṃśatisāhasre caturthaṣaṭke rāviṇīcakre vidveṣakālipaṭalaḥ || ❁ || (fol. 124v1) etc. || samāpto yaṃ mudrāṣaṭkaṃ jayadrathāvatāraḥ || ○ || svasty astu ⟪sarvva⟫sarvvajagatāṃ cchidraṃ mā bhūt kva kiṃ cana | sā eva rakṣatu jagad eva devī karaṃkiṇīṃ || samāptaś ca paramarahasyaś caturviṃśatisahasraṃ sūtrarājajayadrathendraṃ || ○ || asima(!)sakalasāyujyayoginā vṛṃdavaṃditacaraṇayugalasya vividhavidyāvidyotitāṃtaḥkaraṇasya mahākāruṇikasya mahārājādhirājaśrimajjayacaṃdradevapūjitasya kulācāryaśrīdharaśivā(!)devanāmadheyasya śiṣyeṇa paṃḍitaśrījonadevena likhitam iti || śubham astu sarvvasatvānāṃ maṃgalamahāśrī (!) || ○ || (fol. 340r1–5)

subject: Śaivatantra
date_note: = Monday 24 Mar 1664, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti kulāmnāye mahātantre gastyamāhātmye prathamo bdaḥ || 1 || (fol. 4r5) iti nārāyaṇokte 'gastyavratamāhātmye dvitīyo bdaḥ || 2 || (fol. 6v7–7r1) iti rudrokte 'gastyamāhātmye pāpmākhyavadho nāma tṛtīyo bdaḥ || 3 || (fol. 9v5) iti kulārṇṇave mahātantre gastyamahātmye caturtho bdaḥ || 4 || (fol. 12r3) iti kulākulārṇṇave mahātantre gastyamāhātmye paṃcamo bdaḥ || 5 || (fol. 13v3–4) iti kulākulārṇṇave mahātantre gastyamahātmye ṣaṣṭho bdaḥ || 6 || (fol. 15r2) iti kulākulārṇṇave mahātantre gastyamāhātmye saptamo bdaḥ || 7 || (fol. 18v3) || iti kulālikāmnāye mahātantre gastyavratapaddhatiḥ samāptā || || pakṣāntarena karttavyaṃ, vratodyāpanam eva ca | āyurhānir yyaśohāni,r ity evaṃ manur abravīt || yadā saṃkramaṇaṃ prāpte, tṛtīyāditithau tadā | kuṃbhayoner vratasyāpi, kuryyād udyāpanaṃ śubhaṃ || pratipadi dvitīyāyāṃ, prāpte saṃkramaṇaṃ yadā | naiva kuryyāt tadā nūnaṃ, vratodyāpanam eva ca || || yāte bde śrutidantighoṭakamite māse 'site phālguṇe, govindasya tithau di[[ne]] śaśadhare svarggapradāṃ puṇyadām | kumbhodbhūtamahāmuner vratakathāṃ śrīdāṃ śubhāṃ śarmmadāṃ, bhūdevo likhati sma tāṃ gaṇapatir ggovindasevārataḥ || saṃ 784 || || (fol. 23v4–7)
notes: The chronogram śruti(4)-danti(8)-ghoṭaka(7), read right to left, gives 784, which agrees with 'saṃ 784'. The colophon does not name the era. NS is assumed from the Newari script, giving about 1664 CE. 'Govindasya tithi' is taken to mean dvādaśī, Viṣṇu's tithi; ekādaśī is also possible. 'Śaśadhare' (moon) means Monday. Scribe's name: the catalogue gives Bhūdeva. Here bhūdeva is read as the common epithet 'brāhmaṇa' and Gaṇapati as the personal name. The reverse reading is also possible: Bhūdeva as the name, with gaṇapati as an epithet. That is why confidence is medium. The scribe calls himself 'govindasevārata', a devotee of Govinda.
review: Scribe confidence lowered from high to medium: the verse can also be read with Bhūdeva as the personal name (as the catalogue does) and gaṇapati as an epithet; added an alternative-reading note
Tithi given as dvādaśī (Govinda's tithi), with 'govindasya tithau' as the source wording
Chronogram checked: śruti 4, danti 8, ghoṭaka 7, read right to left = 784, matching 'saṃ 784'. Era NS is inferred from the Newari script, so this is noted; ce_approx 1664 confirmed

title: Pīṭhikāstotra
subject: Stotra
date_raw: samvat 555 vaisāṣaśuklapradipadyāṃ(!) tithau aśuninakṣetre(!) siddhijo gevudavāsarot
date_note: = Wednesday 30 Mar 1435, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti samastavyaktavyāptinivatuyo nāma pīṭhakāstotra samāptaḥ || ❁ || samvat 555 vaisāṣaśuklapradipadyāṃ(!) tithau aśuninakṣetre(!) siddhijo gevudavāsarot | liti manate jasyo 'rthena bhavatu svabham(!) astu sarvvadā | śubhaḥ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || (fol. 7v1-3) (exp. 011)
purpose: for the person on whose behalf (yasyārthena) it was written; benediction śubham astu sarvadā
notes: The era is not named. It is taken as Nepāla Saṃvat because of the Newari script and the bare 'samvat' (NS 555 ≈ 1435 CE). The date formula is badly corrupted: aśuninakṣetre = aśvinīnakṣatre; siddhijo gevudavāsarot = siddhiyoge budhavāsare. The phrase 'liti manate jasyo 'rthena bhavatu svabham astu sarvvadā' is probably 'likhitam ... yasyārthena, bhavatu śubham astu sarvadā'. 'liti manate' might hide a scribe's name (e.g. likhitam Anantena), but this is too uncertain, so no person is recorded. Title 'pīṭhakāstotra' = Pīṭhikāstotra; 'samastavyaktavyāptinivatuyo' is corrupt.
review: Normalized the nakshatra and yoga to Aśvinī and siddhi (aśuninakṣetre = aśvinīnakṣatre, siddhijo ge = siddhiyoge); normalized the weekday reading to budhavāsare.
Changed the purpose field from a corrupt quotation to a short gloss: written for the person on whose behalf (yasyārthena) it was copied.
Notes: added that 'liti manate' might hide a scribe's name (e.g. likhitam Anantena). No person was added because the reading is too uncertain.
Kept no persons, NS 555 and 1435 CE.

notes: This is the author's colophon for the work, not a scribal colophon. It says that Devanātha Ṭhakkura (Tarkapañcānana) composed the Tantrakaumudī at the command of King Naranārāyaṇa of Kamatā (Koch Bihar, r. c. 1540–1587), styled Malladeva. review: p1 (Naranārāyaṇa): roles changed from king + commissioner to 'other'. 'kāritāyāṃ' means he commissioned the composition of the original Tantrakaumudī, not this copy, so he is not the reigning king of this manuscript.

colophon: iti saptamīvratakathā samāptāḥ (!) || kīṭalīḍhākṣarāṃ pustīṃ lipidoṣād durakṣaraḥ | asaṃpūrṇṇā samālokya maṇikākhyena pūritā || vahniśūnyaśare yāte nepālābdi vidhīyate | aśunyāś ca site pakṣe tithau kāma bhṛgudine || vīraśiṃhāvidhānena likhitañ ca suśraddhayā | saptamīvratarājeśaṃ dvijāya saṃprabodhitaṃ || śubham astu || ○ || (fol. 10v1–3)
notes: The verses say a worm-eaten, badly written, incomplete pustī was examined and completed (pūritā) by someone named Maṇika. It was then 'written with faith by arrangement (vidhānena) of Vīrasiṃha'. The catalogue makes Vīrasiṃha the scribe. 'vidhāna' can also mean arranging or ordering, so he may be the commissioner, with Maṇika as the actual copyist. The chronogram vahni-śūnya-śara reads 503 NS (1383 CE). 'aśunyāś ca' is a corruption of āśvina/āśvayuja. 'kāma' stands for trayodaśī and bhṛgudina for Friday. The brahmin (dvija) to whom the vrata is imparted is not named.
review: Vīrasiṃha: confidence lowered to medium. 'vīraśiṃhavidhānena likhitam' can mean 'written by arrangement of Vīrasiṃha', which would make him the person who had it done, not the scribe. Scribe role kept to follow the catalogue, with the alternative stated in notes.
Maṇika: confidence lowered to medium. 'pūritā' means he completed or restored the worm-eaten, incomplete copy, which may mean he did the actual writing. Corrector role kept.

title: Vṛttasāra
subject: Chandaḥ
date_note: = Saturday 5 Sep 1874, computed; nothing stated to verify it by; Lakṣmaṇasena era: not verifiable
colophon: iti maithilaśrīmadupādhyāyapada(43r1)prasiddha-śrīramāpatiśarmmaviracito vṛttasāraḥ samāptaḥ || ○ śrīsadāśiva || mahārājādhirā(2)ja-śrīmajjagajjyotirmmallanide〇śena taccaraṇakamalaikāśrayeṇa śrīharide(3)vena likhitam idaṃ pustakaṃ – – – || 〇 la saṃ 755 śrāvana vadi caṃndre – daśamyā ti(4)thau || || śubham astu – – || śrīr astu – – – ||
notes: Date conflict: the colophon says 'la saṃ' (Lakṣmaṇa Saṃvat), and LS 755 + 1119 gives about 1874 CE, which is impossible for King Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur (r. c. 1613–1637). Read as Nepāla Saṃvat, 755 gives 1635 CE, which falls inside his reign. The era label is probably a scribal or cataloguer slip for 'ne saṃ', or a Maithila scribe used LS wrongly. NS 755 (c. 1635) is the likely real date; ce_approx 1874 follows the era as written and should not be relied on. Harideva calls himself a dependent of the king ('taccaraṇakamalaikāśrayeṇa') and copied the book on his order ('nideśena'), so he was probably a Maithila court scribe. No place is given; Bhaktapur is likely from the king, but the colophon does not say so. Ramāpati Upādhyāya is the author of the Vṛttasāra, not a person involved in this copy.

title: Kāvyaprakāśa
subject: Sāhitya
date_note: = Jul 1366, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti kāvyaprakāśikāyāṃ arthālaṅkāro nāma daśama ullāsaḥ samāptaḥ || ❁ || likhitaṃ bhārasiṃhasya viṣṇusiṃhasya sūnunā | kāvyaprakāśikā pustī svārthapāṭhāya śraddhayā || rasadiggajavedābde māse nabhasi pāṇḍare | saṃpūrṇaṃ vyalikhattena ṣaḍbhir divasasaṃjñakaiḥ || (fol. 80r4–5)
notes: The chronogram rasa (6), diggaja (8), veda (4), read right to left, gives 486. The verse names no era. NS is inferred from the Newari script and the catalogue, which gives NS 486 = c. 1366 CE. Nabhas = Śrāvaṇa; pāṇḍara = śukla pakṣa. 'saṃpūrṇaṃ vyalikhat ... ṣaḍbhir divasasaṃjñakaiḥ' says the copying was completed in six days, so no tithi is given. The catalogue lists Viṣṇusiṃha as scribe, but grammatically Viṣṇusiṃha is the father ('viṣṇusiṃhasya sūnunā'), and the scribe is Bhārasiṃha (genitive agent with likhitam). It is possible, though less likely, that 'bhāra' is the title Bhāro, which would make the scribe an unnamed son of Viṣṇusiṃha.
review: Scribe changed from Viṣṇusiṃha to Bhārasiṃha. In 'likhitaṃ bhārasiṃhasya viṣṇusiṃhasya sūnunā', sūnunā ('by the son') is governed by viṣṇusiṃhasya, so the writer is the son of Viṣṇusiṃha. The genitive bhārasiṃhasya with likhitam is the agent ('written by Bhārasiṃha'), and 'viṣṇusiṃhasya sūnunā' stands in apposition to it.
Added the role 'owner' for Bhārasiṃha, because he copied it 'svārthapāṭhāya' (for his own study).
Viṣṇusiṃha's role changed to relative_only (father).
Relation reversed: Bhārasiṃha is son_of Viṣṇusiṃha.
Tithi removed. 'ṣaḍbhir divasasaṃjñakaiḥ' means the copy was finished in six days. It is not the 6th tithi.
Notes rewritten: the reading conflicts with the catalogue's Scribe field, and the era is inferred.

notes: The colophon gives two dates, and they agree. NS: rasa 6, candra 1, ṣaḍmukha 6, read right to left = 616, and 616 + 880 = 1496 CE. Śaka: vasu 8, vidhu 1, samudra 4, abdhija (the moon) 1, reversed = 1418, and 1418 + 78 = 1496 CE. Tithi 'vidhimukha' = the 4 faces of Brahmā = caturthī. Weekday 'suradviṭguru' = Śukra = Friday. The verse containing 'jayaprāk(?)devasya' is unmetrical (cataloguer's note). In context the genitive most likely refers to the author Jayadeva, not to a patron, so it is not entered as a separate person. 'cintāmaṇeḥ prārthināṃ' is an epithet of the king. Jayarāyamalla = Rāya Malla of Bhaktapur, which fits 1496. 'nepāle' only says the copy was made in Nepal; no town is named.
review: Removed p5 'Jayaprākagdeva' as commissioner. The genitive 'jayaprāk(?)devasya' goes with 'nidhuvanam udāraṃ' (the poem of Viṣṇu's love-play), so it almost certainly names the poet Jayadeva (perhaps a corruption, or 'the former Jayadeva'). It does not name a patron, and the colophon has no commissioning verb. Also removed the wrote_for relation that pointed to this person.
Tithi corrected from 1 to 4: 'vidhimukhe' means 'Brahmā's faces' = 4 (caturthī).
Added the scribe's alternative name forms ('vipaścidrūpākhyo', 'śrīrūpadevo'). Dropped 'vipaścit' from titles because it is an epithet.
Added a check of both chronograms to the notes.

review: p3 name: changed to Jayakīrttarāja, the likely intended name, since 'yaja-' looks like a scribal metathesis of 'jaya-'. Confidence lowered to medium. The as_written form is unchanged.
p1 roles: dropped 'author'. Caṇḍeśvara wrote the bhāṣya, so he is the commentator, not the author of the Sūryasiddhānta itself.
p1 titles: removed 'maithila'. It describes where he came from, so it now goes in residence ('Mithilā').
p2 residence: cleared. Bhaktapattana is where he reigned, and it is already recorded under place.

subject: Śaiva Tantra
colophon: iti śrī2madhye pīthipūjāvidhiḥ samāpta(!) || || pithipūjā dhunakā va yā va yajamāna lāsāva svastikasa vidyācake (!) svasti kuryā sadā bighni svasti mārttaṇḍam eva ca yoginī svasti (fol. fol. 33v8–9)
notes: The catalogue lists Jaya Bhūpatīndra Malla (Bhaktapur, reigned c. 1696–1722) as king, but his name is not in the quoted colophon. He may be named somewhere else in the manuscript, so he is not recorded here. The colophon has no date and no named persons. 'yajamāna' in the Newari instruction (pithipūjā dhunakā va ... yajamāna lāsāva svastikasa ...) is a generic ritual role, not a named person. The text after the colophon is ritual instruction followed by svasti verses ('vidyācake (!)' probably stands for 'vidyācakre').
review: Added detail to notes: 'yajamāna' is a generic ritual term, not a named person; the text after the colophon is ritual instruction and svasti verses.

colophon: iti śrī 3 brahmāyanīpithipūjāpaddhati(!) samāptaḥ || || ❁ || (fol. 14t2–3) || iti śrī 3 māheśvarīpīṭhipūjāpa(r)ddhati samāptaḥ || || śrī 3 sveṣṭadevatā prīnātu || || yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭā tād(!)dṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā | yadi śuddham aśudhaṃ vā mama doṣo na dīyate || || śrīnepālasamvat 807 || śrīkarigatasamvat 4788 || śriśākasamvat 1609 || śrīvikramādityasamvat 1744 || vaiśākhamāse || kṛṣṇapakṣe || amāvāsyātithau || bharanīparakṛtikānakṣatre || śobhanayoge || yathākaranamuhūtake || ādityavāśale || vṛṣarāśigate savitari || mekharāśigate candramasi || || thvakhnu śrīśrīsumatijayajitāmitramallavarmmanā svakarena likhitaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || || anena karmmaṇā sveṣṭadevī prīnā(!)tu siddhidā | jñātājñātakṛtaṃ karma kṣatum arhasi me sadā || jitāmitrasya bhūpasya tvāṃ vinā nāsti me gatiḥ | tvadbhaktitvatparāśaktir matir bhūyāt kurāmbike(!) || || ❁ || || śrī 3 maheśvarī prinātu (!) || || (exp. 27b2–28t4)
purpose: Copied with the king's own hand as devotion; merit offered to his chosen goddess (sveṣṭadevī), Māheśvarī
notes: The copy was made by King Jitāmitramalla himself (svakarena likhitaṃ), with a closing prayer in his name (jitāmitrasya bhūpasya). He is the Bhaktapur Malla king, though the colophon names no place. All four eras agree: NS 807+880, Kali 4788−3101, ŚS 1609+78 and VS 1744−57 all give 1687 CE (Vaiśākha amāvāsyā, about May 1687). An earlier colophon at fol. 14 closes a Brahmāyaṇīpīṭhapūjāpaddhati in the same manuscript. 'karigata' stands for kaligata, 'mekha' for meṣa and 'vāśale' for vāsare. The catalogue's 'Varmma' is the varman element of the royal name, not a separate surname.
review: Name normalized to the regnal name 'Jitāmitramalla', which is how the colophon itself refers to him (jitāmitrasya bhūpasya). 'Sumatijaya' is an epithet prefixed to the full name and is now in titles. The first reading had split it oddly ('sumati' as a title, 'Jayajitāmitramalla' as the name).
Titles revised to: sumatijaya (epithet), varman, bhūpa.
Date: weekday normalized to ādityavāra (Sunday); added the sun in Vṛṣa and the moon in Meṣa. All four eras checked and they agree on 1687 CE.
Purpose rephrased: the king copied it with his own hand as an act of devotion, offering the merit to his chosen goddess (sveṣṭadevī).
Notes expanded: era check, first colophon for the Brahmāyaṇī pīṭha, and no place stated.

subject: Karmakāṇḍa

date_note: = Saturday 5 Jun 1926, verified by the pañcāṅga; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti trayodaśo dhyāyaḥ || 13 || iti kātyāyanītantroktaprayogavidhiḥ samāptam || śubhma || iti samvat 1983 sāla jyeṣṭha 23 roja 7 kṛṣṇapakṣe daśamyāṃ tithau likhitam idam pustakaṃ dharmaśa(r)mma śubhma bhūyāt || | granthasaṃkhyā 400 patrasaṃkhyā 7 (fol. 7v8–10)
notes: The era is not named, but 'samvat 1983 sāla' with a solar day count ('jyeṣṭha 23', i.e. the 23rd solar day of Jyeṣṭha) and 'roja 7' (Saturday) fits Vikrama Saṃvat in 20th-century Nepal. That gives May–June 1926 CE. The scribe's name 'dharmaśa(r)mma' is written uninflected and in a corrupt form, for Dharma Śarmā. The colophon calls the text 'kātyāyanītantroktaprayogavidhiḥ', while the catalogue title is 'Mantraprayogavidhi'.
review: Name changed from 'Dharmaśarman' to 'Dharma': 'śarman' is a brahmin suffix, so it now goes in titles
Weekday 'roja 7' now read as Saturday (śanivāra), the 7th day of the week
Notes now explain that 'jyeṣṭha 23' is the solar day of the month (gate)

date_note: doubtful: ≈ 956 CE is too early for a paper manuscript (an abbreviated or misread year, or the exemplar's date)

colophon: iti śrīmahābhārate virāṭaparvvaṇi śatasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyāśikyāṃ virāṭaṃ samāptaṃ || ‥‥‥ (rasa)śaile ca gate nepālavatsare | śukle kṛṣṇāṣṭamī bhaume ‥ ‥ bhāratasaṃhitā | śrīmatprakāśamallena pālite bhaktapaṭṭane | alikhan mohanaḥ śrīmān‥ maḥ (syākhe tvarānvitaḥ) oṁ namo gopījanavallabhāya || ādarśadoṣān mativibhramād vā tvarāviśeṣāl likhanasya vegāt | yad atra śuddhaṃ tad aśuddhavarṇṇaṃ kṣamantu santaḥ khalu leṣakasya || || … (svastasti) te kuśalam astu cirāyur astu gohastivājidhanadhānyasamṛddhir astu aiśvaryyam astu vijayo stu ripukṣayo stu saubhāgyam astu satataṃ haribhaktir astu || (fol. 158v5–159r6)
notes: Chronogram: the units word is lost in the lacuna before '(rasa)'. Read right to left, śaila = 7 (hundreds) and rasa = 6 (tens), so the year is NS 76x (CE 1640–1649). This fits the catalogue's 'NS 76?'. 'Prakāśamalla' is probably Jagatprakāśa Malla of Bhaktapur, who reigned from about NS 764 (CE 1644). If so, the copy dates to NS 764–769 (CE 1644–1649). The colophon itself has only 'prakāśamalla', so the name is kept as written. Date: 'śukle kṛṣṇāṣṭamī' contradicts itself. 'śukle' could be a corruption of 'śukre' (the month Śukra = Jyeṣṭha), or 'kṛṣṇāṣṭamī' could name the festival, so the month is left empty. Scribe: 'alikhan' is plural and is followed by the damaged 'śrīmān‥ maḥ', so a second scribe (e.g. ‥rāma) or a longer name may be lost. '(syākhe tvarānvitaḥ)' is unclear. Bhaktapur is taken as the place of copying because it is named as the realm ruled by the king.
review: Date: the chronogram gives only NS 76x. The units word is lost in the lacuna, rasa = 6 (tens) and śaila = 7 (hundreds). Year changed to '76x' and ce_approx to 1640–1649 instead of the single year 1645.
Date: noted that 'śukle' conflicts with 'kṛṣṇāṣṭamī'. Pakṣa kept as kṛṣṇa; month left empty.
Scribe: confidence lowered to medium. The plural 'alikhan' and the damaged 'śrīmān‥ maḥ' may hide a second scribe or a longer name.
Notes: the identification with Jagatprakāśa Malla is now marked as probable, not certain. The name is kept as written.

notes: The only personal data is a Newari note in the bottom margin of fol. 101v, after the colophon. It appears to record a sale: Meharamān (me haramān, word division unclear) of Ñala deśa bought the book from Sanatkumāra Upādhyāya ('-yaya san' = from) for 111 ṭakā mohar. The words 'sathoṣunu' and '(ñā)che layāke (yāñā)' are unclear or corrupt, and the direction of the sale is my best reading. The date NS 998 (1878 CE) belongs to this note and may not be the date of copying. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Sanatkumāra Upādhyāya' isn't supported by the text: the note says nothing about who wrote the manuscript. Ñala may be Nala, near Banepa, but that is uncertain. It is not Yala (Patan).

Meharamān: role changed from 'other' to 'owner' (buyer, who paid 111 mohar)
Relation reworded as a sale, from the seller to the buyer

title: Pratiṣṭhātantra
subject: Tantra
date_note: = Sunday 3 Feb 1269, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: year + 1, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: iti śrīmatpaści(!)śāsanīyanityānhikatilakaṃ samāptaṃ || ❁ || ślokāṃka 1400 || samvat 389 phālguni(!) śuklapatipradyāṃ(!) śaniścaravāsare likhitam iti || śrī(svayaṃ) śivagalaṭvālakādhivāśinayo(bukkaṃche)krama ācārya(oṃ)nāyakasya nitatilakapuskaṃ(!) || śubham astu || ❁ || ❁ || (fol. 121v4–122r2)
notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as Śrīkaṇṭhasūnu, but that name does not appear in the quoted colophon. It may come from elsewhere in the manuscript, such as another colophon or the author's statement (Śrīkaṇṭha's son?), so no scribe has been added. The colophon names the text Nityāhnikatilaka of the Paścimāmnāya (paści(!)śāsanīya), not Pratiṣṭhātantra as in the catalogue title. The owner's phrase is corrupt: 'śivagalaṭvālakādhivāśinayo(bukkaṃche)krama ācārya(oṃ)nāyakasya'. 'Śivagala ṭvāla' is a locality (tole), possibly Sigaḥ in Kathmandu, though this is not certain. 'bukkaṃche' may be a house or local name. 'krama ācārya' may stand for kramācārya, a Kaula title. 'nāyaka' may be a title (head of a vihāra or lineage) rather than part of the name, so the personal name may really be 'Oṃ' or be missing. The cataloguer's parentheses around 'svayaṃ', 'bukkaṃche' and 'oṃ' seem to mark doubtful readings. 'śrī(svayaṃ)' could mean the owner copied the book himself, but that is too unclear to add the role of scribe.

title: Pratiṣṭhāloka
subject: Tantra
date_note: = Jan 1185, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: samāpto yat kalyāna(!)śrīmitrāoddhṛtaḥ pratiṣṭhāloka iti || ❁ || vikhyāte triśate varaśavānayute nepālasambatsare māghamāse śrīguna(!)kāmadevarāje |kalyāṇena hiraṇyabale sugatabāsasthānena samantabhadhrena svaya(!) lekṣi? || (35r5–6)
notes: The year is written 'triśate varaśavānayute': 300 plus a corrupt word-numeral, probably śara or bāṇa (= 5). That gives NS 305, as the cataloguer reads it. NS 305 falls within Guṇakāmadeva's reign (c. NS 300–316 / 1184–1196 CE), so the date fits. Māgha NS 305 is about January–February 1185 CE. 'kalyāṇena' just before the place phrase is probably an auspicious adverb ('auspiciously'), not part of a name. 'hiraṇyabale' could be a corrupt form of Hiraṇyavarṇa (Mahāvihāra, Patan), but this is unverified, so the place is left unnormalised. 'sugatabāsasthānena' describes the scribe as living in a vihāra. 'svaya(!) lekṣi?' = svayaṃ lekhi ('written by himself'). Ownership is not stated, so no owner role is added. Kalyāṇaśrīmitra is named as the compiler of the text (uddhṛta), so his role is author.
review: p3: affiliation and residence restated. 'hiraṇyabale sugatabāsasthānena' is read as 'living in the Sugata's abode (a vihāra) at Hiraṇyabala'. The vihāra goes in affiliation and Hiraṇyabala in residence.
Date: month normalised to 'Māgha'. Added a note on the chronogram and how it fits Guṇakāmadeva's reign. ce_approx 1185 confirmed: Māgha NS 305 falls in early 1185.
Notes: 'kalyāṇena' flagged as probably an auspicious adverb, not a personal name. Possible identification of Hiraṇyabala with Hiraṇyavarṇa Mahāvihāra flagged as uncertain.

title: Manthānabhairavatantra
subject: Tantra
date_note: ≈ 1185 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: ity ādyāvatāre mahāmaṃthānabhairavayajñaanvaye saptakoṭipramāṇe merumārggavīnirggate lakṣapādādhike ādyapīṭhāvatārite vidyāpīṭhamārggabimalabhedottaraṣaṭkanirṇṇayakādibhede svājñāpārameśvare svāminīmate śricaturviṃsatisāhasre athā(ga)mabhāṣite śrīmate ekavīrātripurābhidhāne navanityā yāgāvikāravarṇane kramādapānān(!) ānandaḥ || ❁ || nandas tu sādhakasiddhasmuho nanda(!) tu siddhagurukkulageho | naṃda(!) tu (maṇi)gaṇagurugotraḥ | naṇda(!) tu kādimatesu pavitraṃ || ❁ || hastād hastaṃ kṣaitau kṣiptaṃ tat kṣiptacaikapālinā | uccair yad vācitaṃ nātha pustakaṃ tat kṣamasva me || || samasta svakriyāyeta śrīmadguṇakāmadevasaṃstutya nepāladeśarājyāsvasti saṃvat 305 || kāyasthaśrīmahādevena likhitam || śrī śrī bhāgeśvara | śrīkarmmaṇāṃ tava ācāryasya pustakaṃ likhitaṃ || yathā dṛṣṭaṃ tathā likhitaṃ, lekhako nāsti dokṣa(!)kam || śubham astu sarvadā || (fol. 89r3–9)
notes: The colophon names no era, but Guṇakāmadeva reigned around NS 300–316 (c. 1180–1196 CE), so NS 305 = c. 1185 CE fits. The line 'śrī śrī bhāgeśvara | śrīkarmmaṇāṃ tava ācāryasya pustakaṃ likhitaṃ' is obscure and possibly corrupt. One reading is that the book was copied for an ācārya named Bhāgeśvara. Another is that 'bhāgeśvara' is an invocation, which would leave the owner unnamed; perhaps read 'śrīkarmācāryasya', making the owner a karmācārya. That is why the owner is set at low confidence. The line may also have been added by a later hand. 'samasta svakriyāyeta' is corrupt. 'dokṣakam' stands for 'doṣakaḥ'.
review: Added Bhāgeśvara (p3) as a probable owner, at low confidence, from 'śrī śrī bhāgeśvara | ... ācāryasya pustakaṃ likhitaṃ'; title ācārya
Place as_written trimmed to 'nepāladeśa'; normalized as Kathmandu Valley
Notes expanded: the reign date fits, the owner line is obscure, and the scribal formulae are corrupt

title: Mālatīmādhavaṭikā
subject: Nāṭaka
date_note: = Sunday 17 Sep 1815, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: iti śrīmahādāmodarapaṇḍitadharmmādhika(11)raṇikaśrījagaddharakṛtaṭīkāyāṃ daśamoṃkaḥ samāptaḥ || || śrīvikramābde karasapta nāga bhūvāre ravau bhādinipūrṇatithau || tannāṭa(12)kaṃ sarvalikheti nūnaṃ padhye ca nāthasya pustakam idaṃ || || (!) (14) samvat 936 pauṣa śudi 15 roja 1 śubhāni santu || || (fol. 87v10–14)
notes: The chronogram kara (2), sapta (7), nāga (8), bhū (1), read right to left, gives VS 1872. The verse dates the copy to a Sunday at the full moon of Bhādra ('bhādini' probably stands for Bhādra), around Aug/Sep 1815. The separate prose line gives NS 936 Pauṣa śudi 15, roja 1 (Sunday), around Dec 1815/Jan 1816. The two years fit the same period, but the months differ by about four months. The second date may mark the end of copying or a later note. The weekdays have not been checked. The verse is corrupt (!). 'padhye ca nāthasya' is read as Padmanātha, following the catalogue; Padmanābha is also possible. 'sarvalikheti' (≈ sarvaṃ likhitam) suggests that Padmanātha wrote the copy, but this is uncertain. 'mahādāmodarapaṇḍita' comes before Jagaddhara's own epithets (dharmādhikaraṇika). It may be a corruption of 'mahāmahopādhyāya' or part of the commentator's epithets. Nothing in the text supports reading it as his father, so it has been left out.
review: Removed Dāmodara (p2) and the son_of relation. The compound 'śrīmahādāmodarapaṇḍitadharmmādhikaraṇikaśrījagaddhara' has no putra/tanaya or any other kinship word, so the filiation is not supported, and Dāmodara has no connection with this copy. See notes.
Jagaddhara: added 'paṇḍita' to titles, since it is one of his own epithets.
Padmanātha: confidence lowered to low. The scribe role is kept but only weakly supported ('sarvalikheti'). The owner role rests on 'pustakam idaṃ'.

Date: the two dates are now kept apart. The VS verse gives Sunday, the full moon of Bhādra(pada), VS 1872. The NS line gives Sunday, Pauṣa śudi 15, NS 936. The first reading had wrongly attached Pauṣa to the VS verse.
ce_approx: changed to 1815–1816. Bhādra VS 1872 falls around Aug/Sep 1815 and Pauṣa NS 936 around Dec 1815/Jan 1816. The unverified exact equation with 14 Jan 1816 was removed.

title: Rukmiṇīharaṇanāṭaka
subject: nāṭaka
date_note: = Saturday 1 May 1700, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit (it would fit with: current year, which fits wrong dates about as often)
colophon: || iti rukaminīharana, śaṃvarāsura(4)vadha nāma nāṭaka paṃcamoṅkaḥ samāptaḥ || || ❁ || saṃvat 820 vaiśākha (5) vaddhi 13 ādityavāra thvakunhu pyākhana pidaṅa dina juro || || thvagula (6) dana śrī 3 buṃgadevayā khvālasa raṃga bolāva vala thutisa || thvaguri dana (7) yayā śrī taravayā bhīmadeva hmaṃ 3 rubora parākasa hmaṃ 1 haṃsa bhoga biyā(exp32b1)va ji parākasa hmaṃ 1 dugu syāṅāva śrī rājakurasa bijyācaku juro || era(2)yā śrī joganarendra malla thākura esa bijyācakāva ṣopoyā jujuṃ bijyāca(3)kāva śrī bhūpārendra malla thākulana thva kāryya yāka juro || || samvat 740 (4) vaiśākha śuddhi 13 somavāra thvakuhnu ivāhārayā śivanārāyaṇācā(5)ryyana thva ghaṃtha coya madhuṃko vaṃlānihma gṛha nivāsita vipra śrījaśo(6)dharana saṃpūrṇa yāṅana coyā dina juro || || śubha || || ❁ || || (exp.32t3-32b6)
notes: The colophon has two dated notes. (1) NS 820 (c. 1700 CE) vaiśākha vaddhi (= badi, kṛṣṇa) 13, Sunday. This is the day the play was performed (pyākhana pidaṅa), on a stage in front of śrī 3 Buṃgadeva (Bungamati). King Yoganarendramalla of Yala/Patan attended, and so did the king of Khopa/Bhaktapur, who is not named. Bhūpālendramalla, king of Kathmandu, organised it ('thva kāryya yāka'). (2) NS 740 (c. 1620 CE) vaiśākha śuddhi 13, Monday. This is the copying itself: Śivanārāyaṇa of Ivāhāra began the copy, and vipra Yaśodhara finished it. Taken as the date of this copy. Conflict: the copying date, NS 740, is about 80 years before the performance note, NS 820, yet the 740 note comes after the 820 note. Either the 820 performance note was added to an older manuscript, or '740' is an error (e.g. for 840?). Because of this, both kings are recorded as 'other' (staging) and not as kings reigning when the copy was made. The catalogue fields agree with these dates. The passage 'thvaguri dana yayā śrī taravayā bhīmadeva hmaṃ 3 rubora parākasa hmaṃ 1 haṃsa bhoga biyāva ...' is unclear. It may describe offerings or participants at the performance, and Bhīmadeva may be a deity (Bhīmasena) rather than a person, so he is not listed. 'Ivāhāra' is probably a vihāra (possibly Ī Bahā/Ibahī, Patan), but this is not certain.
review: Yoganarendramalla: role 'king' changed to 'other'. He is named for the staging of the play in NS 820, not as the reigning king when this copy was made in NS 740. Residence 'era' read as Erayā = Yala (Patan).

Bhūpālendramalla: 'king' role removed and 'other' kept (he organised the staging, 'thva kāryya yāka'). The residence 'yayā' was wrong: that word belongs to the earlier phrase 'dana yayā śrī taravayā'. Residence left empty. Title normalised to ṭhākura.
Śivanārāyaṇa: Ivāhāra also given as residence. Confidence lowered to medium: he only began the copy (coya madhuṃko).
Yaśodhara: residence normalised to 'vaṃlāni (gṛha)'.
Added an 'other' relation: Yaśodhara finished the copy Śivanārāyaṇa had begun.
Place emptied: Ivāhāra and the vaṃlāni house are where the scribes live, not a stated place of copying.
Notes expanded: the date conflict and the unclear Bhīmadeva passage.

title: Smaradīpikā
subject: Kāmaśāstra
date_note: ≈ 1835 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti śrīsmaradīpikāsampūrṇam || || saṃ 955 madhyaśukla 1213 (fol. 13v4)
notes: The era isn't stated, but 'saṃ 955' in a Newari-script manuscript is Nepāla Saṃvat (the catalogue also has NS 955). NS 955 = 1834/35 CE. The month 'madhya' is probably corrupt: most likely Madhu (= Caitra, about March/April 1835) or a slip for Māgha (about January/February 1835). Either way the year is 1835 CE. The tithi '1213' most likely means 12/13, i.e. dvādaśī running into trayodaśī on the same day; it could also be a corrupt figure. The colophon names no persons.
review: Notes expanded only: 'madhya' is more likely Madhu (= Caitra) or a slip for Māgha, and '1213' probably means tithi 12/13 (dvādaśī running into trayodaśī). No change to the data fields.

title: Hitopadeśamitralābha
subject: Nīti
date_note: = Saturday 23 May 1711, weekday verified, nakṣatra not
colophon: iti hitopadeśa, nītisārasaṃgraha mitrarābha juva nāma(3) kathāsaṃgraḥ samāpta || || samvat 831 jyeṣṭha śukla śaniścaravāla ṣaṣṭhi na(4)ṣetra, punavasunakṣetra vṛṃhanayoga thokuhnu jagasiṃṅa || || śubha...stu (5) bijarakvacheyā || || śubham astu sarvvadāḥ || || śivagati (exp. 20t2-5)
notes: The year is NS 831, which matches the catalogue field (= c. 1711 CE, May–June). The Newari phrase 'mitrarābha juva' means 'Mitralābha completed'. 'thokuhnu' means 'on this day'. 'bijarakvacheyā' carries the Newari genitive -yā, so it is the locality Jagasiṃha belongs to. It is recorded as the place only by inference and is not identified. 'jagasiṃṅa' is read as Jagasiṃha. Śivagati comes after the closing blessing and may be in a later hand. It could be a personal name, possibly a later owner, or a pious phrase. The yoga 'vṛṃhana' does not match any standard yoga name, so the reading is uncertain.
review: Normalized the weekday to 'Saturday (śaniścaravāra)' and the nakshatra to Punarvasu; noted that the yoga reading 'vṛṃhana' is uncertain.
Jagasiṃha stays as scribe at medium confidence. No verb of writing is given; the role rests on the usual Newari formula 'thokuhnu' + name + locality.
Śivagati is kept at low confidence with role 'other'. It may be a later owner's or reader's mark, or a pious phrase rather than a name.
Notes now say that Bijarakvache is the scribe's locality (Newari genitive -yā), not explicitly the place of copying.

subject: Saṅgīta
date_raw: nepāle rasaṣaṣṭhiśailavimale jāte śubhe vatsare | bhādre śuklakuje ca manmathatithau svātyāṃ
date_note: = Saturday 22 Sep 1646, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: ? iti śubhaṅkaraviracitāyāṃ hastamuktāvalyāṃ samāpto yaṃ granthaḥ || || || śrībhavānī prīṇātu || || ... ❖ nepāle rasaṣaṣṭhiśailavimale jāte śubhe vatsare | bhādre śuklakuje ca manmathatithau svātyāṃ śubhe puṇyakṛt | śrīmat sūrakulāvataṃsavimalaḥ khyāto vinodātmajo- nantoyaṃ kuladīpano likhad iti muktāvalīpustakaṃ || udakānalacaurebhyo...(fol. 103v3–6)
notes: The chronogram rasa (6), ṣaṣṭhi (taken as 6), śaila (7), read right to left, gives NS 766, which is Bhādra 1646 CE. If ṣaṣṭhi were read literally as 60, the chronogram would not work, so 6 is the likely sense. Manmathatithi = trayodaśī. The catalogue gives King Jagajjyotir Malla, but no king is named in the quoted colophon. NS 766 also falls after his reign (he died c. 1637 CE), so that field is doubtful and no king has been added. The colophon calls the work Hastamuktāvalī by Śubhaṅkara, and the scribe calls it 'muktāvalīpustakaṃ'. The catalogue title is Saṅgītacintāmaṇi, so either the title field is wrong or the manuscript holds more than one text. 'sūrakulāvataṃsa' (ornament of the Sūra family) is read as Ananta's family, which makes it also Vinoda's. Ananta's 'kuladīpana' (lamp of the family) is an epithet, not a title.

title: Kāvyālaṃkāra
subject: Alaṅkāra
date_note: = Tuesday 31 Jan 1673, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti rudraṭakāvyālaṃkāre ṣoḍaśo ʼdhyāyaḥ || || samāpta(5)ñ ca kāvyālaṃkāṛābhidheyaṃ || śāstraṃ kṛti (!) bhaṭṭarudraṭasya || || nepāle varahāyane guṇavilorvvībhṛdbhir udyodite, māghe māsi site maheśvarati(6)thau puṣyarkṣasaṃśobhite, | āyuṣmad budhavāsare makarage bhānau vidhau karkkaṭe, saṃpūrṇṇaṃ likhitaṃ balena dharaṇī devena pustaṃ varaṃ || kāvyavyā(7)karaṇakoṣanigamāgamapurāṇachandassāhityanāṭakaśāstrārthavicāracāṭutaramatiśrīmanoharopādhyāyasya pustakaṃ kāvyālaṃ(8)kārābhidheyaṃ, likhitaṃ śrībalabhadraśarmmanā, (!) svārthahetunā || || sakalajagajjananī bhavānī bhavabhītihāriṇī bhavatu || (fol. 28r4–8)
purpose: svārthahetunā (the book is said to belong to Manohara Upādhyāya)
notes: The chronogram 'guṇa (3) - vila/bila (9) - urvībhṛt (7)' read right to left gives Nepāla saṃvat 793. Māgha śukla of NS 793 falls in early 1673 CE. The astronomy fits: with the sun in Makara and the moon in Karkaṭa (Puṣya), the moon is close to full, which matches the bright fortnight near caturdaśī. 'Maheśvaratithi' most likely means caturdaśī (Śiva's tithi), though aṣṭamī cannot be fully ruled out. The catalogue date 'SAM 1693?' does not match: VS 1693 would be about 1636 CE. It is probably a misreading of the chronogram. 'balena dharaṇīdevena' means 'by Bala, the brāhmaṇa (dharaṇīdeva)'. This is the same scribe as Balabhadraśarman, named later in the colophon. The colophon calls the book Manohara Upādhyāya's, but also says the scribe copied it 'svārthahetunā' (for his own purpose). These pull in different directions: Balabhadra may have copied it for his own use while the book belonged to, or later passed to, Manohara. Balabhadra is therefore not marked as owner. 'Nepāle' marks the era (Nepāla saṃvat) and only loosely the region, so it is not given a normalized place.
review: Persons, roles, date and era kept as in the first reading; the chronogram checks out: guṇa=3, vila (bila)=9, urvībhṛt=7, read right to left = NS 793.
Weekday normalised to Wednesday (budhavāsara).
Notes expanded: the astronomy fits, the ownership vs. svārtha question, why the catalogue date is wrong, and the reading of 'balena dharaṇīdevena'.

'vijayarājñe(!)' stands for vijayarājye ('in the victorious reign'). '///jādhirāja' is most likely 'rājādhirāja'. 'bhavatāra///dhyāya' is probably 'bhavatv ācāryopādhyāya-', a standard merit-transfer formula. The donor formula 'deyadharmo 'yaṃ' is partly lost ('///yaṃ'). No scribe is named, and no place of copying is given.

title: Grahalāghavavivṛtti
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_note: = Sunday 27 Mar 1718, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīmat (!) gaṇakacūḍāmaṇidivākaradaivajñasūtamallāridaivajñaviracitāyāṃ grahalāghavaṭīkāyāṃ graṃthasamāptalaṃkāravyākhyānaṃ samāptaṃ || śubhaṃ bhavat (fol. 106r1-2) ...rāmāya namonamaḥ (7) samvat 1775 samai caitavadī ekādaśī kaha sīdhama ’bhothī (!) || || || || || || || || || || || || (fol. 106r6–7)
notes: 'sūta' stands for suta, so Mallāri is the son of Divākara. Mallāri wrote the commentary on Gaṇeśa Daivajña's Grahalāghava. Gaṇeśa is not named in the colophon, so he is not listed. No scribe, commissioner or owner is named. The date, VS 1775 Caitra vadi 11, falls in early 1718 CE if the month runs full moon to full moon (pūrṇimānta) or in 1719 if it runs new moon to new moon (amānta). Taking simply VS−57 gives 1718. 'kaha sīdhama ’bhothī' (marked (!) by the cataloguer) looks like a corrupt Hindi/Nepali completion formula, roughly 'ko siddham bhayo/bhaī', meaning 'was completed'. It contains no personal name. The Hindi-style date formula ('samai', 'vadī') suggests the copy may have been made outside the Kathmandu Valley.
review: Added notes: 'sūta' stands for suta (son); the date could fall in 1718 or 1719 CE depending on amānta/pūrṇimānta month reckoning; the closing phrase reads as a vernacular completion formula; no scribe is named.

The father's name, 'nṛsiṃha', is in parentheses, probably the cataloguer's addition or a reading that is not certain. review: p2 Divākara: role cut to 'commentator' only. The Makarandavivaraṇa is a commentary on the Makarandasāraṇī, so listing him as both author and commentator counted him twice.
notes: the parentheses around 'nṛsiṃha' are most likely the cataloguer's addition, not a sign that the name is illegible. The note now says this. Confidence stays medium.

title: Aduḥkhanavamīvrata
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
colophon: iti vratakhaṃḍe vyāsadharmasaṃvāde aduḥkhanavamīvratakathā samāptaṃ (!) || || parāḍkaropanāmaka sadāśivātmaja sutasya(!) viṭṭhalena likhitaṃ puskataṃ svahastaṃ || 68 || śrīkṛṣṇārpaṇa (exp. 19t9–11) iti pūjāvidhiḥ (exp. 6t:10) iti skaṃdapurāṇe vyāsaṛṣisaṃvāde aduḥkhanavamīkathā samāptā || ❁ || (exp. 24t:8–9) aduḥkhanavamīvratodyāpanaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || śivarāmeṇa likhita || catuḥṣaṣṭyai namaḥ || ❁ || (exp. 24b:9–10)
notes: Two scribes wrote different parts of this composite manuscript: Viṭṭhala wrote the Aduḥkhanavamīvratakathā (exp. 19t) and Śivarāma wrote the udyāpana section (exp. 24b). This matches the catalogue. Viṭṭhala's colophon is corrupt in 'sadāśivātmaja sutasya(!)'. It most likely means 'Viṭṭhala, son of Sadāśiva, of the Parāḍkara family'. It could also be read as 'Viṭṭhala, son of the son of Sadāśiva', which would make him Sadāśiva's grandson. 'Parāḍkara' (a Marathi-type surname, upanāma) is recorded as the family affiliation. '|| 68 ||' is a verse or section count, not a date. The manuscript is undated. 'svahastaṃ' means only that Viṭṭhala wrote it in his own hand; it is not a statement of ownership.
review: Viṭṭhala→Sadāśiva relation kept as son_of, but 'sadāśivātmaja sutasya(!)' could also mean 'son of Sadāśiva's son' (grandson); the possibility is now in the notes and Sadāśiva's confidence is lowered to medium
Purpose changed from 'śrīkṛṣṇārpaṇa' to a description: a pious dedication to Kṛṣṇa, not a statement of who the copy was for
Notes now say that '|| 68 ||' is a verse or section number, not a date, and that 'svahastaṃ' only means the scribe wrote it in his own hand

p4: name normalized from Śirapatika to Śrīpati. 'śira' is a common miswriting of śrī, and -ka is a suffix. Residence normalized to 'Yāga grāma'.

purpose: Copied from an earlier exemplar (pūrvādarśadarśanena); the learned are asked to correct it (baudhe śodhanīyaṃ).
notes: The cataloguer marks the chronogram as corrupt (†). svāda (taste) = rasa = 6, bhūta (element) = 5, and dig (direction) is normally 10, but here it must be a single digit, so 4 or 8. Read right to left this gives NS 546 (CE 1425/26) or NS 586 (CE 1465/66). Both fit the cataloguer's guess of the 15th century, but neither is certain. The era is not stated; NS is presumed for a Newari-script copy by a Kāyastha. 'pujā(rkka)' probably stands for puṣyārka, i.e. Puṣya nakṣatra on a Sunday; Puṣya on Phālguna śukla 12 is astronomically plausible. Śobhana is the yoga. The toponym 'śrīdavāraṇima' (catalogue: 'Khāraṇima???') is uncertain; it is given as the scribe's residence (adhivāsinā), not explicitly as the place of copying. '(a ‥na)' after the name is a lacuna, perhaps ātmanā. The scribe's name is clear; the place name and date are doubtful.

title: Sāṃvatsarikaikoddiṣtaśrāddhavidhi
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: ≈ 1772 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti sāṃvatsarikaikoddiṣṭaśrāddhavidhiḥ samāptaḥ || śrīśāke 1694 māse 10 dina 14 tithau 1 nakṣatre 22 yoge 16 likhitam idaṃ pustakaṃ śrīgaṃgadharasamanenaḥ (!) subham || || || ya(!)dṛsaṃ pustakaṃ dri(!)ṣṭvā tādri(!)saṃ likhite(!) mayā || yadi śuddhaṃ asuddhaṃ vā mama⟨ḥ⟩ doṣo na di(!)yate || 1 || subham || subham || || (fol. 11r1–6)
notes: The scribe's name is a garbled instrumental, 'śrīgaṃgadharasamanenaḥ', for Gaṅgādharaśarmaṇā. This agrees with the catalogue's 'Gaṅgādhara Śarmā'. The date is given only in numbers: month 10, day (dina) 14, tithi 1, nakṣatra 22, yoga 16. The pakṣa is not stated. If month 10 is the solar month Makara (counted from Meṣa), the date falls around January–February, so the CE year could be 1773 instead of 1772 (ŚS 1694 + 78). Counting from Aśvinī, nakṣatra 22 is Śravaṇa; yoga 16 is Siddhi. The colophon ends with the standard verse 'yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā…', in which the scribe disclaims blame for errors.
review: Name changed from 'Gaṅgādhara Śarman' to 'Gaṅgādhara': the brahmin suffix śarman goes in titles only
Removed the note's claim that month 10 is Māgha. A numbered month is ambiguous: as a solar month counted from Meṣa, the 10th is Makara (mid-Jan to mid-Feb), which falls in Pauṣa or Māgha
Added that ce_approx 1772 could be 1773 if month 10 is Makara
Added a note reading nakṣatra 22 as Śravaṇa and yoga 16 as Siddhi

title: Pratiṣṭhāpaddhati
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
date_note: ≈ 1928 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti pratiṣṭhāpaddhatiḥ samāptā || || yadā nepālabhūpālānantamadhyebhidhāvati | rasa-abhraśayāyuktau śrutiḥ saṃvatadāpaye | kārtikamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe dvitīyāyāṃ kuje dine || kāyasthodayaharṣeṇa harṣeṇa likhitaṃ drutaṃ | bhrāntisaṃśayadoṣo ʼsmiñ chodhanīyo hi dhīdhanaiḥ || bhagnapṛṣṭaḥ kaṭigrīvas tatva(!)karṇam adhomukhaḥ || duḥkhema likhitaṃ śāstraṃ putravat paripālyatām || ity antalekhayutānnevārākṣaralikhitaprācīnatāḍapatrapustakād udhṛtya 1985 saṃvatsare likhitam idam || (fol. 15r1–3)
notes: This Devanagari copy was made in saṃvat 1985. The era is not stated, but it is presumably VS, which gives about 1928/29 CE. The copy was taken from an old palm-leaf manuscript in Newari script, and the copyist of 1985 is not named. The verse colophon belongs to that exemplar and was reproduced with the text. That exemplar was written by Kāyastha Udayaharṣa on Kārttika kṛṣṇa 2, Tuesday (kuja), under a Nepalese king whose name is corrupt: 'nepālabhūpālānantamadhye', probably meaning Anantamalla. The chronogram 'rasa-abhra-śaya(?)-...-śruti' gives rasa = 6, abhra = 0 and śruti = 4. Read right to left this is 406, i.e. NS 406, about 1286 CE, which falls within Anantamalla's reign (NS 394–428). 'śaya' and 'saṃvatadāpaye' are corrupt, so this reading is tentative. The catalogue's Scribe field (Udayaharṣa) names the exemplar's scribe, not the scribe of this copy. Its Place field ('VS 1985') is actually the date.
review: Udayaharṣa is the scribe of the old palm-leaf exemplar, not of this copy. His colophon was copied along with the text ('ity antalekhayuta... tāḍapatrapustakād udhṛtya'). Role changed from scribe to other.

King read as Anantamalla: '-madhye' is probably a corruption of '-malle', i.e. nepālabhūpāle 'nantamalle 'bhidhāvati. His role changed from king to other, because he was reigning when the exemplar was written, not this copy. Confidence raised to medium, since the chronogram fits his reign.
Titles of the king: dropped 'nepālabhūpāla', which is a description, not a title. Residence cleared.

Notes: added the reading of the exemplar's chronogram (rasa 6, abhra 0, śruti 4, read right to left = 406, so NS 406, about 1286 CE, within Anantamalla's reign). Also noted that the catalogue's Scribe field names the exemplar's scribe.

notes: The scribe's note is written in the left margin of fol. 39v. 'hariharabhaṭtalulena' is corrupt or misread: 'bhaṭta' should be 'bhaṭṭa'. 'lula' is unexplained. It could be a family name or byname (Lula/Lūla), giving 'Harihara Bhaṭṭa Lula'. It could also be a misreading of a kinship word such as 'sutena', which would make the scribe an unnamed son of Harihara Bhaṭṭa. Or it could be a misreading of a longer personal name. I took Harihara Bhaṭṭa as the scribe. Vaidyanātha is the author of the Pretakāśī, not someone involved in making this copy. The colophon has no date or place.
review: p2: name reduced to stem 'Harihara'; 'bhaṭṭa' stays in titles and is no longer part of the name. 'lula' is not explained and is discussed in notes.
Notes expanded with alternative readings of 'bhaṭtalulena' and how each would change the scribe's identity.

notes: The colophon names no persons. 'ṛtāṣādri(!)' is marked corrupt by the cataloguer. It could be a word-numeral chronogram (ṛtu = 6, adri = 7, perhaps āśā = 10), but no right-to-left reading gives 1614 cleanly. It could also be a garbled month name (Āṣāḍha), but this is uncertain, so the month is left empty. The closing words 'yadi sudho mama sudho vā mama doṣo na dīyate' are a corrupt form of the usual scribal apology (yadi śuddham aśuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo na dīyate). ŚS 1614 = c. 1692 CE, which matches the catalogue field.

colophon: ītyākāśabhairavakalpe arikhaṇḍe śarab haprayogavidhir nāma catuś catvāṃriṃśaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ śubham astu || || śrīśālivāhanaśake 1605 śaisira ṛtau phālguṇakṛṣṇa dvādaśyāṃ tithau śanivāsare likhitaṃ pustakaṃ kṛṣṇalālaśarmaṇaḥ || rāma rāma rāma rāma rāma rāma (fol. 14r10–14v3)
notes: The catalogue field gives ŚS 1705, but the quoted colophon reads 'śrīśālivāhanaśake 1605'. One of the two is a typo. If 1705 is right, the date would be about 1784 CE. The genitive 'kṛṣṇalālaśarmaṇaḥ' after 'likhitaṃ pustakaṃ' can mean either 'the book of Kṛṣṇalāla' (owner) or 'written by Kṛṣṇalāla' (scribe). Both roles are given. title: Sāṃkhyatattvakaumudī
subject: Sāṃkhya
date_note: = Friday 1 Jul 1785, weekday verified, nakṣatra not; standard (pūrṇimānta months)
colophon: iti śrīvācaspatimiśraviracitā tatva(!)kaumudīsamāptaḥ || śubhaṃ || śubhaṃ || śubhaśrīśāke1707 āṣāḍakṛṣṇadaśamyāṃ revati śukravāsare || muḍiṣusthānavāstavyaṃ liṣyate(!) ravinaṃdane || || yādṛśi(!) pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśi(!) likhitaṃ mayā || yadi śuddham aśudddho(!) vā mama doṣo na dīyate || rāma rāma rāma rāmaḥ || (fol. 48r1‒3)
notes: The scribe line 'muḍiṣusthānavāstavyaṃ liṣyate(!) ravinaṃdane' is ungrammatical. It means roughly 'written (likhyate) by Ravinandana, resident of Muḍiṣu-sthāna', with the instrumental expected but the locative written. Another reading is possible: 'ravinandane' as a locative meaning 'on the day of Ravi's son (Śani)', i.e. Saturday. That reading leaves no scribe name, and Saturday conflicts with 'śukravāsare' (Friday), so the personal-name reading is kept, with low confidence. Muḍiṣu is not identified. The sentence gives the scribe's residence and only implies the place of copying. ŚS 1707 = c. 1785 CE, which agrees with the catalogue. A Revatī nakṣatra on Āṣāḍha kṛṣṇa 10 is astronomically plausible; the weekday has not been checked. Vācaspati's title 'miśra' has been moved to titles.
review: p1 Vācaspatimiśra: role reduced to 'author'. He wrote the Tattvakaumudī, which is itself a commentary on the Sāṃkhyakārikā, so 'commentator' only repeated the same fact.

p2 Ravinandana: confidence lowered to low. 'ravinaṃdane' could also be a locative meaning 'on the day of the son of Ravi', i.e. Saturday (Śani), but that would contradict 'śukravāsare' (Friday). This alternative is now in the notes.
Place: as_written changed to the compound as it appears ('muḍiṣusthāna-vāstavyaṃ'). It is a residence statement, not an explicit statement of where the copy was made.
Notes expanded.

title: Bhagavatīkīlaka
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Friday 9 Oct 1807, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: ī(!)ti śrībhagavatyā[ḥ] ki(!)lakaṃ samāptam || samvat 1864 sālamī(!)ti āśvī(!)na⟪‥⟫sudi mahā-aṣṭami 8 roja 6 mukāma bhīm siṃla śubhaṃ || (dava ⟪‥⟩⟩ṣarāḥ guljāravaghai) (fol. 12r6–7)
notes: The era is not stated, but 'samvat 1864' with the Persian-Nepali words sāla, roja and mukāma points to Vikrama Saṃvat, which gives about 1807 CE and matches the catalogue's 'SAM 1864'. Mahā-aṣṭamī is the Dasain aṣṭamī in Āśvina śukla 8, so the date falls in roughly Sept/Oct 1807; the weekday has not been checked. 'mukāma bhīm siṃla' gives the place of copying (Bhīmsiṃla, not identified). The parenthetical '(dava ⟪‥⟫ṣarāḥ guljāravaghai)' is unclear. It may be a later note or signature: 'dava..ṣarāḥ' might stand for dastakhat ('signature') or for akṣarāḥ ('letters'), followed by the name Gulzār/Guljāra and 'vaghai' (= vagaira, 'etc.'), or 'Guljāravaghai' may be one name. This may be the scribe's signature, but the colophon does not say so, so Guljāra's role is left as 'other' with low confidence.
review: Persons, date and place kept as they were; notes now explain why 'dava ‥ṣarāḥ' may be a signature or a word for 'letters', and note that Guljāra cannot safely be called the scribe

title: Hariprakāśa
subject: (Vaiṣṇava) Darśana ?
date_note: = Monday 31 Aug 1846, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti śrīvihāfīsotikṛta śatasaī-hriprakāśa saṃpūrṇam(!) ❖ (fol. 56r7-56v1) || iti śrīhariprakāśaḥ samāptaḥ śubham samvat 1903 sāla miti bhādra śudi 9 somavāsaraḥ tasmin dine saṃpūrṇam likhitaṃ lalitāpurīya śrīmahābauddhopāsakaśrījīvānandeti śubhaṃ bhūyāt ❖ (fol. 57r1-3)
notes: The phrase 'śrīvihāfīsotikṛta' is corrupt. It must refer to Bihārī (Vihārī/Bihārīdāsa), who wrote the Satsaī (śatasaī). The Hariprakāśa is a commentary on the Satsaī, usually attributed to Haricaraṇadāsa, but this colophon does not name him. Bihārī is recorded as author of the base text. The era VS fits the Nepali formula 'sāla miti', and the year 1903 matches the catalogue. I did not verify the weekday. 'lalitāpurīya' says that the scribe belongs to Lalitapura (Patan). It is not a direct statement of where the copy was made, though the catalogue gives Lalitapura as the place of copying. 'mahābauddhopāsaka' can be read two ways: 'great Buddhist lay devotee', or a lay devotee of the Mahābauddha temple in Patan.
review: p1: residence normalised to Lalitapura (Patan); 'mahābauddhopāsaka' kept as a title, with a note that it could also mean a lay devotee attached to the Mahābauddha temple in Patan
p2: given Bihārī's evident identity, confidence raised from low to medium; noted that he wrote the base text (Satsaī), not the Hariprakāśa commentary
weekday normalised to Monday (somavāra)
paksa normalised to śukla
place: noted that 'lalitāpurīya' describes where the scribe lives; it is not an explicit place of copying

title: Śivamahimnastotra and Mahimākhyastutivyākhyā
subject: Stotra
date_note: = Aug 1862, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: iti śrīpuṣpadantaviracitā mahimnākhya⟨ḥ⟩stutiḥ samāptam(!) || || (fol. 39v9) || iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryyaśrīmadviśveśvarasarasvatīcaraṇāravinda-madhukareṇa madhusūdanasarasvatī‥mākhyādhareṇa kecid (!) viracitā mahimākhyāstutivyākhyā samāptā || || ślokāntyayojyā(!) paṭhanīyaślokaḥ || || asitagirisamaṃ syāt kajjalaṃ siṃdhupātraṃ(!) surataruvaraśākhālekhanī patram urvī || likhati yadi gṛhītvā sāradā sarvakālaṃ tad api tava guṇānām īśa pāraṃ na yāti || 3 || … dīkṣādānaṃ tapas tīrthaṃ homaṃ yāgādikāḥ kriyāḥ || mahimnaḥ pāṭhamātrasya kalān nārhanti ṣoḍaśīṃ || 41 || || iti śrīpuṣpadantanāmagaṃdharvarājaviracitaṃ mahimanaḥ stotraṃ samāptam || || naipālikābde karanāganande māse site bhādrapade tuhīne || śrīsiṃhanarsiṃhasurārcitas taṃ lilekha svārthaṃ mahimākhyapustaṃ || 1 || (fol. 39v12–40r2 and 10–12)
notes: The chronogram kara (2), nāga (8), nanda (9), read right to left, gives NS 982, about 1862 CE. This matches the catalogue. 'site' is the bright fortnight (śukla). 'tuhīne' is not a tithi word; it may be a metrical filler or a corrupt reading of a tithi, so the tithi is left empty. The scribe's name appears in the verse as 'śrīsiṃhanarsiṃhasurārcitas', which corresponds to the catalogue's Narasiṃha Siṃha. Siṃha (family name) seems to come before the personal name Narsiṃha (= Narasiṃha). 'surārcitas' ('honoured by the gods'?) is unclear: it may be an epithet, or part of the name. Madhusūdanasarasvatī is the author of the commentary, and Viśveśvarasarasvatī is named only as their guru. Neither had anything to do with making this copy. 'kecid (!)' in the commentary colophon is corrupt (perhaps for 'kenacid').
review: p2 Viśveśvarasarasvatī: role changed from 'teacher' to 'other'. They are the commentator's guru and had nothing to do with making this copy; the pupil_of relation is kept.

p4 scribe: name normalised to Narasiṃha. The written form is 'narsiṃha', and 'siṃha' is moved to titles as a family name. This matches the catalogue's 'Narasiṃha Siṃha'. Confidence lowered to medium because the verse word order is odd and 'surārcitas' is unclear.
date.tithi: 'tuhīne' removed. It is not a tithi word; it is probably a metrical filler or a corrupt reading. Noted below.
p2 titles split into 'paramahaṃsa' and 'parivrājakācārya'.
purpose normalised to 'svārtha (for the scribe's own use)'.
Chronogram checked: kara 2, nāga 8, nanda 9, read right to left = 982. NS 982 + 880 = 1862 CE. Confirmed.

notes: 'phaḍakopanāmaka' = phaḍake + upanāmaka, 'whose surname is Phaḍake'. This is the Marathi brahmin surname Phaḍke/Phadke, which suggests the scribe was Maharashtrian. The scribe is not tagged as owner because the copy was made for others as well as for himself ('svārthaṃ parārthaṃ'), and the colophon does not say the book is his. The colophon has no date and no place.

Normalized purpose to 'svārtha and parārtha (for himself and for others)'.
Expanded the notes: surname reading, the odd 'jayati', no date or place, and why the scribe is not also tagged as owner.

title: Saṃvatsarakṛtyaprakāśa
subject: Dharmaśāstra
date_note: = Sunday 30 May 1756, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: iti śrīmatsāmaṃtacakracūḍāmaṇiruciracitanīrājanānīrājitakāśīśvarapaṃcamagahira-vāravividhavirūdāvalīvirājamānamahārājādhirājaśrīmadiṃdramaṇinṛpatinaṃdana-śrīmatkumārayaśavaṃtasiṃhapreritaśrīmatkāśyapānvayasaṃbhavāgnihotrikula-tilakāyamānaśrīmadāyājibhaṭṭasūnubhāskaraviracite yaśavaṃta⟪siṃhapreritaśrīmatka⟫bhāskare saṃva[tsa]rakṛtyaprakāśaḥ saṃvat 1813 varṣe jyeṣṭhamāse śuklapakṣe dvitīyā guruvāsare likhitaṃ gamoḍhacāturvedītrīpāṭhi /// śvarapuruṣottama śubhaṃ bhūyāt || śīkāśīviśveśvarasaṃnidhau lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ śu /// || śrīrāmajī satya || || śrī || || ❁ || || śrī || || ❁ || || śrī || śrī || || ❁ || || (fol. 112v4–11)
notes: The patron (Yaśavantasiṃha, son of Indramaṇi) and the author (Bhāskara, son of Āyājibhaṭṭa) belong to the composition of the Yaśavantabhāskara. They are not connected with this VS 1813 copy, so no reigning king is named. The scribe's name is damaged: 'Gamoḍha' (a brahmin subcaste?), 'cāturvedī' and 'trīpāṭhi' are titles or surnames, and the personal name after the lacuna reads '...śvara-puruṣottama'. It could be a compound name (e.g. ...śvara as the father's name) or an epithet. The catalogue's scribe field 'Gamoḍha Cāturvedī Trīpāṭhī' records only the titles. 'śīkāśī' is probably an error for 'śrīkāśī': the copy was made near Viśveśvara in Kāśī. VS 1813 = 1756 CE; the weekday has not been checked. The doubled phrase ⟪siṃhapreritaśrīmatka⟫ is a scribal dittography marked by the cataloguer.
review: p2 Yaśavantasiṃha: role changed from 'commissioner' to 'other'. 'prerita' means he urged Bhāskara to compose the work (the Yaśavantabhāskara). He did not have this copy made. Name normalised to 'Yaśavantasiṃha'.
p1 Indramaṇi: 'king' removed. He is named only as the father of the patron of the original work, not as the king reigning when this copy was made in VS 1813. Role is now relative_only.
p3 Āyājibhaṭṭa: confidence lowered to medium because the form may be corrupt (Āpājī?). Lineage moved to Bhāskara, with whom the compound connects it.
p5 scribe: 'Gamoḍha' moved to titles as a caste or subcaste name. Confidence lowered to low because of the lacuna before '...śvara-puruṣottama'.
place: normalised to 'Vārāṇasī'. 'śīkāśī' is taken as an error for 'śrīkāśī'.
notes expanded.

files: mirror/B 458-17 Kātaṃtravṛttipañjikā; a commentary on Durga Siṃha’s Kātantra.html
purpose: transliterated from Bengali script at the order of a munirāṭ
notes: The colophon has two layers. (1) 'śakābde 1586 || pratilikhitaṃ' (ŚS 1586 = 1664 CE) comes right after the author's colophon. It is followed by the note 'baṃgālyakṣarato bhisāritam', so it most likely gives the date of the Bengali-script exemplar, not of this copy. (2) The final verse dates the Nepal copy. Reading the chronogram from right to left, 'vidhu-vāṇa-ratna' (1-5-9) gives Nepal Saṃvat 951. 'drībhebhabheṭ' (Vikrama) is corrupt; the catalogue suggests VS 1887 (= 1830). The Śaka part 'kṣā-śuga ‥ la-bhūmi' is damaged and read as ŚS 1751(?), though ŚS 1752 would match Kārttika 1830. The month is ūrja (Kārttika), on the full moon (rākā). The three eras roughly agree on 1829–1830 CE; ŚS 1751 is a year off from NS 951 / VS 1887. The scribe is not named. He calls himself 76 years old ('ṣaṭsaptativārṣikena') and says he acted at the order of an unnamed 'munirāṭ' ('munirāḍājñāpareṇāmunā'). The munirāṭ may be his teacher or patron, perhaps the effective commissioner, but no name is given, so no person entry was created. 'bhisāritam' = abhisāritam (transliterated). The verse between the two dates ('no atra nanv atra pade…') is a grammatical note and names no persons.
review: Date: the main date of this copy is now the Nepal verse date NS 951, Kārttika (ūrja) full moon (rākā) = c. 1830 CE. Śakābde 1586 / pratilikhitaṃ comes before the Bengali-script note and is most likely the date of the exemplar, not of this Devanagari copy.
ce_approx changed from 1664 to 1830 (Kārttika NS 951 falls in Oct–Nov 1830).
date.as_written now keeps only the verse date; the 1586 date and the clashes between eras are explained in notes.

title: Sacatuṣṭapāṇinīyaśikṣya
subject: Vyākaraṇa
date_raw: saṃvan saptadaśe śate badhur ddaśe varṣenduṣaśūklādvādaśī guro(!)
date_note: = Thursday 17 Jan 1658, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: iti pañcamo ʼdhyāyaḥ | samātaḥ | saṃvan saptadaśe śate badhur ddaśe varṣenduṣaśūklādvādaśī guro(!) | upādevajīnena mohanajīkena likhiteyaṃ pustikā | śivam astu lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ | śrīḥ | ❁ | śrīḥ ālohannamīnīpothī | ḍhānovamaḍīmītākī | rādhīyasarasīño hī | (fol. 22v3–5) || iti paṃcamo ʼdhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ | (fol. 70r5–6)
notes: 'saṃvan saptadaśe śate badhur ddaśe varṣe' means 'in the 17th century of the era (the 1700s), in the year …-daśa'. 'badhur ddaśe' is corrupt. Reading it as caturdaśe gives 1714, but other readings (e.g. vidhu = 1 → 1711) are possible. The era is not named; VS is assumed (Devanagari script, North Indian formula), which gives about 1657/58 CE. The month 'induṣa' (from 'varṣenduṣa') is probably corrupt, perhaps for pauṣa. 'upādevajīnena' is unclear. It could be a haplography for upā[dhyāya]-devajī-[sū]nunā ('son of Upādhyāya Devajī'), which is the reading used here. Alternatively the title upādhyāya may belong to the scribe, or Devajī may be a co-scribe. The scribe's name follows the catalogue (Mohanajīka); -jī is an honorific, so the base name may be Mohana. The lines 'ālohannamīnīpothī | ḍhānovamaḍīmītākī | rādhīyasarasīño hī' look like a corrupt Hindi/Braj verse, possibly an owner's or reader's jotting ('pothī' = book). No person can be read from them with confidence.

notes: The scribe's name follows a lacuna: '(‥)vāviṣṇupatinā' (catalogued as '?vāviṣṇupati'). The 'vā' may be the end of a lost first part of the name (e.g. a compound name or a title), so the scribe is given as Viṣṇupati with medium confidence. The place name '(acauśī)' is in the cataloguer's brackets, so the reading is uncertain. It is the scribe's place of residence ('grāmāvasthitena'), and here it is assumed to be where the copy was made. '(mairujyārastu)' is corrupt, probably part of the benedictory formula, and not a name. LS 376 + 1119 = c. 1495 CE. The date has not been checked against a calendar.
review: Weekday normalized to 'Sunday (ravai)'; tithi kept as aṣṭamī.
Place: noted that the colophon gives only the scribe's residence ('grāmāvasthitena'); this is taken as the place of copying by inference.

Notes expanded: the syllable 'vā' before Viṣṇupati may belong to a longer name or prefix lost in the lacuna; '(mairujyārastu)' is corrupt and not a person's name; the verse after the colophon is a benedictory verse with no names.

title: Godānaprayoga
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
colophon: iti sāmānyagodānavidhiḥ | ghṛtadānaṃ ca || idaṃ pustakaṃ soreśvarasāḍhe ity upanāmakena || (fol. 3v9)
notes: The colophon reads 'soreśvarasāḍhe', but the catalogue gives Moreśvara Sāḍhe. This is probably a ma/sa confusion, either in the manuscript or in the transcription. Moreśvara is the likely name. 'Sāḍhe' is a Marathi family name, perhaps a form of Sāṭhe, and the text itself calls it an upanāman. That points to a Maharashtrian brahmin scribe. The sentence 'idaṃ pustakaṃ ... ity upanāmakena' has no verb. The instrumental agent suggests 'likhitam' (copied) dropped out, which would make him the scribe, as the catalogue says. An ownership statement cannot be ruled out. The manuscript has no date and no place of copying.
review: Name normalized to Moreśvara, following the catalogue. In Devanagari म and स are easily confused, and Moreśvara is a common Marathi name while Soreśvara is unattested. The written form is kept in as_written.
Changed as_written to the name alone. 'ity upanāmakena' is only the phrase that introduces the surname.
Kept the role as scribe at medium confidence. The sentence breaks off before its verb; the instrumental suggests something like 'likhitam' was meant, but it could also have recorded ownership.
Expanded the notes.

title: Bhavānīsahasranāmastotra
subject: Stotra

date_flat.year: 1730? (kha 0, agni 3, (a)ga 7?, rūpa 1; read right to left)

colophon: iti śrīrudrayāmale naṃdikeśvarasaṃvāde bhavānīsahasranāmastotraṃ samāptaṃ || śubham || || śāke khāgnigarūpabheditiśubhe yoge jñavārorjjage sūrye mārgavadī tithert(!) tudivase lagne ghaṭa(!) saṃyute || likhet śarmagaṇgādharakaraḍiyādhīmāṃ paṭhet sarvadā nāpatyaṃ vijayai sadābhila(!)khitaiḥ satputrapautrārthakaiḥ || || śrī3bhavānīśaṃkarebhya[ḥ] namaḥ (fol. 34r2–5)
purpose: for constant recitation, for victory and for good sons and grandsons (satputrapautrārthakaiḥ)
notes: The chronogram 'khāgnigarūpa' is unclear. Kha = 0, agni = 3 and rūpa = 1 are secure. 'ga' is probably 'aga' (mountain = 7), which gives ŚS 1730 = c. 1808 CE. The catalogue gives only ŚS 1?30, so the middle digit and the CE date are tentative. 'bhediti' is probably a corruption of 'bhedite'. 'tithert(!) tudivase' is read as 'tithe ṛtu-divase' (6th tithi). 'ūrjjage sūrye' puts the sun in Ūrja (Kārttika), which sits oddly with lunar Mārga vadī unless the months are reckoned differently (amānta/pūrṇimānta). The verse is corrupt and pāda c is unmetrical (cataloguer's note). 'Karaḍiyā' is most likely the Karāḍa (Karhāḍā) brahmin group or a family name. 'dhīmān' is an epithet. 'paṭhet sarvadā' is a generic phala statement: it names no reader or owner.

title: Mṛtyuñjayastavarāja
subject: Stotra
colophon: iti śrīpārameśvaratantre caturaśītisa(!)hasre śrīmṛtyuṃjayastavarāja samāptam || || yad akṣata(!)padabhraṣṭa[ṃ] mātrāhīnaṃ ca yad bhavet tat sarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva prasīda parameśvara || śivārpaṇam astu || lekhakapāṭhakayo śubhaṃ yo(!) ti(!)rthadadattapanthaśarmaṇaṃ(!) || || || || (fol. 7r5–7v3)
notes: The closing formula is corrupt: 'lekhakapāṭhakayo śubhaṃ yo(!) ti(!)rthadadattapanthaśarmaṇaṃ(!)'. 'yo(!)' may be a damaged 'bhūyāt' ('may there be good fortune for scribe and reader'). The name follows, probably meant as 'tīrthadattapantaśarmaṇaḥ', a genitive: 'of Tīrthadatta Panta Śarman'. 'tirthadadatta' has a doubled 'da' (dittography). 'Pantha' is probably the Nepali brahmin surname Panta (Pant). The genitive suggests owner ('the book of …'), but he may be the scribe. The colophon is undated and names no place.
review: p1 role changed from 'other' to 'owner'. The name ends in a genitive, 'śarmaṇaṃ(!)', which should be 'śarmaṇaḥ', meaning 'of Tīrthadatta Panta Śarman'. This genitive closes the colophon, which most naturally marks ownership. Confidence lowered to low because he could also be the scribe.
p1 evidence trimmed to the name itself. 'Pantha' is normalized to the surname Panta (Pant) in titles. The extra 'da' in 'tirthadadatta' is treated as dittography.
Purpose rephrased: 'śivārpaṇam astu' is a dedication formula, not a statement of who the copy was for.
Notes expanded.
