title: Abhisamayālokānyāṣṭasahasrikāprajñāpāramitāvyākhyā
subject: Bauddha Sūtra
date_note: = Sunday 1 Jul 1894, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: abhisamayālaṃkāroʼnyāṣṭasahasrikāprajñāpāramitāvyākhyā samāptā || || kṛtir iyam ācāryyabharibhadrapādānāṃ || || pakṣavānanandagoyute samvate || āṣāḍhakṛṣṇatrayodasyān tithau dine || likhiteyaṃ vajrācāryyajyotimānandena śubhaṃ bhūyāt || || || || || || || || || || || || śrīśāke 1816 śrīsamvat 1951 nepālīsamvat 1015 miti caitravadi 8 roja śubham (fol. 167r3–6)
notes: The colophon has two dates. (1) The verse chronogram pakṣa(2) vāṇa(5) nanda(9) go(1) = 1952, Āṣāḍha kṛṣṇa 13. The era is not named but is presumably VS: about June/July 1895. (2) The closing note: Śāke 1816, saṃvat 1951, NS 1015, Caitra vadi 8. These three years agree with each other, giving about March/April 1895. The two dates are only months apart and do not conflict. The Āṣāḍha date goes with 'likhiteyaṃ', so it probably marks when copying finished. The catalogue's VS 1952 matches the chronogram, not the 1951 of the closing note. 'bharibhadra' is a corrupt form of Haribhadra. The catalogue spells the scribe's name 'Jyotimānada'; the colophon reads Jyotimānanda.
review: Decoded the chronogram: pakṣa=2, vāṇa=5, nanda=9, go=1, read right to left = 1952 (presumably VS).
Main date changed to the verse date that goes with 'likhiteyaṃ': VS 1952 Āṣāḍha kṛṣṇa 13, about mid-1895 CE. The closing Śāke 1816 / VS 1951 / NS 1015 Caitra vadi 8 date is moved to notes.

title: Guṇakāraṇḍavyūha
subject: Bauddha(Mahāyāna) Sūtra
date_note: ≈ 1843 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: iti śrījinaśrī(rā)japaripṛcchajayaśrīsambhāṣitaśrīmadāryyāvalokoteśvarase(!) guṇakāraṇḍavyūhāyā(!) mahāyānasūtraṃ rājaṃ dvāviṃśatitame(!) prakaraṇaṃ samāpta(!) || ❁ || ye dharmmā hetu⟨ta⟩prabhā(!)vā hetu(!) teṣāṃ tathāgata(!) hy avaja(!) teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha(!) yavaṃvādi (!) mahāśramaṇaṃ || ❁ || śubhasaṃvat 963 stiṣoṣasudi 13 sahnayāyā gumajiya ñāhnu guta nā ṅo coyā jula | liṣitaṃ vajrācāryyanaumilokadralivāyijoḥ || || dānapatijajomānaragaṃto lakṣyā vāhāra sivikṣā ka ‥ ‥ ta juvura dhuranaṃ sva ikṣā mana bā ‥ | naṃ thva gunakāra dhuviha pustakadayakā jura śubhaṃ || trailāt dakṣa jalādakṣa muṣīkām agnisādinaṃ mūrṣahaste na dātavyaṃ evaṃ vadanti pustakāḥ || || thvate yā puṇyanaṃ dānapati yājana dhanasaṃtāna saptavṛddhiphala tvaritaṃ prāptanuyāt bhavantu śubhaṃ || || (fol. 200v1–6)
purpose: Merit transfer: by this merit, may the dānapati (yajamāna) quickly obtain wealth, offspring and sevenfold increase
notes: The month 'stiṣoṣa' is corrupt and cannot be identified with confidence. 'sahnayāyā gumajiya ñāhnu' looks like a festival or day name, not a weekday. 'guta nā ṅo coyā jula' means the copy was finished. The scribe string 'naumilokadralivāyijoḥ' is unclear. 'joḥ' is probably an honorific ending (cf. Newari -ju), and 'dralivāyi' could be part of the name or a locality, so the catalogue's 'Naumiloka' is kept. In the donor's name, 'dānapati jajomāna' = yajamāna, and 'ragaṃto' is probably the Newari 'rogaṃto' ('together with the household'). 'lakṣyā vāhāra' looks like a Patan bāhā. 'sivikṣā' probably stands for śākyabhikṣu, but that reading is uncertain. The personal name is lost in a lacuna. The phrase 'juvura dhuranaṃ sva ikṣā mana bā ‥' may name further family members, but it is too garbled to extract. 'pustakadayakā jura' = 'had the book made', so the donor is the commissioner.
review: p1 scribe: confidence lowered to medium, because the name is run together with the unclear string 'dralivāyijoḥ'. The name could be longer than 'Naumiloka', and the evidence substring now includes it.
p2: 'lakṣyā vāhāra' moved from residence to affiliation, since it reads as a vihāra (bāhā) name. Evidence now quotes the dānapati phrase. The śākyabhikṣu title is kept, but it is uncertain.
Purpose shortened to a summary of the merit transfer instead of the raw quotation.
Date: the month 'stiṣoṣa' is flagged as corrupt. NS 963 + 880 = 1843 CE is confirmed.
Notes expanded.

colophon: iti śrīmadbhagavataḥ śākyasiṃhasya jātakamālāvadānasūtraṃ samāptam || || śubham || || śrīśāke 1818 śrīsamvat 1951 śrīnepāliyasaṃvat 1015 sāla miti pauṣa śukla 8 roja śubhm

review: Primary era changed from ŚS 1818 to VS 1951. VS 1951 and NS 1015 agree with each other; ŚS 1818 does not. Under ŚS+78, ŚS 1818 would give 1896, not the 1895 the first reading recorded.
ce_approx stays 1895: Pauṣa śukla 8 of VS 1951 / NS 1015 falls in January 1895.

(fol. 334r8–v4)
purpose: merit for the welfare of the world (jagaddhite)
notes: The scribal colophon is badly damaged and names no scribe. The dated Newari entries after it are reading notes. (1) NS 894 (1774 CE): Amṛtānanda began a vyākhyā (recitation and exposition) of the Mahajjātakamālā on Śrāvaṇa śu 1, Monday, and finished it on Bhādrapada kṛ 9. Dhanasiṃha is named in a gap and his role is unclear; he may have been the patron or a listener. (2) NS 927 (1807 CE), Āśvina śu 15, Friday: Pūrṇānanda gave a Jātakamālā vyākhyā in the city called Amarāvatī (nugasa = 'in the centre'?). The place is not identified; Amarāvatī may be a poetic name for a Newar town. Jagajjitānanda's role is lost in a lacuna. The copy was therefore made in or before NS 894. The catalogue's scribe and date fields probably come from these notes. Amṛtānanda may be the well-known paṇḍita Amṛtānanda (fl. late 18th to early 19th century), but this is not certain.
review: Amṛtānanda: roles scribe+commentator changed to reader. In Newari, 'jātakamālāvyākhyā … yāṅā … saṃpūrṇaṃ' records a ritual recitation and exposition (vyākhyāna) of the text that ran from Śrāvaṇa śu 1 to Bhādrapada kṛ 9. It does not record copying or writing a commentary.
Pūrṇānanda: roles scribe+other changed to reader, because the same vyākhyā formula is used. Amarāvatī moved out of residence: it is where the reading took place, not a stated home.
No scribe is named in the colophon. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Amṛtānanda? Pūrṇānanda?' is a misreading of the reading notes.

title: Lalitavistara
subject: Bauddha Sūtra
date_note: = Friday 28 Apr 1559, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: pūrṇimānta months
colophon: iti nigamamam aparivarto nāma saptā(!)viṃśatitamaḥ || ❁ || śrīsarvabodhisatvacaryāprasthāno lalitavistaro nāma mahāyānasūtraṃ ratnarājam iti samāptaḥ || ❁ || ye dharmā hetuprabhā(!)vā hetu[s] teṣāṃ tathāgataḥ | hyavadad [teṣāṃ ca yo] nirodhaḥ evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ || ❁ || śubham astu sarvvadādāt (!) || || śreyostu || nepārābde ratnamunidhātu jeṣṭavadi 7 śukravāla thva kuhnu śrī śrīlalitavistara saṃpūrṇa || likhita śrīmānadevasaṃskārita cakramahārāvasthita śrīśrīvajrācāryya guṇasāgraju śrīvajrācārya kuladatta deva ju nihma sana coya dhuṃkā juro || || dānapati ⟪...⟫ sākyavaṃśaśrīdharmarājajuna dayakā juro || || yādiṣṭa puṣṭakaṃ ditvā tā diṣṭā likhitaṃ mayā || yadi śuddham aśodhaṃ vā mama doṣaṃ na diyate || śubhaṃ bhūyāt || ❁ || śrīdhanasiṃju dhanapati siṃju manohari (rahnā)vatī dhananā nadhimayaju dhanamā++bhāju dhana thvati svana manaharṣamānajuyā va dayakā juro || ❁ || (fol. 241v4–242r4)
notes: Chronogram, read right to left: ratna = 9, muni = 7, dhātu = ?. This gives NS 679 (CE 1559), the catalogue date, only if dhātu = 6, as in the Buddhist six dhātus (ṣaḍdhātu). That reading fits a Buddhist Newar colophon. The usual value is dhātu = 7, which would give NS 779 (CE 1659). A rough mean-lunation check of Jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa 7 puts it on about a Sunday in 1559 and about a Thursday in 1659, so it is not clearly a Friday in either year and does not settle the question. I kept NS 679. The place reads 'cakramahārāvasthita', probably a corruption of cakramahāvihārāvasthita (cataloguer's note). It describes where the two scribes live, not explicitly where the copy was made, and I have not confirmed which present-day vihāra it is. The final sentence ('śrīdhanasiṃju ... dhana thvati svana manaharṣamānajuyā va dayakā juro') is unclear. It looks like a list of family members, probably of Manaharṣamāna, who also had the copy made; it may be a later addition. Where the names divide is uncertain ('dhananā nadhimayaju', 'dhanamā++bhāju', the stray 'dhana'). 'mayaju' and 'bhāju' are honorifics. The name of the d̄ānapati Dharmarāja is preceded by a deletion (⟪...⟫).
review: p2: name changed from Kuladattadeva to Kuladatta. The 'deva ju' in 'kuladatta deva ju' reads as an honorific, and he is not a king.
p4–p10: roles changed from donor to commissioner. 'dayakā juro' means they had the copy made; none of them is called dānapati.
p8/p9: 'mayaju' and 'bhāju' are honorifics (for a woman and a man), not real titles; both kept at low confidence.
place.normalized: 'Patan' removed. The emendation to Cakramahāvihāra is likely, but which present-day vihāra this is cannot be confirmed from the colophon.
Notes: explained why dhātu = 6 here and gave the alternative year; flagged the final list of names as unclear.

notes: The donor passage is corrupt. 'paramopāśikaḥ' looks like the feminine upāsikā, while '‥jasarāmakasya' is a masculine genitive. notes: Aśoka and Upagupta are the framing speakers of the avadāna and are left out. 'asanipāṇi' should be read 'aśanipāṇi' (aśani = vajra). The verb 'lekhayāmi' is causative ('I have it written') but comes with the instrumental 'dhīmatā ... -vajreṇa' ('by the wise ...'), which is a mixed construction. Following the catalogue, he is treated as the scribe, but he may have been the commissioner.
review: p1 confidence lowered from high to medium. 'lekhayāmi' is a causative verb in the 1st person, but it comes with an instrumental agent, which is ungrammatical. So it is unclear whether he wrote the copy himself or had it written. Scribe is kept as the most likely reading.
Notes now explain that 'aśanipāṇi' (aśani = vajra) is a Sanskritised form of 'vajrācārya' or 'vajrapāṇi'. It stays a title.

title: Mahālakṣmīmāhātmya OR Mahālakṣmīvratamāhātmya
subject: Māhātmya
date_note: = Wednesday 18 Sep 1387, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: iti mahālakṣmīmāhātmye prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ || 1 || (fol. 4v) iti mahālakṣmīmāhātmye dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || 2 || (fol. 6v) ... iti gālavaprokte mahālakṣmīmāhātmye .. .. .. rī saṃprāptā nāma pañcadaśamaḥ paṭalaḥ || 15 || (fol. 30r) || iti gālavaprokte mahālakṣmīmāhātmye vyākhyā .. .. .. .. .. ṣoḍaśaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ || 16 || rājāśrīsthitirājamallanṛpatau rājādhirāje pi sa .. bde saptakhakāmabāṇasahite mayā .i(ken)i(r).. .. .. (fol. 43v) (śukle r-ā)śvini pañcamītithiyute candrātmajevāsare vyākhyānaṃ likhitaṃ trivarggaphaladaṃ śraddhāvatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ || śubham astu sarvvasatvāḥ (sa) .i .. .. .. .. (fol. 43r4–v1)
notes: The chronogram 'sapta (7) kha (0) kāmabāṇa (5)', read right to left, gives 507. The colophon does not name the era ('sa .. bde' is damaged), but Sthiti(rāja)malla reigned c. NS 502–515 (1382–1395 CE), so the era must be NS. That matches the catalogue. NS 507 runs from about October 1386 to October 1387, so Āśvina śukla 5 falls in September/October 1387 CE. Candrātmaja (Budha) = Wednesday. After 'mayā' a scribe's name may have stood, but only '.i(ken)i(r).. .. ..' survives. This is unreadable and may not even be a name, so no scribe is recorded. 'śraddhāvatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ' describes the text's benefit to faithful listeners; it is not a purpose of copying.
review: Dropped p2: '.i(ken)i(r)..' is an illegible fragment after 'mayā', not a readable name. It may not be a name at all (e.g. a form of kenacit). The scribe is anonymous in effect, so the fragment is kept in notes only

Notes: confirmed the chronogram and era, and explained why ce_approx is 1387 (Āśvina falls at the end of NS 507)

notes: The colophon names no era ('saṃvacchara ... 341'). NS is inferred because the year fits the reign of Abhayamalla (c. NS 336–375 / 1216–1255 CE). This agrees with the catalogue (NS 341 ≈ 1221 CE). The king's name is written abha(!)malla for Abhayamalla. The colophon also calls Hāla Śātavāhana (śrīśātavāhanakośe). The scribe's name appears only inside a later insertion [[ni.ulāvaracaṃdreṇa]], which replaces a deleted passage ⟪...⟫. It may come from a second hand and is partly unreadable: a possible reading is Nikulāvaracandra or similar. 'svārthaṃ parārthahetvarthaṃ' may mean the scribe also owned the copy, but the colophon does not say so clearly, so the owner role was not added. The verse after it (yena trayeta(?)trimuni...) has lacunae and no usable names.
review: Date: the colophon gives no era name. NS is inferred from the reign of Abhayamalla (c. 1216–1255 CE, about NS 336–375), which fits year 341. Kept NS 341 / 1221 CE and added a note explaining this.
Hāla: added the colophon's other name for Hāla, Śātavāhana ('śrīśātavāhanakośe'), to the notes. Hāla is the author of the root text, the kośa.
Scribe: noted that the name sits in an insertion [[...]] that replaces a deleted passage ⟪...⟫, so it may have been written by a second hand. The reading stays doubtful.
Purpose shortened to a summary.
Everything else confirmed: Tribhuvanapāla as commentator, Abhayamalladeva as reigning king, the under_reign_of relation, and Jyeṣṭha 341.

title: Suśrutasaṃhitā + Sauśrutanighaṇṭu
subject: Āyurveda
date_raw: Mānadeva Saṃvat 301 (Sunday, 13th April, 878 C.E.; see below)
date_note: = Sunday 13 Apr 878, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: Since the manuscript consists of folios from different manuscripts of the Suśrutasaṃhitā and its supplement, there are at least two different colophons. The following is the colophon of the Suśrutasaṃhitā proper in the folio numbered 209 with letter numerals and 109 in Devanagari numerals: yathākramaṃ yathāpraśnaṃ yathātatvaṃ yathāvidhi[ṃ](!)| yathāpratijñañ ca mayā bhavatāṃ prakīrttitaṃ|| sahottaran tv etad adhītya tantraṃ svāyaṃbhuvaṃ [taṃ] ⟪vidhinā⟫ kīrttitena| na hīyate rtthāṃ manaso bhyupetād evaṃ vaco .rā(hya)m atīva satyam iti|| mūtradoṣo mūtraghāto yonyamānuṣa eva ca|| apasmāronmādakaś caiva rasabhedas tathaiva ca| svastharakṣāvidhāṇañ(!) ca tantrayuktiś ca doṣabhit| ity ebhir daśakaṃ proktaṃ punaḥ kāyacikitsite|| ❁ || samāptañ cedaṃ sahottaran tantram ity avo(!) nighaṇṭur bha⟪va⟫viṣyati|| ❁ || ⟪.. ..⟫ [[rājñi]] śrī . ānadeve pṛthusitayaśasi prodyadinduprakāśe| kāle puṇyārjjanasya saka[la]janamanohlādiramye ⁅vasante⁆| varśe caikottare smiṃs tritayaśatagate mādhave māsi śukle| saptamyāṃ puṣya ṛkṣe da[..]śatakiraṇāvāsare siddhayoge| utpattyādyambuvelākulavividharujā⁅gr⁆āhajuṣṭhātiro(!)dre saṃsāre sāgare smiñ jagad idam akhilaṃ glāninaṃ sampravīkṣya| tasmāc chrīharṣacandro nniratiśayaghṛṇābhāvito moktukāmaḥ prītyā cai . i///⌣−−⌣⌣⌣⌣⌣⌣taṃ prākhilat(!) suśrutākhyam| śrīgaṇadevadevakuladūnīścalakanivāsino vaidyavasuvarmaṇaḥ pustakam idaṃ paṭhitvārtham avagamya sarvaṃm satvānām upadeśaṃ vidhātuṃ pratipāditam atas tadādhiśruyābhyāṃ na kaścid dātavyam| yadā nopakriyate tadā..a
purpose: Copied out of compassion for the suffering world (moktukāmaḥ); Vasuvarman's book is to be used to instruct beings and not given to anyone else
notes: The king's name is damaged ('śrī . ānadeve'); Mānadeva is the cataloguer's reading, and 'rājñi' is an editorial supplement. The year 301 is not given an era name in the colophon. The catalogue calls it 'Mānadeva Saṃvat' and gives 878 CE, so ce_approx follows the catalogue. The epoch is about 576/577 CE, the same as the Aṃśuvarman/Mānadeva era. Harṣacandra is called the scribe on the strength of 'prākhilat' ('wrote'). He could also have been the person who had the copy made, because the verse is damaged at the point where it might give his role. 'Gaṇadevadevakula' is where Vasuvarman lived. The catalogue lists it as the place of copying, but the colophon only states it as his residence. 'Dūnīścalaka' is unclear: it may be the name of a locality, or a corrupt reading. The text was compiled from folios of several manuscripts. The Nighaṇṭu colophon (fol. 219v) names nobody.

purpose: for attaining bodhi (bodhi saṃlabdhahetoḥ); merit for the donors (etat puṇyānubhāvena phalaṃ prāptotu)
notes: Chronograms: 'nabha-nayana-nava' = 0-2-9 → NS 920, which matches 'samvat 920'. The inserted verse <<...>> ('gagana ca nayana randhra') also gives 920. That verse, however, has 'śuke māse' (perhaps śuci, i.e. Āṣāḍha/Jyeṣṭha) and 'vāsare sūryyaputre' (Saturday), which conflict with the main colophon (Śrāvaṇa, bhumiputra/aṅgāravāra = Tuesday). It may be a rejected first draft. NS 920 Śrāvaṇa śukla 1 falls around 22 July 1800, which was a Tuesday, so it fits the main colophon. The catalogue lists 'Vajrācārya Śripati' as a third scribe. But 'śrepateya' carries the Newari genitive -ya, and only Bhājupati and Bhājudeva carry the Sanskrit instrumental of agency. So they are probably Śrīpati's sons and the actual scribes, though the son relation is inferred. The verse says Matyaṅa made the book, while the Newari prose names his three sons as dānapati. Matyaṅa is therefore marked commissioner with medium confidence.
review: p1 Matyaṅa: removed 'donor' (the Newari names his three sons as dānapati); kept 'commissioner' on the strength of the Sanskrit verse (pustakaṃ yā'karoc ... matyaṅasamabhidhaḥ), confidence lowered to medium; residence wording normalized
p2–p4: confirmed as donor (dānapati) + commissioner (dayakā julo)
wrote_for relations now also point to the dānapati sons p2–p4, not only to p1
son_of relations for the scribes (p6, p7 → p5): rest on the Newari genitive 'śrepateya'; flagged as an inference
Place as_written replaced by the scribes' location (Jasodharavihāra mūladvāla, Lalitapur); the donors' residence moved to the person records

notes: The name 'Dhanavṛ' (marked (!) by the cataloguer) is probably corrupt or abbreviated. Possible readings include Dhanavīra, Dhanavṛddhi and Dhanavajra. The colophon has no date or place.
review: No substantive changes. Notes now add Dhanavīra as another possible reading of the corrupt name.

title: Yatirājasaptatiṭīkā
subject: Vedānta
date_note: = Thursday 29 Mar 1742, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: samaravṛṣadeśikadayāprāptatrayyaṃta(bhā)ṣyatatvena rāmānujena viduṣākhyā(!) yatirājasaptater vihitā iti śrīdeśikakṛtayatirājasaptativyākhyānaṃ samāptaṃ saṃvat 1799 miti kā caitrāṣṭamī bader asti (fol. 31r11-12)
notes: The commentator Rāmānuja calls himself a pupil of Samaravṛṣadeśika. Since vṛṣa and puṅgava both mean 'bull', this is possibly a synonym form of Samarapuṅgava. The root text Yatirājasaptati is by Vedāntadeśika, named as 'śrīdeśika' in the colophon. No scribe, place or purpose is stated. Date: 'saṃvat 1799' can only be VS here (NS 1799 is impossible), giving about 1742 CE, which matches the catalogue. 'miti kā' is unclear: 'kā' might be a stray syllable or an abbreviation. 'bader asti' probably means 'badi' (dark fortnight) plus 'asti'. No weekday can be safely read from it, so the earlier reading 'raver' (Sunday) was dropped.
review: p1 Rāmānuja: removed 'vidvas' from titles; viduṣā is only the epithet 'learned', not a title or office

p2 Samaravṛṣa: role changed from 'teacher' to 'other'. He is the commentator's teacher and played no part in making this copy. Confidence lowered to medium because the name may be a synonym form of Samarapuṅgava
Added p3 Deśika (Vedāntadeśika) as author of the root text Yatirājasaptati, from 'śrīdeśikakṛta-' in the colophon (medium confidence)
Notes: dropped the guess 'bade raver asti' (Sunday) and recorded the doubtful 'kā' and 'bader asti' instead

purpose: Deyadharma (pious gift) by the family of Rugudeva and Jayatasiṃha: merit for children, wealth and health, protection from dangers, and attainment of anuttarajñāna. The copy was consecrated at a lakṣāhuti homa in Devadatta Mahāvihāra.
notes:
Date: the catalogue gives 25 Sept 1732, but that conflicts with the reign of Siddhinarasiṃha Malla of Patan (c. 1619–1661). Reading 'manda' as 'nanda' (9), with rudrānana 5 and giri 7, gives NS 759 = Āśvina 1639 CE. That fits the reign; the 1732 date is probably a cataloguer's error. The digit values are still tentative.

King's name: 'satva' is probably a corruption of 'malla'.

Donors: 'rudrabhā(pre)' between Rugudeva and Jayatasiṃha is unclear. It may be a corrupt 'bhrātṛ', which would make them brothers. The second vihāra name, 'jayatarddhana' (perhaps Jayavardhana?), is corrupt. In 'śrī‥devasya putra dhanadeva' the father's name is lost; it may be Rugudeva. 'dhūtiyānapatiyā mātā uhlāpa' is obscure Newari: Uhlāpā is the mother of someone named there (Dhūti / Ānapati?).

Devasundara: 'yāke kāmyaṃ (kāyāṃ?) coyā' probably means the text was copied from his exemplar, so he is not treated as commissioner.

Scribes: Devendra is named as head of the scribes. 'Hnavanadeva' may stand for Bhuvanadeva. 'jyaṣṭha' before Jinadeva probably means 'elder'. 'Rukravāhāra' may be a garbled Ukubāhāḥ (Rudravarṇa).

Place: Patan context (Uku Bahal, Bu Bahal, Naka Bahī), but the colophon does not say where the copy was made.
review: King: name normalised to Siddhinarasiṃhamalla. 'jaya' is an honorific prefix and 'satva' looks like a corruption of 'malla'. He is Siddhinarasiṃha Malla of Patan (r. c. 1619–1661).

Date: the chronogram is worked out as (n)anda 9, rudrānana 5, giri 7, read right to left, giving NS 759 (Āśvina 1639 CE). That fits his reign. The catalogue's 1732 does not, since Patan had a different king in 1732. ce_approx changed from 1732 to 1639.
Tithi: 'krauñcavidāraṇa' (Skanda) read as ṣaṣṭhī. Nakṣatra Jyeṣṭhā, yoga Śobhana. The weekday is unclear.

Devasundara: role changed from commissioner to other. 'X-yāke kāyāṃ coyā' most likely means the text was taken (copied) from his exemplar, not that he ordered the copy. The wrote_for relation is removed.
Family members in the donor list (Bhatu, Hera, Dhanadeva, Ratikara, Uhlāpā): role changed from relative_only to donor, because they are named as co-donors in the deyadharma formula.
Rugudeva: Rudravarṇa Mahāvihāra is now given as his residence/affiliation (vāstavya), and the second vihāra name is marked as corrupt.
Place: cleared. The colophon does not say where the copy was made; the vihāras named are the donors' and scribes' homes. Patan is only implied.
Scribe titles and residences checked; notes on Hnavanadeva (possibly Bhuvanadeva) and Jinadeva's 'jyeṣṭha' added.

notes: The Kundamālā's author appears as 'kāvar(!) dvāranāgasya'. Read 'kāvar' as kaveḥ ('of the poet'). The play is usually attributed to Dhīranāga, sometimes to Diṅnāga. Dvāranāga is probably a corruption of Dhīranāga; it is kept as written. Chronogram: śaśi = 1, vāṇa = 5, bhūta = 5. Read right to left this gives NS 551 (c. 1431 CE), which matches the catalogue. vahnitithi means tṛtīyā (the 3rd); śitapakṣa means śuklapakṣa (the bright half); āditye means Sunday. 'sayyāsane' (śayyāsane?) is unclear. It may be a corrupt nakṣatra name or part of the wordplay in the verse. 'vūddhike' probably refers to the yoga Vṛddhi. The date verse plays on the subject of the play, Sītā's banishment. No scribe, commissioner or owner is named. The other colophons in the manuscript (Rāmāyaṇasāvitrī, Pañcavaktrastuti, Hariharātmakastava from the Harivaṃśa) contain no personal data.

colophon: iti śrīmohanatantre pārvvatīmahādevasamvāde śrīguroḥ sahasranāmastotraṃ saṃpūrṇṇaṃ || || saṃvat 840 āṣāḍhaśuklapūrṇṇamāsi śukrabāla thva kuhnu vipra śrīpurarājena likhita[ṃ] pustakaṃ || (fol. 26r5–26v4; 1st foliation) || iti śrīrudrajāmale tripurāmaheśvarasaṃvāde gaurīkalpe gurustotraṃ samāptaṃ || sahajānaṃdāya, śrīguruḥ prīṇātu⟨ḥ⟩ || ❁ || (fol. 10r6–10v2; 2nd foliation)
purpose: dedicatory wish at the end of the Gurustotra: may the Guru be pleased, for (or on behalf of) Sahajānanda
notes: The era is not named ('saṃvat 840'). It is taken as NS because the script is Newari, the Newari phrase 'thva kuhnu' is used, and the catalogue says NS 840. NS 840 = c. 1720 CE (Āṣāḍha pūrṇimā, around June/July 1720). The weekday has not been checked. The date and the scribe Purarāja ('vipra' = brahmin) come from the colophon of the Gurusahasranāmastotra (1st foliation). The Gurustotra (2nd foliation, ascribed to the Rudrayāmala) has no date or scribe of its own, so it may or may not be by the same hand. 'sahajānaṃdāya' (dative) could be the initiate name of the owner or patron, for whom the Guru's favour is asked. It could also just be the abstract term 'innate bliss' (sahajānanda), with no person meant, so p2 is uncertain. 'prīṇātu⟨ḥ⟩': the cataloguer marks the visarga as wrong.

purpose: sattvahetoḥ (for the benefit of beings): this is in the later line about consecration and donation, not in the copying colophon
notes: The year is written in words: 'śate sāṣṭakaviṃśayute' = 100 + 28 = 128. The colophon does not name the era. Bendall takes it as Nepal Saṃvat, which gives 128 + 880 = A.D. 1008, matching his conversion. The text says 'dvirājyaka': a joint rule of Nirbhaya and Rudradeva. 'शुक्लपञ्चे' is probably 'शुक्लपक्षे' (compare 'नचचरस्य' = नक्षत्रस्य), so the day of the month is not given. The phrase 'राज्ये परि... कवितवौरि संघे' is corrupt. The vihāra name 'श्रील्लुम्बिहार' is uncertain: it is marked (?) by Bendall and could not be identified. No scribe or donor is named in the part that can be read. The later line in fresher ink ('प्रणम्य प्रतिष्ठापनञ्चैवमस्या ... कारयन् सत्त्वहेतोः') records a later consecration of the book with gifts and feasts for monks. It mentions a 'वराचार्य' but gives no personal name.

title: SUVARṆA-PRABHĀSA
date_raw: dated N. s. 914 (A.D. 1794) reign of Rāṇa-bahādura
date_note: ≈ 1794 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: यदत्र पुण्यं तन्नवलाचार्योपाध्यायमाता नेपालेश्वर श्रीमन्महा- राज हिन्दुपति बात्साह श्रीश्रीश्री रण बहादूर साह बहादूर समसेर (?) जंग देवानां सदा समरविजयिनां विजयराज्ये । युतीन्दुनन्द युत हायने स्मिन्तयावदाते (?) तिशिरामचन्द्रे तिथ्याडुवायां (?) बुधवासरे च सुरे च कुम्भशशिकर्कदेशे (sic) । दानपति कान्तिपूरे महानगरे कमिलाच्छितोल धालसिका नामगृहाधिवासित पुण्यात्मानुराधेन (?) बालमुकुन्द सहोदर- भाह भाजुधंपुत्र जयप्रतापसिं पिता महिजयलक्ष्मिता रत्न- वति दारा जगलक्ष्मी एते सहानुमतेन श्री ३ सुवर्णप्रभास° पुस्तकम जम्बूनन्देन चूर्णेन लिखापथिला प्रतिष्ठापितमभूत । अस्य देशभखा ।
purpose: merit (यदत्र पुण्यं); the dānapati and his family had the book written in gold and consecrated
notes:
The text comes from Bendall 1883 (Cambridge Add. 875). He warns that the gold-on-black readings are unreliable.

**Date.** The chronogram युतीन्दुनन्द is read right to left as 4-1-9 = 914, which agrees with Bendall's N.S. 914 = A.D. 1794. This falls within the reign of Raṇa Bahādura Śāha (1777–1799). The month is not stated. The sun in Kumbha (कुम्भ) points to about Phālguna. 'अवदाते' probably means the bright fortnight. 'रामचन्द्रे' may encode tithi 13. All three are uncertain.

**Family list.** The donor passage is corrupt. I take Bālamukunda as the dānapati, with brother Bhājudhaṃ ('भाजु' may be a Newari honorific), son Jayapratāpasiṃha, pitāmahī Jayalakṣmī ('पिता महि' = pitāmahī), mother Ratnavatī ('ता' = [mā]tā) and wife Jagalakṣmī. 'एते सहानुमतेन' makes them joint sponsors. An alternative reading, used by the first reader, makes Jayapratāpasiṃha the son of Bhājudhaṃ. 'पुण्यात्मानुराधेन (?)' is unclear and may hide another name.

**Scribe.** The scribe is not named. Bendall mentions invocations on the scribe's Ācārya parents, and 'नवलाचार्योपाध्यायमाता' may contain a personal name (Navala?), but this is too uncertain to record as a person.
review: Main dānapati/commissioner changed from Jayapratāpasiṃha to Bālamukunda. He is named first after the residence formula and the list then gives his relatives (brother, son, grandmother, mother, wife), all joined by 'एते सहानुमतेन'.

Jayapratāpasiṃha is now read as Bālamukunda's son ('पुत्र'), not as the son of Bhājudhaṃ. Bhājudhaṃ is read as Bālamukunda's brother ('सहोदर-भाह' ≈ sahodara bhrātā), with 'bhāju' perhaps the Newari honorific.
Kinship terms are now tied to Bālamukunda: pitāmahī Jayalakṣmī, mātā Ratnavatī and dārā Jagalakṣmī.
King's name normalized to IAST stem 'Raṇa Bahādura Śāha', with titles given in IAST. Shah kings do not take a -deva regnal name; 'devānāṃ' is an honorific plural.
Titles are now given in IAST instead of Devanāgarī. Inappropriate 'relative_only'+'commissioner' mixing removed.
Date: the paksa is now marked as an inference from 'अवदाते'. A possible tithi 13 (rāma=3, candra=1, read right to left) is recorded as uncertain. Notes added on the sun in Kumbha / moon in Karka.
Notes added on the unnamed scribe and the possible name 'Navala' in 'नवलाचार्योपाध्यायमाता'.

date_note: = Thursday 16 Sep 829, computed; nothing stated to verify it by; Bendall's Harṣa era read as the Aṃśuvarman ('Mānadeva') saṃvat, i.e. the Kārttikādi Śaka with 500 dropped (Malla 2005)
colophon: द्वा० प० म० दीक्षाप्रकरणे दीक्षामुक्तिपटं श्लोकाः चत्वारिंशतं। समाप्तश्च दीक्षाप्रकरणैकत्वेन दे श्लोकसहस्रपञ्चशतकदुत्तरे॥ अश्वयुज शृङ्गपूरणिमलिलित संवत् २५२†॥ 62b (१८३).

title: NĀMA-SAṄGĪTĪ and SRAGDHARĀ-STOTRA
colophon: इत्यार्थताराभट्टारिकायाः अग्रधास्तोत्रं (sic) संपूर्णं। कतिरा- चार्यपण्डित श्रीसर्वज्ञमित्रपादानां कश्मीरिकानां ताराचरणं कृधूलिध्वसराणां (?)

title: NĀMA-SAṄGĪTĪ-TIPPANĪ or AMṚITA-KAṄIKĀ
date_note: = Thursday 4 Jan 1392, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: इति उष्णीषादिमणिशिखरान्तस्थानसप्तकेषु निरावरणी- कृतस्त्रचस्य....क्रियाषट्कविशुद्ध्या (?) दाचवारिशतश्लोका प्रत्य- वेक्षणं ज्ञानव्याख्या ॥ ‖ इति दादशाङ्गनिरीधदादशभूमिप्रतिलम्बविशुद्ध्या समता- ज्ञानगाथास्तुर्विश्रतिः ॥ 44b. ‖ इति निरावरणपञ्चदशकलाविशुद्ध्या सर्वतथागतसमाधि- गतकार्यकारणलक्षणकृत्यानुष्ठानज्ञानगाथाव्याख्या ॥ 49b. ‖ इति पञ्चतथागतज्ञानस्तुतिगाथाः पञ्च 50b. ‖ इत्यमृतकणिका नाम श्रीनामसंगीतिटिप्पनी परिसमाप्ता ॥ 52b.
notes: The genitive 'vīrasiṃhanāmadheyasya' is used where an instrumental is syntactically required with 'samavasthitena' and 'vyākhyānārthakāṅkṣiṇā', indicating Vīrasiṃha copied and/or studied the text together with his pupil Ratnacandra. The text mentions having come from Panarīnagara (śrīmatpanarīnagarītaḥ samāgatā?). Bendall identifies the place as Navakoṣṭha (Nuwakot) and notes Ratnajyoti was likely a local ruler.

colophon: श्रीगणेशाय नमः । अविर्लमदजलनिवहंभ्रमरकुलानिक- सेविकपोलं ।
notes: The manuscript ends abruptly without a colophon; no persons, date, or place of copying are recorded.

title: PAṄCA-RAKSHĀ
notes: The end of the manuscript is torn and the colophon is entirely obliterated; no date, place, or persons are preserved.

colophon: इति तथागतव्याप्तादिखिति...गस्थिरोभवं एवन्तु पृथिवि- विमण्डलं भवन्तु वज्रकवचः ॥ इति श्रीदजसवकायस्थ तथागत- व्याप्तसतं (sic) समाप्तः ॥ शुभं ॥
notes: The colophon names no people, date or place. Bendall describes the manuscript only as 'modern' (coarse brown paper, 4 leaves). In the ending, 'śrīdajasavakāyastha' is a corruption of 'śrīvajrasattvakāyastha', compare 'namaḥ śrīvajrasavāya' at the start. It refers to Vajrasattva and does not name a kāyastha scribe. Text title: Tathāgatavyāptaśata (Bendall marks it with '?').
review: Added to notes that Bendall describes the manuscript only as 'modern', with no date.

colophon: समाप्ता बोधिस्त्वावदानकल्पलता। क्षतिरियं महाकवेः चेमेन्द्रस्य। ‖ नेत्राद्यश्चिद्युताब्दके च समये राधे श्रिते पञ्चके। ‖ आशायाश्च तिथौ दिवाकरदिने वाह्निदिषद्भक्के (?)॥ ‖ श्रीमद्भुद्धसुतावदानशतकं वस्वङ्गितं मोचदं। ‖ राज्ये श्रीमदनन्तमल्लनृपतेर्लक्ष्म्या वल्लेखि स्वयं॥ ‖ लक्ष्म्या भद्रकवेर्विधाय विधिवद्वाख्यानमत्यङ्कृतं। ‖ चेमेन्द्रेण कृतं गम्भीरमधुरं बुद्धावदानं मया॥ ‖ नेपाले भुवि मञ्जुभद्रसुधिना यत्पुण्यमासादितं। ‖ स्त्वास्तेन भवाद्धि (?) मध्यपतिता बुद्धा भवन्तु स्फुटं॥
purpose: यत्पुण्यमासादितं। स्त्वास्तेन भवाद्धि (?) मध्यपतिता बुद्धा भवन्तु स्फुटं

title: DHĀRAṄĪ-SAṄGRAHA

colophon: इति स्कण्डपुराने<sup>(sic)</sup> शनिश्चस्वस्तीत्र समाप्तः। इति धा- रणीसंग्रहः संचित्रः परिसमाप्तः। ये धर्मा°। देयधर्मीऽयं प्रवरमहायानयायिनः...etc. अत्रिलीकर-स्त्री पूर्णावती द्वयो प्रमुखादिसगणपरिवाराणां यत्युष्ण° etc.।...नेपालेश्वर...श्रीशज- यमहीन्द्रसिंहमल्लदेव† परमभट्टारकदेवानां .. विजयराज्ये। ‖ सम्बत् ८३६ भाद्रवपदमास शुक्लपक्षे... etc. ‖ लिखितं। लेखकस्य काष्ठमण्डप महानगले तलमूर महा- विहारे खण्डचूकमहापुष्करिण्यां पूर्वदिशस्थित वज्रदेव्या- चरणाम्बुज श्रेवित महापात्रकुलश्रीवज्राचार्य श्रीपतिदेवेन लिखितसम्पुर्णं करोमि। यथा दृष्टं...। भग्नपृष्ठ...

One stavatotra is attributed to 'चर्युतिया'. Bendall marks this reading (?), so it is probably corrupt and may not be a personal name at all. It is kept as an author with low confidence.

title: UTPĀTA-LAKSHAṄA-[LOKEṢVARA-BHĀSHITAM]
colophon: इति उत्यातलक्षणलोकेश्वरभाषितं तारा प्रच्छति समाप्तः । लिखितं यदिति तोल काथ बहालया श्रीवज्राचार्य कुलवजनं लिखापितादिनकुल गुरुभं ॥
notes: The colophon is in corrupt Newari: 'likhitaṃ yaditi tola kātha bahālayā śrīvajrācārya kulavaja-naṃ likhāpita dina kula gurubhaṃ'. I take कुलवजनं as Kulavajra plus the ergative -na, the agent of likhāpita ('caused to be written'). That makes him the commissioner. It is also possible that he copied the text himself, since the colophon begins with likhitaṃ. 'dina kula gurubhaṃ' is unclear. It may say the day of writing, perhaps a Thursday (guru), with the weekday garbled. It may also contain 'kulaguru' (family priest). I do not record it as a person. 'Kātha Bahāl' could be Kāṭhe Bahāl and 'Yadi tol' could be Yaṭkhā tol, both in Kathmandu, but neither identification is certain. The number ३३५ at the end is probably a verse or grantha count, not a date. There is no date: Bendall classes the manuscript only as 'modern'.
review: p1: name read as Kulavajra (कुलवजनं = Kulavaja[ra] + Newari ergative -na); role changed from scribe to commissioner, because the ergative agent goes with लिखापित 'caused to be written'; the initial लिखितं does not name a separate scribe
p1: Kāṭha Bahāl kept as affiliation and Yadi tol as residence, transliterated to IAST
p2 'Ādinakula' removed: दिनकुल गुरुभं most likely continues the Newari sentence (dina 'day' … guru, possibly the weekday Thursday, guruvāra), not a personal name
wrote_for relation removed (no separate scribe or commissioner pair can be established)
place transliterated to IAST

title: STOTRAS
date_note: ≈ 1785 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: इति सारदातवतोचं स°
notes: Bendall does not quote the vernacular (Newari) colophon. He only paraphrases it: 'written in the year given above by Ṣrīvajrācārya Bhājudhanamṛcay-āviyā (?) at Kāntipur (Kathmandu).' He marks the name as doubtful. The ending '-mṛcay-āviyā' is very likely a misreading of Newari '-na coyāviyā' (ergative -na + coyā biyā, 'written by'). On that reading the name is Bhājudhana ('Bhāju' may be the Newari honorific 'Bhāju' + Dhana). The date NS 905 = 1785 CE (NS+880) matches Bendall's conversion. No month or tithi is reported.
review: Name re-read as 'Bhājudhana'. The rest of Bendall's '-mṛcay-āviyā' is probably a misreading of the Newari ergative plus verb 'na coyāviyā' ('written by'), not part of the name. Confidence stays low.
Residence removed: Kāntipur is given as the place of writing, not as the scribe's residence.
Notes expanded with the reasoning for the name.

title: RĀMĀṆKA-NĀṢIKĀ by DHARMAGUPTA, and fragment
date_note: ≈ 1360 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: श्रीधर्मगुप्तः कृती। पित्रा पुत्रकृपापरेण निपुणं शास्त्रान्वयं शिचित् एताम्भावरसीञ्चलां स कृतवान् रामाङ्गितान्नाटिकां। श्रेयो ऽस्तु। सम्वत् ४८० शुक्लिकदशम्यां रवि वासो। तेनैव धर्म- गुप्तेन श्रीमता रामदासिना। बालवागीश्वरेणैयं लिखिता रा- माङ्गनाटिका॥ शुभमस्तु सर्वदा॥
notes: Bendall describes the manuscript as the author's own copy (autograph). Dharmagupta, called Bālavāgīśvara and son of Rāmadāsa, both wrote and copied the Rāmāṅka-nāṭikā. The catalogue heading 'RĀMĀṆKA-NĀṢIKĀ' is an OCR garbling of Rāmāṅka-nāṭikā; the text itself also writes रामाङ्ग-. The era is not named in the text (just 'सम्वत् ४८०'); Bendall reads it as N.S. 480 = A.D. 1360 (480+880). No month is named: 'शुक्लिकदशम्यां' is corrupt, perhaps 'शुक्ल-दशम्यां' with the month dropped, or a garbling of a month name. Bendall calls Rāmadāsa 'a magistrate of Nepal', rendering नेपालावनपालमण्डलगुरुः. The prologue mentions Lalitāpura (Patan) as the place where the play is produced. That makes copying in Patan likely, but it is not stated as the place of copying.
review: Place: cleared. Lalitāpura (ललितापुरम्) is named in the prologue as the place where the play is staged or produced. It is not given as the place of copying, so it is now only mentioned in notes.

title: ASHTASAHASRIKĀ PRAJÑĀPĀRAMITĀ
date_note: = Sunday 7 Oct 1263, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: देयधर्मी ऽयं प्रवरमहायानयायिनः परमोपाश्रिक-श्रीरा- मपासिडख (?) यदत्रपुण्यं... etc. ।
purpose: deyadharma (pious gift) by the donor; merit-transfer formula (yad atra puṇyaṃ ...)
notes: The year is written in letter-numerals, one digit per sign: ci = 3, a doubtful middle sign, and phrā = 4. Bendall reads the middle sign as 8 (ह/ङ) rather than 5 (ट), "on chronological grounds" because the colophon names king Abhayamalla, which gives N.S. 384 = A.D. 1264. ce_approx follows Bendall. However, the modern chronology (Petech) places Abhayamalla's reign at about N.S. 336–375 (A.D. 1216–1255). On that chronology, N.S. 354 (A.D. 1234) would fit the reign better, and 384 would fall after it. The date therefore needs checking. The donor's name is corrupt and Bendall marks it (?). The reading Rāmapāsiḍakha is mechanical; the first element is probably Rāma-. The title written परमोपाश्रिक is taken as paramopāsaka (lay devotee). No scribe is named. Bendall prints the beginning of the colophon only in part ("etc."), so the 1883 transliteration has been converted.
review: Date as_written now includes the year letter-numerals (चि-ह(?)-फ्रा) and the date words; tithi normalized to dvitīyā (दतीयाया = dvitīyāyāṃ); weekday normalized to Sunday (ādityavāra).
Donor titles normalized: paramopāsaka (written परमोपाश्रिक); the Mahāyāna epithet is kept as an epithet.
Purpose expanded to deyadharma with a merit-transfer formula.
Notes: added the conflict between N.S. 384 and the modern chronology of Abhayamalla's reign, and the corrupt donor name.

notes: The date and the king's name are on the last leaf only. This leaf is on different paper and in a slightly later hand. Bendall takes it to be a fresh copy of a damaged original leaf, so N.S. 802 (A.D. 1682) is probably the date of the original manuscript and was recopied onto the supply leaf. Bendall's physical description dates the hand to the 18th century, which does not quite fit 1682; the supply leaf itself is undated. Bendall prints the year as ८°२ and reads it as 802. 'खस्सुसंस्वत्' is a garbled form of the era word (saṃvat). The royal name 'प्रथितुन्द्रमल्लदेव' is a corrupt form of Pārthivendramalladeva, king of Kathmandu, who reigned c. N.S. 800–807 (1680–1687). The year 802 falls in his reign. 'मयूरच्छत्र-खड्गशीर्षिकामनाथं (?)' and 'याकूरधर्माचक्रविजयराज्ये' are corrupt epithets and reign formulas. No scribe, donor or place is named. The two cover leaves from a Tantric Sūtra are unrelated to this copy.

title: A collection of DHĀRANĪS, etc
date_note: ≈ 1677 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: श्रीयो ऽसु संवत् ७८७ (month, nakshatra, day etc.) ... एतद्दिने लिखितं... काष्टमण्डपनगरे... श्रीरत्नवज्रिण (?)...।
notes: The two figures for the year do not agree. Bendall's physical description gives 'N. S. 797 (A.D. 1677)', but his Devanāgarī excerpt of the colophon prints 'संवत् ७८७' (NS 787 = 1667 CE). One of them is probably a misprint, and I can't tell which. I followed the colophon as printed (787 / 1667); if the heading is right, the year is NS 797 = 1677 CE. Bendall leaves out the month, nakṣatra and day. 'श्रीयो ऽसु' is probably a garbled 'श्रेयो ऽस्तु'. Bendall puts a query (?) after the scribe's name. 'रत्नवज्रिण' probably stands for the instrumental Ratnavajriṇā, after 'likhitaṃ'. I took the stem as Ratnavajrin; Ratnavajra is also possible. 'Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa-nagara' is Kathmandu.
review: Kept all extracted content; expanded notes on the conflicting year (797 vs 787) and on the probable instrumental form of the scribe's name

title: AMARA-KOṢA
date_raw: श्रीमन्नेपालिकसम्बन्धरे। सम्बत ५०० मार्गः शुद्ध श्रीपञ्चम्या तिथौ रैवतिनक्षत्रे साध्ययोगे सोमवासरे
date_note: = Tuesday 15 Nov 1379, not verified: the stated weekday does not fit
colophon: नेपालाभुवमण्डलेश्वर प्रभूपते...। देवश्रीजयार्जुनो (*sic*) हि... परे लोकात्मम् (? 1. त०) भूपति।
purpose: for the study (adhyayanārtham) of Mahāpātra …tyaguṇamasiṃha and Mahāpātra Raghusiṃhadeva
notes: The year in the colophon ('सम्बत ५००') is in the retouched, modern-ink passage, so it is not reliable. NS 500 Mārgaśīrṣa = late 1379 CE. Bendall dates the manuscript from the note on the back of the leaf, which is probably in a contemporary hand: 'abdhi-vindu-viṣaye' = NS 504, Māgha kṛṣṇa 5 = A.D. 1384. That note also names King Jayārjunadeva (reigned c. 1361–1382). This conflicts with Bendall's 1384, since by 1384 Jayasthiti was ruling according to Add. 1395. Erasures in the colophon make the names hard to read. 'puṣā nāma maḍāpātra' may be a personal name (Puṣā) followed by the title mahāpātra, or a corruption; reading Puṣā as commissioner and resident of Lalitapur is conjectural. 'त्यगुणम सिंह' is preceded by an erasure, so the name is incomplete. The plural '-devānām' suggests more than one beneficiary.
review: Commissioner reassigned: the subject of 'likhāpitaḥ' is most plausibly the person resident in Lalitapur introduced by '…sitaḥ puṣā nāma', so Puṣā is now the commissioner (low confidence). Tyaguṇamasiṃha is now a beneficiary, as the genitive plural '-devānām adhyayanārthaṃ' covers more than one person.
'mahāpātra' is now treated as a title that comes before each name ('maḍāpātra śrī … tyaguṇama siṃha', 'mahāpātra śrīRaghusiṃhadeva').
Lalitāpurī residence moved from the scribe Jasacandra to the commissioner. The colophon does not say where the scribe lived.
Relations rebuilt: the commissioner commissioned the copy from the scribe; the scribe wrote it for the commissioner; both mahāpātras are linked to the commissioner as beneficiaries ('other').
King Jayārjunadeva's epithets reduced to titles. The reign relation is kept at medium confidence because the king is named only in the note on the back of the leaf.
Notes expanded to cover the retouched date: the colophon has 500, the note on the back has 504.

title: ḌAMBŪKĀVADĀNA
date_note: = Wednesday 15 Oct 1427, computed; nothing stated to verify it by
colophon: सम्भूकावदाननिदानकथा समाप्तः॥ स° ५४७ अष्टुनि कृष्ण १° लिखित श्री डंखाचोकवज्राचार्य श्री पंडजसः (?)
notes: Bendall marks the scribe's name with a query ('पंडजसः (?)'). The reading Paṇḍajasa is uncertain. It may be corrupt, for example for Paṇḍita Jasa(rāja), Padmajasa or a similar name. Ḍaṃkhācoka (डंखाचोक) is probably a locality or quadrangle (cuka/coka) in the Kathmandu Valley that the vajrācārya scribe belonged to. It is recorded as his residence, not as the stated place of copying. The month 'अष्टुनि' is likely a misreading or corruption of Āśvina. The tithi '१°' is taken as 10, but the ° could also be Bendall's abbreviation mark (compare 'स°'), in which case the tithi would be 1. NS 547 + 880 = 1427 CE, which agrees with Bendall's date. If the month is Āśvina, the date falls in about September/October 1427.
review: Place of copying cleared: डंखाचोक is given only as the scribe's residence or affiliation in a 'written by' phrase. It is not stated as the place of copying, so it is kept under the person's residence.
Notes expanded: the tithi reading '१°' is ambiguous, and the month and name readings are doubtful.
Person, date (NS 547 = 1427 CE) and roles confirmed.

title: RATNAGUṆA-SAṄCAYA
date_note: ≈ 1830 CE, year only (± 1)
colophon: रिषितेयं (i.e. लिखि<sup>०</sup>) काय-वाहारया श्रीवजवाक्ष्य पद्या- कलिासंहिन।
notes: Bendall says the MS is 'barbarously incorrect'. He does not quote the date line in Devanāgarī; he gives only 'N. s. 950 (A.D. 1830)'. NS 950 = 1829/30 CE. रिषितेयं = likhiteyam. श्रीवजवाक्ष्य is probably a garbled śrī-vajrācāryeṇa/-sya, so the title vajrācārya is conjectural. पद्याकलिासंहिन is most likely Padmākarasiṃhena; Padmākalisiṃha is also possible. काय-वाहारया looks like a Newari genitive, 'of Kāya-bahāra/bahāl'. This is a vihāra name that cannot be identified for certain (perhaps Kwā Bahā). It is taken as the scribe's affiliation, not as the stated place of copying. notes: The date fields conflict. Bendall's header reads 'N. s. 926 (A.D. 1806)', but the Devanāgarī colophon as transcribed reads 'समत् ५२७', i.e. NS 527 = c. 1407 CE. The Devanāgarī comes from OCR and is heavily garbled (च for क्ष throughout, e.g. भिचु, नचत्र), and OCR can confuse ५ and ९, or ६ and ७. So the transcribed figure is not fully reliable either. NS 527 is preferred here because a palm-leaf manuscript of 494 leaves fits the early 15th century much better than 1806. This should still be checked against the printed catalogue or the manuscript. 'गुरुकूपचे' is taken as an OCR corruption of 'शुक्लपक्षे'. 'चिन्ता' = Citrā; 'वज' = Vajra yoga. The phrases 'यथाकर्ममहीन्तक (?) … शकुह – श्रीरचभगवतिः … चौपधुनकादिनजरो' (Newari, apparently 'the writing was completed …') are unclear and contain no secure personal name. Bendall himself marks the scribe's name 'ज्ञाजणग्लन' (?) as doubtful; it may be a garbled Newar name. The title header 'ĀTASĀHASRĪ' is an OCR error for ŚATASĀHASRĪ (the colophon reads शतसाहस्र्या).
review: Place: removed the modern identification (Cuka Bāhā / Kathmandu). Which vihāra 'Mānadeva-saṃskārita Cakra Mahāvihāra' refers to today is not certain, and the colophon names it as the scribe's vihāra, not explicitly as the place of copying.
Date: read the OCR-garbled 'गुरुकूपचे' as 'शुक्लपक्षे' and recorded this. Kept NS 527 = 1407 CE, but the notes now explain the conflict with Bendall's header (NS 926 = 1806) and why 527 is preferred.

notes: Main colophon (verse): the year is NS 135 = 1015 CE, as Bendall gives it. Caitra, daśamī. 'danujaripuguru' means Bṛhaspati, i.e. Thursday. Śukla pakṣa is inferred from 'himābhā' ('moon-bright') and is tentative. The colophon was written during the joint rule of Bhojadeva and Rudradeva, with Lakṣmīkāmadeva holding half the kingdom. The scribe Sujatabhadra (probably Sujātabhadra) copied it in the Śrī-Lhaṃ-vihāra of Nepālamaṇḍala. 'तपसीरखुसागरे' is corrupt; 'खुधीः' is probably सुधीः. In it someone redeemed the book from a faithless person ([śra]ddhāhīna-jana). The name 'कर्तुणपूर्वण वज्रिण' is taken as karuṇāpūrveṇa vajriṇā = Karuṇāvajra; this reading is uncertain. Only the original date is entered in the date fields.

title: SĀDHANA-SAMUCCAYA
date_note: = Thursday 14 Jan 1216, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: The colophon runs thus: सवत् [३३६] (see above) पौषकृष्णा- ष्टम्यां षट्हसतिवासरे वैशाखनक्षत्रे राजाधिराजपरमेश्वर श्रीमदरिमल्ल दे [वस्य विजराज्ये (*sic*) लिखितमिदं साधनसमुच्चयं नाम पुस्तकं]
notes: The scribe is not named. Bendall says the year figures [336] have clearly been retouched, possibly by a later hand. He suggests they may originally have been 2s, and says that, according to Prof. Adams, the weekday and month do not tally for 336, so the restoration is probably wrong. NS 336 would fall within Arimalla's reign (c. NS 320–336), so ce_approx 1215/16 stands only provisionally. 'षट्हसतिवासरे' is presumably a printing or scribal error for बृहस्पतिवासरे (Thursday). 'विजराज्ये' (sic) stands for vijayarājye. The bracketed words 'वस्य विजराज्ये ... पुस्तकं' were rewritten by a second hand. Ānandajīvabhadra is known only from the cover note (ārādhana in NS 458 = 1338 CE at the Ārinaka-vihāra). He is a later user, not part of the original production. The relation entry for him is a placeholder and can be dropped. Kumudākara and Ratnākaragupta are authors of individual sādhanas named in the index and are not included as persons of this copy.
review: Added Ānandajīvabhadra (later user who performed an ārādhana with the MS in NS 458 at the Ārinaka-vihāra, per Bendall's note on the cover) with role 'other'
Year marked as uncertain because it was retouched; ce_approx refined to 1215/1216 (Pauṣa NS 336 falls in Dec 1215–Jan 1216)
Era NS is inferred: the colophon has only 'saṃvat', but Arimalla's reign confirms it
Notes expanded: weekday misprint, 'vijarājye' (sic), second-hand restoration of the bracketed words, Bendall's suggestion that the figures may be 2s

date_note: = Friday 15 Aug 1068, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: आर्यभद्र चरीप्रणिधानराजं समाप्तः ॥ ये धर्मा... ॥ संवत् १८८ भाद्रपद शुक्ल पौर्णमास्याः शुक्रदिने। उपासक चिन्मिश्र पाकस्य पुस्तको ऽयं लिखितमिति ॥
notes: This is one item of Bendall's composite number Add. 1680 (XXIV): a Bhadracarīpraṇidhānarāja on 6 palm leaves. Bendall reads the date as N.S. 188 = A.D. 1068, which agrees with NS+880. The colophon does not name a scribe. The owner's name is uncertain. Bendall prints 'चिन्मिश्र पाकस्य' with a space, so it may be one compound name, Cinmiśrapāka, or 'Cinmiśra' followed by some other element. It could also be a garbled form of a Newar name. Because he is called upāsaka, '-miśra' here is probably not the brahmin suffix. He is listed only as owner: the text says the book is his ('pustako 'yaṃ') and that it was written ('likhitam'), but nothing shows he commissioned it.

Lowered confidence for p1 to low because the name's form and division are uncertain (Bendall prints 'चिन्मिश्र पाकस्य' with a space)

colophon: आर्यकारण्ड्यहमहायानसूत्ररत्नराजं समाप्तं। ये धर्मा<sup>०</sup> (date v. supra)। श्रीवज्राचार्य- वीलसिंहदेवेन चौयाथचुक वा- हाराया-श्रीहृवदेवजयात। श्री भक्तापुरीमहानगरया राजा- धिरानश्री\* ३ जगज्ज्योतिर्मलदेवयाति क्रियासंग्रह चौयाया- ज्यालाविया पुस्तक खकालन्द्यूहपुस्तकं (*sic*) ररितापुरिमहा- नगर्थां गुरुद्धवावतारे श्रीरं सिद्धिनलसिंहमल्लदेव\*॥ तस्य पुत्र वृषधवावतारं श्रीशनिदास्सल्ल\* तस्य उभयराज्ये गुरुभं।
purpose: The book was given to Hṛvadeva as wages (jyālā biyā) for his writing a Kriyāsaṃgraha for King Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur
notes: Bendall printed the date only in his description (NS 753 = AD 1633) and replaced the colophon's date line with 'date v. supra', so the year cannot be checked against the colophon. Bendall says the manuscript was written at Bhatgāon under Jagajjyotir Malla, but the colophon does not support this. Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur appears only as the king for whom Hṛvadeva wrote a Kriyāsaṃgraha. The Kāraṇḍavyūha copy itself is placed in Lalitapurī (ररितापुरि, i.e. Patan) during the joint reign (ubhayarājye) of Siddhinarasiṃhamalla and his son Śrīnivāsamalla. A joint reign with Śrīnivāsa as early as 1633 is unusually early and is worth checking. Jagajjyotirmalla (r. c. 1614–1637) fits 1633. The Newari is heavily corrupt: वीलसिंह probably stands for Vīrasiṃha; हृवदेवजयात is read as Hṛvadeva-jū-yāta ('to Hṛvadeva'), and the true name may be different. थचुक वाहार is the name of a vihāra and has not been identified. Other corrupt spellings: सिद्धिनलसिंह = Siddhinarasiṃha, श्रीशनिदास्सल्ल = Śrīnivāsamalla, गुरुद्धवावतार = garuḍadhvajāvatāra. The colophon does not say who paid the wages (perhaps the king), so no donor is assigned.
review: p1 name read as Vīrasiṃhadeva (Vīla- for Vīra-, r/l interchange as in the rest of the colophon); confidence lowered to medium for the spelling, role scribe kept

p2 Hṛvadeva: stem without the Newari honorific + dative -jū-yāta ('Hṛvadevajayāta' = Hṛvadeva-jū-yāta, 'to Hṛvadeva'); role beneficiary dropped, kept owner (book given to him) and added 'other' (he wrote a Kriyāsaṃgraha for the Bhaktapur king); confidence low because the name is corrupt
p3 Jagajjyotirmalla: role changed from king to other; he is king of Bhaktapur, named only because the Kriyāsaṃgraha was written for him, while this copy was made in Lalitapur under the Patan kings
Relation p1 wrote_for p3 removed. It was Hṛvadeva who wrote the Kriyāsaṃgraha for Jagajjyotirmalla, so this is now recorded as p2 –other→ p3
Added relation p1 wrote_for p2 (the copy went to Hṛvadeva)
Purpose reworded
Notes: Bendall's 'Written at Bhatgāon in the reign of Jagajjyotir Malla' is contradicted by the colophon

title: PAṄCA-RAKSHĀ

title: ASHTASAHASRIKĀ PRAJÑĀPĀRAMITĀ
script: Kuṭila or early Devanāgarī hand as modified in the XIIth cent. A.D
date_note: = Sunday 18 Jul 1165, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: संवत् २८५ आवण गुरुत्ताष्टम्यामादित्यदिने। श्रीमदानन्ददेवस्य विजयराज्ये ॥ लिखितेदं (?) श्रीमस्वक्रयां (?) वन्ताण्डुल्लके (?) श्रीधर्मचक्रमहाविहाराधिवासिन शाक्यभिद्युमञ्जुश्रियेणेति ॥ श्रीधानपिङ्गविषयाधिवासिन बुद्धौभावे (?) नामधेयस्य यदत्र पुण्यं तद्भवत्वाचार्यध्यायमातापितृपर्वङ्गमङ्गला सकलसत्त्वराशेरनुत्तरज्ञानावाप्त्यादिति ॥
purpose: Merit transfer: the merit goes to the person from Dhānapiṅga-viṣaya, to be shared with teachers and parents and given to all beings for supreme knowledge (यदत्र पुण्यं तद्भवत्वाचार्य...सकलसत्त्वराशेरनुत्तरज्ञानावाप्तये).
notes: This is Bendall's catalogue (1883), and his Devanāgarī shows OCR or typographical corruption. Bendall also says the latter part of the colophon is partly obliterated. 'आवण' is read as श्रावण. 'गुरुत्ताष्टम्याम्' is probably शुक्लाष्टम्याम्, so the pakṣa is inferred. 'शाक्यभिद्यु' stands for शाक्यभिक्षु. 'श्रीमस्वक्रयां (?)' cannot be read. 'वन्ताण्डुल्लके (?)' looks like a locality name but is uncertain. Date: NS 285 + 880 = 1165 CE, which agrees with Bendall's 'A.D. 1165'; the weekday (Sunday) has not been verified. The king is Ānandadeva, as Bendall says. The third person's name is very doubtful: Bendall gives 'बुद्धौभावे (?)', which could be a corruption of something like Buddhabhāva or Buddhadeva. The person resides in Dhānapiṅga-viṣaya. The colophon assigns this person the merit, which suggests they were the donor or commissioner, but the colophon does not state that role.
review: p2 (Mañjuśrī): affiliation normalized to Dharmacakra-mahāvihāra. Bendall gives this as the scribe's residence, so it is also entered as residence. The place 'वन्ताण्डुल्लके (?)' is too doubtful to stand alone as residence.

p3: name reading lowered to low confidence (Buddhabhāva?). Roles changed from commissioner+donor to beneficiary: the colophon only assigns him the merit ('नामधेयस्य यदत्र पुण्यं'). It has no likhāpita or deyadharma.
Removed the p2→p3 wrote_for relation because the colophon gives no explicit commissioning.
Purpose rewritten to follow the colophon wording. The first reading had added words ('kṛtvā', 'upādhyāya') that are not in the text.
Place: as_written shortened to the actual locative. Normalized left empty.
Notes expanded: the OCR/typographical corruptions are explained and the date is checked.

title: GUHYĀVALĪ-VIVṚITI by GHANADEVĀ
date_raw: dated in the 37th year of Govinda-Pāla (A.D. 1198, cf. No. I)
date_note: ≈ 1198 CE, Bendall's own conversion (no era-dated colophon to recalculate)
colophon: गोविन्दपालदेवानां सं ३७ आमण(*sic*)दिने ११ लिखितमिदं पुस्तकं काशीगयाकरेणति ॥
notes: The year is the 37th of Govindapāla. Bendall converts it to A.D. 1198, which fits the usual reckoning of this era from c. 1161. The same scribe copied the other works in Add. 1699 over three successive years (1198–1200) in Bengali script. The month 'āmaṇa' is marked (sic) by Bendall and is corrupt; the intended month is uncertain. 'dine 11' is probably a day of the month rather than a lunar tithi. Bendall's English general note gives the scribe as 'Kācṛīgayākara'. This is almost certainly an OCR corruption of 'Kāçīgayākara' (= Kāśīgayākara), which matches the Devanāgarī 'काशीगयाकरेणति' (= -kareṇeti). Ghanadeva calls himself 'bhikṣu' in the opening verses and 'paṇḍita sthavira' in the colophon. Daṇḍīpāda, whose method (krama) the vivṛti follows, is the author of the root text, not a person connected with this copy, so he is left out.
review: p2 Govindapāladeva: removed 'deva' from titles (kept as part of the regnal name).
p1 Ghanadeva: evidence also covers 'भिक्षुश्रीघनदेवेन विवृतिः क्रियते' for the bhikṣu title. Kept roles author/commentator because he wrote the vivṛti on Daṇḍīpāda's work.
Date: month normalised to IAST 'āmaṇa (sic)'. Day 11 entered in the tithi field as 'dine 11'.

title: YOGARATNA-MĀLĀ, a commentary on the HEVAJRA by KRISHṆA or KĀHNA
date_note: ≈ 1200 CE, Bendall's own conversion (no era-dated colophon to recalculate)
colophon: ॐ वज्रपद्मयोरधिष्ठानं येनाधिष्ठ्यते (*sic*) । योगरत्नमालायां क्वा हेवज्रपञ्चिकायाम् । यत्पुण्यमाचितं तेन निष्क्रेशः स्याद- खिलो जनः ॥ श्रीहेवज्रपञ्चिका योगरत्नमाला समाप्ता ॥ ॥ कृतिरियं पण्डिताचार्यश्रीकाङ्कपादानामिति ॥ परमेश्वरेत्या- दि राजावली पूर्ववत् । श्रीमद्गोविन्दपालदेवानां सं ३६ भा- द्रदिने १४ लिखितमिदं पुस्तकं काशीगयाकरेणिति ॥

Scribe's name is read as 'Kācṛīgayākara' in Bendall's English note, but the colophon reads 'Kāśīgayākara'. The author/commentator Kāhṇa / Kṛṣṇa is named as Kāṅkapāda in the final colophon.

title: PAṄCA-RAKSHĀ
date_note: = Friday 4 Jun 1389, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: °पञ्चरत्नामहायानसूत्राणि समाप्तेति। ये धर्मा°। देय- धर्मो ऽयं प्रवरमहायानयाचिन श्रीललितक्रमाया श्रीमाणिग- लके\* श्रीवच्चविहाराधिवांत-शाक्यपुत्र परसीगत-संध श्रीमले- चजजकस्य ॥ यदत्रपुण्यं etc.... ज्ञानफलं प्राप्तमिति ॥ श्री- योऽस्तु सम्वत ५०६ ज्येष्ठशुक्ल दशम्याया तिथौ शुक्रवासरे राजाधिराजश्री२ जयस्थितिराजमखराजेशुभः (*sic*) ॥
purpose: deyadharma (pious gift) of the donor, merit formula yad atra puṇyaṃ
notes: The transcribed Devanāgarī prints ५०६, but Bendall's description gives N.s. 509 = A.D. 1389. I followed Bendall and took ५०६ as a probable OCR confusion of ९ with ६. Bendall notes that the date and the king's name are in a different, apparently contemporary hand. There is another date inside the cover, probably of a recitation, but it is nearly obliterated. 'मखराजे' stands for 'मल्लराज्ये'. The donor's name 'मलेचजजक' is corrupt, either in the manuscript or in the OCR. 'परसीगत-संध' probably stands for 'paramasaugata-saṃgha'/'paramasaugata'. 'प्रवरमहायानयाचिन' stands for 'pravaramahāyānayāyin'. 'वच्चविहार' may stand for Vatsavihāra; the name is uncertain.
review: Date year changed from 506 to 509 (ce 1386 → 1389): Bendall's description states N.s. 509 (A.D. 1389). The '५०६' in the transcription is probably an OCR misreading of ५०९, since ६ and ९ are easily confused. 509 also falls within Jayasthitimalla's reign.
Donor name confidence lowered to low (corrupt). Added the title paramasaugata, the probable reading of 'परसीगत'. Separated affiliation (vihāra) from residence.
Purpose reworded as a pious gift (deyadharma) for merit, in place of the quoted formula.
Place: kept the normalization to Patan (Lalitakrama = Lalitapattana; Māṇigala = the Patan palace quarter). The vihāra name was removed from the place string.

title: BODHISATTVA-BHŪMI
colophon: **तथा पराक्रमणः निष्ठाप्रतिष्ठां प्रतिलभते यत उत्तरिभूयो(?) न पयेषते(?) अनुत्तर[र]्यं प्राप्नः बो[धिस्त्वभू]\*मेरनुक्रमः प्राप्नः ॥ समाप्ता च बोधिस्त्वभूमिः ॥**
notes: No scribal colophon preserved; the manuscript ends with the textual closing formula (समाप्ता च बोधिस्त्वभूमिः). Cecil Bendall assigns the manuscript to the 9th century CE purely on palaeographical grounds.

title: VAJRĀVALĪ by ABHAYĀKARAGUPTA
date_note: = Saturday 3 Sep 1429, verified by the pañcāṅga
colophon: **महापन्दिता** (*sic*) **अभयाकरगुप्त-विरचिता वज्रावली नाम मण्डलोपायिका समाप्तः । ये धर्मं । सं ५४७ भाद्रपद शुक्लः पञ्चम्याया** (*sic*) **तित्यौ विश्राषणचत्रे शणिचर वासरे राजं जयजन्मलदेवस्य विजयराज्ये लिखित श्री माणिकलकेः उत्रविहारे श्रीहर्षवर्णमहाविहारावस्थितमिचु श्रीजिवयीभट्टेण स्वहस्तेन लिखितं । जथा दृष्टं etc. ॥**
notes: The Devanāgarī transcript reads सं ५४७, but Bendall's description gives N.S. 549 (A.D. 1429). The OCR probably confused ९ with ७, so 549 is followed here. The king's name 'जयजन्मलदेवस्य' is corrupt. It is read as Jayayakṣamalladeva because he reigned in NS 549, after Jayajyotirmalla, who died c. 1428. If the year were really 547, the king would be Jayajyotirmalla. Either way the identification is uncertain. Bendall names the scribe 'Jivayibhadra' in his English note, and the transcript's 'भट्टेण' is taken as a corruption of 'भद्रेण'. 'मिचु' = भिक्षु. 'विश्राषणचत्रे' = विशाखानक्षत्रे. 'माणिकलकेः' = Māṇigala, i.e. Patan. 'उत्रविहारे' and 'हर्षवर्णमहाविहार' are probably corrupt. They might stand for Rudravarṇa-mahāvihāra (Uku Bahal, Patan), but this is uncertain.
review: Year: Bendall reads N.S. 549 (A.D. 1429). The OCR '५४७' is most likely a misreading of ५४९, so year 549 and ce_approx 1429 are used, with the discrepancy noted.

King: the name was read as Jayayakṣamalladeva, with medium confidence. 'जयजन्मलदेवस्य' is corrupt, and in NS 549 Yakṣamalla was reigning, not Jyotirmalla, who died c. 1428. The title 'rājan' was dropped.
Scribe: the name was corrected to Jivayibhadra, following Bendall's English note. 'भट्टेण' is an OCR corruption of 'भद्रेण'.
Nakshatra: 'विश्राषणचत्रे' is normalised to Viśākhā (विशाखानक्षत्रे).
Affiliation: the vihāra name is flagged as uncertain in the notes.
Relation evidence shortened.

title: KHAḌGA-PŪJĀVIDHI
date_raw: dated N. s. 381, middle figure doubtful (A. D. 1261)
date_note: = Tuesday 4 Oct 1261, verified by the pañcāṅga with one departure from the standard reading: tithi current later that day or expired
colophon: खड्गपूजाविधि समाप्तः । समाप्तः ३८१ (?) अश्विनि [? द]शम्यां तिथौ अञ्जार (?) दिने लिखितमिति । राजादिराजप्रमेश्चर (sic) श्री [?] ह मालदेवकारित । शके वैहारश्रीभिचु देव- मना लिखित ।
notes: Bendall reads the date as N.S. 381, with the middle figure doubtful (A.D. 1261). The colophon does not name the era, but N.S. is implied. Bendall's conversion is kept for ce_approx. The king's name is damaged: 'श्री [?] ह मालदेव'. One possible reading is Jayasīhamalladeva, who reigned about N.S. 391–394 (1271–1274 CE). If so, the doubtful middle figure could be 9, giving N.S. 391 (1271 CE). In 1261 the reigning king was Jayabhīmadeva, and his name does not fit '…ha malladeva'. This is unresolved. 'कारित' is taken to mean that the king commissioned the copy, but it could be only a formula of royal patronage. अञ्जार is probably aṅgāra (Tuesday). The scribe's name and his vihāra ('शके वैहारश्रीभिचु', perhaps Śākya-vihāra śrī-bhikṣu, or a corrupt 'śākyabhikṣu') are corrupt. The name could also be read Devamaṇi or Devamati.
review: King's name: confidence lowered to low; noted possible reading Jayasīhamalladeva (NS 391–394), which would fit if Bendall's doubtful middle figure is 9 rather than 8
Scribe's name normalized to the stem 'Devamana' (देवमना read as a nominative); confidence lowered to low
Scribe's affiliation given as a corrupt vihāra name (perhaps Śākya-vihāra) rather than 'Śake-vaihāra'; place of copying left empty because the colophon does not say where the copy was made
Added an under_reign_of relation from the scribe to the king
Notes expanded: the date and the king may not match, and several readings are uncertain

title: ÇAMBARA-PAÑJIKĀ
script: writing similar to that of No. I
colophon: स्ववरा (*sic*) पञ्चिकेयं समाप्तं। सर्वज्ञमित्रपादानां य (?) गुरु परंपरा .... ता। समादि सर्वसत्त्वराम् निस्सामसत्त्व (?)।
notes: This is part IX of Bendall's composite entry Add. 1706: 7 palm leaves of a Śambara-pañjikā, a manual of Śambara worship. The ending is corrupt ('स्ववरा (sic) पञ्चिकेयं समाप्तं' presumably stands for शम्बरपञ्जिकेयं). The verse after it names the guru lineage (गुरुपरंपरा) of Sarvajñamitra. He may be the author of the manual or only the head of the teaching lineage it comes from; his link to this copy is uncertain. He is possibly the Kashmiri Sarvajñamitra, author of the Sragdharāstotra, but that is not certain. No scribe, donor, owner, king, date or place of copying is given. Bendall gives no date for this part; he says only that the writing is similar to that of No. I.
review: Sarvajñamitra: dropped role 'teacher' (no teacher–pupil link to the scribe or owner of this copy is stated; he is named as the head of a guru lineage in the text's closing verse). Kept 'author' at low confidence.
Removed 'pāda' from titles: it is an honorific plural (-pādānām), not a caste or office title.
Purpose cleared: 'समादि सर्वसत्त्वराम्...' is a corrupt part of the work's closing verse, not a statement of why this copy was made.
Notes expanded: no scribe, donor, date or place is given.

purpose: perpetual land grant (kṣetraṃ akṣayaṃ dattaṃ) to the Mānavihāra, with a eulogy of the royal line
notes:
The inscription is badly damaged.

Line 2: '. . . devasuta radevo' keeps only the endings of two names. Reading them as [Vṛṣa]devasuta [Śaṅka]radeva is a conjecture. It rests on Rajavamsi's reading 'śaṅkara-iti' in line 6 and on the known genealogy (Vṛṣadeva → Śaṅkaradeva → Dharmadeva → Mānadeva). Mānadeva is traditionally credited with founding the Mānavihāra, so the inscription may come from his reign or later. However, no reigning king, donor or recipient survives by name: 'rājā' appears only in line 13 and 'narendra' only in line 2.

Line 27, 'sāgraṃ śataṃ varṣāṇām', is part of the eulogy ('more than a hundred years'), not a date formula. No date survives.

p2: 'devasuta' gives only the end of the father's name. Read as [Vṛṣa]deva (Vṛṣadeva), low confidence.
p1 roles: changed from king/donor to relative_only. Śaṅkaradeva appears in a genealogical eulogy as an ancestor. The donor and reigning king are not preserved by name.
Removed 'narendra' as a title of p1. It stands separately in a broken context and may refer to someone else.

notes: The inscription is badly damaged: the top dozen or so lines are lost, so the issuing king's name and the grant details are gone. What survives is mostly the closing imprecatory verses and the date. The name before the date ends in '-na-gomī' (followed by 'iti'). purpose: Fragment; probably records a pious act (perhaps an endowment) for the liṅga Paṃkeśa. The text breaks off.
notes: Only line 1 survives, and it breaks off. The editor says only 'mentioned śrī-Paṃkeśa' (DV 175). Paṃkeśa looks like the name of a Śiva liṅga (founder's name + īśa, as in Licchavi usage), so it is not listed as a person. The founder (Paṃka?) is not named outright. 'jareṃ' is unclear, possibly corrupt or the start of a lost word. 'puṇyādhāre' is read as 'on an auspicious occasion'. The year is in the Licchavi saṃvat, left unconverted as instructed.
review: Removed Paṃkeśa from persons. A Licchavi name ending in -īśa/-eśa (Paṃka + īśa) is almost certainly a Śiva liṅga named after its founder, so it is a deity, not a person; the founder's name may be Paṃka, but the text does not say so.

Changed purpose from 'water conduit' to 'fragmentary; probably concerns the liṅga Paṃkeśa'. Puṇyādhāre most likely means 'on an auspicious occasion', not a reservoir, and nothing in the text points to a water conduit.

Date: as_written now keeps the full wording 'saṃvat 187 māghaśukladivā 5'.

It sets out jurisdiction (adhikaraṇas, dauvārikas, pāñcālikas), a schedule of fines and dues, and draṅga status for the villages Tāmrakuṭṭaśālā, Māneśvara, Śāmbhapura, Hmapriṃga, Puṭhampriṅga, Jamayambī and Puṃdaṭṭa. It ends with an imprecatory verse and a long list of boundaries.
notes: Lines 1–9 are worn away and lines 10–18 are almost unreadable, so the issuing king is lost. The roughly 9–10 lines after line 73, which would have held the dūtaka and the date, are also illegible. The date is lost entirely. Offices are mentioned without personal names: dauvārika (roga-mācau-, sindrira-, vetra-, sthāna-dauvārika), mahāpratīhāra (whose house compound is a boundary mark), and pāñcālikas. Jīvavarman is not listed as a person because he occurs only in the monastery name jīvavarmma-vihāra (l. 60), a boundary mark. The name 'vottarino' (l. 58), read as Vottarin, the maker of a water conduit, is uncertain and may be a corrupt reading. 'śrī-tukāṇa...' Place: added the find-spot detail and the present location (National Museum).
Notes: added the lost dūtaka and date, the unnamed officials, and the doubtful readings.

2. dattā eṣāṃ śilādroṇi sattvānāṃ hitahetave ||
purpose: gift of a stone water basin (śilādroṇī) by a nun for the welfare of beings (sattvānāṃ hitahetave)
notes: Fragment, badly damaged; R. 154. Undated. The verse is an irregular śloka: 'pauna pānyāṃ bhikṣuṇī | sadyobhoga dayā svayam | dattā eṣā(ṃ) śilādroṇī | sattvānāṃ hitahetave'. The first quarter-verse has only 7 syllables, so something may be lost. The donor is a bhikṣuṇī, but her name is uncertain: either 'Dayā', or 'dayā' = dayayā ('out of compassion') with the name hidden in 'sadyobhoga' (Sadyobhogā?). 'pauna pānyāṃ' may be a locative place name (the site of the gift) or a corrupt word, possibly part of a name. It is not used as a residence.
review: Kept the nun as the only person (donor), but the name is uncertain: Dayā, or possibly Sadyobhogā if dayā stands for dayayā ('out of compassion'). Explained in notes.

title: Viṣṇupādukā hill
subject: inscription
colophon:
1. devyāḥ
karttavyatābuddhyā śrīpādai . . . grajaḥ śailastambhakriyārambhe kedumbāṭo
niyojitaḥ
notes: This is a fragmentary, undated inscription (DV 8) on a column near a water conduit on Viṣṇupādukā hill. Kedumbāṭa was appointed (niyojitaḥ) to start the work on the stone pillar, apparently by royal order (śrīpādaiḥ). The king is not named. The queen (devyāḥ, 'for the queen' or 'of the goddess') is not named either. The lacuna 'śrīpādai . . . grajaḥ' may hide a word ending in -agrajaḥ ('elder brother'). If so, someone named in the lost text is described as an elder brother, possibly Kedumbāṭa himself, but this cannot be checked. 'Kedumbāṭa' is taken as a personal name, but it is not certain.
review: Kedumbāṭa: confidence lowered from high to medium, because the text is a fragment and the word could be a title or designation rather than a personal name. His role is kept as official, since he was appointed (niyojitaḥ) to the work.
place.normalized cleared: Viṣṇupādukā hill is in the northern Kathmandu Valley, but no modern place is certain enough to give.
